questionEn: What is the literal linguistic meaning of the Arabic word 'Umrah' in classical Arabic?
optionsEn: A long journey across desert valleys
Sacrificing an animal during Eid
Standing at an elevated mountain peak
A visit or visiting a populated place
explanationEn: Linguistically, 'Umrah' derives from 'i'timar', meaning a visit (al-ziyarah), and in Shari'ah refers specifically to visiting the Sacred House (Kaaba) to perform prescribed rituals.
reference: Lisan al-Arab; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse explicitly commands believers to complete both Hajj and Umrah solely for the sake of Allah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Mulk 67:2
Surah Al-Kawthar 108:2
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:196
Surah Al-Ikhlas 112:1
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:196) begins with the divine command: 'And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah' (Wa atimmul-hajja wal-'umrata lillah).

questionEn: What is the ruling of performing Umrah once in a lifetime according to the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools of jurisprudence?
optionsEn: Recommended exclusively during the month of Shawwal
Merely permissible (Mubah) with no extra recommendation
Obligatory only upon residents of Madinah
Obligatory (Fard / Wajib) upon every financially and physically able adult Muslim
explanationEn: The Shafi'i and Hanbali schools hold that Umrah is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who possess the means (istita'ah), citing Qur'an 2:196 and Hadith reports.
reference: Al-Majmu' by al-Nawawi; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

questionEn: How do the Hanafi and Maliki schools classify the legal ruling of performing Umrah?
optionsEn: A communal obligation (Fard Kifayah)
An optional act valid only after Hajj
A pillar of Islam alongside Salah and Zakah
A strongly emphasized Sunnah (Sunnah Mu'akkadah) once in a lifetime
explanationEn: According to the Hanafi and Maliki schools, performing Umrah once in a lifetime is Sunnah Mu'akkadah, though once begun it becomes obligatory to complete.

questionEn: Even in schools that consider initiating Umrah a Sunnah, what happens once a pilgrim enters Ihram for Umrah?
optionsEn: Completing all its rituals becomes obligatory (Wajib)
It may be abandoned at will before Tawaf without penalty
It automatically converts into a voluntary prayer
It remains optional until after Sa'i
explanationEn: By scholarly consensus based on Qur'an 2:196 ('Complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah'), once a person enters Ihram for Umrah, completing it becomes mandatory.

questionEn: In a famous Hadith narrated by Ibn Umar (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ say about pilgrims performing Hajj and Umrah together as Allah's guests?
optionsEn: Only residents of the Hijaz are counted as Allah's delegation
The warrior in Allah's path, the pilgrim of Hajj, and the performer of Umrah are Allah's delegation; if they call upon Him, He answers them
Only those who travel on foot receive answers to their supplications
Their delegation status ends before entering Makkah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ described the fighter in Allah's cause, the Hajji, and the Mu'tamir (Umrah pilgrim) as the delegation of Allah (Wafd Allah) whose supplications are answered and forgiveness granted.

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, what spiritual effect does performing one Umrah followed by another Umrah have?
optionsEn: It serves as an expiation for the minor sins committed between the two
It exempts a Muslim from praying Jumu'ah for a year
It cancels the obligation of Fard Hajj
It replaces the obligation of paying annual Zakah
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'From one Umrah to the next is an expiation for whatever (sins) occurred between them.'

questionEn: In the Hadith reported by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA), what two things did the Prophet ﷺ say alternating Hajj and Umrah eliminates?
optionsEn: Debts owed to non-Muslims automatically
Hunger and thirst during summer travel
Disagreements between scholars in Madinah
Poverty and sins, just as a blacksmith's bellows removes dross from iron, gold, and silver
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'Follow up Hajj and Umrah consecutively, for they remove poverty and sins just as the bellows removes impurities from iron, gold, and silver.'

questionEn: When Aisha (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ whether women have an obligation of Jihad, what did he ﷺ reply?
optionsEn: Only charitable endowments for mosques
Yes, a Jihad in which there is no fighting: Hajj and Umrah
No, women have no comparable worship to Jihad
Only fasting Mondays and Thursdays in Madinah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Aisha (RA) that women have a noble Jihad without combat, namely performing a righteous Hajj and Umrah.

questionEn: Which Sahabiya was told by the Prophet ﷺ that performing Umrah in Ramadan equals Hajj (or Hajj with him ﷺ) in reward?
optionsEn: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA)
Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib (RA) alone
Umm Ma'qil (RA), though narrations also mention an Ansari woman named Umm Sinan
Fatimah bint Asad (RA)
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ comforted an Ansari woman (narrated as Umm Ma'qil or Umm Sinan) who missed Hajj with him by saying: 'Umrah in Ramadan is equivalent to Hajj with me.'

questionEn: Does performing Umrah in Ramadan fulfill the obligatory Fard Hajj of Islam?
optionsEn: No, it equals Hajj in spiritual reward only, not in fulfilling the legal pillar of Hajj
Yes, if repeated three times during Ramadan
Yes, if performed in the last ten nights of Ramadan
Only for pilgrims under the age of thirty
explanationEn: Scholars unanimously agree that the Hadith refers to equivalence in spiritual reward, whereas the once-in-a-lifetime pillar of Hajj still remains obligatory upon those who are able.

questionEn: How many times did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform Umrah after the Hijrah to Madinah?
optionsEn: Once during the Farewell Pilgrimage only
Two times
Six times
Four times
explanationEn: According to Ibn Abbas (RA) and Anas ibn Malik (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ performed four Umrahs after the Hijrah: Hudaybiyyah, al-Qada', al-Ji'ranah, and the Umrah accompanying his Hajj.

questionEn: In which Islamic lunar month did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ enter Ihram for all four of his post-Hijrah Umrahs?
optionsEn: Ramadan
Dhul-Qa'dah (including his Hajj Qiran Umrah, though he exited the last one in Dhul-Hijjah)
Muharram
Rajab
explanationEn: Anas (RA) noted that all four of the Prophet's ﷺ Umrahs were initiated in Dhul-Qa'dah, demonstrating the merit of performing Umrah in Dhul-Qa'dah as well.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ tell Aisha (RA) that her reward for Umrah is proportional to her expenditure and effort?
optionsEn: To prohibit riding animals during pilgrimage
To teach that wealthy pilgrims always receive less reward
To console her and affirm that sincere hardship and spending in Umrah increase reward
To encourage pilgrims to pay excessive amounts unnecessarily
explanationEn: During her Umrah from al-Tan'im, the Prophet ﷺ told Aisha (RA): 'Your reward is according to your fatigue (or spending),' teaching that hardship endured sincerely for Allah is rewarded.

questionEn: Which two terms distinguish Umrah from Hajj in classical Islamic texts?
optionsEn: Umrah is called 'al-Rihlah' and Hajj is 'al-Siyahah'
Umrah is called 'al-Safar' and Hajj is 'al-Ziyarah'
Umrah is called 'al-Hajj al-Asghar' (the Minor Pilgrimage) and Hajj is 'al-Hajj al-Akbar' (the Major Pilgrimage)
Umrah is called 'al-Fajr' and Hajj is 'al-Dhuhr'
explanationEn: Umrah is traditionally termed the Minor Pilgrimage (al-Hajj al-Asghar) because it shares Ihram, Tawaf, and Sa'i with Hajj without Arafah, Muzdalifah, Mina, or Jamarat.

questionEn: During which days of the year is performing a separate Umrah prohibited or invalid according to many scholars for pilgrims engaged in Hajj?
optionsEn: Every Friday afternoon throughout the year
During the entire month of Sha'ban
During the active days of Hajj (Day of Arafah through the Days of Tashriq, 9–13 Dhul-Hijjah)
During the first ten days of Muharram
explanationEn: While Umrah is generally valid year-round, the Hanafi school deems it makruh tahriman on 9–13 Dhul-Hijjah, and the majority note that active Hajj pilgrims cannot initiate a separate Umrah while in Hajj rituals during those days.

questionEn: What is the key difference in pillars between Umrah and Hajj?
optionsEn: Umrah requires only three circuits of Tawaf instead of seven
Umrah requires fasting three days before leaving Makkah
Umrah does not require entering Ihram at a Miqat
Umrah has no standing at Arafah, no overnight stay at Muzdalifah or Mina, and no stoning of the Jamarat
explanationEn: Umrah consists of Ihram, Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir, whereas Hajj adds standing at Arafah, Muzdalifah, Mina, Jamarat, and Farewell Tawaf.

questionEn: What are the two universally agreed-upon pillars (Arkan) of Umrah according to the Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanbali schools, alongside Ihram?
optionsEn: Tawaf around the Kaaba and Sa'i between Safa and Marwah (with Ihram making three pillars)
Standing at Arafah and drinking Zamzam
Kissing the Black Stone and praying inside Hijr Ismail
Sacrificing a sheep and visiting Masjid Quba
explanationEn: The majority of scholars identify three pillars of Umrah: Ihram (intention to enter the ritual), Tawaf, and Sa'i (while Hanafis classify Tawaf as the pillar and Sa'i/Halq as Wajib).

questionEn: Which act in Umrah is classified as Wajib (obligatory, whose omission requires a sacrificial penalty) rather than a pillar by most scholars?
optionsEn: Drinking Zamzam water after Tawaf
Touching Rukn al-Yamani
Entering Ihram from the Miqat and shaving/trimming hair (Halq or Taqsir)
Doing Raml in the first three circuits
explanationEn: Assuming Ihram at the appointed Miqat and performing Halq or Taqsir are Wajibat of Umrah according to the Hanbali and Shafi'i majority views on Miqat/Halq (though Shafi'is count Halq/Taqsir as a pillar).

questionEn: Why is performing Umrah with unlawful (haram) wealth strongly warned against in Islamic teachings?
optionsEn: It prevents a pilgrim from drinking Zamzam
Allah is Pure and accepts only what is pure, as taught in authentic Hadith
It renders the airplane ticket invalid at Miqat
It doubles the number of Tawaf circuits required
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught: 'Allah is Pure (Tayyib) and accepts only that which is pure,' reminding pilgrims to fund their Umrah solely from halal earnings.

questionEn: When a young pre-pubescent child performs Umrah under a guardian's supervision, is the child's Umrah valid?
optionsEn: Yes, and it permanently exempts the child from adult Hajj and Umrah
Yes, it is valid and rewarded, though it does not fulfill the obligatory lifetime Umrah after puberty
No, children under fifteen cannot enter Ihram
Only if the child is a male
explanationEn: A woman lifted her child to the Prophet ﷺ asking if Hajj counts for him; he ﷺ replied: 'Yes, and you will have a reward.' Scholars apply the same principle to Umrah.

questionEn: Under what condition is performing Badal Umrah (Umrah on behalf of another person) permissible?
optionsEn: When the beneficiary is healthy but busy with work
Only for residents of Makkah
For anyone who wants to save travel expenses
When the beneficiary is deceased or permanently incapacitated physically (such as chronic illness or extreme old age)
explanationEn: Scholars permit Badal Umrah for someone who has passed away or is permanently unable to travel due to incurable illness or frailty, based on the Hadith of the Khath'amiyyah woman and Abu Razin.

questionEn: What condition must a proxy pilgrim satisfy before performing Umrah on behalf of someone else according to the Hadith of Shubrumah?
optionsEn: The proxy must be a blood sibling of the deceased
The proxy must have already performed their own Umrah first
The proxy must perform two Tawafs back-to-back
The proxy must reside in Madinah for a month
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ heard a man intending pilgrimage for Shubrumah, he asked: 'Have you performed your own?' When he said no, the Prophet ﷺ told him: 'Perform it for yourself first, then for Shubrumah.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1811; Sunan Ibn Majah 2903

questionEn: What advice did the Prophet ﷺ give to Abu Razin al-Uqayli (RA) when he asked about his elderly father who could neither perform Hajj nor Umrah?
optionsEn: Give one silver coin to a neighbor
Perform Hajj and Umrah on behalf of your father
Build a water trough in Ta'if
Fast thirty consecutive days instead
explanationEn: Abu Razin (RA) asked about his frail father unable to sit securely on a mount, and the Prophet ﷺ instructed him: 'Perform Hajj on behalf of your father and perform Umrah.'

questionEn: Before departing for Umrah, what moral duty toward family and fellow human beings should a pilgrim fulfill?
optionsEn: Avoid informing family of travel dates
Fast continuously during the flight
Repent sincerely, settle debts or secure permission from creditors, and reconcile broken ties
Sell all personal belongings regardless of dependents
explanationEn: Scholars emphasize sincere repentance (tawbah), returning trusts, paying due debts (or obtaining the creditor's consent), and leaving sufficient provision for dependents before travel.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj (22:32), what does honoring the sacred symbols (Sha'a'ir) of Allah—such as the rites of Umrah—reflect?
optionsEn: Social status among tribes
The piety (taqwa) of the hearts
Knowledge of Arabic poetry
Mastery of trade routes
explanationEn: Allah states: 'And whoever honors the sacred symbols of Allah—indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.'

questionEn: What does the Prophet's ﷺ statement 'The Hajj and Umrah pilgrims are guests of Allah' encourage in a pilgrim's conduct?
optionsEn: Speaking loudly during every prayer
Demanding VIP seating inside the Mataf
Humility, patience, abundant dua, and refraining from harming others in the Sanctuaries
Rushing ahead of elderly pilgrims in Tawaf
explanationEn: Being hosted by Allah calls for reverence, gentle manners, constant supplication, and utmost care not to jostle or offend fellow guests of Allah.

questionEn: Which type of Hajj combines an Umrah first, exiting Ihram after Umrah, and then re-entering Ihram for Hajj on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: Umrah al-Mufradah
Hajj al-Qiran
Hajj al-Tamattu'
Hajj al-Ifrad
explanationEn: In Hajj al-Tamattu', the pilgrim performs Umrah during the Hajj months, exits Ihram completely via Taqsir/Halq, and later assumes Ihram again for Hajj.

questionEn: In Hajj al-Qiran, how are Umrah and Hajj performed?
optionsEn: Umrah is performed in Rajab and Hajj in Dhul-Hijjah
Both Umrah and Hajj are combined under a single continuous state of Ihram without exiting in between
Two separate sacrifices are replaced by two Tawafs
Only Umrah is performed while Hajj is skipped
explanationEn: In Hajj al-Qiran, the pilgrim declares intention for both Hajj and Umrah together at Miqat and remains in Ihram until completing the rites of Yawm al-Nahr (10th Dhul-Hijjah).

questionEn: During the Farewell Pilgrimage, what did the Prophet ﷺ command companions who had not brought sacrificial animals (Hady) to do with their Ihram?
optionsEn: Discard their Izar and Rida' at Mina
Return immediately to Madinah without Tawaf
Fast ten days inside Makkah before Tawaf
Convert their pilgrimage into Umrah (Tamattu') by completing Tawaf, Sa'i, and trimming hair
explanationEn: Those without Hady were instructed by the Prophet ﷺ to make their intention Umrah, perform Tawaf and Sa'i, shorten their hair, and exit Ihram until Hajj began.

questionEn: Which two Sahabis initially wondered about performing Umrah during the months of Hajj before the Prophet ﷺ demonstrated its permissibility?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr and Umar banned Umrah permanently
Bilal and Salman refused to travel in Dhul-Qa'dah
The Arabs of Jahiliyyah considered Umrah in Hajj months one of the worst sins, which the Prophet ﷺ abolished
Mu'adh and Abu Musa restricted Umrah to Muharram
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that pre-Islamic Arabs viewed Umrah during the Hajj months as a grave sin; the Prophet ﷺ overturned that misconception by performing Umrah in Dhul-Qa'dah and teaching Tamattu'.

questionEn: What are the three Islamic 'months of Hajj' (Ashhur al-Hajj) in which performing Umrah before Hajj constitutes Tamattu'?
optionsEn: Rajab, Sha'ban, and Ramadan
Muharram, Safar, and Rabi' al-Awwal
Jumada al-Ula, Jumada al-Akhirah, and Rajab
Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and the first ten days (or all) of Dhul-Hijjah
explanationEn: The months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah (specifically the first 10 days according to many scholars, or the full month in Maliki fiqh).

questionEn: Is performing multiple Umrahs in a single brief journey to Makkah Sunnah according to the practice of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions?
optionsEn: Performing a second Umrah in a year invalidates the first
Doing voluntary Tawaf without Umrah is forbidden
It is strictly required to perform seven Umrahs per week in Makkah

Most scholars note the Prophet ﷺ and Companions performed one Umrah per journey, focusing afterward on voluntary Tawaf and Salah, though repeating Umrah from al-Hil is permissible with scholarly nuance
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ performed one Umrah per visit and Aisha's (RA) extra Umrah from Tan'im was because she had entered menstruation before her first Umrah; thus many scholars advise prioritizing abundant Tawaf and prayer while recognizing permissible views on repeating Umrah after a reasonable gap.

questionEn: Why did Aisha (RA) perform a second Umrah from al-Tan'im at the end of the Farewell Pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Because all female pilgrims are required to perform two Umrahs each trip
To compensate for having merged her earlier Umrah into Hajj Qiran when menstruation delayed her Tawaf
Because the Prophet ﷺ forgot to stop at Miqat
Because her first Tawaf was done without a veil
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) felt saddened that others had performed an independent Umrah while she had converted to Qiran; to comfort her, the Prophet ﷺ sent her brother Abd al-Rahman to take her to al-Tan'im for a separate Umrah.

questionEn: What is the minimum financial capability (Istita'ah) required for Umrah to be obligatory upon a Muslim?
optionsEn: Owning real estate in Makkah or Jeddah
Borrowing high-interest loans to fund travel
Saving gold equal to a full year's harvest
Having safe transport and expenses beyond basic needs, debts, and family maintenance
explanationEn: Istita'ah means possessing the physical health, safe passage, and surplus wealth needed for round-trip travel and expenses after fulfilling debts and dependents' needs.

questionEn: Should a Muslim borrow money on interest or neglect dependents' sustenance to perform a voluntary Umrah?
optionsEn: Yes, if the Umrah takes place in Rajab
No; interest is prohibited and fulfilling dependents' rights takes precedence over voluntary travel
Yes, because any loan taken for Umrah is automatically forgiven
Only if the borrower skips Sa'i
explanationEn: Islamic law forbids riba (usury) and prioritizes obligatory family maintenance and settling due debts over voluntary acts of worship.

questionEn: What travel Sunnah did the Prophet ﷺ practice when setting out on journeys such as Umrah?
optionsEn: Leaving on journeys only during solar eclipses
Refusing to recite any supplications until reaching the Kaaba
Praying two rak'ahs before departing (or upon returning), reciting the travel dua, and preferring Thursday departures when possible
Traveling alone without companions at night
explanationEn: Ka'b ibn Malik (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ loved setting out on Thursdays, recited the travel dua ('Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha...'), and prayed two rak'ahs in the masjid upon returning.

questionEn: What should a group of Muslims traveling together for Umrah do regarding leadership during the journey?
optionsEn: Travel separately and never consult one another
Avoid appointing any coordinator
Appoint one capable person among them as leader (Amir) to coordinate decisions and harmony
Allow only the youngest child to decide prayer times
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ advised: 'When three people set out on a journey, let them appoint one of them as their leader,' ensuring order and unity during Umrah travel.

questionEn: Is there a specific month called 'Rajab Umrah' mandated by the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: No; Aisha (RA) explicitly clarified that the Prophet ﷺ never performed Umrah in Rajab
Yes; Rajab Umrah is mandatory for every Muslim once every decade
Only during the 27th night of Rajab
Yes; Umrah in Rajab carries greater reward than Ramadan
explanationEn: When Ibn Umar (RA) mentioned the Prophet ﷺ performed an Umrah in Rajab, Aisha (RA) corrected this, noting he ﷺ never performed Umrah in Rajab (all four were in Dhul-Qa'dah), though Umrah in Rajab remains permissible.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim dedicate the spiritual reward of an optional Umrah to a deceased Muslim parent?
optionsEn: Only if the parent died inside Makkah
Yes, performing Umrah on behalf of a deceased Muslim parent is widely permitted and praised by scholars
No, only living people can benefit from Badal Umrah
Only after fasting sixty consecutive days
explanationEn: Based on authentic narrations permitting pilgrimage on behalf of deceased parents, performing Umrah for a deceased mother or father is an act of filial devotion (birr).

questionEn: Which of the following best describes the relationship between repentance (Tawbah) and Umrah?
optionsEn: Umrah should be preceded by sincere repentance from sins and a resolve to maintain righteousness afterward
Umrah forgives sins even while intentionally persisting in major wrongdoing
Umrah removes the need to return stolen property to its rightful owner
Repentance is only valid after returning home from Jeddah
explanationEn: True repentance requires remorse, abandoning sin, resolving not to return, and restoring people's rights; combining this with Umrah brings immense mercy.

questionEn: In the Hadith of Abu Hurayrah (RA), what reward did the Prophet ﷺ promise for a 'Hajj Mabrur'—and how does that principle apply to an accepted Umrah?
optionsEn: It guarantees worldly wealth within forty days
An accepted pilgrimage free of sin, ostentation, and quarrel earns Paradise and spiritual renewal
It grants exemption from honoring parents
It removes the duty of daily prayers afterward
explanationEn: Scholars teach that an 'Umrah Mabrurah'—performed with halal funds, correct Sunnah, sincerity, and good character—similarly leads to forgiveness and renewed righteousness.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding spending generously on a journey for Umrah or Hajj compared to spending in Allah's cause?
optionsEn: Spending on Umrah receives no extra reward beyond travel
Pilgrims should never spend money on food during travel
Only charity given in Madinah is multiplied
Spending in Hajj and Umrah is like spending in the path of Allah, multiplied seven hundred fold
explanationEn: In Musnad Ahmad and Sunan narrations (from Buraydah RA), spending for pilgrimage is likened to spending in the path of Allah, multiplied seven hundred times.

questionEn: What is the ruling if someone dies after entering Ihram for Umrah before completing Tawaf or Sa'i?
optionsEn: They are washed with water and lote leaves, shrouded in their two Ihram cloths without perfume or head covering, and will be raised reciting the Talbiyah
Their face must be covered during burial for men
They are buried in stitched silk garments with perfume
Their family must pay a hunting penalty
explanationEn: When a pilgrim in Ihram passed away at Arafah, the Prophet ﷺ ordered him shrouded in his two Ihram garments with head uncovered and no perfume, saying he will be resurrected reciting Talbiyah.

questionEn: If a person made a vow (Nadhr) to perform Umrah, what is the Islamic ruling on fulfilling it?
optionsEn: A vow of Umrah may be ignored without expiation
Fulfilling a valid vow of obedience such as Umrah becomes obligatory (Wajib)
Only vows made inside Masjid al-Haram count
A vow converts Umrah into a single Tawaf
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him.' Thus a vow to perform Umrah makes its performance obligatory.

questionEn: Which quality must accompany every step of Umrah so that the ritual is accepted by Allah?
optionsEn: Carrying a written certificate from a travel agency
Recording every circuit on social media live streams
Reciting in loud unison with a microphone inside the Mataf
Ikhlas (pure sincerity for Allah alone) and Mutaba'ah (following the Prophet's ﷺ Sunnah)
explanationEn: Every act of worship requires two foundational conditions for acceptance: pure intention for Allah's sake (ikhlas) and conformity with Prophetic guidance (mutaba'ah).

questionEn: Why did Allah remind pilgrims in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:197) to take provisions, adding that 'the best provision is Taqwa'?
optionsEn: To balance practical travel preparation with the supreme importance of God-consciousness and avoiding reliance on begging
To teach that only scholars may perform Umrah
To require fasting throughout the entire stay in Makkah
To forbid bringing food from home
explanationEn: This verse corrected people from Yemen who traveled without provisions claiming reliance on Allah and then begged others, reminding them to prepare materially while prioritizing Taqwa.

questionEn: What are the three cardinal sins of speech and behavior specifically forbidden in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:197) during pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Rafath (lewdness/marital intimacy), Fusuq (sinful disobedience), and Jidal (quarrelling/disputing)
Eating dates, speaking quietly, and sleeping at noon
Walking slowly, wearing sandals, and drinking cold water
Asking directions, carrying water, and sitting in shade
explanationEn: Allah declares: 'Whoever undertakes pilgrimage therein, let there be no sexual relations (rafath), no wickedness (fusuq), and no disputing (jidal) during the pilgrimage.'

questionEn: Is there any restriction on the number of times a Muslim may perform Umrah in their lifetime?
optionsEn: Yes, a maximum of three Umrahs per lifetime
Yes, only once every five years
No; it is praiseworthy to perform Umrah whenever genuinely able across different journeys
Only one Umrah is valid before Hajj
explanationEn: The Hadith 'From one Umrah to the next is an expiation for what is between them' shows that performing Umrah repeatedly across journeys is encouraged and rewarding.

questionEn: Which great Companion was commanded by the Prophet ﷺ to invite people to Umrah and taught pilgrims its concise rulings after him?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) and Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) were among the foremost transmitters of Umrah and Hajj fiqh
Musaylamah al-Kadhdhab
Ubayy ibn Khalaf
Only Abu Jahl
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Jabir ibn Abdullah, and Aisha (RA) preserved detailed eyewitness narrations of the Prophet's ﷺ Ihram, Tawaf, Sa'i, and Umrah rulings.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Umrah; Sahih Muslim

questionEn: Does performing Umrah require obtaining permission from one's parents when the Umrah is voluntary (Nafl)?
optionsEn: Permission is only needed for travel by sea
Yes, seeking parents' consent and honoring their needs is strongly emphasized for voluntary travel
No, parents have no rights once a child reaches age twelve
Only the father's uncle must consent
explanationEn: Jurists teach that for voluntary Umrah, a child should seek parents' permission and not leave them in hardship or need, honoring the high rank of birr al-walidayn.

questionEn: If a person performs a valid Umrah before ever performing Hajj, is that permissible?
optionsEn: No, Hajj must always precede Umrah
Only for men over forty
Only if performed during Shawwal
Yes, Umrah is completely valid whether performed before or after Hajj
explanationEn: Performing Umrah prior to Hajj is fully valid—indeed, thousands of Companions performed Tamattu' Umrah before their Hajj during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

questionEn: What is the significance of performing Umrah before Hajj in terms of the 'Ashhur al-Hajj' ruling for non-residents of Makkah?
optionsEn: Performing Umrah during Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, or early Dhul-Hijjah and staying in Makkah for Hajj makes the pilgrim a Mutamatti' obligated to offer a Hady
It cancels the need to stand at Arafah
It turns Umrah into a voluntary fasting week
It exempts the pilgrim from Tawaf al-Ifadah
explanationEn: Allah states in 2:196 that whoever enjoys (tamatta'a) Umrah up to Hajj offers what is feasible of sacrificial animals (Hady) or fasts 3 days in Hajj and 7 upon returning.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ praise the humility of Umrah pilgrims even in their outward appearance?
optionsEn: Because arriving 'ash'atha aghbar' (disheveled and dusty) in simple Ihram demonstrates total humility before Allah
Because torn clothes are preferred over clean ones
Because pilgrims must walk barefoot across deserts
Because pilgrims are forbidden from washing their hands
explanationEn: In Qudsi and Prophetic narrations (such as Muslim 1348 regarding Arafah and Ibn Hibban regarding pilgrims), Allah boasts to the angels about His servants coming humble, disheveled, and sincere in devotion.

questionEn: When a Muslim greets a pilgrim returning from Umrah, what is a Sunnah-grounded prayer to say to them?
optionsEn: Reciting Surah al-Fil seven times
Asking Allah to accept their Umrah, forgive their sins, and replace their expenses (e.g., 'Qabilallahu nusukaka...')
Asking them to pay a special travel tax
Asking them never to visit Madinah again
explanationEn: Narrations from Ibn Umar (RA) and classical scholars mention welcoming returning pilgrims and asking them for dua before they enter their homes, alongside praying for acceptance of their pilgrimage.

questionEn: Is there any restriction against combining a visit to Madinah (Ziyarah of Masjid al-Nabawi) with an Umrah trip?
optionsEn: Visiting Masjid al-Nabawi is mandatory before Umrah can be valid
Yes, Madinah may never be visited in the same trip as Umrah
No; visiting Masjid al-Nabawi is highly meritorious at any time, though it is not a ritual pillar of Umrah itself
Only residents of Egypt may visit Madinah after Umrah
explanationEn: Visiting Masjid al-Nabawi is a virtuous Sunnah journey of its own ('Do not undertake a special journey except to three mosques...'), though Umrah itself is valid even if one visits Makkah directly.

questionEn: What is the reward of a single prayer performed inside Al-Masjid al-Haram during an Umrah trip?
optionsEn: Equal to 10 prayers
Equal to 1,000 prayers
Better than 100,000 prayers in any other mosque
Equal to 500 prayers
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'A prayer in my mosque is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except Al-Masjid al-Haram, and a prayer in Al-Masjid al-Haram is better than one hundred thousand prayers elsewhere.'

questionEn: Does the 100,000-fold reward apply only to the area immediately around the Kaaba or to the entire Sanctuary of Makkah?
optionsEn: Only to the two-meter strip beside Maqam Ibrahim
Only to the roof of Safa
Only during the Fajr prayer
According to many scholars, it applies to Al-Masjid al-Haram and the broader sacred precinct (Haram) of Makkah, with the Masjid itself being foremost
explanationEn: While all scholars agree on the immense virtue of Al-Masjid al-Haram itself, a large body of scholars (including Ibn Abbas and Ata) extend this virtue to mosques within the Sacred Haram limits of Makkah.

questionEn: Why is performing Umrah sometimes more peaceful for elderly or first-time pilgrims outside peak seasons?
optionsEn: Lower crowd density allows calmer Tawaf, unhurried prayer behind Maqam Ibrahim, and focused Sa'i without altering any Islamic ruling
Because Miqat rules are suspended outside Ramadan
Because Talbiyah is omitted in cooler weather
Because winter Umrah requires only 5 circuits of Tawaf
explanationEn: All pillars and rulings of Umrah remain identical throughout the year, while less crowded months help elderly or weak pilgrims fulfill the rites with greater tranquility.

questionEn: What does 'Tawaf' mean literally, and why is it central to Umrah?
optionsEn: Sacrificing a camel at Mina
Walking in a straight line between two hills
Circling around something; circling the Kaaba seven times is the primary act of worship around Allah's Sacred House
Standing silently in one corner
explanationEn: Tawaf means circumambulation—circling the Kaaba seven times in devotion, echoing the angels who circle Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur in the heavens.

questionEn: Which prophet originally raised the foundations of the Kaaba along with his son Isma'il (AS), establishing the sanctuary where Umrah is performed?
optionsEn: Prophet Dawud (AS)
Prophet Isa (AS)
Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
Prophet Musa (AS)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:125–127) records how Ibrahim and Isma'il (AS) raised the foundations of the House and prayed for its acceptance as a place of worship and safety.

questionEn: Why must a Muslim have full mental sanity (Aql) for Umrah to become obligatory upon them?
optionsEn: Because insane persons are barred from entering Makkah
Because legal accountability (Taklif) in Islam requires sanity and maturity
Because sanity is only needed during Sa'i
Because Umrah requires memorizing 100 verses first
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that the pen is lifted from three: the sleeper until waking, the child until maturity, and the person lacking reason until recovering.

questionEn: If a person converts to Islam after having visited Makkah earlier in life as a non-Muslim, is their previous visit counted as Umrah?
optionsEn: Yes, any sightseeing trip counts as Umrah
Yes, if they wore white clothing
No; Islam is a prerequisite for valid worship, so they must perform Umrah as a Muslim if able
Only if they drank Zamzam water
explanationEn: All acts of ritual worship require faith in Islam and valid intention (niyyah), and non-Muslims are not permitted within the Haram boundaries.

questionEn: In the Hadith of Jibril, is Umrah explicitly listed among the five structural pillars of Islam, or is Hajj listed?
optionsEn: Umrah is listed instead of Zakah
Hajj is explicitly listed as the fifth pillar, while Umrah is closely linked to pilgrimage in Qur'an 2:196
Neither Hajj nor Umrah is mentioned
Both Hajj and Umrah are listed as the sixth and seventh pillars
explanationEn: In the Hadith of Jibril and Ibn Umar (RA), the five pillars of Islam are Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm Ramadan, and Hajj; Umrah is an additional deeply revered pilgrimage rite.

questionEn: What is the linguistic and legal meaning of 'Nusuk' in the context of Umrah and Hajj?
optionsEn: A silver coin minted in Makkah
Devotional rites of pilgrimage and worship (and sometimes specifically a sacrificial offering)
A desert caravan route
A type of leather sandal
explanationEn: Nusuk (plural manasik) refers to acts of worship and specifically the prescribed rites of Hajj and Umrah, as in Qur'an 2:196 and 2:128 ('Wa arina manasikana').

questionEn: What did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) ask Allah in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:128 right after raising the Kaaba's foundations?
optionsEn: 'Abolish the month of Ramadan'
'Grant us palaces of marble in Yemen'
'Make Umrah obligatory every week'
'Our Lord, make us Muslims submitting to You... and show us our rites (manasikana) and accept our repentance'
explanationEn: Ibrahim and Isma'il (AS) supplicated for steadfast submission, knowledge of the pilgrimage rites (manasik), and divine acceptance.

questionEn: If a pilgrim dies on the way to perform an obligatory Umrah after genuinely preparing and intending it, what do scholars say about their reward?
optionsEn: Only their travel agent receives reward
Allah records their full reward by virtue of their sincere intention and setting out
Their effort is wasted completely
They are punished for failing to reach Jeddah
explanationEn: Based on Qur'an 4:100 ('Whoever leaves his home migrating to Allah and His Messenger and death overtakes him, his reward is incumbent upon Allah'), a sincere pilgrim passing away en route receives full divine reward.

questionEn: Does a woman need a Mahram to perform obligatory Umrah according to the Shafi'i and Maliki schools compared to the Hanafi and Hanbali schools?
optionsEn: Hanafi and Hanbali schools require a Mahram (or husband) for travel, while Shafi'is and Malikis allow a trustworthy group of women for obligatory pilgrimage
No school has ever discussed women's travel safety
All four schools forbid women from ever performing Umrah
All four schools require three brothers to accompany every woman
explanationEn: Classical jurists differ on safety conditions: Hanafis and Hanbalis stipulate a Mahram based on travel hadiths, whereas Malikis and Shafi'is permit safe, trustworthy female companionship for obligatory pilgrimage.

questionEn: Which companion led an expedition or reminded people that 'whoever goes out for Hajj or Umrah and dies, Allah writes for him the reward until the Day of Resurrection'?
optionsEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrated a report to this effect in Musnad Abu Ya'la and al-Bayhaqi
Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf
Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah
Abu Lahab
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrated the virtue of someone who sets out solely for Hajj, Umrah, or Jihad and passes away along the way, receiving ongoing reward.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Umrah with a group or tour guide versus performing it individually?
optionsEn: Both are completely valid; having a knowledgeable guide helps avoid mistakes, while worship remains personal
Umrah is invalid unless performed with at least 40 people
Only solo Umrah counts for reward
Umrah is invalid if a pilgrim uses a guide
explanationEn: Umrah is an individual act of devotion—one may perform it alone or in a group, and learning the Sunnah beforehand ensures one does not rely blindly on unverified practices.

questionEn: Why should pilgrims avoid reciting loud, synchronized group chants invented by tour leaders during Tawaf and Sa'i?
optionsEn: Because it was not the Prophetic way, creates noise, and distracts other worshippers from humble personal dua
Because speaking Arabic in Tawaf breaks Wudu
Because silence is mandatory throughout Umrah
Because only children are allowed to speak in the Haram
explanationEn: Scholars advise each pilgrim to supplicate quietly with humility in their own words or Prophetic duas, avoiding loud rhythmic group shouting that disturbs fellow worshippers.

questionEn: What is the primary goal of learning the Fiqh of Umrah before boarding a flight to Saudi Arabia?
optionsEn: To finish Tawaf in under five minutes
To worship Allah upon sure knowledge, avoid violating Miqat or Ihram rules, and fulfill every pillar properly
To avoid paying for airport meals
To debate other pilgrims during Tawaf
explanationEn: Seeking knowledge before acting is a duty; knowing Miqat boundaries, Ihram prohibitions, Tawaf conditions, and Sa'i rules protects one's Umrah from errors.

questionEn: If a Muslim owes an urgent, due debt whose repayment date has arrived, what should they do before spending money on a voluntary Umrah?
optionsEn: Ignore the creditor until returning from Makkah
Repay the due debt first or obtain the creditor's explicit consent to delay repayment
Give the money to a hotel instead of the creditor
Perform Umrah secretly under another name
explanationEn: Fulfilling financial obligations to people is mandatory and takes priority over voluntary travel; if a debt is deferred with the creditor's agreement, travel is permissible.

questionEn: What does the phrase 'Labbaika Allahumma bi-'Umrah' represent at the start of Umrah?
optionsEn: Verbal expression of the Niyyah (intention) to enter the ritual of Umrah
The concluding prayer after leaving Safa and Marwah
The greeting spoken when entering Madinah
A supplication before eating dates
explanationEn: When entering Ihram for Umrah, pilgrims intend Umrah in their heart and utter 'Labbayk Allahumma bi-'Umrah' (or 'Allahumma labbayk 'Umrah'), initiating the sacred state.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim announce aloud to everyone around them, 'I intend to perform Umrah for Allah...' with a long scripted formula?
optionsEn: Only if recited in five different languages
Yes, it must be written on paper and placed inside the Izar
No; intention resides in the heart, and the Sunnah verbal utterance is simply 'Labbayk Allahumma 'Umrah' (or 'Allahumma labbayk bi-'Umrah')
Yes, a ten-line declaration must be read aloud in front of witnesses
explanationEn: In Islam, Niyyah is in the heart; for pilgrimage specifically, the Prophet ﷺ taught uttering the Talbiyah naming the rite ('Labbayk 'Umrah').

questionEn: Which surah reminds believers of the story of the People of the Elephant who tried to destroy the Kaaba, highlighting Allah's protection of His House?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Qadr (Chapter 97)
Surah Al-Tin (Chapter 95)
Surah Al-Nasr (Chapter 110)
Surah Al-Fil (Chapter 105)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Fil recounts how Allah protected the Sacred House from Abrahah's army in the year of the Prophet's ﷺ birth, preserving the sanctuary of Makkah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj (22:26), what did Allah instruct Ibrahim (AS) to do regarding the Sacred House?
optionsEn: Close the House to all visitors outside Quraysh
Move the Black Stone to Jerusalem
Do not associate anything with Allah and purify the House for those who perform Tawaf, stand in prayer, bow, and prostrate
Build a wall around Safa and Marwah to block walking
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hajj (22:26) affirms strict monotheism and keeping the Sacred House pure physically and spiritually for pilgrims who perform Tawaf and Salah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in Sahih al-Bukhari when asked whether a person who already performed Hajj can also perform a separate Umrah?
optionsEn: No, Umrah is forbidden after Hajj
Only once twenty years after Hajj
Only if performed without Tawaf
Yes; Umrah can be performed independently as well as alongside Hajj
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ performed three independent Umrahs before his Farewell Hajj and approved Aisha's (RA) independent Umrah afterward.

questionEn: If a resident of Madinah travels to Makkah solely for business or visiting relatives without intending Umrah or Hajj, are they required to enter Ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah according to the majority?
optionsEn: According to the majority (Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali), Ihram at Miqat is required only when intending Hajj or Umrah; Hanafis require Ihram when entering Makkah unless exiting and returning as a local
All four schools forbid entering Makkah for business ever
Business travelers must perform three Tawafs before speaking
Every visitor to Jeddah must shave their head
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah on the Day of Conquest wearing a helmet (without Ihram), which the majority cite to show Ihram at Miqat applies to those intending Hajj or Umrah.

questionEn: How does the Prophet's ﷺ entry into Makkah at the Conquest (8 AH) without Ihram inform fiqh on Miqat?
optionsEn: It showed that helmets replace Ihram garments for men
It meant Umrah is only for residents of Madinah
It abolished the Miqat stations permanently
It proves that crossing the Miqat without intending Umrah or Hajj is permissible according to the majority of jurists
explanationEn: Anas (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah on the Conquest wearing a helmet on his head without Ihram, supporting the view that Miqat Ihram binds those intending pilgrimage.

questionEn: What is the difference between 'entering Ihram' and 'wearing the Ihram garments'?
optionsEn: Putting on the white towels at home automatically forbids perfume even before Niyyah
There is no difference; putting on sandals begins Umrah
Entering Ihram happens only at Maqam Ibrahim
Wearing the two sheets is merely preparation; entering Ihram occurs only when making the Niyyah (intention) to begin Umrah
explanationEn: A pilgrim may wear the Izar and Rida' hours early at the airport or hotel, but the sacred state of Ihram—and its prohibitions—begin only upon forming the Niyyah at or before the Miqat.

questionEn: What is the virtue of performing Umrah during the last ten nights of Ramadan in particular?
optionsEn: It allows wearing tailored clothes inside Ihram
It eliminates the need for Halq or Taqsir
It combines the Hajj-equivalent reward of Ramadan Umrah with seeking Laylat al-Qadr in Al-Masjid al-Haram
It reduces the number of Sa'i laps from seven to three
explanationEn: While every day of Ramadan carries the reward of Hajj for Umrah, combining it with the blessed final nights in Makkah multiplies worship and Qiyam al-Layl.

questionEn: If a fasting pilgrim in Ramadan reaches Makkah exhausted at midday for Umrah, what travel concession applies?
optionsEn: As a traveler meeting the valid travel distance, they are permitted to break their fast if needed and make it up after Ramadan
They must pay a sheep as fidyah for breaking a travel fast
Travelers are forbidden from fasting even if they feel strong
Breaking the fast invalidates Umrah
explanationEn: Allah grants travelers the concession to break the Ramadan fast and make up the missed day later (Qur'an 2:184–185), enabling them to perform Tawaf and Sa'i safely without fainting.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do with non-Muslim coworkers or neighbors if asked about the purpose of Umrah?
optionsEn: Say it is solely a commercial trade fair
Claim it replaces daily prayer for life
Refuse to speak to anyone before departure
Explain clearly and graciously that Umrah is a sacred pilgrimage to Makkah celebrating monotheism, humility, and renewal
explanationEn: Presenting Umrah as a peaceful spiritual pilgrimage rooted in the Abrahamic tradition of pure devotion to One God reflects wisdom and good character.

questionEn: Which Prophet's wife, Hajar (AS), is remembered most vividly during the Umrah ritual of Sa'i?
optionsEn: The mother of Isma'il (AS), whose trust in Allah and urgent search for water between Safa and Marwah are commemorated
Asiyah, wife of Pharaoh
Maryam, mother of Isa (AS)
Bilqis, Queen of Sheba
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari how Hajar (AS) ran seven times between Safa and Marwah looking for water for baby Isma'il before Zamzam gushed forth.

questionEn: In Ibn Abbas's (RA) narration in Sahih al-Bukhari, why did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) leave Hajar and Isma'il (AS) in the barren valley of Makkah?
optionsEn: Because Makkah was already a lush orchard
Because they lost their caravan map
To search for silver mines
By direct command of Allah, trusting that Allah would never abandon them
explanationEn: When Hajar (AS) asked 'Did Allah command you to do this?' and Ibrahim (AS) said 'Yes', she replied with certainty: 'Then He will not let us perish!'

questionEn: What did Ibrahim (AS) pray in Surah Ibrahim (14:37) when settling his family in the barren valley near Allah's Sacred House?
optionsEn: 'Exempt this city from prayer'
'Keep all travelers away from this valley'
'Turn the mountains into silver'
'Our Lord, incline hearts among the people toward them and provide them with fruits so that they may be grateful'
explanationEn: Allah answered Ibrahim's (AS) heartfelt supplication (14:37): believers' hearts have yearned for Makkah across every century, and abundant provision flows to it.

questionEn: Which of the following acts is a Sunnah during Umrah rather than a pillar or Wajib?
optionsEn: Shaving or trimming hair at the end
Performing Raml in the first three circuits of Tawaf and Idtiba' for men
Completing seven circuits of Tawaf
Entering Ihram with Niyyah
explanationEn: Raml and Idtiba' are emphasized Sunnahs of Umrah Tawaf for men; omitting them due to crowding or forgetfulness does not invalidate Umrah nor incur any fidyah.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim omits a Sunnah act of Umrah (such as touching Rukn al-Yamani or praying two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim)?
optionsEn: They must fast thirty days upon returning home
They must sacrifice two camels in Makkah
Their Umrah remains completely valid and no sacrificial penalty (Dam) is owed, though they miss the extra Sunnah reward
Their entire Umrah is annulled and must be repeated from Miqat
explanationEn: Missing a Sunnah act never invalidates Umrah nor obligates a Dam; only omitting a pillar invalidates a ritual until completed, while omitting a Wajib incurs a Dam.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Umrah on behalf of a living person who is physically healthy and able to travel?
optionsEn: Not valid for obligatory Umrah (and disallowed for voluntary Umrah by the majority, with narrow Hanbali/Hanafi differences for nafl)
Valid only if done via video call
Mandatory for every employed worker
Encouraged so healthy people never have to travel
explanationEn: A healthy, able Muslim must perform their own obligatory pilgrimage personally; proxy (Badal) is sanctioned for the deceased or permanently incapacitated.

questionEn: During which Umrah of the Prophet ﷺ did Quraysh vacate Makkah for three days so the Muslims could perform their rites peacefully?
optionsEn: The Farewell Hajj (10 AH)
The Battle of Badr (2 AH)
Umrat al-Qada' (7 AH), fulfilled under the terms of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
Umrat al-Ji'ranah (8 AH)
explanationEn: In Dhul-Qa'dah 7 AH, under the Hudaybiyyah accord, Quraysh withdrew to the hills while the Prophet ﷺ and ~2,000 Companions performed Umrat al-Qada' for three days.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ instruct his Companions to perform Raml (brisk jogging/walking) during Umrat al-Qada'?
optionsEn: To demonstrate the Muslims' vitality and strength to the Quraysh watching from Qu'ayqi'an hill
Because they were forbidden from walking slowly
Because rain flooded the Mataf
To finish before noon heat
explanationEn: Quraysh spread rumors that Madinah's fever had weakened the Muslims; the Prophet ﷺ ordered Raml in the first three circuits (between the Black Stone and Rukn al-Yamani, walking behind the Kaaba) to display strength.

questionEn: What historical event prevented the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions from completing their intended Umrah in 6 AH?
optionsEn: They forgot their Ihram garments in Madinah
Quraysh blocked their entry into Makkah at al-Hudaybiyyah
They reached Makkah after Dhul-Hijjah ended
A flood destroyed the road from Madinah
explanationEn: In 6 AH, Quraysh halted the unarmed Muslim pilgrims at al-Hudaybiyyah; this led to Bay'at al-Ridwan and the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, which Allah called a 'clear victory' (Fath Mubin).

questionEn: Whose wise advice did the Prophet ﷺ follow at al-Hudaybiyyah when the Companions were initially heartbroken to exit Ihram without reaching the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb
Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah
Umm Salamah (RA), who advised him to go out silently, sacrifice his camel, and shave his head first
Suhayl ibn Amr
explanationEn: When the Companions hesitated out of grief, Umm Salamah (RA) advised the Prophet ﷺ to offer his sacrifice and shave his head without speaking; immediately seeing him do so, the Companions rushed to follow.

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ enter Ihram for his third Umrah (Umrat al-Ji'ranah) in 8 AH after the Battle of Hunayn and siege of Ta'if?
optionsEn: Al-Ji'ranah, outside the Haram boundaries northeast of Makkah
Dhul-Hulayfah near Madinah
Yalamlam south of Makkah
Jeddah port
explanationEn: While distributing the spoils of Hunayn at al-Ji'ranah, the Prophet ﷺ assumed Ihram there at night, entered Makkah for Umrah, and returned to al-Ji'ranah before dawn.

questionEn: Which surah was revealed on the Prophet's ﷺ return journey from al-Hudaybiyyah, praising the treaty and promising an imminent opening of Makkah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Anfal (Chapter 8)
Surah Al-Ma'idah (Chapter 5)
Surah Al-Munafiqun (Chapter 63)
Surah Al-Fath (Chapter 48)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Fath ('Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest') was revealed after Hudaybiyyah, affirming Allah's pleasure with the believers under the tree and foretelling peaceful entry into Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fath (48:27), what vision of the Prophet ﷺ did Allah promise to fulfill truthfully?
optionsEn: Building a fortress on Mount Arafah
Entering Al-Masjid al-Haram in safety, with heads shaved and hair shortened, without fear
Ending pilgrimage after 7 AH
Abandoning the Black Stone forever
explanationEn: Allah fulfilled the Prophet's ﷺ true dream one year later in Umrat al-Qada', when the Muslims entered Makkah securely and completed Umrah with Halq and Taqsir.

questionEn: What is the difference between 'Umrah al-Mufradah' (independent Umrah) and 'Umrah al-Tamattu''?
optionsEn: Umrah al-Mufradah has 14 laps of Tawaf
Umrah al-Mufradah does not require Ihram
Umrah al-Mufradah is performed on its own outside a Hajj package, whereas Umrah al-Tamattu' is performed during Hajj months followed by Hajj in the same season
Umrah al-Tamattu' skips Sa'i
explanationEn: The core rituals (Ihram, Tawaf, Sa'i, Halq/Taqsir) are identical, except Umrah al-Tamattu' is linked to performing Hajj in that same season and carries a Hady obligation.

questionEn: Which greeting is uniquely fitting when departing from Makkah or saying goodbye to fellow Muslims going for Umrah?
optionsEn: Throwing salt behind the traveler
'Astawdi'ullaha dinaka wa amanataka wa khawatima 'amalik' (I entrust to Allah your religion, your trust, and the final deeds of your life)
Reciting Surah al-Masad three times
Staying silent for 24 hours
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ would bid farewell to travelers with this beautiful dua entrusting their faith, trusts, and final deeds to Allah.

questionEn: Does a pilgrim need to seek an 'Umrah certificate' from an authority for their worship to be valid before Allah?
optionsEn: Only if signed inside Hijr Ismail
Yes, without a framed paper certificate the Tawaf is void
Official permits replace the Miqat requirement
No; validity before Allah depends on sincerity and fulfilling the Shari'ah rites, though official travel/Nusuk permits are required for orderly organization and safety
explanationEn: Ritual validity depends solely on Islamic criteria, while complying with official entry/Nusuk permits supports crowd safety and lawful obedience to organizing authorities.

questionEn: What spiritual lesson does the simplicity of Umrah's white Ihram garments teach every pilgrim?
optionsEn: That cultural heritage should be discarded forever
That colorful fabrics are sinful year-round
Equality of all believers before Allah regardless of wealth, race, or status, and remembrance of the funeral shroud
Superiority of wealthy travelers over laborers
explanationEn: Standing shoulder-to-shoulder in simple unsewn sheets strips away worldly rank and evokes both equality in servitude and readiness to meet Allah.
reference: Ihya' Ulum al-Din (Asrar al-Hajj); Adab al-Haramayn

questionEn: Why does Islamic law forbid bargaining or conducting commercial sales inside the prayer area of Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Because trade is forbidden anywhere in Saudi Arabia
Because mosques are built strictly for worship and remembrance of Allah, not commercial trade
Because pilgrims are not allowed to buy food in Makkah
Because coins melt in Makkah's heat
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade buying and selling inside mosques; shops outside the mosque boundary serve pilgrims' needs while keeping the Sanctuary dedicated to worship.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about finding lost property (Luqatah) inside the Sacred Sanctuary of Makkah?
optionsEn: Only residents of Ta'if may keep lost items
Anyone who finds money in the Mataf may keep it immediately
Lost items must be buried under Safa
It is not permissible to pick up a lost item in Makkah except to publicly announce and return it to its owner
explanationEn: In his Conquest of Makkah sermon, the Prophet ﷺ declared Makkah's sanctity, stating its lost items (luqatah) may not be picked up except by one who announces them to restore them to their owner.

questionEn: Which two acts in Umrah mirror one another as seven-fold movements of devotion?
optionsEn: Halq and Taqsir
Two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim and two rak'ahs at Miqat
Drinking Zamzam and reciting Talbiyah
Tawaf (seven circuits around the Kaaba) and Sa'i (seven laps between Safa and Marwah)
explanationEn: Both major movement rites of Umrah—circumambulating the House (Tawaf) and traversing between Safa and Marwah (Sa'i)—consist of seven complete circuits/laps.

questionEn: What is the role of 'Tadabbur' (reflection) during Umrah compared to rushing through rituals mechanically?
optionsEn: Thinking about meanings replaces the need for Wudu
Reflection invalidates Raml
Pondering the meaning of Talbiyah, Tawaf, and dua elevates Umrah from empty motion into transformative worship
Pilgrims should rush to complete all rituals in twenty minutes
explanationEn: Allah reminds pilgrims that outward rites express inner Taqwa (22:32, 22:37); reflective presence of heart (khushu') brings the full spiritual fruit of Umrah.

questionEn: Can a Muslim perform Umrah while having a physical disability that requires a wheelchair or motorized cart?
optionsEn: No, only walking on foot is accepted
They must skip Sa'i completely
They must pay a sheep for using a wheelchair
Yes, performing Tawaf and Sa'i while carried or using a wheelchair/cart is completely valid
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ himself performed Tawaf riding his camel when crowded or ill, establishing clear precedent that riding or using a wheelchair/scooter for Tawaf and Sa'i is fully valid.

questionEn: If an able-bodied person pushes a wheelchair-bound elder through Tawaf and Sa'i while also intending Umrah for themselves, does it count for both?
optionsEn: Only the person in the wheelchair gets credit
They must complete 14 circuits together
No, the helper must stay outside the Haram
Yes, according to the majority of scholars, each person's single Tawaf/Sa'i counts for both the pusher and the one being pushed if both intend it
explanationEn: Most contemporary jurists affirm that a pilgrim pushing an elderly parent's wheelchair while in Ihram performs valid Tawaf and Sa'i for both themselves and the person they assist, earning double reward for service (khidmah).

questionEn: Is it permissible for a Muslim to work or conduct lawful trade alongside a pilgrimage journey (such as bringing lawful goods)?
optionsEn: Only residents of Sham may trade
No, working any trade during the same year invalidates Umrah
Yes; Surah Al-Baqarah (2:198) explicitly states there is no blame in seeking bounty from your Lord during pilgrimage
Only selling dates in Mina is permitted
explanationEn: Some early Muslims hesitated to trade during pilgrimage; Allah revealed 2:198 ('There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord'), permitting lawful commerce outside worship spaces.

questionEn: What is the meaning of 'Tahallul' in Umrah?
optionsEn: Putting on the white sheets at home
Exiting the sacred state of Ihram upon shaving or trimming the hair after completing Tawaf and Sa'i
Reaching Jeddah airport
Reciting the Talbiyah on the airplane
explanationEn: Tahallul means returning from the restricted state of Ihram to normal lawful status, which in Umrah takes place completely through Halq or Taqsir after Sa'i.

questionEn: How does a pilgrim show respect for Al-Masjid al-Haram when taking photographs or using phones during Umrah?
optionsEn: Stop in the middle of the Black Stone line to film long videos
Keep filming continuously during every rak'ah of Salah
Avoid blocking pathways, avoid filming others without consent, and avoid turning sacred devotion into distraction or showing off (riya')
Use flash photography directly in worshippers' faces
explanationEn: Scholars warn against distraction, ostentation (riya'), violating others' privacy, and obstructing Tawaf/Sa'i traffic with excessive filming.

questionEn: If someone sincerely intends Umrah and reaches Makkah, what is the very first ritual act inside Al-Masjid al-Haram upon arrival?
optionsEn: Shaving the head at Bab al-Salam
Praying four rak'ahs before looking at the Kaaba
Walking seven times between Safa and Marwah before Tawaf
Proceeding to perform Tawaf al-Umrah around the Kaaba (rather than praying a separate Tahiyyat al-Masjid)
explanationEn: Just as Aisha (RA) narrated, the first thing the Prophet ﷺ did upon arriving in Makkah was perform Wudu and circumambulate the Kaaba (Tawaf), which itself serves as the greeting of Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ describe the black-stone-to-Kaaba journey as wiping away sins like the day one's mother bore them (for Hajj), and how does Umrah relate to forgiveness?
optionsEn: Umrah also brings immense forgiveness—wiping out sins between consecutive Umrahs and purifying the believer's heart
Umrah grants zero forgiveness unless repeated ten times
Umrah only forgives sins committed inside Madinah
Forgiveness applies only to residents of Makkah
explanationEn: Combined with sincere repentance, 'From one Umrah to the next is an expiation for whatever occurred between them' promises great spiritual cleansing.

questionEn: What is the role of 'Sabr' (patience) during Umrah rituals?
optionsEn: Arguing loudly with security guards
Staying calm amidst crowds, heat, delays, and fatigue without losing one's temper or snapping at fellow pilgrims
Shoving harder so you finish Tawaf faster
Abandoning Wudu when lines are long
explanationEn: High crowd density tests character; maintaining patience, courtesy, and abstaining from jidal (disputing) directly fulfills Qur'an 2:197.

questionEn: Why is Umrah accessible to more Muslims worldwide throughout the year compared to Hajj?
optionsEn: Because Umrah is not restricted to fixed days in Dhul-Hijjah and takes only a few hours to perform once in Makkah
Because Umrah can be performed in any city outside Makkah
Because Umrah has no Tawaf requirement
Because Umrah requires no Miqat or Ihram
explanationEn: Umrah's rites take only a couple of hours and can be performed during almost any month, enabling millions across the globe to experience the Sacred House.

questionEn: What is the meaning of 'Miqat Makani' (spatial Miqat) in the jurisprudence of Umrah?
optionsEn: The barber shop row near Mount Marwah
The designated geographical boundary beyond which an intending pilgrim must not pass toward Makkah without entering Ihram
The lunar month in which Umrah is forbidden
The exact square meter inside Al-Masjid al-Haram where Sa'i ends
explanationEn: Miqat Makani refers to the five fixed geographical stations (and outer boundaries) designated by the Prophet ﷺ where pilgrims intending Umrah or Hajj must enter Ihram before proceeding.

questionEn: Who are the 'Afaqi' pilgrims in classical Umrah terminology?
optionsEn: Guides licensed to push wheelchairs in Safa and Marwah
Pilgrims born inside the walls of the Kaaba
Residents of Mina and Arafah exclusively
Pilgrims arriving from outside the outer Miqat boundaries toward Makkah
explanationEn: An 'Afaqi' (from 'afaq', horizons) is any traveler coming from beyond the five Miqat stations; they must assume Ihram at or before the Miqat on their route.

questionEn: Which Miqat is located closest to Madinah—roughly 9 to 11 km south of Masjid al-Nabawi—and farthest from Makkah (around 420–450 km)?
optionsEn: Al-Juhfah (near Rabigh)
Dhul-Hulayfah (commonly known as Abyar Ali)
Yalamlam (al-Sa'diyyah)
Qarn al-Manazil (al-Sayl al-Kabir)
explanationEn: Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali) sits just outside Madinah and is the farthest Miqat from Makkah; pilgrims traveling from Madinah enter Ihram there.

questionEn: Which Miqat did the Prophet ﷺ appoint for pilgrims arriving from Syria (al-Sham), Egypt, North Africa, and western routes?
optionsEn: Dhul-Hulayfah
Qarn al-Manazil
Al-Juhfah (near modern Rabigh, approximately 183–187 km northwest of Makkah)
Dhat Irq
explanationEn: Al-Juhfah was designated by the Prophet ﷺ for people coming from the direction of Sham, Egypt, and the Maghrib; today pilgrims commonly enter Ihram at nearby Rabigh.

questionEn: Which Miqat serves pilgrims arriving from Najd (such as Riyadh) and eastern Arabian regions via Ta'if's northern road?
optionsEn: Qarn al-Manazil (known today as al-Sayl al-Kabir, roughly 75–90 km from Makkah)
Dhul-Hulayfah
Yalamlam
Al-Tan'im
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ designated Qarn al-Manazil (modern al-Sayl al-Kabir, with Wadi Muharram on its parallel ridge) for pilgrims coming from Najd and eastward.

questionEn: What is the relationship between Wadi Muharram (near al-Hada, Ta'if) and Qarn al-Manazil?
optionsEn: Wadi Muharram lies parallel (muhadhi) to Qarn al-Manazil along the upper mountain route from Ta'if to Makkah
Wadi Muharram is a valley inside Madinah
Wadi Muharram is an airport terminal in Jeddah
Wadi Muharram is another name for Safa and Marwah
explanationEn: Pilgrims descending from Ta'if via the al-Hada mountain road cross Wadi Muharram, which aligns directly with Qarn al-Manazil and serves as a valid Miqat point.

questionEn: Which Miqat was appointed for pilgrims arriving from Yemen and southern coastal or maritime routes (such as South and Southeast Asia by sea)?
optionsEn: Al-Juhfah
Dhat Irq
Yalamlam (al-Sa'diyyah, roughly 92–120 km south/southeast of Makkah)
Dhul-Hulayfah
explanationEn: Yalamlam was appointed for travelers coming from the direction of Yemen and southern routes toward Makkah.

questionEn: Which Miqat serves pilgrims arriving from Iraq, Iran, and northeastern regions?
optionsEn: Yalamlam
Dhat Irq (known as al-Daribah, northeast of Makkah)
Al-Hudaybiyyah
Dhul-Hulayfah
explanationEn: Dhat Irq is the Miqat for Iraq and northeastern routes; Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) fixed its alignment (and Sunan reports also attribute its designation to the Prophet ﷺ).

questionEn: How did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) determine the Miqat of Dhat Irq when people from Kufah and Basrah complained that Qarn al-Manazil was out of their way?
optionsEn: He ordered them to fly directly to Jeddah without Miqat
He exempted Iraqis from Ihram altogether
He told them to look for a point directly opposite (parallel to) Qarn al-Manazil along their route, establishing Dhat Irq
He moved the Kaaba border to Baghdad
explanationEn: Umar (RA) established the principle of Muhadhat (parallel alignment): finding a station on their road equal in distance to Qarn al-Manazil—which became the legal basis for airplane Miqat alignment too.

questionEn: What is the 'Muhadhat' principle established by Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and applied by modern scholars to air travel?
optionsEn: Entering Ihram when one's route runs parallel to (aligned with) the nearest Miqat station without passing beyond it
Asking the hotel receptionist to make intention later
Entering Ihram only after touching the Black Stone
Waiting until baggage is collected at Jeddah airport
explanationEn: Because aircraft fly above the Miqat boundary rather than stopping on the ground, passengers enter Ihram onboard just before or as the plane aligns parallel to their route's Miqat.

questionEn: Is King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah itself a Miqat for international air travelers arriving from abroad for Umrah?
optionsEn: Yes, Jeddah is the sixth Miqat for all airplanes
Only for women pilgrims
No; Jeddah lies inside the Miqat perimeter, so international pilgrims arriving for Umrah must enter Ihram onboard before crossing the Miqat line
Only for flights arriving after midnight
explanationEn: Jeddah is situated inside the outer Miqat ring; therefore, anyone traveling from outside the Miqats with the intention of Umrah must enter Ihram before flying past the Miqat boundary.

questionEn: If a pilgrim flies into Madinah first before heading south to Makkah for Umrah, when should they enter Ihram?
optionsEn: They must enter Ihram at their home airport before flying to Madinah
They do not need Ihram on the flight to Madinah; they enter Ihram later at Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali) when departing Madinah for Makkah
They must fly from Madinah to Jeddah to enter Ihram
They skip Ihram altogether because Madinah is in Saudi Arabia
explanationEn: Since the traveler's immediate destination is Madinah (outside the Makkah Miqat zone), they travel normally to Madinah and then assume Ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah when leaving for Makkah.

questionEn: Why does the Prophet's ﷺ Hadith state 'These Miqats are for the people of those regions and for whoever passes through them from other lands intending Hajj or Umrah'?
optionsEn: To forbid people of Syria from ever visiting Madinah
To require traveling through all five Miqats in one trip
To restrict each Miqat by nationality only
To clarify that a pilgrim follows the Miqat lying on their actual route of travel, even if it is not their homeland's direction
explanationEn: For instance, an Egyptian or Indonesian pilgrim who visits Madinah first takes Ihram from Madinah's Miqat (Dhul-Hulayfah), not Rabigh or Yalamlam, because that is the Miqat they pass through.

questionEn: Where do residents living inside the Miqat boundary—between the Miqat and the Haram (known as Ahl al-Hil, such as residents of Jeddah or Bahrah)—enter Ihram for Umrah?
optionsEn: They must travel back to Dhul-Hulayfah
They must drive to Riyadh
From their own residence/location where they form the intention
They must enter the Kaaba first
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'And whoever is within that (boundary), their starting point is from where they set out—even the people of Makkah from Makkah' (with Umrah requiring stepping out to al-Hil for locals).

questionEn: If a resident of Makkah (living inside the Haram sanctuary boundaries) wishes to perform Umrah, where must they go to enter Ihram?
optionsEn: Only to Mina
All the way to Madinah
Directly from their living room inside Makkah without leaving the Haram
Outside the Haram boundary into al-Hil—most commonly to al-Tan'im (Masjid Aisha) or al-Ji'ranah
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ instruction to Aisha (RA) via her brother Abd al-Rahman to go out to al-Tan'im (outside the Haram boundary), anyone inside Makkah steps out to al-Hil to assume Ihram for Umrah.

questionEn: Why must someone inside Makkah step out into al-Hil for Umrah, whereas for Hajj a Makkah resident enters Ihram inside Makkah?
optionsEn: Because Hajj does not require Ihram
Because Makkah residents have no Miqat at all
Because Umrah combines both al-Hil and al-Haram in its journey (as established in Aisha's RA Umrah from al-Tan'im), whereas Hajj includes Arafah which is already in al-Hil
Because Masjid Aisha is the only mosque with Wudu water
explanationEn: Scholars explain that every pilgrimage combines both the profane zone (al-Hil) and the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram): Hajj achieves this by going out to Arafah (in al-Hil), while Umrah requires entering from al-Hil.

questionEn: What is Masjid al-Tan'im commonly called today by Umrah pilgrims?
optionsEn: Masjid al-Khaif
Masjid al-Ghamamah
Masjid al-Qiblatain
Masjid Aisha (RA)
explanationEn: Located about 7 km northwest of Al-Masjid al-Haram just beyond the Haram boundary, Masjid al-Tan'im is named Masjid Aisha because the Prophet ﷺ sent Aisha (RA) there to enter Ihram for Umrah.

questionEn: Which valley outside Madinah is Masjid Dhul-Hulayfah situated in, which the Prophet ﷺ described as a 'blessed valley'?
optionsEn: Wadi Fatimah
Wadi Muhassar
Wadi Hunayn
Wadi al-Aqiq
explanationEn: Umar (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ heard a voice in Wadi al-Aqiq telling him: 'Pray in this blessed valley and say: Umrah merged into Hajj.'

questionEn: If a pilgrim mistakenly crosses the Miqat while intending Umrah without having entered Ihram, what should they do?
optionsEn: Proceed directly to Tawaf without Ihram
Pay a cash fine at Jeddah baggage claim and skip Tawaf
Wait until the next lunar year
Return to the Miqat (or any equal outer Miqat) to enter Ihram properly; if they enter Ihram inside the boundary without returning, they owe a Dam (sacrificial penalty) according to the majority
explanationEn: Returning to the Miqat before beginning rituals fulfills the Wajib and absolves the pilgrim of Dam; failing to return after crossing intentionally or mistakenly requires a Dam to be distributed to the poor of the Haram.

questionEn: If a traveler flying to Jeddah falls asleep and wakes up inside Jeddah after passing the Miqat without entering Ihram for Umrah, what is the easiest way to avoid owing a Dam?
optionsEn: Enter Ihram at Jeddah hotel and skip Dam automatically
Travel from Jeddah out to the nearest Miqat (such as Rabigh / al-Juhfah or al-Sayl al-Kabir) and enter Ihram there before going to Makkah
Shave their head in Jeddah airport
Go to al-Tan'im instead of the outer Miqat
explanationEn: An Afaqi who bypassed the outer Miqat cannot replace it with al-Tan'im (which is only for those already inside Makkah); returning to an outer Miqat like Rabigh or al-Sayl al-Kabir lifts the Dam obligation.

questionEn: When flying toward Jeddah for Umrah, what is the recommended practical procedure regarding changing into Ihram garments?
optionsEn: Wear stitched underwear underneath the Izar during Tawaf
Change at the baggage carousel in Makkah
Change into the Izar and Rida' before boarding or comfortably onboard before the pilot announces the Miqat, and make the Niyyah right before crossing the Miqat line
Wait until landing in Jeddah to change and make intention
explanationEn: Putting on the Ihram sheets beforehand avoids cramped airplane restrooms, while delaying the Niyyah until ~15–20 minutes before the Miqat prevents accidentally violating Ihram prematurely or passing Miqat un-muhrim.

questionEn: Is it permissible to enter Ihram at home before boarding a long international flight to Jeddah?
optionsEn: Only if the flight lasts under two hours
No, entering Ihram early invalidates Umrah
Yes, and doing so removes the need to perform Tawaf
Yes, entering Ihram before the Miqat is valid, though scholars generally advise delaying the Niyyah until approaching the Miqat so one does not bear Ihram prohibitions unnecessarily for many hours
explanationEn: Assuming Ihram prior to the Miqat is valid by consensus (as 'Imran ibn Husayn and others discussed), yet the Prophet's ﷺ Sunnah is entering Ihram at the Miqat itself for ease and accuracy.

questionEn: If an airplane route approaches Jeddah from the north (e.g., Europe or North America) and flies down the Red Sea, which Miqat does it typically align with?
optionsEn: Al-Juhfah (Rabigh)
Dhat Irq
Yalamlam
Qarn al-Manazil
explanationEn: Flights approaching Jeddah from Europe, North Africa, the Levant, or North America along the Red Sea corridor align with al-Juhfah (Rabigh) north-northwest of Makkah.

questionEn: If a flight arrives in Jeddah from South Asia (such as India, Pakistan, or Bangladesh) or Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Indonesia), which Miqat does it commonly align with?
optionsEn: Yalamlam (or Qarn al-Manazil if flying over central Arabia/Najd)
Dhul-Hulayfah
Al-Juhfah
Masjid Aisha
explanationEn: Southern Asian and Maritime Southeast Asian flights typically align with Yalamlam over the southern route (or Qarn al-Manazil when crossing via Riyadh/central Najd); passengers follow the exact flight-path announcement.

questionEn: What hygienic Sunnah acts should a pilgrim perform right before entering Ihram at or before the Miqat?
optionsEn: Fasting for 24 hours before putting on Ihram
Taking a complete bath (Ghusl), clipping nails, trimming mustache/body hair as needed, and for men applying light perfume to the body only (not the Ihram cloths)
Shaving the beard completely
Applying heavy perfume directly onto the white Rida' and Izar sheets
explanationEn: Before making Niyyah, performing Ghusl, attending to natural hygiene (fitrah), and applying scent to the head/beard (for men) follow the Prophetic Sunnah before prohibitions take effect.

questionEn: What did Aisha (RA) narrate about applying perfume to the Prophet ﷺ before he entered Ihram?
optionsEn: He applied perfume onto his Izar sheet after crossing Miqat
He forbade using any perfume even before entering Ihram
He washed off all scent three times after entering Ihram
She applied the best scent to his body before Ihram, and she could still see the glistening of musk in the parting of his hair while he was in Ihram
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) confirmed that pre-Ihram perfume applied to the body/hair before Niyyah is Sunnah and its lingering trace afterward is harmless, though scent must not be applied directly onto the Ihram garments.

questionEn: What instruction did the Prophet ﷺ give Asma bint Umays (RA) when she gave birth at Dhul-Hulayfah just before pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Wait forty days at Dhul-Hulayfah before making Niyyah
Skip Umrah and Hajj permanently
Return immediately to Madinah without entering Ihram
Perform Ghusl, tie a cloth securely for bleeding, and enter Ihram normally
explanationEn: This narration establishes that menstruating and postnatal women still perform Ghusl and enter Ihram at the Miqat normally; they simply delay Tawaf around the Kaaba until pure.

questionEn: Is there a special two-rak'ah prayer specifically called 'Salat al-Ihram' commanded by the Prophet ﷺ before making Niyyah?
optionsEn: Yes, a mandatory four-rak'ah prayer is a pillar of Umrah
Praying any Salah at the Miqat invalidates Ihram
Only residents of Egypt pray two rak'ahs at Miqat
Scholars differ: many consider two rak'ahs Sunnah (or praying after an obligatory prayer if its time coincides), noting the Prophet ﷺ entered Ihram after Dhuhr prayer at Dhul-Hulayfah
explanationEn: Ibn Taymiyyah and others note there is no standalone 'Salat al-Ihram' command, while praying two rak'ahs (such as Tahiyyat al-Wudu or an obligatory Salah like Dhuhr, as the Prophet ﷺ did) before Niyyah is widely practiced and virtuous.

questionEn: When did the Prophet ﷺ actually enter Ihram (say the Talbiyah) when departing Dhul-Hulayfah?
optionsEn: Inside his home in Madinah before packing
Three days after leaving Madinah
Only after arriving at Wadi Fatimah
After praying at Dhul-Hulayfah and mounting his camel (al-Qaswa') as it stood upright to set off
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) reconciled different reports by explaining the Prophet ﷺ began Talbiyah upon mounting and riding away from Dhul-Hulayfah (and continued at al-Bayda').

questionEn: What is the exact wording of the Prophetic Talbiyah as recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim?
optionsEn: Allahu Akbar kabira wal-hamdulillahi kathira
Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, la sharika lak
SubhanAllahi wal-hamdulillahi wa la ilaha illAllahu wahdahu
HasbunAllahu wa ni'mal-wakil
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) preserved this exact wording: 'Here I am, O Allah, here I am! Here I am, You have no partner, here I am! Truly all praise, favor, and sovereignty belong to You; You have no partner.'

questionEn: Which core Islamic principle does the Talbiyah emphasize twice in its short verses?
optionsEn: Praising seasonal harvests
Seeking superiority over other tribes
Pure Tawhid—'You have no partner' (La sharika lak)—rejecting every form of shirk
Listing personal genealogies
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) described the Prophet's ﷺ Talbiyah as 'Ahalla bit-Tawhid'—raising his voice in pure monotheism, contrasting with pre-Islamic polytheists who added partners to the chant.

questionEn: How did pre-Islamic polytheists corrupt the Talbiyah, and how did the Prophet ﷺ respond when hearing their version?
optionsEn: They added names of rivers in Syria
