They added 'except a partner You own and whatever he owns'; the Prophet ﷺ cut them off at 'la sharika lak', affirming pure monotheism
They replaced it with poetry about horses
They recited it only in silence
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that when polytheists chanted 'except a partner You have...', the Prophet ﷺ cried 'Woe to you! Stop! Stop!' right after 'La sharika lak.'

questionEn: Who visited the Prophet ﷺ and commanded him to instruct his Companions to raise their voices in the Talbiyah?
optionsEn: Salman al-Farisi (RA)
Angel Jibril (AS)
Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
Angel Israfil (AS)
explanationEn: Khallad ibn al-Sa'ib reported from his father that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Jibril came to me and commanded me to order my companions to raise their voices with the Ihlal (Talbiyah).'

questionEn: How should women recite the Talbiyah compared to men?
optionsEn: Women are forbidden from reciting the Talbiyah
Men raise their voices clearly, while women recite softly enough only for themselves or immediate companions to hear
Women must shout louder than men in airports
Men must whisper while women use microphones
explanationEn: Scholars teach that raising the voice in Talbiyah is Sunnah for men, whereas women recite at a modest, low volume to maintain modesty.

questionEn: What did Sahl ibn Sa'd (RA) report that the Prophet ﷺ said joins a Muslim whenever they recite the Talbiyah?
optionsEn: Angels stop recording good deeds
Every stone, tree, and clod of earth to their right and left responds with Talbiyah until the earth's horizons end
Rain falls immediately at noon
Only camels join in the chant
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ gave glad tidings that when a Muslim recites the Talbiyah, rocks, trees, and soil to the right and left join in praising Allah across the earth.

questionEn: What is the best time window to begin reciting the Talbiyah frequently during Umrah?
optionsEn: Only after finishing Halq or Taqsir
Only after returning to one's home country
Immediately upon entering Ihram at the Miqat and continuously along the journey until beginning Tawaf
Only inside the Zamzam distribution hall
explanationEn: Talbiyah is the motto of the pilgrim in Ihram; it begins at Niyyah at the Miqat and continues through travel, entering Makkah, and up to starting Tawaf at the Black Stone.

questionEn: When does a pilgrim in Umrah stop reciting the Talbiyah?
optionsEn: After completing the seventh lap of Sa'i
Three days after leaving Makkah
Upon touching or saluting Al-Hajar al-Aswad to start the first circuit of Tawaf
Before landing at Jeddah airport
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) and Abdullah ibn Amr reports in al-Tirmidhi confirm that the Prophet ﷺ kept reciting Talbiyah in Umrah until he touched the Black Stone to begin Tawaf.

questionEn: Which two garments constitute the Sunnah Ihram attire for men, and what color is most recommended?
optionsEn: A tailored linen suit without sleeves
A green velvet cloak and trousers
A black stitched jubbah and silk turban
Two clean white unsewn sheets: the lower wrap (Izar) and upper wrap (Rida')
explanationEn: White clothing is praised by the Prophet ﷺ ('Wear white clothes, for they are among the best of your garments'), and the two unsewn wraps (Izar and Rida') symbolize purity and humility.

questionEn: Is wearing white mandatory for men's Izar and Rida', or is any clean unsewn wrap valid if white is unavailable?
optionsEn: Only bright yellow is valid
White is Sunnah and strongly preferred, though any clean permissible unsewn fabric suffices in necessity
Wearing white is forbidden in winter
Any color invalidates Tawaf
explanationEn: White is recommended (Mustahabb) for purity and following the Prophet's ﷺ practice, though colored unsewn wraps remain valid if clean and non-ostentatious.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in Sahih al-Bukhari when asked what clothing a male pilgrim in Ihram may NOT wear?
optionsEn: He may not carry a cloth bag
He may not wear sandals with straps
He may not wear a shirt (qamis), turban ('imamah), trousers (sarawil), hooded cloak (burnus), or leather socks (khuffayn) unless he has no sandals, in which case he cuts them below the ankles
He may not wear a belt or eyeglasses
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated this comprehensive list of fitted/tailored garments prohibited for men in Ihram, establishing what jurists call 'al-mukhayyat' (garments tailored to body limbs).

questionEn: What common misunderstanding does the phrase 'no stitched clothing (mukhayyat)' cause among new male pilgrims?
optionsEn: Thinking they must weave their own cotton
Thinking eyeglasses with screws are forbidden
Thinking they cannot wear an Ihram belt, stitched hems on an Izar towel, or stitched sandals—whereas 'mukhayyat' actually means garments tailored to fit limbs (shirts, trousers, underwear, socks)
Thinking stitches on a wound bandage invalidate Umrah
explanationEn: Classical jurists clarify that 'mukhayyat' refers to form-fitting tailored garments sewn to encase body parts—not sewn towel edges, money belts, bandages, or sandal straps.
reference: Majmu' Fatawa Ibn Taymiyyah; Al-Sharh al-Mumti'

questionEn: Can a male pilgrim wear regular underwear beneath his Izar while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Yes, if the underwear is white
No; underwear/briefs are form-fitting tailored garments covering the lower body and are prohibited for men in Ihram
Yes, during Tawaf only
Only if bought inside Makkah
explanationEn: Underwear falls under 'sarawil' (fitted lower garments) explicitly forbidden for men in Ihram; men wear only the wrapped Izar around the waist.

questionEn: If a male pilgrim realizes during Tawaf that he accidentally kept his underwear on under his Izar, what should he do?
optionsEn: Remove the underwear as soon as he remembers; if he wore it out of forgetfulness or ignorance, there is no penalty according to major scholars (and his Tawaf remains valid)
Repeat all seven circuits barefoot in Jeddah
Keep wearing it until Halq
Abandon Umrah and fly home immediately
explanationEn: One who wears a prohibited garment out of forgetfulness or ignorance must remove it immediately upon realizing; the majority/authentic view holds no fidyah is due for genuine forgetfulness (Qur'an 33:5).
reference: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:5; Majmu' Fatawa Ibn Uthaymin

questionEn: Is it permissible for a male pilgrim in Ihram to fasten his Izar with a belt, waist pouch, or safety pins?
optionsEn: Only leather ropes from Mina are allowed
Yes, securing the Izar with a belt or waist pouch (hizyam) is fully permissible and helps preserve modesty
Belts require fasting three days
No, belts count as trousers
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) and classical jurists permitted wearing a belt or money pouch around the waist over the Izar to hold belongings and prevent the wrap from slipping.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Hajj, Bab al-Hizyam); Al-Mughni

questionEn: May a male pilgrim wear a wristwatch, prescription glasses, or a hearing aid while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Glasses are permitted only after Sa'i
Only watches without leather straps are allowed
Yes, wearing watches, glasses, medical devices, and rings is completely permissible in Ihram
No, metal objects break Ihram
explanationEn: Watches, glasses, and medical aids are not body-tailored clothing and carry no restriction in Ihram.

questionEn: Can a male pilgrim use an umbrella or ride inside a roofed bus/car while in Ihram?
optionsEn: No, pilgrims must stay under direct sun at all times
Umbrellas are only allowed for women
Yes; indirect shade from a vehicle roof, tent, or handheld umbrella is completely permissible
Vehicles require removing the roof before entering Makkah
explanationEn: Umm al-Husayn (RA) reported seeing the Prophet ﷺ shaded by a cloth held over him during pilgrimage, showing indirect shade (not touching the head like a cap or turban) is allowed.

questionEn: What is the rule about men covering their heads with a cap, beanie, turban, or pulling the Rida' over the head while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Only red turbans are forbidden
Pulling the Rida' over the head is Sunnah while sleeping
Men must keep the head uncovered—avoiding caps, turbans, hoods, or draping the Rida' directly over the head
Men must wear a white kufi at all times
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explicitly forbade turbans and hooded cloaks for men in Ihram and ordered the deceased muhrim's head left uncovered, establishing that direct head coverings are prohibited for men.

questionEn: If a male pilgrim in Ihram accidentally covers his head with a blanket while sleeping or forgets and puts on a cap, what should he do?
optionsEn: Uncover his head as soon as he wakes or remembers; unintentional covering out of sleep or forgetfulness incurs no penalty
Fast ten days in Madinah
Shave his head immediately at the hotel
Restart Umrah from his home country
explanationEn: A person who forgets or acts unintentionally while asleep is excused in Islamic law (Qur'an 2:286) and simply removes the covering once aware.

questionEn: What footwear is permitted for men in Ihram?
optionsEn: Ankle-high leather hiking boots
Closed running sneakers with thick socks
Sandals or slippers that expose the ankles and upper foot joints (below the ankle bones)
Only wooden clogs
explanationEn: Male pilgrims wear open sandals exposing the ankles; if sandals are unavailable, the Prophet ﷺ allowed wearing leather socks/shoes cut below the ankles (with later Arafah reports even permitting uncut khuff when no sandals exist).

questionEn: Can men wear socks while in Ihram if their feet get cold or blistered?
optionsEn: Yes, wool socks are Sunnah for men in Ihram

Regular stitched socks covering the ankles and heels are prohibited for men in Ihram; if medical necessity forces wearing them, fidyah applies (unless cut below the ankle per classical concessions when no sandals exist)
Socks are required inside Masjid al-Haram
Only black socks are permitted
explanationEn: The Hadith of Ibn Umar (RA) explicitly bars khuffayn (ankle-covering footwear/socks) when sandals are available; medical necessity allows them with fidyah.

questionEn: What is the Islamic ruling on women wearing socks and closed shoes while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Strictly forbidden just like for men
Allowed only inside hotel rooms
Women must walk barefoot in Tawaf
Permissible and recommended for women to cover their feet comfortably in Ihram
explanationEn: The prohibition on tailored garments and closed shoes applies specifically to men; women wear their ordinary modest garments, including socks and comfortable shoes.

questionEn: Which two specific garments did the Prophet ﷺ forbid a woman in Ihram from wearing?
optionsEn: An abaya and headscarf
Socks and sandals
A stitched face veil (niqab/burqa) and gloves (quffazayn)
A loose outer cloak (jilbab)
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'A woman in Ihram must not wear a niqab (face veil) nor wear gloves.'

questionEn: If a woman in Ihram ordinarily covers her face in front of non-mahram men, how does she maintain modesty without wearing a tailored niqab?
optionsEn: By putting on a fitted surgical mask permanently
By loosely draping (sadl) her headscarf/khimar over her face when non-mahram men pass nearby, as Aisha (RA) practiced
By staying locked in a room until midnight
By tying a stitched niqab tightly behind her ears
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) reported: 'Riders used to pass by us while we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Ihram; when they came alongside us, each of us would let her jilbab hang down from her head over her face, and when they passed, we uncovered it.'

questionEn: May a woman in Ihram wear colored or patterned modest dresses instead of white?
optionsEn: Only dark green dresses are valid
Women must wear bright white abayas only
No, women must wear two unsewn white sheets like men
Yes, any modest, non-ostentatious clean clothing in any color is completely valid for women in Ihram
explanationEn: There is no special color requirement for women's Ihram attire; she wears her normal modest clothing free of perfume, without niqab or gloves.

questionEn: Does entering Ihram require women to remove simple gold jewelry such as a wedding ring or small earrings?
optionsEn: Jewelry must be left at the Miqat mosque
No, women are permitted to wear modest jewelry in Ihram, though keeping valuables safe in crowds is wise
Yes, all metal jewelry invalidates Ihram
Only silver rings are allowed
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) and classical jurists confirmed that wearing jewelry does not violate Ihram for women, provided it is covered modestly and not displayed ostentatiously.

questionEn: If a pilgrim needs a medical surgical mask in crowded areas while in Ihram, what do contemporary jurists advise for men and women?
optionsEn: Men may wear a medical mask if needed for health/respiratory protection (avoiding covering the whole head), while for women many scholars allow it for genuine medical necessity (some advising fidyah if worn as a face-cover without medical need, though health necessity is widely accommodated)
Medical masks are punishable by canceling Umrah
Only blue masks are forbidden
Masks may only be worn during Halq
explanationEn: For men, covering the nose/mouth is not the same as covering the head; for women, wearing a medical mask strictly for respiratory/health necessity is accommodated by modern scholars without invalidating Umrah.

questionEn: What is the ruling on applying scented lotion, cologne, or scented soap AFTER making the Niyyah of Ihram?
optionsEn: Permitted for women only
Permitted if applied only to the feet
Allowed inside hotel rooms
Prohibited for both men and women until completing Halq or Taqsir
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ strictly forbade wearing garments touched by saffron or wars (dyed perfumes) or applying fragrance during Ihram; unscented soaps and lotions should be used instead.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if they use hotel soap or sanitizer unaware that it is scented, and notice the fragrance after entering Ihram?
optionsEn: Fast seven consecutive days
Wash off the scented residue immediately with plain water; if done unintentionally or out of ignorance, there is no sin or penalty
Repeat Umrah from Jeddah
Leave Makkah immediately
explanationEn: Hadith of Ya'la ibn Umayyah (RA) shows the Prophet ﷺ instructed the man who entered Ihram wearing a perfumed cloak to wash the perfume off three times and remove the cloak, without imposing a penalty on the ignorant questioner.

questionEn: Are unscented soaps, unscented deodorants, and fragrance-free moisturizers permissible during Ihram?
optionsEn: No, even plain water with soap bubbles is forbidden
Yes, hygiene products genuinely free of added fragrance are permissible to stay clean and avoid harming others with body odor
Only sand may be used for washing
Deodorant is forbidden even if completely unscented
explanationEn: Prohibition applies to perfume (tib) and scented substances; unscented cleansers and unscented medical creams are permissible.

questionEn: What is the ruling on brushing teeth with toothpaste or using a Miswak while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Brushing teeth is strictly forbidden in Ihram
Using a Miswak is Sunnah and completely permissible; mint-flavored toothpaste is also allowed by many scholars as mouth hygiene is not perfume (though plain/unscented paste avoids any doubt)
Miswak is forbidden between Miqat and Sa'i
Using toothpaste breaks Umrah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ used the Miswak regularly including while traveling; refreshing breath with a Miswak or normal toothpaste does not constitute wearing perfume.

questionEn: Is bathing (taking a shower) or washing one's Ihram sheets permissible while in the state of Ihram?
optionsEn: No, a pilgrim may not bathe until shaving their head
Only washing the hands is allowed
Yes, both bathing gently with unscented water/soap and changing into clean Ihram wraps are completely permissible
Changing dirty Ihram wraps breaks Ihram
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) and Umar (RA) bathed while in Ihram, and the Prophet ﷺ himself washed his head gently in Ihram using his hands without scratching harshly.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ demonstrate washing his head while in Ihram without causing hair to fall out unnecessarily?
optionsEn: He used dry sand instead of water
He forbade water from touching his hair
He shaved his head at the well first
He poured water over his head and gently moved his fingers forward and backward without rubbing vigorously
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Hunayn narrated that Ibn Abbas and al-Miswar confirmed the Prophet ﷺ washed his head while in Ihram by pouring water and gently passing his hands over it.

questionEn: What if a few loose hairs fall naturally while bathing, combing gently, or performing Wudu in Ihram?
optionsEn: It invalidates Tawaf completely
The pilgrim must return to the Miqat
Natural shedding without intentional plucking or pulling incurs no sin and no penalty
Each single fallen hair requires sacrificing a sheep
explanationEn: Only intentional shaving, cutting, or plucking hair is prohibited in Ihram; hairs that fall out naturally during washing or Wudu incur nothing.

questionEn: What is the ruling on intentionally clipping fingernails or toenails while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Prohibited until exiting Ihram via Halq or Taqsir (unless a broken nail is causing painful injury, in which case only the broken piece causing harm may be trimmed)
Encouraged every morning during Tawaf
Permissible before Sa'i
Allowed for toenails only
explanationEn: Cutting hair and nails is among the prohibitions of Ihram; however, if a nail splits painfully, trimming only the detached hanging fragment to prevent injury is permitted without penalty.

questionEn: What is the rule regarding hunting land animals while in the state of Ihram?
optionsEn: Allowed outside Al-Masjid al-Haram
Only birds are protected
Strictly forbidden to hunt, kill, or even point out land game to a hunter (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:95–96)
Allowed if using a bow instead of a rifle
explanationEn: Qur'an 5:95 forbids killing land game while in Ihram, and the Hadith of Abu Qatadah (RA) confirms a muhrim may neither hunt nor assist/point out game to a non-muhrim.

questionEn: What did Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:96) declare completely permissible for pilgrims in Ihram regarding food?
optionsEn: Catching pigeons inside Al-Masjid al-Haram
Eating meat hunted specifically for the muhrim
Hunting desert gazelles for dinner
Game of the sea (fish and seafood) and its food are lawful for pilgrims in Ihram
explanationEn: Allah says: 'Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and the travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in Ihram.'

questionEn: If a non-muhrim hunts a land animal on their own (without being asked or pointed to it by a muhrim), may a pilgrim in Ihram eat from it?
optionsEn: No, pilgrims in Ihram must remain strictly vegetarian
Yes; as proven in the Hadith of Abu Qatadah (RA), a muhrim may eat game hunted by a non-muhrim provided the muhrim did not hunt it, ask for it, or point it out
Only if eaten standing up
Only if cooked in Madinah
explanationEn: When Abu Qatadah (RA), who was not in Ihram, hunted a wild donkey without the muhrim Companions aiding or pointing, the Prophet ﷺ asked: 'Did any of you command him or point to it?' When they said no, he ﷺ said: 'Then eat what remains of its meat.'

questionEn: Which five harmful creatures did the Prophet ﷺ permit pilgrims to kill even inside the Haram and while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Pigeons, sparrows, camels, sheep, and horses
The crow, the kite (bird of prey), the scorpion, the mouse/rat, and the rabid/biting dog (plus venomous snakes)
All wild birds inside Makkah
Cats, goats, gazelles, rabbits, and falcons
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ termed these five 'fawasiq' (harmful pests) that may be killed in both al-Hil and al-Haram to protect human safety.

questionEn: What is the ruling on entering into a marriage contract (Nikah) or proposing marriage while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Prohibited; a muhrim may neither marry, give someone else in marriage, nor propose until exiting Ihram
Permitted for men only
Recommended right after Tawaf
Valid if conducted inside Jeddah airport
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'A person in Ihram must neither marry, nor give in marriage, nor propose.' (The majority hold such a contract invalid until Tahallul.)

questionEn: What is the ruling on marital sexual relations (intercourse or lustful foreplay) while in Ihram for Umrah?
optionsEn: Strictly prohibited until exiting Ihram via Halq/Taqsir; sexual intercourse before Tahallul invalidates the Umrah and requires a sacrificial penalty plus completing and making up the Umrah
Permitted before Sa'i
Permitted inside hotel rooms after Tawaf
Requires only washing hands
explanationEn: Qur'an 2:197 forbids 'rafath' (sexual intimacy) during pilgrimage; intercourse before exiting Ihram is the gravest violation, spoiling the Umrah (though the pilgrim still finishes it, sacrifices a sheep/camel per scholarly detail, and repeats it).

questionEn: Are a husband and wife in Ihram permitted to hold hands gently to avoid getting separated in heavy Haram crowds?
optionsEn: No, spouses cannot speak or walk side by side
Yes, holding hands for safety or guidance without lustful desire is completely permissible
Holding hands requires sacrificing a goat
They must walk on opposite floors of the Haram
explanationEn: Only sexual intimacy and lustful touching (shahwah) are forbidden; holding an elderly or frail spouse's hand to prevent getting lost in crowds is normal kindness and safety.

questionEn: What is the ruling on cutting wild trees or uprooting natural vegetation growing within the boundaries of the Makkah Haram?
optionsEn: Permitted for residents of Makkah
Prohibited for everyone—both those in Ihram and non-muhrims—except idhkhir (lemon grass) which the Prophet ﷺ exempted for practical needs
Only prohibited during Ramadan
Permitted if the pilgrim needs firewood
explanationEn: During the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ declared its thorn-trees and fresh plants inviolable; when al-Abbas (RA) asked about idhkhir grass for smiths and graves, the Prophet ﷺ exempted idhkhir.

questionEn: If a pilgrim in Ihram suffers a severe headache or skin irritation and must shave part of their head for medical treatment, what does Qur'an 2:196 prescribe?
optionsEn: They must endure the pain without treatment
Their Umrah is permanently canceled
They must repeat Ihram from Madinah
They may shave for medical relief and offer Fidyah al-Adha: fasting 3 days, feeding 6 poor persons, or sacrificing a sheep
explanationEn: Ka'b ibn Ujrah (RA) suffered lice on his head during Hudaybiyyah; the Prophet ﷺ told him to shave his head and choose between fasting three days, feeding six poor people (half sa' each), or sacrificing a sheep—as revealed in 2:196.

questionEn: In the Fidyah of Ka'b ibn Ujrah (RA) for shaving due to ailment or violating hair/nail/perfume/clothing prohibitions out of necessity, how much food is given to each of the six poor people?
optionsEn: One date per person
Ten kilograms of meat per person
One handful of salt
Half a Sa' (roughly 1.5 kg) of staple food per poor person (totaling three Sa's for six people)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Ka'b ibn Ujrah (RA): 'Fast three days, or feed six poor people—half a Sa' of food for each poor person—or sacrifice a sheep.'

questionEn: Does a pilgrim choosing the 'fast three days' option of Fidyah al-Adha have to fast those three days inside Makkah?
optionsEn: Fasting is never an option for Fidyah
Yes, all three days must be fasted inside Hijr Ismail
Yes, only during Shawwal
No, fasting the three days may be done anywhere, whereas feeding the poor or sacrificing is generally distributed to the poor of the Haram (or place of violation)
explanationEn: Fasting is an act of personal devotion unrestricted by place, whereas sacrificial meat and feeding the poor benefit the needy of the Sacred Sanctuary (unless excused).

questionEn: What is 'Ishtirat' (making a conditional Ihram) and when is it recommended?
optionsEn: Promising to run during all 7 laps of Tawaf
Saying at the time of Niyyah: 'If anything stops me, my place of exiting Ihram is wherever You detain me'—recommended when fearing illness, pregnancy complications, or border/travel obstacles
Making a condition to skip Tawaf if tired
Paying half price for Zamzam
explanationEn: When Duba'ah bint al-Zubayr (RA) felt ill before pilgrimage, the Prophet ﷺ advised her to make this condition ('Mahalli haythu habastani'), allowing exit without sacrificial penalty if genuinely prevented from continuing.

questionEn: What does 'Ihsar' mean in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:196, and what must a pilgrim do if genuinely prevented from reaching the Kaaba without having made Ishtirat?
optionsEn: Being blocked by illness, enemy, or insurmountable obstruction; they offer a sacrificial animal (Hady) where detained (or sent to Haram), shave/trim their hair, and exit Ihram
Staying in Ihram clothes for the rest of their life
Performing Tawaf around their hotel
Paying a fine to the airline
explanationEn: Following 2:196 and the Prophet's ﷺ precedent at Hudaybiyyah, an obstructed pilgrim offers an available sacrifice (or fasts 10 days per some jurists if unable to obtain a sacrifice) and shaves/trims to exit Ihram.

questionEn: Is a pilgrim in Ihram permitted to apply bandages, take prescribed insulin injections, or undergo emergency blood tests?
optionsEn: Yes; medical dressings, injections, blood tests, and life-saving treatments are completely permissible in Ihram
No, needles invalidate Ihram
Only after finishing Sa'i
Bandages are forbidden on the arms
explanationEn: In fact, the Prophet ﷺ himself underwent cupping (hijamah) on his head while in Ihram; necessary medical care is permitted (only shaving hair unnecessarily triggers fidyah, and even that is forgiven in urgent necessity).

questionEn: Can a pilgrim in Ihram wear a surgical cast or sling if they fracture a limb?
optionsEn: They must stay outside Makkah until healed
Yes, wearing medical splints, casts, or slings is completely permissible with no penalty
Yes, but only if made of wool
No, they must remove the cast at Miqat
explanationEn: Medical supports and casts fall under necessity and are not garments worn for normal attire or adornment.

questionEn: What if a male pilgrim cannot find sandals or regular Ihram sheets due to lost airline luggage right as the flight nears Miqat?
optionsEn: He may wear shorts instead of Izar without changing later

If he has no unsewn sheets, he may enter Ihram at Miqat in trousers/shoes (necessity) and switch to Izar/Rida' as soon as acquired—if truly unable to find Ihram before Miqat, scholars hold no sin and fidyah rulings depend on availability (per Ibn Abbas RA's hadith on trousers when no Izar exists)
He must cross the Miqat without making Niyyah and enter Ihram in Makkah
He must cancel Umrah completely
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ said at Arafah: 'Whoever cannot find an Izar may wear trousers, and whoever cannot find sandals may wear leather socks (khuffayn)'—showing Islam's ease in genuine unavailability until regular Ihram is obtained.

questionEn: Why should pilgrims pack their Ihram garments and unscented toiletries inside their carry-on bag rather than checked luggage?
optionsEn: So they can wash them in the plane sink
So they can access them easily before the onboard Miqat announcement even if checked bags are delayed
Because luggage holds make Ihram impure
Because airlines ban white towels in checked bags
explanationEn: Keeping Ihram sheets, belt, and sandals in carry-on luggage prevents arriving at the Miqat line unprepared if checked luggage is delayed or inaccessible mid-flight.

questionEn: What is the ruling on applying henna (dye) to hair or hands while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Only men apply henna during Ihram
Henna invalidates Sa'i
It should be avoided during Ihram (especially scented henna or covering hair), though henna applied before entering Ihram whose color remains is harmless
Applying fresh henna during Tawaf is Sunnah
explanationEn: Scholars advise avoiding beautification dyes and scented substances during Ihram; if applied prior to Niyyah without ongoing fragrance, there is no issue.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim look into a mirror or comb their hair gently while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Both mirrors and glasses are banned in Makkah
Looking in a mirror requires sacrificing a sheep
Looking in a mirror is completely permissible; combing hair is generally avoided to prevent accidentally pulling out hairs (though gently straightening with fingers is fine)
Combing with fine teeth forcefully is Sunnah in Ihram
explanationEn: There is no prohibition against mirrors; regarding combing, jurists recommend avoiding tight combs so hairs are not torn out, whereas running fingers gently while washing is permitted.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim in Ihram uses kohl (eyeliner) without fragrance for medical eye relief versus cosmetic adornment?
optionsEn: Unscented kohl used for medical need is permitted by many scholars, while cosmetic/scented kohl for adornment is avoided during Ihram
Eye drops invalidate Wudu and Ihram
Cosmetic makeup is encouraged in Ihram
All eye drops are forbidden in Ihram
explanationEn: Medical eye drops and unscented kohl for eye ailments are allowed, whereas beautification and scented cosmetics conflict with Ihram's simplicity.

questionEn: What should a woman do if her menstrual period begins right before she reaches the Miqat?
optionsEn: Perform Ghusl, enter Ihram at the Miqat with Niyyah and Talbiyah like everyone else, and wait in Makkah until pure before performing Tawaf
Perform Tawaf anyway during menstruation
Return home immediately without entering Makkah
Skip entering Ihram at the Miqat and enter Makkah normally
explanationEn: When Aisha (RA) began menstruating at Sarif before Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ told her: 'Do what all pilgrims do, except do not perform Tawaf around the House until you become pure.'

questionEn: Which acts of Umrah CAN a menstruating woman perform while waiting to purify for Tawaf?
optionsEn: She can shave her head and finish Umrah without Tawaf

Entering Ihram, reciting Talbiyah, making dua, dhikr, reading/reciting Qur'an (without directly touching the Mushaf per majority, or from memory/screen), and attending Masjid al-Haram courtyard only per scholarly details—waiting for purity before entering the Mosque for Tawaf
She can perform Tawaf immediately on the roof
She cannot make any dua or dhikr at all
explanationEn: She remains in Ihram engaging in abundant dhikr, dua, and Talbiyah, delaying only Tawaf (and entering the mosque prayer hall) until Ghusl after menstruation ends.

questionEn: Can a woman take doctor-approved medication to delay her menstrual cycle safely during a short Umrah trip so she can complete Tawaf before her return flight?
optionsEn: Only if taken after Sa'i
Taking medicine invalidates Ihram
No, all medical tablets are prohibited in Makkah
Yes, jurists permit using safe, medically supervised cycle-delaying pills for pilgrimage if it does not harm her health
explanationEn: Classical and contemporary scholars permit safe temporary delay of menstruation for pilgrimage convenience, provided a qualified physician confirms no harm to the woman's health.
reference: Fatawa al-Lajnah al-Da'imah; Al-Mughni (on safe remedies)

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Ihram and uses a blanket that accidentally touches their head briefly while awake, should they worry about fidyah?
optionsEn: No; removing it immediately when noticed is enough, and brief accidental contact incurs no penalty
Yes, they must repeat Ihram from Miqat
Yes, they owe a camel
They must skip Sa'i
explanationEn: Penalties apply to deliberate wearing/covering of the head, not momentary accidental contact promptly removed.

questionEn: What is the status of wearing a stitched face mask or protective visor for men vs women if required by health regulations during a pandemic?
optionsEn: Valid under necessity (darurah/hajah); men may wear a mask since it does not cover the head, and women wear it for health necessity without invalidating Umrah
Only paper bags may be worn
Pilgrims must hold their breath instead
It renders Umrah completely invalid
explanationEn: Islamic law is built on removing hardship ('Allah intends ease for you'); obeying legitimate public health mask requirements during epidemics is fully accommodated.

questionEn: Why is it important to inspect your Ihram garments before leaving home or Madinah?
optionsEn: To make sure they are dyed dark red
To ensure they are clean, thick enough not to become transparent when wet or sunlit, and properly sized so modesty is preserved during Tawaf and Sa'i
To ensure they have sewn pockets
To check for official gold stamps
explanationEn: Thin or overly short Ihram wraps can slip or expose Awrah during movement or Raml; choosing sturdy, opaque cotton towels and a secure belt preserves dignity and valid Awrah coverage.

questionEn: If a male pilgrim wears a stitched safety-pin or metal clasp to fasten his Izar, does that violate the rule against 'stitched clothing'?
optionsEn: Pins invalidate Wudu
Yes, every metal pin requires a sheep sacrifice
Only plastic clips are banned
No; fasteners, clips, and belts are not tailored garments and are permissible
explanationEn: Using pins or belts to secure the lower sheet does not turn it into a tailored garment like trousers or a shirt.

questionEn: What is the ruling on changing one's Izar or Rida' for a fresh pair if they become dusty or stained during Umrah?
optionsEn: Completely permissible without affecting Ihram or needing a new Niyyah
Requires returning to the Miqat
Requires repeating Talbiyah 100 times
Prohibited until after Halq
explanationEn: Ihram is a legal state entered by intention, not tied to a single piece of cloth; swapping dirty sheets for clean ones is encouraged.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim enters Ihram intending Hajj by mistake when they actually wanted Umrah (or vice versa) and realizes immediately?
optionsEn: They must wait until next year
They must perform both simultaneously without preparation
Their pilgrimage is permanently void
What truly counts is what they intended in their heart; if they misspoke on their tongue, their inner intention prevails, and one may clarify before starting rites
explanationEn: Based on 'Deeds are by intentions' (Bukhari 1), sincere intention in the heart outweighs a slip of the tongue.

questionEn: When entering Makkah by bus or train from Madinah or Jeddah, what should pilgrims do as they approach the Sacred Sanctuary boundaries?
optionsEn: Maintain humility, continue Talbiyah, recite supplications of entering Makkah, and keep focus rather than taking casual selfies
Remove the Rida' completely on the bus
Stop reciting Talbiyah at the city highway sign
Start running inside the bus aisle
explanationEn: Pilgrims maintain Talbiyah all the way through entering Makkah and Masjid al-Haram until standing before the Black Stone to start Tawaf.

questionEn: Which boundary markers around Makkah indicate the limits of the Sacred Haram (al-Haram al-Makki) where plants, hunting, and Makkah-resident Umrah Ihram rules apply?
optionsEn: The traffic lights of Ta'if
The outer fence of Madinah
The walls of Jeddah airport
Historic white boundary pillars (A'lam al-Haram) placed along the approaches such as al-Tan'im, Arafat road, Hudaybiyyah, and Ji'ranah
explanationEn: These boundary markers distinguish the Sacred Sanctuary (Haram) from the outer non-sacred zone (al-Hil); they are NOT the Miqat for outside Afaqi pilgrims, though they mark where Makkah residents step out for Umrah.

questionEn: What common mistake do some pilgrims make regarding the Haram boundary markers at al-Tan'im versus the five Miqats?
optionsEn: Thinking women cannot enter al-Tan'im
Thinking an international pilgrim who forgot Ihram at the Miqat can simply go to Masjid Aisha (al-Tan'im) instead of returning to an outer Miqat
Thinking al-Tan'im is in Madinah
Thinking al-Tan'im is inside the Kaaba
explanationEn: Al-Tan'im is only for people already inside Makkah initiating a new Umrah; an Afaqi who crossed the outer Miqat without Ihram must return to one of the five outer Miqats to avoid Dam.

questionEn: If a pilgrim arrives in Makkah intending only to visit family or attend a conference (without intending Umrah), and later decides while in Makkah to perform Umrah, where do they enter Ihram?
optionsEn: They must fly back to their home country first
They must drive all the way to Dhul-Hulayfah
They enter Ihram inside their hotel room in Makkah
From the nearest point outside the Haram boundary (al-Hil), such as al-Tan'im
explanationEn: Because they formed the Umrah intention only after arriving inside Makkah, they carry the same ruling as Makkah residents for that Umrah and step out to al-Hil (e.g., al-Tan'im).

questionEn: What is the meaning of the phrase 'Innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk' in the Talbiyah?
optionsEn: We are the noblest travelers on earth
Bless only our tribe and homeland
Indeed, all praise, all favor/grace, and all sovereignty belong solely to You, O Allah
Give us wealth and mansions in this world
explanationEn: This clause anchors the pilgrim's heart in gratitude (hamd & ni'mah) and awe of Allah's absolute dominion (mulk) before setting foot in the Sacred House.

questionEn: Did the Prophet ﷺ add anything on occasion to the Talbiyah wording, or did Companions like Ibn Umar (RA) add brief phrases?
optionsEn: Adding praise invalidates Ihram
Yes, they added songs in Persian
No Companion ever recited anything beyond two words
Yes; Ibn Umar (RA) sometimes added 'Labbayk wa sa'dayk, wal-khayru bi-yadayk...' while keeping the Prophetic wording primary
explanationEn: Sahih Muslim records Ibn Umar (RA) adding 'Labbayk wa sa'dayk, wal-khayru bi-yadayk, labbayk war-raghba'u ilayka wal-'amal', while preserving the Prophet's ﷺ foundational wording.

questionEn: What is the ruling on traveling by high-speed train (Haramain Railway) between Madinah and Makkah while wearing Ihram?
optionsEn: Completely valid; passengers enter Ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah before boarding (or right at/before crossing the Dhul-Hulayfah boundary line as announced on the train)
Ihram may only be worn on camels or buses
Passengers must stand the entire journey
Trains are forbidden for pilgrims in Ihram
explanationEn: Transport method does not alter Miqat rules; pilgrims riding the Haramain train from Madinah commonly perform Ghusl and change at their hotel, pray/prepare, and make Niyyah before the train crosses the Miqat zone.

questionEn: If someone is performing Umrah via Ta'if and stops at Masjid Qarn al-Manazil (al-Sayl al-Kabir), what facilities exist there for pilgrims?
optionsEn: Only a camel market
Only an ancient stone wall with no water
Wudu and Ghusl areas, prayer halls, and Ihram preparation facilities right on the Miqat boundary
It is strictly closed to non-residents
explanationEn: All five Miqat stations today have spacious mosques, clean bathing facilities, and prayer areas dedicated to helping arriving pilgrims enter Ihram properly.
reference: Saudi Ministry of Hajj & Umrah Guides

questionEn: Which Miqat is situated near the historic Red Sea town of Rabigh today, replacing the older marshy site of al-Juhfah?
optionsEn: Dhat Irq
Yalamlam
Dhul-Hulayfah
Al-Juhfah / Rabigh Miqat mosque complex
explanationEn: Because old al-Juhfah became sparsely inhabited, travelers from Egypt, Syria, and the West commonly enter Ihram at nearby Rabigh (or the modern al-Juhfah mosque built near its historical site).

questionEn: Does a deaf or speech-impaired pilgrim who cannot utter the Talbiyah aloud still have a valid Ihram?
optionsEn: No, speaking aloud is a pillar without which Umrah fails
They must pay a fidyah
Yes, 100% valid; intention resides in the heart, and they may move their lips or express it silently as able
They must hire someone to recite for them
explanationEn: Islamic law never burdens a soul beyond its capacity (2:286); inner Niyyah suffices for anyone unable to speak.

questionEn: What is the difference between 'Ihlal' and 'Ihram' in Hadith texts?
optionsEn: Ihram means leaving Makkah
Ihlal means shaving the head
Ihram is entering the sacred state by intention, while Ihlal specifically refers to raising the voice with the Talbiyah (though often used interchangeably for initiating pilgrimage)
Ihlal means drinking Zamzam
explanationEn: In Sahih narrations ('ahalla bi-'umrah'), Ihlal denotes raising one's voice in Talbiyah as one enters Ihram, highlighting how vocalizing Talbiyah accompanies the heart's Niyyah.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is unsure whether they crossed the Miqat on a plane because the crew forgot to announce it, what precaution should they take?
optionsEn: Only rely on guesswork after baggage claim
Wait until arriving at the Makkah hotel lobby
Skip Umrah and visit Ta'if
Put on Ihram garments early and make Niyyah about 30–40 minutes before landing in Jeddah (check flight tracker map showing Rabigh/Yalamlam/Qarn al-Manazil)
explanationEn: Monitoring flight tracking screens or setting an alarm ~40 minutes prior to Jeddah arrival ensures a pilgrim enters Ihram safely before crossing the Miqat line even if crew announcements are delayed.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do with their regular stitched clothes after changing into Ihram at Miqat?
optionsEn: Throw them into the trash
Pack them neatly in their travel bag to wear again after completing Halq or Taqsir in Makkah
Leave them abandoned at the Miqat mosque
Give them away permanently as a requirement of Ihram
explanationEn: Regular clothes remain clean personal property and are simply packed away until Tahallul at the end of Umrah.

questionEn: Why is it forbidden to wear a sewn thobe or shirt while in Ihram, even if a pilgrim wears no underwear beneath it?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ explicitly listed the shirt (qamis) among forbidden garments for men in Ihram
Because shirts are too heavy for Makkah's climate
Only colored shirts are forbidden
Shirts are allowed if short-sleeved
explanationEn: All form-fitting tailored upper and lower garments—shirts, t-shirts, jackets, trousers—are excluded by the explicit wording of the Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari 1542.

questionEn: Can a male pilgrim drape a thin unstitched towel or shawl over his shoulders for warmth in an air-conditioned plane or mosque while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Warm blankets require a Dam
Yes, wearing an extra unstitched blanket/shawl over the shoulders (without covering the head or tailoring it into a shirt) is completely permissible
No, only one single Rida' layer is allowed even in freezing cold
Yes, even if pulled completely over the head
explanationEn: An unstitched blanket or additional shawl covering the shoulders/body (excluding the head and face) is permitted to protect from cold.

questionEn: Can a male pilgrim in Ihram cover his feet with a blanket while sleeping in a hotel or plane?
optionsEn: Yes, covering the body and feet with a flat blanket while sleeping is permissible as long as the head stays uncovered and no fitted socks are worn
Only sleeping sitting upright is allowed
Sleeping under any blanket requires fidyah
No, feet must stay uncovered even in winter
explanationEn: Sleeping under a loose sheet or blanket up to the neck (leaving the head exposed) is completely permissible in Ihram.

questionEn: What is the ruling on applying mosquito repellent or unscented sunscreen while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Unscented medical creams, sunscreens, and odorless repellents are permissible; scented varieties should be avoided
All skin lotions invalidate Ihram
Repellent requires shaving early
Sunscreen is allowed only on the back
explanationEn: Protection from sunburn or insects using fragrance-free creams does not constitute perfume (tib) and is completely lawful.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about a man who entered Ihram wearing a garment dyed with saffron/khaluq perfume?
optionsEn: He ordered him to sacrifice ten camels
He expelled him from Makkah
He told him to keep wearing it until Arafah
He ordered him: 'Wash off the perfume three times, take off the jubbah, and do in your Umrah what you do in your Hajj'
explanationEn: Ya'la ibn Umayyah (RA) narrated this famous incident at al-Ji'ranah, showing both the prohibition of perfume/tailored cloaks in Ihram and the Prophet's ﷺ gentle, corrective guidance.

questionEn: How does the Hadith of the man in al-Ji'ranah ('do in your Umrah what you do in your Hajj') demonstrate the similarity between Umrah and Hajj?
optionsEn: It confirms that Ihram prohibitions and the core rites of Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir follow the same standards in Umrah as in Hajj
It proves Umrah requires standing at Arafah
It exempts Umrah pilgrims from Miqat
It proves Hajj has no Tawaf
explanationEn: Scholars rely on this authentic Hadith to affirm that Ihram rules (avoiding perfume, tailored garments, etc.) and Tawaf/Sa'i procedures apply uniformly to Umrah.

questionEn: If a person travels directly from Madinah to Makkah by car at night, where must they enter Ihram?
optionsEn: Wait until Fajr inside Makkah
At Bab al-Salam
At Masjid Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali), which stays open 24 hours a day
At a gas station halfway to Jeddah
explanationEn: Entering Ihram is valid day or night; Dhul-Hulayfah facilities remain accessible around the clock for travelers departing Madinah.

questionEn: Why is it important to check that your sandal straps do not cover the top ankle bones (ka'bayn) or entire upper surface of the foot unnecessarily for men?
optionsEn: Because Prophetic guidance for men in Ihram favors open sandals leaving the ankles and upper foot exposed
Because shoes are banned for women too
Because sandals must be made of green plastic
Because covered toes require fasting 3 days
explanationEn: In classical fiqh, sandals exposing the ankles and major part of the upper foot (avoiding enclosed shoes/khuffayn) ensure compliance with Ibn Umar's (RA) narration.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim has no physical sandals and must wear cut leather shoes or open-heeled clogs in Ihram?
optionsEn: Must walk barefoot on hot asphalt
Invalidates Niyyah
Forbidden under all circumstances

Allowed when sandals are unavailable—and per Ibn Abbas's (RA) Hadith from Arafah, wearing regular shoes when lacking sandals is permitted (though Hanbalis and others differ on whether cutting below the ankle is required)
explanationEn: Two authentic reports exist: Ibn Umar (RA) mentions cutting below the ankles, while Ibn Abbas (RA) narrates the Prophet ﷺ later allowed khuffayn without cutting when sandals were unavailable.

questionEn: When making Niyyah for Umrah at the Miqat, should a pilgrim specify in their heart whether it is for themselves or as Badal Umrah for someone else?
optionsEn: No, one can decide whose Umrah it is after completing Sa'i
Niyyah is made only after Halq
Yes, the specific intention (for oneself or on behalf of the named beneficiary) must be made at the time of entering Ihram at the Miqat
One can assign it to five different people after returning home
explanationEn: An act of worship takes its identity at its start; a proxy cannot convert an Umrah performed for themselves afterward into someone else's Badal Umrah.

questionEn: Can one single Umrah be performed with the intention of sharing it for two deceased parents at the same time?
optionsEn: No; an Umrah is performed for one specific person at a time (e.g., one trip/Umrah for mother, another for father), though one may make abundant dua for both
Yes, up to ten people per Umrah
Only during Sha'ban
Only if you do 14 circuits of Tawaf
explanationEn: Classical jurists rule that ritual pilgrimage (Badal) represents one soul per Umrah, just as fasting a missed day or praying an obligatory prayer represents one person; separate Umrahs may be done for each parent.

questionEn: How does a guardian enter Ihram on behalf of an infant or toddler too young to understand Umrah?
optionsEn: Infants must recite Talbiyah on their own
Infants perform only 2 laps of Tawaf
Children under seven enter Makkah without Ihram even if intending Umrah

The guardian makes Niyyah of Ihram for the child, dresses a boy in two tiny unstitched sheets (or modest dress for a girl), avoids perfume/prohibitions on the child, and carries them through Tawaf and Sa'i before trimming a little hair
explanationEn: As recorded in Sahih Muslim 1336, a mother lifted her infant to ask if Hajj counted for him and the Prophet ﷺ affirmed it; guardians manage Niyyah, Ihram rules, and carrying the child through the rites.

questionEn: What if a toddler in Ihram accidentally tears off their tiny Rida' or soils their diaper during Tawaf?
optionsEn: The parent's own Tawaf is invalidated
They must exit Masjid al-Haram and fly home
There is no sin or penalty; the guardian simply cleans the child, changes the diaper/cloths cleanly, and continues smoothly
The toddler owes a sheep sacrifice
explanationEn: Note that if a parent touches impurity while changing a child, the parent ensures no najasah remains on their body/clothes and refreshes Wudu if needed before continuing Tawaf, while a clean diaper itself is permitted for an infant.

questionEn: Does a pre-pubescent child who is capable of understanding (Mumayyiz, e.g., age 7+) make their own Niyyah for Umrah?
optionsEn: Only if they travel alone
Yes, with their guardian's permission and supervision, a discerning child makes their own Niyyah and recites Talbiyah
No, nobody under age 25 can make Niyyah
They must skip Sa'i
explanationEn: A Mumayyiz child who understands prayer and worship enters Ihram by their own intention with guardian approval, earning reward while learning the rites early.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if they inadvertently step on an ant or small insect while walking toward the Haram in Ihram?
optionsEn: Pay a sheep penalty for each ant
Stop performing Sa'i
Avoid harming living creatures purposefully, while accidental stepping incurs no penalty
Return to the Miqat immediately
explanationEn: The prohibition on hunting targets wild edible land game (sayd al-barr); unintentional stepping on tiny insects incurs no compensation.

questionEn: Is wearing a wedding ring or watch made of leather or metal permitted for men in Ihram?
optionsEn: Yes, rings, watches, and belts are permissible for men in Ihram (keeping in mind gold is always forbidden for Muslim men whether in Ihram or not)
Leather watch straps count as khuffayn
Gold rings become halal during Umrah
No, metal watches break Ihram
explanationEn: Men are always barred from wearing gold jewelry in Islam, while silver rings, watches, and leather belts are completely fine during Ihram.

questionEn: Why is the valley of Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali) such a memorable landmark for pilgrims traveling from Madinah?
optionsEn: It is where Zamzam water was discovered
It is where Safa and Marwah are located
It is the site of the Battle of Badr
It is the very site where the Prophet ﷺ prayed and initiated his Ihram when departing Madinah for his Umrahs and Farewell Hajj
explanationEn: Standing in Masjid Dhul-Hulayfah connects modern pilgrims physically and spiritually to the exact starting point of the Prophet's ﷺ own journeys to Makkah.

questionEn: What should pilgrims beware of regarding unauthorized 'photographers' or sellers pressing unsolicited items near Miqat mosques?
optionsEn: Engage in loud arguments inside the prayer hall
Skip praying at the Miqat
Remain polite, safeguard belongings, and focus on spiritual preparation without getting pulled into disputes or unnecessary distractions
Buy perfume and apply it after Niyyah
explanationEn: Calm focus, avoiding jidal (quarrelling), and keeping personal items secure help preserve the serenity of entering Ihram.

questionEn: If a flight passes over two Miqats or flies parallel along a coastal corridor, how should a passenger determine the safest moment for Niyyah?
optionsEn: Wait until entering the bus in Makkah
Wait until the plane touches the runway in Jeddah
Follow the captain's Miqat announcement—or if unsure, make Niyyah slightly earlier rather than risking passing the Miqat without Ihram
Wait until seeing the Kaaba
explanationEn: Entering Ihram a few minutes before the Miqat line is universally valid and safe, whereas crossing the Miqat without Ihram violates a Wajib.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim enters Ihram at Miqat with a general intention ('I intend pilgrimage') without specifying Umrah or Hajj, and clarifies it before reaching Makkah?
optionsEn: According to scholars who permit 'Ihram Mutlaq' (unspecified Ihram), they may specify Umrah shortly thereafter before starting rituals
Their Ihram is permanently invalid
They must return to Madinah
They must perform both Hajj and Umrah in Ramadan
explanationEn: Classical jurists recognize 'Ihram Mutlaq' (as occurred with Ali RA and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari RA in Yemen before specifying at Makkah), though clearly intending Umrah from the start is best.

questionEn: What did Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) say when he returned from Yemen to join the Prophet ﷺ at Makkah without knowing which rite the Prophet ﷺ had chosen?
optionsEn: 'I declare myself free of Ihram until next year'
'I will wait in Yemen'
'O Allah, I enter Ihram with the same intention Your Messenger ﷺ entered Ihram with'
'I will only perform two laps of Tawaf'
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated how Ali (RA) used this wording and the Prophet ﷺ approved it, directing him to remain in Qiran since the Prophet ﷺ had brought Hady.

questionEn: Is there any restriction against wearing eyeglasses with black frames or sunglasses in Ihram?
optionsEn: Eyewear is banned inside Masjid al-Haram
Only clear glasses are allowed
Sunglasses are forbidden as head covering
No restriction at all; sunglasses and prescription eyewear are fully permissible for both men and women in Ihram
explanationEn: Sunglasses protect eyes from bright sun glare on white marble plazas and do not cover the head or function as a niqab.

questionEn: May a pilgrim carry a backpack or shoulder bag over their Rida' while in Ihram?
optionsEn: No, shoulder straps count as sewn sleeves
Only handheld plastic bags are permitted
Yes, carrying a backpack, sling bag, or waist pouch is completely permissible in Ihram
Backpacks must be checked at the Miqat
explanationEn: Bags and straps do not constitute tailored garments; keeping light essentials secure while leaving the bag outside crowded Mataf zones if bulky is practical and permitted.

questionEn: Why do scholars advise men not to apply scented soap or cologne onto their Izar and Rida' sheets before Niyyah, even though perfuming the body is Sunnah?
optionsEn: Because perfume evaporates only in Madinah
Because fragrance attracts pigeons
Because the Prophet ﷺ prohibited wearing any garment touched by saffron or wars perfume in Ihram, whereas Aisha (RA) perfumed his body/hair only before Niyyah
Because soap stains white cotton permanently
explanationEn: Distinguishing body vs garment ensures compliance with both authentic narrations: perfuming the body prior to Ihram is Sunnah, while keeping the Ihram wraps fragrance-free avoids violating the garment rule.

questionEn: If a pilgrim forgets and puts a drop of attar on their Rida' sheet BEFORE Niyyah, what should they do before making Niyyah?
optionsEn: Wash that spot or switch to an unscented sheet before making Niyyah
Wait until after Sa'i to wash it
Sacrifice a goat immediately
Nothing can fix it; discard the trip
explanationEn: Before Niyyah, there is no sin or penalty at all—simply swapping or rinsing the cloth ensures one enters Ihram cleanly.

questionEn: What is the ruling on trimming one's beard while in the state of Ihram?
optionsEn: Removing or trimming hair from the head or beard is prohibited in Ihram (in addition to the general Prophetic command to leave the beard grow)
Required before entering Makkah
Trimming the beard is Sunnah right after Tawaf
Allowed on Fridays during Umrah
explanationEn: During Ihram, removing hair from any part of the body—head, beard, underarms, etc.—is forbidden until Halq/Taqsir (and at Tahallul, only head hair is shaved/trimmed).

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if a loose hangnail or torn piece of skin on their finger catches on their Ihram cloth and bleeds?
optionsEn: Gently remove only the loose dead skin/broken tip causing harm, wash any blood cleanly, and cover with an unscented bandage without penalty
Leave it bleeding during Tawaf around the Kaaba
Pay a Dam for touching the hangnail
Restart Umrah from Miqat
explanationEn: Removing harmful broken skin or a split nail tip that causes injury is excused, and keeping blood off one's body and the Haram carpet is essential.

questionEn: Can a woman in Ihram tie her hair back with a hairband or wear an undercap (bonnet) beneath her headscarf?
optionsEn: Only metal hairpins are banned
Yes, women are permitted to wear hair ties, undercaps, and headscarves in Ihram; the prohibition on covering the head applies to men only
Undercaps require a fidyah
No, women must leave their hair loose and uncovered
explanationEn: Women are required to cover their hair modestly before non-mahram men at all times, including Ihram, and may wear any normal modest hijab and undercap.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim enters Ihram at Miqat while wearing scented clothes by mistake and realizes an hour later?
optionsEn: They must immediately change into unscented Ihram wraps and wash off any scent on their skin; if done out of ignorance or forgetfulness, no fidyah is owed according to the strong scholarly view
They must stay in the scented clothes until Makkah
Their Umrah is nullified forever
They must pay three sheep
explanationEn: Just as the Prophet ﷺ instructed the companion at al-Ji'ranah to wash off the fragrance and take off the cloak without imposing a fidyah upon him for acting in ignorance, prompt correction suffices.

questionEn: Why do pilgrims say 'Allahu Akbar' or make dua while looking at the hills of Makkah as they approach the Sacred City?
optionsEn: To express awe, gratitude, and reverence as guests approaching the sanctuary blessed by Ibrahim's (AS) prayer and the Prophet's ﷺ mission
To scare away desert wildlife
Because shouting at hills is an obligatory pillar
To signal the end of Umrah
explanationEn: Approaching Makkah after reciting Talbiyah stirs deep reverence; Ibn Umar (RA) and early Muslims entered Makkah humbly with remembrance of Allah.

questionEn: Did the Prophet ﷺ bathe before entering Makkah after reaching Dhi Tuwa (a valley just outside Makkah)?
optionsEn: Yes; Ibn Umar (RA) used to spend the night at Dhi Tuwa, bathe in the morning, and enter Makkah by day, stating the Prophet ﷺ did that
No, bathing between Miqat and Tawaf was forbidden
He entered Makkah only at noon on Wednesdays
He bathed only inside Zamzam well
explanationEn: Nafi' reported that Ibn Umar (RA) never entered Makkah without spending the night at Dhi Tuwa until dawn, bathing, and entering Makkah by day, attributing this Sunnah to the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: Is spending the night at Dhi Tuwa and bathing before entering Makkah obligatory for Umrah pilgrims today, or a praiseworthy Sunnah when feasible?
optionsEn: It is a strict pillar without which Umrah is invalid
It is a recommended Sunnah (Mustahabb) to freshen up cleanly before entering Masjid al-Haram, not an obligation
Only residents of Madinah do it
It requires paying a sacrificial fee if skipped
explanationEn: Arriving clean, refreshed, and bathed before entering Al-Masjid al-Haram honors the sanctity of the House, though pilgrims arriving directly by bus or train face no blame if unable to stop at Dhi Tuwa.

questionEn: Through which historic entrance did the Prophet ﷺ enter Makkah and Al-Masjid al-Haram when arriving from Madinah?
optionsEn: From the southern peak of Mina
Entering Makkah from its upper pass (Kada') and entering the Mosque through Bab Bani Shaybah (near today's Bab al-Salam side)
Through Jeddah seaport
Through an underground tunnel
explanationEn: Sahih narrations note the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah from the upper pass (al-Thaniyyah al-'Ulya / Kada') and entered the Sacred Mosque from the Bab Bani Shaybah direction, though any clean gate is valid today.

questionEn: Does entering Al-Masjid al-Haram through a gate other than Bab al-Salam affect the validity of Umrah?
optionsEn: Yes, only Bab al-Salam leads to a valid Tawaf
No; a pilgrim may enter through any convenient gate of Al-Masjid al-Haram, stepping in with the right foot and reciting the mosque-entry dua
Women must enter through Bab al-Fath only
Only Bab al-Umrah is valid for Umrah
explanationEn: All gates of Al-Masjid al-Haram lead equally to the Sacred House; choosing an uncrowded gate recommended by mosque staff eases entry and safety.

questionEn: What dua is Sunnah to recite as you step inside Al-Masjid al-Haram with your right foot?
optionsEn: 'Bismillah, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala Rasulillah, Allahummaftah li abwaba rahmatik' (and seeking refuge from Shaytan as narrated in Abi Dawud)
Remaining completely silent until Sa'i
Reciting Surah al-Kafirun aloud seven times
Asking for worldly wealth only
explanationEn: The universal Prophetic Sunnah when entering any mosque—including Al-Masjid al-Haram—is stepping with the right foot, sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and asking Allah to open the doors of His mercy.

questionEn: Is there a specific authentic Hadith mandating a unique fixed prayer upon first laying eyes on the Kaaba, or is heartfelt personal dua encouraged?
optionsEn: One must close their eyes for the first three laps
Pilgrims must raise both shoes above their heads

Sincere personal dua and praising Allah upon seeing the Kaaba are encouraged (and Umar RA's dua 'Allahumma antas-salam wa minkas-salam...' is reported in al-Bayhaqi), though no single fixed formula is obligatory
Looking at the Kaaba breaks Wudu
explanationEn: Reports from Umar (RA) and early scholars encourage praising Allah, thanking Him, and asking for goodness upon first seeing the Kaaba, without imposing an unauthentic fixed formula.

questionEn: What famous supplication is reported from Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) or classical manuals upon first seeing the Kaaba?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, allow only Quraysh inside'
'Allahumma zid hadhal-bayta tashrifan wa ta'ziman wa takriman wa mahabah' (O Allah, increase this House in honor, greatness, nobility, and awe) and praying for Islam and peace
'O Allah, reduce the height of Safa'
'O Allah, hide this House from travelers'
explanationEn: While attributed in weak/mursal chains or as a Companion/early-scholar supplication (by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib/Umar's era), its meaning is sound and beautiful as voluntary dua—alongside Umar's (RA) 'Allahumma antas-salam...'.
reference: Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah; Al-Adhkar by al-Nawawi

questionEn: What should you avoid doing right at the busy entrance doors of the Mataf when seeing the Kaaba for the first time?
optionsEn: Saying 'SubhanAllah' quietly
Heading toward the Black Stone alignment line
Stopping abruptly in the middle of the narrow entrance corridor or raising a selfie stick, which blocks hundreds of pilgrims behind you
Walking smoothly toward an open spot to make dua without obstructing flow
explanationEn: Stepping aside out of walking lanes before pausing to gaze and make dua honors both the Kaaba and the safety of fellow pilgrims.

questionEn: When a pilgrim enters Al-Masjid al-Haram in Ihram for Umrah, should they pray two rak'ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid before starting Tawaf?
optionsEn: Yes, two rak'ahs at the door are mandatory before Tawaf
They must wait until Asr before starting Tawaf
Yes, four rak'ahs behind Safa
No; Tawaf itself serves as the greeting (Tahiyyah) of Al-Masjid al-Haram for one arriving to perform Umrah, unless a congregational Fard prayer is about to start
explanationEn: Just as the Prophet ﷺ went straight to Tawaf upon entering Makkah, jurists agree that the greeting of Al-Masjid al-Haram is Tawaf—except when the Iqamah for obligatory prayer is called or one enters solely to sit/pray without intending Tawaf.

questionEn: What should a newly arrived Umrah pilgrim do if they walk into Al-Masjid al-Haram just as the Iqamah for an obligatory prayer (such as Maghrib or Isha) is called?
optionsEn: Join the congregational Fard prayer immediately, and begin Tawaf right after finishing Salah
Pray their own separate prayer behind Maqam Ibrahim
Leave the mosque until the prayer finishes
Ignore the congregation and start walking around the Kaaba alone
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'When the prayer is called, there is no prayer (nor Tawaf) except the prescribed one'; joining congregation takes priority, after which Tawaf begins.

questionEn: If a pilgrim arrives at Al-Masjid al-Haram completely exhausted or needing to use the restroom and renew Wudu first, what is best?
optionsEn: Perform Tawaf without Wudu to save time
Rush into Tawaf while holding back the urge to use the restroom
Skip Tawaf and begin Sa'i first
Take care of restroom needs, rest briefly if dizzy, make fresh calm Wudu, and then enter Tawaf with full focus and purity
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade praying while resisting the call of nature ('la salata bi-hadratil-ta'am wa la wa huwa yudafi'uhul-akhbathan'); likewise calm Wudu ensures serene Tawaf.

questionEn: What is 'Idtiba'' in Umrah, and when does a male pilgrim arrange his Rida' into Idtiba'?
optionsEn: Removing the Rida' completely during Sa'i
Covering both ears with the Rida' at the airport
Passing the middle of the Rida' under the right armpit and draping both ends over the left shoulder, leaving the right shoulder bare—done right before starting Umrah Tawaf
Wrapping the Izar above the knees
explanationEn: Ya'la ibn Umayyah (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ performed Tawaf in Idtiba', uncovering his right shoulder exclusively during the arrival/Umrah Tawaf.

questionEn: Do women practice Idtiba' (uncovering the right shoulder) or Raml (brisk jogging) during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Yes, women uncover their right shoulder too
Yes, women perform Raml in all seven circuits
Women perform Idtiba' only during Sa'i
No; both Idtiba' and Raml are exclusively for men, while women remain fully covered and walk at a calm, dignified pace
explanationEn: Ibn al-Mundhir and all four legal schools record consensus that women do neither Idtiba' nor Raml, preserving full modest covering and composure.

questionEn: Should men uncover their right shoulder (Idtiba') while at the Miqat, on the plane, or during Fard prayers before Tawaf?
optionsEn: Yes, during every Fard prayer in Makkah
No; Idtiba' is only for the 7 circuits of Tawaf—during Fard prayers and outside Tawaf, both shoulders should remain covered
Idtiba' is only during the two rak'ahs after Tawaf
Yes, men must bare their right shoulder from the Miqat until shaving their head
explanationEn: Leaving the shoulder bare during Salah violates the Prophetic instruction not to pray in a single garment without covering the shoulders; hence Idtiba' starts at Tawaf and ends immediately before Salah.

questionEn: If a male pilgrim forgets to do Idtiba' during Tawaf and keeps both shoulders covered throughout all seven laps, is his Tawaf valid?
optionsEn: No, he must repeat all seven laps
Yes, completely valid with no penalty, because Idtiba' is a Sunnah and not a pillar or condition of Tawaf
His Umrah is invalid
He owes a sacrificial goat
explanationEn: Idtiba' is an emphasized Sunnah of arrival/Umrah Tawaf; omitting it—whether by forgetfulness or cold weather—never invalidates Tawaf.

questionEn: Which corner of the Kaaba serves as both the exact starting point and ending point of every circuit of Tawaf?
optionsEn: Al-Rukn al-Iraqi (the Iraqi corner)
The middle of Hijr Ismail
Al-Rukn al-Shami (the Levantine corner)
The corner containing Al-Hajar al-Aswad (the Black Stone)
explanationEn: Every circuit of Tawaf begins precisely aligned with the Black Stone corner, circles counter-clockwise with the Kaaba to the left, and finishes back at the Black Stone line.

questionEn: How do pilgrims in the Mataf and on upper floors know the exact line of Al-Hajar al-Aswad when beginning each lap of Tawaf?
optionsEn: By aligning with the Black Stone corner directly (or the green guidance light/markers installed across the mosque walls/pillars facing the corner)
By starting from Safa hill
By guessing from the northern gate
By listening for a bell
explanationEn: Even when far from the Kaaba or on upper levels, visual alignment with the Black Stone corner (aided by the green marker line) ensures each circuit begins and ends accurately.

questionEn: What is the rule regarding passing INSIDE Hijr Ismail (the semi-circular low wall area called al-Hatim) during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Women walk inside Hijr Ismail while men walk outside
Pilgrims must walk through Hijr Ismail on lap 7 only
One MUST walk outside the curved wall of Hijr Ismail, because roughly 3 meters (6+ cubits) of that area belong to the original foundation of the Kaaba
Walking inside Hijr Ismail saves time and still counts
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ confirmed the Hijr belongs to the House (built outside only when Quraysh lacked halal funds); therefore cutting through Hijr Ismail skips part of the Kaaba and invalidates that lap.

questionEn: If a pilgrim realizes on lap 5 that they walked inside Hijr Ismail on lap 2, what must they do?
optionsEn: Restart Umrah from Jeddah
Pray two extra rak'ahs instead
Nothing; cutting through Hijr Ismail is fine once
Discard the invalid lap and perform an extra complete circuit outside Hijr Ismail so they achieve seven full valid circuits around the entire Kaaba
explanationEn: Because a circuit passing inside Hijr Ismail does not encircle the entire Kaaba, it does not count as a valid circuit and must be replaced by a full circuit outside the curved wall.

questionEn: What is the 'Shadhrawan' at the base of the Kaaba walls, and should pilgrims step on it during Tawaf?
optionsEn: The wooden barrier around Zamzam
The top golden roof gutter
The sloping marble ledge around the lower base of the Kaaba; pilgrims must NOT walk on it during Tawaf as jurists consider part of it part of the Kaaba's foundation
The marble floor of Safa
explanationEn: Because scholars regard the Shadhrawan (excluding the door side per some details) as part of the original foundation wall of the Kaaba, stepping up onto it during Tawaf risks invalidating part of the circuit.

questionEn: In which direction must Tawaf around the Kaaba always be performed?
optionsEn: Facing the Kaaba while walking sideways on all 7 laps
Counter-clockwise, keeping the Kaaba continuously to one's left side
Alternating clockwise and counter-clockwise
Clockwise, keeping the Kaaba to one's right side
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ kept the House on his left (counter-clockwise) throughout Tawaf, which is an obligatory condition across all four schools.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if they turn their chest directly toward the Kaaba to gesture at the Black Stone during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Pause briefly in alignment or point while keeping forward counter-clockwise motion so they do not walk past sections with their back or chest instead of left shoulder toward the Kaaba
Walk backward for ten meters
Stand facing the Kaaba for five minutes blocking others
Spin around 360 degrees at every corner
explanationEn: Facing the Black Stone briefly at the start of the lap to raise the right hand and say 'Allahu Akbar' is Sunnah, after which one immediately turns left shoulder to the Kaaba and walks forward.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when comparing Tawaf around the Kaaba to Salah (ritual prayer)?
optionsEn: Tawaf around the House is like Salah, except that Allah has permitted speech in it—so whoever speaks should speak only good
Tawaf requires remaining completely silent like Salah
Tawaf has only two circuits like Fajr prayer
Tawaf requires bowing and prostrating after every corner
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ compared Tawaf to Salah in requiring purity and focus, while permitting lawful beneficial speech during Tawaf.

questionEn: What is the position of the majority of jurists (Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali) regarding Wudu (ritual purity) for Tawaf?
optionsEn: Wudu is required only for the seventh lap
Being in a state of Wudu (free from minor and major impurity) is a required condition for the validity of Tawaf
Only men need Wudu for Tawaf
Wudu is discouraged during Tawaf
explanationEn: Based on the Prophet ﷺ performing Wudu before Tawaf (Bukhari 1614) and saying 'Tawaf is like Salah', the majority stipulate Wudu as a condition of validity, while Hanafis consider Wudu Wajib (requiring Dam if omitted, while major impurity/hayd requires a higher penalty).

questionEn: If a pilgrim loses Wudu during the 4th circuit of Tawaf in heavy crowds, what should they do?
optionsEn: Exit the Mataf calmly, renew Wudu, and then either resume from the 4th circuit (per Hanbali/Hanafi/one view of Ibn Taymiyyah) or restart the Tawaf (per Shafi'i/Maliki caution)
Keep walking all remaining circuits without Wudu
Leave Makkah immediately
Skip the rest of Tawaf and go straight to Sa'i
explanationEn: Because renewal of Wudu is required, the pilgrim steps out cleanly; Shafi'is and Malikis advise restarting from lap 1, whereas Hanafis and Hanbalis (as well as Ibn Baz/Ibn Uthaymin for crowded situations) allow resuming from where Wudu broke if the interruption is brief.

questionEn: What happens if an obligatory prayer (e.g., Asr or Maghrib) or a Janazah prayer starts while you are in the middle of Tawaf?
optionsEn: Note the exact spot and circuit number you reached, join the congregational prayer, and immediately after Salah resume Tawaf from that exact spot
Discard all previous laps and always restart from zero
Keep walking around the Kaaba while everyone else prays
Go straight to Safa and Marwah without finishing Tawaf
explanationEn: All four schools permit interrupting Tawaf for Fard or Janazah prayer; once the congregation concludes, you continue from the spot and lap number where you stopped.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim loses count and becomes unsure during Tawaf whether they completed 5 or 6 circuits?
optionsEn: Stop immediately and guess
Ask a stranger nearby to decide for you
Build upon certainty—assume the lower number (5)—and complete the remaining circuits from there
Always assume the higher number (6)
explanationEn: Just as in Salah when doubting the number of rak'ahs, Islamic jurisprudence requires relying on the certain minimum count (al-yaqin) and adding whatever remains.

questionEn: If a pilgrim firmly believes they finished 7 circuits and later doubts after leaving the Mataf and starting Sa'i, should they restart Tawaf?
optionsEn: No; doubts that arise AFTER completing an act of worship (unless backed by clear certainty) are disregarded so the believer is not plagued by whispers (waswas)
Yes, repeat the whole Umrah from Jeddah
Fast three days for doubting
Yes, repeat Tawaf three times whenever a stray thought occurs
explanationEn: Scholars establish the golden rule that post-completion doubt (al-shakk ba'da al-faragh min al-'ibadah) carries no weight unless certainty proves a lap was missed.
reference: Al-Ashbah wal-Naza'ir by al-Suyuti; Fatawa Ibn Uthaymin

questionEn: Is performing Tawaf on the upper floors or the roof of Al-Masjid al-Haram valid?
optionsEn: Only valid for men over sixty
Yes, completely valid because the entire mosque structure encompasses the space around the Kaaba upward
No, only the ground marble floor counts
Upper-floor Tawaf counts as half a circuit per lap
explanationEn: Jurists unanimously validate Tawaf on upper tiers and roofs of Al-Masjid al-Haram, as the sacred space surrounding the Kaaba extends vertically upward.

questionEn: Does covering the Awrah remain a strict condition during Tawaf?
optionsEn: No, Awrah rules are lifted inside Masjid al-Haram
Yes; both men and women must keep their Awrah properly covered throughout every circuit (even men doing Idtiba' keep navel-to-knees and left shoulder securely covered)
Only for women
Only during the first three laps
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade nakedness during Tawaf (Bukhari 1622); keeping the Izar securely fastened from above the navel to below the knees preserves validity and modesty.

questionEn: What did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) and Ali (RA) proclaim during the 9 AH pilgrimage before the Farewell Hajj regarding Tawaf?
optionsEn: That Tawaf should be done only at night
That no polytheist may perform pilgrimage after that year, and no naked person may circumambulate the Sacred House
That Sa'i is abolished
That only Quraysh may touch the Kaaba
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ sent Ali (RA) alongside Abu Bakr (RA) to announce these foundational decrees, restoring the pure Abrahamic dignity and modesty of the Kaaba.

questionEn: What is 'Muwalat' (continuity) in Tawaf, and when is a brief break permitted?
optionsEn: Running without stopping to breathe
Doing one lap per day over a week
Performing the seven circuits consecutively without long unrelated gaps; brief pauses for resting if exhausted, drinking water, renewing Wudu, or joining Fard Salah are excused
Taking a three-hour dinner break between lap 3 and lap 4
explanationEn: Majority jurists (Malikis, Hanbalis) treat continuity as a condition of Tawaf while excusing brief rest for elderly/sick pilgrims, refreshing Wudu, or obligatory congregation.

questionEn: If someone is dizzy or severely fatigued during Tawaf, what should they do?
optionsEn: Force themselves to collapse in the moving crowd
Step safely to the side/edge of the Mataf, sit down, sip water or rest briefly, and resume from the lap they paused on—or use a wheelchair if needed
Skip the remaining laps
Abandon Umrah and return home
explanationEn: Brief rest due to fatigue or heat preserves safety and still respects continuity; using a wheelchair on the upper ring is also fully valid.

questionEn: During which circuits of Umrah Tawaf is 'Raml' (walking briskly with short firm steps and proud posture) Sunnah for able-bodied men?
optionsEn: Only the seventh circuit
The first three circuits only, followed by normal calm walking in circuits 4 through 7
Circuits 5, 6, and 7
All seven circuits of every Tawaf
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ performed Raml in the first three circuits from the Black Stone back to the Black Stone, and walked normally in the last four.

questionEn: What should a male pilgrim do if heavy congestion around the Kaaba makes performing Raml impossible without bumping or shoving others?
optionsEn: Walk calmly and steadily; never push or harm fellow pilgrims just to perform a Sunnah
Push aggressively through women and elders to run
Skip Tawaf altogether until midnight
Climb over barriers to jog
explanationEn: Scholars universally emphasize that avoiding harm to Muslims is obligatory, whereas Raml is a Sunnah; if space is tight, walking calmly is required and incurs no penalty.

questionEn: Does a pilgrim perform Raml or Idtiba' in voluntary (Nafl) Tawafs done later in the week after finishing Umrah?
optionsEn: Only during Tawaf al-Wada'
Only on Mondays and Thursdays
Yes, in every single Tawaf forever
