No; Raml and Idtiba' are Sunnah only in the initial arrival/Umrah Tawaf (Tawaf al-Qudum / Tawaf al-Umrah), not in subsequent voluntary Tawafs or Tawaf al-Wada'
explanationEn: Jurists affirm that Idtiba' and Raml apply exclusively to the initial Tawaf upon arriving in Ihram (such as Umrah Tawaf), not in extra voluntary Tawafs later on.

questionEn: What is the Arabic term for greeting or saluting Al-Hajar al-Aswad (the Black Stone) at the start of each Tawaf circuit?
optionsEn: Ihram
Istilam
Ihsar
Taqsir
explanationEn: Istilam refers to greeting the Black Stone—by kissing it if accessible without crowding, touching it with the hand and kissing the hand, touching it with a staff, or pointing toward it from afar with the right hand.

questionEn: What words did the Prophet ﷺ say when pointing to or saluting Al-Hajar al-Aswad in Tawaf?
optionsEn: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdik' ten times
'Allahu Akbar' (and 'Bismillah, Allahu Akbar' is reported from Ibn Umar RA in authentic practice)
'As-salamu alaykum ya hajar'
'Allahu Akbar' silently while bowing to the stone
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ circled the House on his camel and whenever he came to the Corner, he pointed to it with something in his hand and said 'Allahu Akbar.'

questionEn: Should a pilgrim kiss their hand after pointing at Al-Hajar al-Aswad from a distance?
optionsEn: Yes, one must kiss both palms ten times
One must point with the left foot
Yes, kissing the air loudly is mandatory

No; kissing the hand is narrated when actually touching the Stone directly with one's hand—when pointing from afar, one simply raises the right hand briefly, says 'Allahu Akbar', and lowers it without kissing the hand
explanationEn: Hadith show the Prophet ﷺ kissed the Stone directly, touched it with his hand/staff and kissed that, or pointed from his camel saying 'Allahu Akbar' without kissing his hand afterward.

questionEn: What did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) famously declare while kissing Al-Hajar al-Aswad, teaching pure Islamic monotheism?
optionsEn: 'You are greater than the entire Qur'an'
'You are a stone that grants wealth on your own'
'Every pilgrim must kiss you or their Umrah fails'
'Indeed I know that you are a stone that neither harms nor benefits; had I not seen the Prophet ﷺ kiss you, I would never have kissed you'
explanationEn: Umar's (RA) statement in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim clarifies that venerating the Black Stone is pure obedience to the Sunnah (ittiba'), free from any superstition or stone-worship.

questionEn: What instruction did the Prophet ﷺ give to Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) about reaching Al-Hajar al-Aswad in heavy crowds?
optionsEn: 'Climb on top of the Kiswah to reach it'
'Stand there for two hours blocking the lane'
'O Umar, you are a strong man—do not crowd the Black Stone and harm the weak; if you find an opening, touch it, otherwise face it, say Tahlil and Takbir, and move on'
'Push everyone aside because touching it is obligatory'
explanationEn: Reported in Musnad Ahmad, this gentle counsel reminds strong pilgrims never to jostle elderly, women, or frail worshippers just to touch the Stone.

questionEn: According to authentic Hadith in al-Tirmidhi and Ahmad, what is the origin of Al-Hajar al-Aswad (the Black Stone)?
optionsEn: It descended from Paradise whiter than milk, and the sins of the children of Adam turned it black
It was brought from Yemen during the 3rd century
It was quarried from Mount Uhud
It was carved by Roman emperors
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The Black Stone descended from Paradise whiter than milk, and the sins of the sons of Adam blackened it.'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in Jami' al-Tirmidhi about Al-Hajar al-Aswad on the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: It will turn into water
It will judge against everyone who performed Umrah
Allah will raise it on the Day of Judgment with two eyes to see and a tongue to speak, bearing witness in truth for everyone who touched/saluted it
It will sink beneath the Red Sea
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'By Allah, Allah will bring it forth on the Day of Resurrection having two eyes with which it sees and a tongue with which it speaks, testifying in favor of whoever touched it in truth.'

questionEn: How does the treatment of Al-Rukn al-Yamani (the Yemeni Corner) differ from Al-Hajar al-Aswad during Tawaf?
optionsEn: One must kiss Rukn al-Yamani seven times
Rukn al-Yamani is climbed before Sa'i

If accessible without crowding, one touches Rukn al-Yamani gently with the right hand WITHOUT kissing it or kissing one's hand—and if crowded, one simply passes by WITHOUT pointing or saying Takbir specifically at it
One must point at Rukn al-Yamani with both hands and shout
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ touched only the two Yemeni corners (Black Stone and Rukn al-Yamani), touching Rukn al-Yamani with his hand without kissing it, and no authentic report supports pointing from afar at Rukn al-Yamani.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ touch ONLY the Black Stone and Al-Rukn al-Yamani, and NOT the Iraqi or Levantine (Shami) corners?
optionsEn: Because only two corners face Madinah
Because those two corners stand on the original foundations built by Ibrahim (AS), whereas the Iraqi and Shami corners were moved inward when Quraysh rebuilt the Kaaba excluding Hijr Ismail
Because the Shami corner was built of wood
Because the Iraqi corner was closed by guards
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) and classical scholars explain that Quraysh lacked sufficient lawful funds to rebuild over the Hijr Ismail portion, leaving the two northern corners inside the original Abrahamic foundations.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic supplication did the Prophet ﷺ regularly recite in the segment between Al-Rukn al-Yamani and Al-Hajar al-Aswad?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Fatihah seven times
'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la'
'Allahumma zid hadhal-bayta...'
'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:201)
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib (RA) heard the Prophet ﷺ recite this comprehensive Qur'anic dua between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone asking for good in this world, good in the Hereafter, and protection from the Fire.

questionEn: Are there seven specific mandatory printed prayers—one assigned to each lap of Tawaf—that pilgrims must read from a booklet?
optionsEn: No; there are no prescribed lap-by-lap duas in the Sunnah—a pilgrim is free to supplicate from the heart, recite Qur'an, make dhikr, and ask Allah in any language
Only Arabic poetry is allowed in lap 4
Only Surah Yasin is valid in Tawaf
Yes, skipping the booklet's third-lap prayer voids Tawaf
explanationEn: Scholars clarify that printed Tawaf booklets assigning fixed prayers to laps 1–7 have no Prophetic basis and often distract pilgrims from genuine heartfelt connection with Allah.

questionEn: What is the virtue of touching the Black Stone and Al-Rukn al-Yamani gently when possible without harming anyone?
optionsEn: Ibn Umar (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ said touching them both is an expiation for sins
It turns copper into silver
It replaces fasting Ramadan
It waives the need for Sa'i
explanationEn: In Jami' al-Tirmidhi and Ahmad, Ibn Umar (RA) narrated: 'Touching the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone erases sins'—always balanced with the command never to harm others in crowds.

questionEn: What is 'Al-Multazam', and what is its etiquette?
optionsEn: The elevated roof above Safa
The section of the Kaaba wall (about 2 meters) between Al-Hajar al-Aswad and the Kaaba door, where Companions sometimes stood clinging/pressing in humble dua after Tawaf when uncrowded
The entrance gate to Madinah
The silver dome over Maqam Ibrahim
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) and Amr ibn Shu'ayb reports note the Multazam is a blessed place for heartfelt dua, though when crowded one should make dua from nearby without pushing or causing harm.

questionEn: Is walking barefoot during Tawaf mandatory, or may pilgrims wear clean, impurity-free light slippers/socks?
optionsEn: Only green sandals are allowed inside the Mataf
Walking barefoot is forbidden in Islam
Walking barefoot is common and comfortable on cool marble, while wearing clean, impurity-free leather socks (khuffs) or clean mosque slippers is also permissible
Shoes worn outdoors on dirty streets must be worn on the prayer carpets
explanationEn: Clean feet or strictly clean indoor footwear free of street impurity preserve the purity of the Sacred Mosque; outdoor street shoes should be carried neatly in a shoe bag.

questionEn: Is reciting Qur'an quietly during Tawaf permissible?
optionsEn: Yes, reciting Qur'an, making dhikr, sending salutations upon the Prophet ﷺ, and personal dua are all excellent acts during Tawaf
Only Surah Al-Nas is permitted
No, Qur'an may never be recited in Tawaf
Reciting Qur'an cancels Raml
explanationEn: Since Tawaf was instituted for establishing the remembrance of Allah (Tirmidhi 902), Qur'an recitation, tasbih, istighfar, and sincere supplication fill Tawaf with light.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say Tawaf, Sa'i, and stoning the Jamarat were legislated in Jami' al-Tirmidhi 902?
optionsEn: To display regional garments
To test athletic speed
'Tawaf around the House, going between Safa and Marwah, and pelting the Jamarat were instituted only to establish the remembrance of Allah (Dhikrullah)'
To count historical years
explanationEn: This narration summarizes the heart of all pilgrimage rites: cultivating deep remembrance and consciousness of Allah.

questionEn: At the end of the 7th circuit of Tawaf, when reaching the Black Stone line for the final time, does a pilgrim point/salute again?
optionsEn: They must walk backward to Maqam Ibrahim

Some scholars recommend saluting the Black Stone once at the start of each lap (7 times total, ending cleanly at the line without an 8th), while others note saluting at the final completion is fine; either way, a pilgrim must NOT perform an 8th circuit
Yes, and they must add an 8th lap for safety
They must sit down right in front of the Black Stone
explanationEn: Beginning lap 1 at the Black Stone and completing lap 7 back at the Black Stone totals 7 circuits; saluting 7 times (at each start) or completing at the line then covering the right shoulder for Salah aligns cleanly with Sunnah.

questionEn: What must a male pilgrim do with his Rida' immediately after finishing the 7th circuit of Tawaf?
optionsEn: Throw the Rida' over his head during Salah
End Idtiba' by covering both shoulders properly before standing to pray the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim
Remove the Rida' completely and pray bare-chested
Keep his right shoulder uncovered during Salah
explanationEn: Idtiba' applies solely during Tawaf; the Prophet ﷺ forbade praying with both shoulders bare, so covering both shoulders before the two rak'ahs is essential.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse did the Prophet ﷺ recite as he moved toward Maqam Ibrahim after finishing Tawaf?
optionsEn: 'Iqra bismi rabbikalladhi khalaq' (96:1)
'Wattakhidhu min maqami Ibrahima musalla' — 'And take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:125)
'Inna a'taynakal-kawthar' (108:1)
'Qul a'udhu bi-rabbil-falaq' (113:1)
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that after finishing Tawaf, the Prophet ﷺ walked to Maqam Ibrahim reciting 'Wattakhidhu min maqami Ibrahima musalla', positioning the Maqam between himself and the Kaaba.

questionEn: Which two surahs did the Prophet ﷺ recite after Al-Fatihah in the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah and Surah Al-Imran
Surah Al-Fil and Surah Quraysh
Surah Al-Falaq and Surah Al-Nas
Surah Al-Kafirun (109) in the first rak'ah and Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) in the second rak'ah
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) confirmed the Prophet ﷺ recited the two Surahs of pure Tawhid—'Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun' and 'Qul huwAllahu ahad'—in the two Tawaf rak'ahs.

questionEn: What is the wisdom of reciting Surah Al-Kafirun and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the two rak'ahs after Tawaf?
optionsEn: Because only those two surahs existed before Hijrah
They proclaim complete renunciation of shirk and pure affirmation of Allah's absolute Oneness right in front of His House
Because they are mandatory pillars without which Tawaf fails
Because longer surahs are forbidden in Makkah
explanationEn: These two surahs—called the two Surahs of Sincerity (Ikhlas)—seal Tawaf with crystal-clear monotheism, though reciting any other Qur'an if one forgot them still leaves the prayer completely valid.

questionEn: If the space directly behind Maqam Ibrahim is densely crowded with Tawaf walkers, where should a pilgrim pray the two Sunnah rak'ahs?
optionsEn: Wait inside the hotel lobby in Jeddah
Force others out of the way right against the glass casing
Step further back out of the Tawaf circulation path and pray anywhere inside Al-Masjid al-Haram behind the line of Maqam Ibrahim
Skip the two rak'ahs completely forever
explanationEn: Praying directly inside moving Mataf lanes endangers both the worshipper and walkers; moving back to designated prayer mats anywhere behind Maqam Ibrahim in Al-Masjid al-Haram fulfills the Sunnah safely.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1627 (Umar RA's action); Fatawa Ibn Baz

questionEn: What is the legal ruling of the two rak'ahs after Tawaf across the four Sunni schools?
optionsEn: Only for pilgrims under age forty
Strongly emphasized Sunnah according to Shafi'is and Hanbalis, and Wajib according to Hanafis and Malikis (for obligatory Tawaf), though never a pillar that invalidates Umrah if delayed or forgotten
A sixth pillar of Islam
Forbidden after Asr and Fajr in all schools
explanationEn: Scholars also note that the two rak'ahs of Tawaf are valid at any time of day—even during general forbidden prayer times after Fajr or Asr—per the Prophet's ﷺ Hadith to Banu Abd Manaf.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say to Banu Abd Manaf about praying after Tawaf during times when voluntary prayers are normally disallowed (like after Fajr or Asr)?
optionsEn: 'Do not prevent anyone from circling this House and praying at any hour of night or day they wish'
'No one may pray after Asr even after Tawaf'
'Tawaf is forbidden between Fajr and sunrise'
'Wait six hours before praying the two rak'ahs'
explanationEn: Recorded in Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i, this Hadith establishes that Tawaf and its two rak'ahs are exempted from time-of-day restrictions.

questionEn: What actually is 'Maqam Ibrahim' inside the golden/crystal enclosure near the Kaaba?
optionsEn: The grave of Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
A meteorite from Mount Sinai
The stone upon which Prophet Ibrahim (AS) stood while building the upper walls of the Kaaba, preserving the impression of his footprints
The throne of King Sulayman (AS)
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that when the walls rose above Ibrahim's (AS) reach, he stood on this stone moved around by Isma'il (AS), and Allah preserved his footprints as a clear sign (Qur'an 3:97).

questionEn: Is it Sunnah to wipe or kiss the metal/glass casing of Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: One must circle Maqam Ibrahim seven times
Yes, tying threads onto the casing brings health
No; kissing or rubbing the enclosure of Maqam Ibrahim for blessings is an unsupported practice—the Sunnah is solely to pray two rak'ahs behind it
Yes, kissing the glass casing is a pillar of Umrah
explanationEn: Scholars clarify that neither the Prophet ﷺ nor his Companions rubbed or kissed Maqam Ibrahim; honoring it means obeying Allah's command to take it as a place of prayer.
reference: Fatawa al-Lajnah al-Da'imah; Majmu' Fatawa Ibn Taymiyyah

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do immediately after praying the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim and before heading to Safa during his pilgrimage?
optionsEn: He slept for four hours
He walked directly to Mina
He drank from Zamzam water (and poured some on his head) and returned to touch/salute the Black Stone if possible before exiting toward Safa
He shaved his head right behind Maqam Ibrahim
explanationEn: After the two rak'ahs, drinking Zamzam, making heartfelt dua, and saluting the Black Stone once more (if easy without crowding) before walking to Safa is the complete Sunnah sequence.

questionEn: If heavy crowds prevent a pilgrim from walking back to touch the Black Stone after praying the two rak'ahs, should they push through to reach it before Sa'i?
optionsEn: Yes, one must push through at all costs
Wait five hours until midnight
No; returning to the Black Stone after the two rak'ahs is merely a Sunnah—if crowded, simply head peacefully toward Mount Safa after drinking Zamzam
Without touching it again, Sa'i is invalid
explanationEn: Avoid crowding or hurting others; proceeding straight to Safa after drinking Zamzam preserves ease and safety.

questionEn: How did the spring of Zamzam originally appear in the valley of Makkah?
optionsEn: Angel Jibril (AS) struck the earth with his heel (or wing) after Hajar (AS) ran seven times between Safa and Marwah, causing water to gush forth for baby Isma'il (AS)
Roman engineers built an aqueduct
Prophet Dawud (AS) dug a canal from Ta'if
Rain filled a cave after the Farewell Hajj
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari 3364 records how Hajar (AS) heard a voice upon completing her seventh trip at Marwah, saw an angel at the spot of Zamzam digging with his heel/wing, and contained the water saying 'Zam! Zam!'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about Zamzam water in Sahih Muslim (2473) when speaking to Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA)?
optionsEn: 'It should never be drunk by travelers'
'It expires after three days'
'It is ordinary desert water with no blessing'
'Indeed, it is blessed; it is food that nourishes (and a healing for illness in another authentic wording)'
explanationEn: Abu Dharr (RA) survived thirty days in Makkah on nothing but Zamzam water, and the Prophet ﷺ affirmed: 'It is blessed; it is a nourishing food (ta'am tu'm)' (and al-Bazzar/al-Tabarani add 'shifa' suqm').

questionEn: What famous Hadith reported by Jabir (RA) in Sunan Ibn Majah encourages pilgrims to make sincere dua while drinking Zamzam?
optionsEn: 'Zamzam is only for washing sandals'
'Drink Zamzam only once a year'
'The water of Zamzam is for whatever purpose it is drunk for' (Ma'u Zamzama lima shuriba lah)
'Never speak or make dua around Zamzam'
explanationEn: Great scholars and Companions—such as Ibn Abbas (RA) who prayed for beneficial knowledge, vast provision, and healing from every disease—modeled making heartfelt dua when drinking Zamzam.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah etiquette reported from Companions like Ibn Abbas (RA) when drinking Zamzam water?
optionsEn: Mix it with perfume before drinking
Pour it onto the carpet
Drink in one gulp while walking backward
Say 'Bismillah', face the Qiblah, drink in three breaths/sips to one's fill (tadhalla'), make sincere dua, and say 'Alhamdulillah'
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) emphasized facing the Kaaba, invoking Allah's name, drinking deeply until quenched (as a sign distinguishing believers from hypocrites who do not drink their fill of Zamzam), and praising Allah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the sign differentiating believers from hypocrites regarding drinking Zamzam water?
optionsEn: 'The sign between us and the hypocrites is that they do not drink their fill (la yatadalla'un) from Zamzam'
'Believers never drink Zamzam at night'
'Hypocrites only drink chilled Zamzam'
'Hypocrites drink ten cups at once'
explanationEn: Narrated in Sunan Ibn Majah (3061) and al-Daraqutni, 'tadhalla'' means drinking abundantly with faith and appreciation of Allah's blessing.

questionEn: Is it permissible to drink Zamzam water while standing, or is sitting better?
optionsEn: Drinking Zamzam while standing is a major sin
Both are permissible; Ibn Abbas (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ drank Zamzam while standing, while sitting when convenient is the general Sunnah for drinking
Drinking Zamzam while sitting is forbidden
Only elders may sit while drinking
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated: 'I served the Prophet ﷺ Zamzam water and he drank it while standing' (Bukhari 1637), proving standing is completely lawful especially in crowded areas.

questionEn: Is it Sunnah to take Zamzam water home as a gift for family and sick loved ones after Umrah?
optionsEn: Only residents of Madinah may carry Zamzam
Yes; Aisha (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ himself carried Zamzam water with him in containers and poured it over the sick to seek healing
No, taking Zamzam outside Makkah is forbidden
Zamzam loses all blessing once outside Jeddah
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) confirmed the Prophet ﷺ carried Zamzam in waterskins and flasks, sprinkling and giving it to the sick to drink, making bringing Zamzam home an authentic Sunnah.

questionEn: What should pilgrims avoid doing with disposable Zamzam cups inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Stack cups against Maqam Ibrahim
Leave half-full cups on the Mataf floor
Wash sandals using Zamzam dispensers
Never leave used cups on prayer carpets or spill water where worshippers walk or prostrate; place used cups cleanly in designated bins
explanationEn: Keeping Allah's Sacred House spotless, dry, and safe from slipping hazards respects both fellow worshippers and the Masjid's sanctity.

questionEn: What is 'Hijr Ismail' (also called al-Hatim) historically, and is praying inside it equivalent to praying inside the Kaaba?
optionsEn: It is the tomb of Quraysh chiefs
No, it is an unrelated garden outside Makkah
It is a storage room for Zamzam flasks
Yes; when Aisha (RA) wanted to pray inside the Kaaba, the Prophet ﷺ told her to pray inside the Hijr because it is part of the House
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Aisha (RA): 'Pray in the Hijr if you wish to enter the House, for it is a piece of the House'—remembering this is for voluntary prayer AFTER Tawaf, NOT for cutting through during Tawaf!

questionEn: What is the 'Mizab al-Rahmah' (Spout of Mercy) on the Kaaba?
optionsEn: The golden rainwater spout projecting from the upper northern wall of the Kaaba over Hijr Ismail
The door lock of Masjid al-Haram
A bronze pillar in Dhul-Hulayfah
A fountain inside Mount Marwah
explanationEn: The Mizab channels rainwater from the Kaaba's roof downward into Hijr Ismail; many pilgrims love making dua beneath it when entering Hijr Ismail after Umrah.

questionEn: Who was the custodian of the Kaaba's key (Sidanah) to whom the Prophet ﷺ returned the key permanently on the Conquest of Makkah?
optionsEn: Khalid ibn al-Walid
Suhayl ibn Amr
Uthman ibn Talhah (RA) and his cousin Shaybah ibn Uthman from Banu Abd al-Dar
Abu Lahab
explanationEn: Declaring 'Today is a day of loyalty and righteousness', the Prophet ﷺ returned the Kaaba's key to Uthman ibn Talhah (RA) and Banu Shaybah, reciting Qur'an 4:58 ('Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due').

questionEn: What is the black silk cloth covering the Kaaba called, and what is inscribed upon its golden belt?
optionsEn: The Rida' al-Qiblah
The Kiswah, adorned with Qur'anic verses woven in gold-plated silver threads
The Sitr of Madinah
The Izar al-Haram
explanationEn: The Kiswah is renewed annually on 9 Dhul-Hijjah (or Muharram per modern schedule) and embroidered with Qur'anic verses honoring the Sacred House.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1592; History of the Kaaba

questionEn: Is there any Islamic basis for rubbing the Kiswah cloth with handkerchiefs, tearing threads from it, or kissing the walls of the Kaaba outside the Black Stone?
optionsEn: Every pilgrim must kiss all four walls
Yes, taking a piece of Kiswah is required for valid Umrah
No; only Al-Hajar al-Aswad (kiss/touch) and Al-Rukn al-Yamani (touch) are sanctioned in the Sunnah; pulling threads from the Kiswah or rubbing walls for barakah is avoided
Wiping shoes on the Kiswah is encouraged
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) rebuked Mu'awiyah (RA) when he touched the other two corners, saying the Prophet ﷺ touched only the Black Stone and Yemeni Corner—teaching strict adherence to Prophetic bounds.

questionEn: If a pilgrim forgets to do the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim after Tawaf and remembers while already doing Sa'i or back at the hotel, what should they do?
optionsEn: Sacrifice a camel immediately
Pray the two rak'ahs wherever they remember (inside the Haram or anywhere if they already left), and their Umrah remains completely valid
Restart Tawaf from lap 1
Their Sa'i is automatically void
explanationEn: Because the two rak'ahs are Sunnah (or Wajib outside the pillars), praying them whenever remembered—even at home if forgotten until departure—suffices without invalidating Sa'i.

questionEn: Does performing Tawaf require having completed Sa'i first, or must Tawaf ALWAYS precede Sa'i in Umrah?
optionsEn: The order does not matter at all
Pilgrims may alternate 1 lap of Tawaf and 1 lap of Sa'i
Sa'i may be done before Tawaf whenever Safa is less crowded
Tawaf MUST always precede Sa'i; performing Sa'i before a valid Tawaf does not count as Umrah Sa'i
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ performed Tawaf first, then prayed two rak'ahs, then went to Safa saying 'I begin with what Allah began with'; jurists agree Sa'i is valid only after a valid Tawaf.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performed Tawaf without Wudu by mistake, finished Sa'i, and then realized they had broken Wudu before Tawaf, what do majority scholars say?
optionsEn: They do nothing because Wudu never applies to Tawaf
According to the majority (Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali), since Wudu is a condition of Tawaf, they repeat Tawaf with Wudu and repeat Sa'i afterward (and trim a bit more hair if they already trimmed)
They only drink extra Zamzam
They only repeat the 7th lap
explanationEn: Wait: Hanafis consider Tawaf valid with a Dam if done without Wudu, whereas the majority require repeating Tawaf in purity and then Sa'i so Sa'i follows a valid Tawaf.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim discovers a small speck of dried impurity (Najasah) on their Izar AFTER completing Tawaf?
optionsEn: If they were unaware of it during Tawaf, their Tawaf remains valid according to major jurists (analogous to praying unaware of impurity, based on the Prophet's ﷺ Hadith removing shoes with impurity during prayer without restarting)
They must repeat all Umrah rituals from Miqat
They owe a camel sacrifice
They must shave twice
explanationEn: Using the precedent of the Prophet ﷺ removing impure sandals mid-prayer when Jibril informed him without restarting the prayer (Abi Dawud 650), many scholars (Maliki/Hanbali/Shaykh Ibn Uthaymin) hold Tawaf valid when impurity was unknown.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim perform a voluntary Tawaf on behalf of a deceased loved one (or gift its reward), just like Badal Umrah?
optionsEn: Yes, many scholars allow performing voluntary Tawaf and dedicating its reward (or doing a complete Badal Umrah) for a deceased Muslim, though doing full Badal Umrah or making dua is most clearly attested
No, voluntary Tawaf is strictly prohibited in Makkah
Only residents of Jeddah may do voluntary Tawaf
Voluntary Tawaf requires Ihram from Miqat
explanationEn: Voluntary (Nafl) Tawaf requires NO Ihram at all—pilgrims staying in Makkah after finishing Umrah can perform abundant voluntary Tawafs in their regular clothes!

questionEn: Do you need to be in the state of Ihram (wearing Izar and Rida') to perform a voluntary (Nafl) Tawaf while visiting Makkah?
optionsEn: Only women can do Nafl Tawaf in regular clothes
Yes, without Ihram sheets a voluntary Tawaf is sinful
Yes, every Tawaf requires going to Masjid Aisha first
No; Ihram is required only when entering Umrah or Hajj—after exiting Ihram, men and women perform voluntary Tawaf in their normal clean modest clothing
explanationEn: Because of crowd limits in the lower Mataf, security occasionally reserves the ground Mataf for people in Ihram during peak seasons while directing non-muhrim voluntary Tawaf pilgrims to upper floors—yet religiously, Nafl Tawaf requires no Ihram.

questionEn: What is the virtue of performing Tawaf in the rain or intense heat when visiting Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Umrah is doubled in lap count when raining
Enduring heat, rain, or fatigue patiently increases reward, while staying safe on wet marble floors (avoiding slipping or running)
One must stop Tawaf immediately if a drop of rain falls
Rain cancels all seven laps automatically
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ reminded Aisha (RA) that reward corresponds to effort endured sincerely; walking carefully on wet marble prevents injury while rejoicing in Allah's mercy.

questionEn: What did Ibn Abbas (RA) report the Prophet ﷺ said about the reward of performing 50 circuits (or 7 circuits) of Tawaf, or freeing a slave?
optionsEn: Every lap removes all duties of prayer for a month
It exempts one from Zakah
Walking seven laps gives automatic prophethood

In al-Tirmidhi and Ahmad, Ibn Umar (RA) narrated: 'Whoever circles this House seven times and keeps track of it, it is like freeing a slave; and he does not lift a foot or set it down except Allah removes a sin and writes a good deed'
explanationEn: Recorded in Jami' al-Tirmidhi (959) and Musnad Ahmad (4462) from Ibn Umar (RA), this stirring narration highlights how every single step around the Kaaba erases sins and elevates rank.

questionEn: Why is it unwise to tie oneself or a group together with ropes or hold hands in a long wide human chain across the Mataf during Tawaf?
optionsEn: A chain adds extra laps
Ropes are prohibited by the Qur'an
Holding hands breaks Wudu
A wide human chain acts like a barrier blocking behind-coming pilgrims, causing collisions, tripping, and distress to others
explanationEn: While keeping one elderly parent or child close beside you in single/double file is helpful, wide group chains block the circular flow of Tawaf and cause harm.

questionEn: When is the best time of day to perform Umrah Tawaf if traveling with elderly parents or young children?
optionsEn: Only during solar noon
After Isha late at night, after Fajr once morning crowds ease, or mid-morning—avoiding midday sun or right after Maghrib/Jumu'ah peak rush when possible
Strictly at 12:30 PM on Friday
Only right as Maghrib Iqamah starts
explanationEn: Umrah is valid 24 hours a day; choosing cooler, less congested hours protects frail pilgrims from heat exhaustion and crushing.

questionEn: If a pilgrim accidentally starts Tawaf at Al-Rukn al-Yamani instead of Al-Hajar al-Aswad, what counts as their first complete circuit?
optionsEn: It still counts as a full first lap
They must walk clockwise to fix it
Their lap count properly starts only when they pass Al-Hajar al-Aswad—the partial segment from Rukn al-Yamani to Black Stone is ignored, and they complete 7 full laps from Black Stone to Black Stone
They must start over from Jeddah
explanationEn: Because every circuit must begin and end at Al-Hajar al-Aswad, any walking prior to reaching the Black Stone line does not count as Lap 1.

questionEn: What is the 'Hatim'—is it another name for Hijr Ismail, or the area between Black Stone and Kaaba door?
optionsEn: It is the roof of Marwah

Most scholars use 'al-Hatim' to refer to the semi-circular Hijr Ismail area (or specifically its curved low wall), while a few early reports used it for the space between Black Stone, Maqam, and Zamzam
It is a mountain outside Makkah
It is the entrance to Madinah
explanationEn: In contemporary Makkah terminology, al-Hatim denotes the semi-circular wall/area of Hijr Ismail on the northwestern side of the Kaaba that must be circled outside during Tawaf.

questionEn: Did the Prophet ﷺ perform Tawaf on foot or riding a camel during his pilgrimages?
optionsEn: He only walked on his knees
He performed Tawaf on foot during Umrah and also rode his camel during parts of Hajj so crowds could see him clearly and ask questions without crushing him
He forbade riding any mount or wheelchair in Tawaf
He always flew above the Kaaba
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) and Jabir (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ circled the Kaaba on his camel during the Farewell Pilgrimage so people could see him and hear his rulings clearly—providing the basis for wheelchairs today.

questionEn: What is the name of the white/grey marble courtyard area immediately surrounding the Kaaba where Tawaf takes place?
optionsEn: Al-Jamarat
Al-Mataf
Al-Mas'a
Al-Rawdah
explanationEn: Al-Mataf is the open circumambulation plaza around the Kaaba (paved with special heat-reflective Thassos marble to stay cool underfoot), while al-Mas'a is the corridor between Safa and Marwah.

questionEn: Why does the marble floor of Al-Mataf stay remarkably cool even under Makkah's midday summer sun?
optionsEn: It uses special white marble (Thassos marble) that naturally reflects sunlight and heat, aiding pilgrims' comfort during Tawaf
Sunlight never reaches Makkah
Ice blocks are buried beneath every tile daily
Pilgrims are forbidden from stepping there in summer
explanationEn: This engineering care eases the worship of millions circling barefoot throughout hot seasons.

questionEn: When moving toward Safa after Tawaf, two rak'ahs, and Zamzam, what should a pilgrim check on the way?
optionsEn: Remove their Izar and Rida' before Sa'i
Verify they clearly counted all 7 Tawaf circuits, completed the 2 rak'ahs cleanly, and stay hydrated before starting the 7 laps of Sa'i
Shave their head before reaching Safa
Wait until the next day to start Sa'i
explanationEn: Confirming Tawaf is complete before crossing into al-Mas'a ensures smooth continuity in the Sunnah sequence.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim take a short rest or meal break between finishing Tawaf/2 rak'ahs and starting Sa'i if they feel weak or have low blood sugar?
optionsEn: Eating before Sa'i requires a sheep sacrifice
Yes; strict immediate continuity between Tawaf and Sa'i is Sunnah (not a condition of validity), so resting, eating, or using the restroom before Sa'i is completely permissible
No, pausing even five minutes invalidates Umrah
One must wait inside Hijr Ismail for 12 hours
explanationEn: Jurists agree that separating Tawaf and Sa'i briefly for rest, food, medication, or prayer does not invalidate either rite, though performing Sa'i promptly afterward follows the Prophet's ﷺ practice.

questionEn: In which direction relative to the Kaaba is Mount Safa located?
optionsEn: North of Mount Uhud
Inside the city of Madinah
Southeast of the Kaaba, connected to the eastern wing of Al-Masjid al-Haram inside al-Mas'a
West of Jeddah harbor
explanationEn: After exiting the Mataf eastward past the Zamzam side, pilgrims reach Mount Safa at the southern end of the enclosed Mas'a corridor, facing Mount Marwah to the north.

questionEn: What is the approximate distance between Mount Safa and Mount Marwah for a single lap?
optionsEn: About 20 meters total
About 100 yards total for all 7 laps
Roughly 394 to 450 meters (so 7 laps total around 2.8 to 3.15 km)
Exactly 15 kilometers per lap
explanationEn: Knowing the ~3 km total walk helps elderly or diabetic pilgrims pace themselves calmly, hydrate well, and use a wheelchair if needed.

questionEn: What did Urwah ibn al-Zubayr ask Aisha (RA) regarding Surah Al-Baqarah 2:158 ('There is no blame upon whoever performs Sa'i between Safa and Marwah')?
optionsEn: He asked if pilgrims must crawl between them

He wondered if 'no blame' meant Sa'i was optional; Aisha (RA) explained the Ansar once hesitated because of pre-Islamic idols (Isaf and Na'ilah) placed on Safa and Marwah, so Allah revealed there is no sin in doing the obligatory/prescribed rite
He asked whether Safa was taller than Marwah
He asked whether Sa'i replaced Salah
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) famously corrected Urwah's linguistic misunderstanding: had it been optional, Allah would have said 'no blame if you do NOT do Sa'i'; instead, He removed the Ansar's pre-Islamic scruple and affirmed Sa'i among His sacred rites.

questionEn: What is the fiqh status of Sa'i between Safa and Marwah in Umrah across the four Sunni schools?
optionsEn: A Pillar (Rukn) of Umrah according to the Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanbali schools, and an Obligatory act (Wajib) according to the Hanafi school
Required only for men
Forbidden outside Hajj
A mere optional Sunnah
explanationEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ said 'Perform Sa'i, for Allah has prescribed Sa'i upon you' (Musnad Ahmad), the vast majority treat it as an essential Pillar without which Umrah is incomplete.

questionEn: Which hill MUST a pilgrim begin Sa'i on, and which verse did the Prophet ﷺ recite upon approaching it?
optionsEn: Start at either hill randomly
Begin halfway between the two hills
Begin at Mount Safa, reciting 'Innas-Safa wal-Marwata min sha'a'irillah' (2:158) once and saying 'Abda'u bima bada'Allahu bih' (I begin with what Allah began with)
Begin at Mount Marwah reciting Surah al-Kawthar
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated this exact opening of Sa'i: starting with Safa because Allah mentioned Safa first in Qur'an 2:158.

questionEn: How are the seven laps of Sa'i counted accurately?
optionsEn: Only walking northward counts
A round trip from Safa to Marwah and back to Safa counts as 1 lap
Pilgrims end at Safa on lap 7
Safa to Marwah = 1; Marwah to Safa = 2; Safa to Marwah = 3; Marwah to Safa = 4; Safa to Marwah = 5; Marwah to Safa = 6; Safa to Marwah = 7 (ending at Marwah)
explanationEn: Each single one-way crossing counts as one lap—so odd laps (1, 3, 5, 7) go from Safa to Marwah, and even laps (2, 4, 6) go from Marwah to Safa, finishing on Marwah.

questionEn: What common mistake regarding Sa'i lap counting would cause a pilgrim to walk twice the required distance (or miss finishing properly)?
optionsEn: Starting at Safa
Counting Safa to Marwah as 1 lap
Ending at Marwah
Mistakenly counting one full round trip (Safa -> Marwah -> Safa) as 1 lap instead of 2 laps
explanationEn: A round trip equals 2 laps, not 1; seven one-way crossings starting at Safa always conclude on Marwah.

questionEn: If someone mistakenly begins Sa'i at Marwah and walks to Safa, does that first crossing count as Lap 1?
optionsEn: Yes, if they recite Talbiyah
It invalidates their earlier Tawaf
No; because Sa'i must start at Safa, that Marwah-to-Safa walk is ignored, and Lap 1 begins once they reach Safa and walk toward Marwah
Yes, it counts as Lap 1 and they end at Safa
explanationEn: Every crossing before starting at Safa is disregarded, so the seven counted laps run Safa->Marwah (1) through Safa->Marwah (7).

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do upon ascending Mount Safa at the beginning of Sa'i (and similarly at Marwah)?
optionsEn: He prayed two rak'ahs of Salah on top of Safa
He jumped down immediately without pausing

He climbed up enough to face the Kaaba, raised both hands in supplication, recited 'Allahu Akbar' three times, proclaimed 'La ilaha illAllahu wahdahu la sharika lah...' three times, and made long personal dua in between
He touched the stone walls with his forehead
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) described the Prophet ﷺ facing the Qiblah on Safa, declaring Allah's Oneness ('La ilaha illAllahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir, la ilaha illAllahu wahdah, anjaza wa'dah, wa nasara 'abdah, wa hazamal-ahzaba wahdah'), and supplicating deeply three times.

questionEn: Are you required to climb all the way onto the rough exposed bedrock of Safa and Marwah, or does reaching the base/inclined slope suffice?
optionsEn: Reaching the base/beginning of the hill's slope is sufficient (though ascending slightly onto the lower slope if uncrowded is Sunnah), ensuring one covers the full span between the two hills
You must sit on the rocks for 15 minutes
You must climb to the highest rocky pinnacle regardless of crowds
Stopping 50 meters before the hill suffices
explanationEn: To fulfill 'between Safa and Marwah', one must reach the actual edge/slope of each hill (not turn around early before the marble markers), while climbing high is unnecessary when crowded.

questionEn: What do the bright green fluorescent lights along the ceiling/pillars of the Mas'a corridor mark?
optionsEn: The exit door to Jeddah
The valley floor (Batn al-Mas'a / al-Milayn al-Akhdarayn) where Hajar (AS) ran quickly—so able-bodied men jog briskly between the green lights and return to normal walking afterward
A zone where women must sprint
The exact midpoint where Sa'i stops
explanationEn: In Jabir's (RA) Hadith, the Prophet ﷺ walked calmly on Safa and Marwah and ran briskly in the low valley floor between the two green markers; women always walk calmly through the green zone.

questionEn: What supplication is authentically reported from Companions such as Ibn Mas'ud (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) while jogging/walking in the Mas'a?
optionsEn: 'Rabbighfir warham, innaka antal-a'azzul-akram' (My Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the Most Mighty, the Most Generous)
'Allahu Akbar' 100 times without stopping
'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' only
Surah Al-Kahf from start to finish
explanationEn: Reported in Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Bayhaqi from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Umar (RA), this brief, deeply moving dua is often recited during Sa'i alongside any personal prayers.

questionEn: Is having Wudu (ritual purity) an obligatory condition for the validity of Sa'i between Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: Yes, breaking Wudu in Sa'i nullifies the entire Umrah
Sa'i requires Ghusl before every lap
Yes, only men must keep Wudu in Sa'i
No; Wudu is Sunnah/recommended during Sa'i, NOT a condition—so if a woman's menstruation begins after completing Tawaf, or someone loses Wudu during Sa'i, their Sa'i remains completely valid
explanationEn: All four schools agree Wudu is not a prerequisite for Sa'i (the Prophet ﷺ only barred Aisha RA from Tawaf around the House during menstruation, not from Safa-Marwah once Tawaf is done); having Wudu remains praiseworthy.

questionEn: Does a male pilgrim keep his right shoulder uncovered (Idtiba') during Sa'i, or cover both shoulders?
optionsEn: He must keep Idtiba' until Halq
He must uncover both shoulders during Sa'i
He uncovers his left shoulder during Sa'i
He covers both shoulders after Tawaf before praying the two rak'ahs and keeps both shoulders covered during Sa'i
explanationEn: Idtiba' is specifically prescribed for Umrah Tawaf alone; covering both shoulders from the post-Tawaf prayer onward is the established Sunnah.

questionEn: On the seventh and final lap of Sa'i, arriving at Mount Marwah, should a pilgrim stand making dua facing the Kaaba before exiting to shave/trim?
optionsEn: Making dua at Marwah after lap 7 (just as on previous turns, or concluding humbly in praise) is Sunnah before heading out for Halq or Taqsir (some scholars hold dua at the end of lap 7 is omitted since no lap follows, while making general dua of gratitude is always welcome)
One must pray two rak'ahs on Mount Marwah
One must return to Safa for an 8th lap
One must sleep on Marwah for one hour
explanationEn: Scholars differ gently on whether the triple dhikr/dua is repeated at the very end of lap 7 on Marwah; pausing briefly in gratitude and dua to conclude Sa'i is wholesome before moving to Halq/Taqsir.

questionEn: Are the upper floors and basement/mezzanine levels of the expanded Mas'a corridor completely valid for Sa'i?
optionsEn: Basement Sa'i requires 14 laps
Upper floors count only for wheelchairs
Yes; multi-level Sa'i corridors built directly above the original path between Safa and Marwah are fully valid
No, only the ground dirt floor counts
explanationEn: Just like upper floors of the Mataf, the airspace directly between Mount Safa and Mount Marwah holds the same legal ruling, easing movement for millions.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim rest on the benches along the Mas'a or sip Zamzam water mid-Sa'i if tired?
optionsEn: Sitting requires restarting from lap 1
Only drinking soda is permitted, not Zamzam
No, sitting during Sa'i voids all previous laps
Yes; taking short rests, sitting for a few minutes, or drinking Zamzam during Sa'i is completely permissible
explanationEn: Continuity (muwalat) in Sa'i is even more flexible than in Tawaf; pausing to catch one's breath, drink water, or pray congregational Salah does not harm Sa'i.

questionEn: After finishing the 7th lap of Sa'i at Marwah, what final rite must be performed to complete Umrah and exit Ihram?
optionsEn: Washing the Izar in Zamzam
Halq (shaving the entire head) or Taqsir (trimming hair evenly across the head) for men, and Taqsir (trimming a fingertip's length) for women
Standing at Arafah
Circling the Kaaba three more times
explanationEn: Halq or Taqsir marks the completion of Umrah and brings full Tahallul, lifting all Ihram restrictions.

questionEn: Which act did the Prophet ﷺ pray three times for mercy and forgiveness upon, compared to once for the other?
optionsEn: Three times for those who run in Sa'i and once for walkers
He prayed three times: 'O Allah, have mercy on those who shave their heads (al-muhalliqin)' and once for 'those who trim their hair (al-muqassirin)'
Three times for those who wear perfume and once for those who fast
Three times for those who visit Ta'if
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) narrated this authentic Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, showing Halq carries higher virtue for men (especially when not performing Hajj Tamattu' shortly afterward).

questionEn: When is Taqsir (trimming) specifically recommended for men over Halq (shaving completely)?
optionsEn: When performing Umrah al-Tamattu' only a few days before Hajj, so hair remains to shave during Hajj on 10 Dhul-Hijjah
Only for barbers
Never—shaving twice in three days is mandatory
Only during winter months
explanationEn: During the Farewell Pilgrimage, Companions doing Tamattu' trimmed their hair after Umrah (as advised by the Prophet ﷺ) so they could shave cleanly on Yawm al-Nahr after Hajj.

questionEn: What common mistake do some male pilgrims commit when performing Taqsir after Umrah?
optionsEn: Shaving the entire head cleanly
Clipping only a few tiny snips from one small patch of hair instead of trimming evenly across the entire head
Trimming evenly across the whole head with clippers or scissors
Using a barber outside Marwah
explanationEn: Jurists agree that Taqsir must shorten hair generally over the head (all four quarters / whole scalp)—merely snipping 3–4 random hairs from the front does not suffice according to major schools.

questionEn: How should a woman perform Taqsir cleanly and modestly after Sa'i?
optionsEn: Shave her head completely bald at a street barber
Pull out three hairs by hand
Cut off half her hair in public outside Marwah
Gather her hair (or braids/sections evenly) and trim roughly a fingertip's length (~1.5–2 cm) from the ends in private or at the hotel, never in front of non-mahram men
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated: 'Shaving is not prescribed for women; rather, women trim (their hair).' Gathering the ends and cutting a fingertip's length privately at the hotel preserves both validity and modesty.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1985; Fatawa al-Lajnah al-Da'imah

questionEn: Does a pilgrim remain in Ihram after finishing Sa'i until they actually perform Halq or Taqsir?
optionsEn: No, Ihram ends automatically at the exit door of Marwah
Ihram ends as soon as one buys a razor
Men exit Ihram at Marwah while women exit at Safa
Yes; finishing Sa'i alone does NOT end Ihram—all Ihram restrictions remain binding until Halq or Taqsir is completed
explanationEn: Putting on regular stitched clothes or applying perfume right after Sa'i BEFORE shaving/trimming is a common mistake; Tahallul occurs only upon Halq or Taqsir.

questionEn: If a pilgrim forgets to perform Halq or Taqsir after Sa'i, puts on regular clothes, and remembers back at the hotel (or even after flying home), what must they do?
optionsEn: Fast sixty days
Immediately remove stitched clothes (if not yet shaved/trimmed), perform Halq or Taqsir right away wherever they are—their Umrah becomes complete (with no sin for genuine forgetfulness)
Repeat Tawaf seven times
Fly all the way back to Jeddah before cutting hair
explanationEn: Unlike Hajj Hady, Halq/Taqsir is valid anywhere if forgotten until leaving Makkah (though doing it in Makkah is best); if done in ignorance/forgetfulness, most jurists impose no penalty, and once cut, Tahallul is complete.

questionEn: What should a completely bald man (having no hair on his scalp) do at the end of Umrah?
optionsEn: Shave his eyebrows instead
Skip Umrah altogether
Shave his beard completely
Pass a clean razor lightly over his bald scalp symbolically (or nothing is obligated upon him if completely smooth, per scholarly views—passing the blade covers both opinions safely)
explanationEn: Most scholars recommend passing the razor over the bald head in conformity with the symbolic rite (while Shafi'is note nothing is due if zero hair exists; passing the razor safely satisfies all).

questionEn: Can a pilgrim who has not yet exited Ihram (not yet trimmed their own hair) trim or shave another pilgrim's hair after Sa'i?
optionsEn: No, touching scissors invalidates Umrah
Only if they pay a Dam
Yes; cutting another pilgrim's hair at the moment of Tahallul does not violate one's own Ihram (the prohibition is removing one's own hair), though trimming oneself first is also very easy
Only barbers born in Makkah may cut hair
explanationEn: Jurists explain that trimming another pilgrim's hair when that person has reached Tahallul is permissible and helpful (for instance, a husband trimming his wife's hair ends after Sa'i before shaving his own head).

questionEn: What hygiene caution should male pilgrims observe at barber shops outside Mount Marwah?
optionsEn: Never use electric clippers
Ensure the barber uses a brand-new, sealed single-use blade (or sanitized clippers) to prevent bloodborne infections
Shave only the left half of the head
Insist on reusing the previous customer's blade
explanationEn: Health and safety are Islamic priorities; insisting on fresh disposable blades protects every pilgrim.

questionEn: What is the scholarly ruling on performing a Farewell Tawaf (Tawaf al-Wada') before leaving Makkah after completing Umrah?
optionsEn: Strictly forbidden after Umrah
Required even when walking from the Kaaba to the hotel
Requires re-entering Ihram at Masjid Aisha

Recommended (Mustahabb) according to the majority (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i) when departing Makkah after an Umrah stay, and Wajib according to some Hanbalis/scholars (like Ibn Baz) if staying beyond Umrah before departure—while if one leaves Makkah immediately after finishing Umrah, the Umrah Tawaf itself suffices
explanationEn: Performing a final Farewell Tawaf in regular clothes just before departing Makkah is a rewarding Sunnah (and fulfills the cautious Wajib view if one stayed days in Makkah afterward), making one's last moments at the Sacred House.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1755; Al-Mughni; Fatawa Ibn Baz

questionEn: If a pilgrim's bus to Madinah or Jeddah leaves immediately after they finish Sa'i and Halq/Taqsir, do they need an additional Farewell Tawaf?
optionsEn: No; their Umrah Tawaf/Sa'i serves as their farewell act if departing right away without lingering
Yes, they must miss their flight to do another Tawaf
They must repeat Sa'i before leaving
They must pay a Dam
explanationEn: Even scholars who favor Tawaf al-Wada' after Umrah agree it is only when one remains in Makkah afterward; leaving immediately after completing Umrah requires nothing further.

questionEn: Does a menstruating woman who already completed her Umrah Tawaf and Sa'i while pure need to perform a Farewell Tawaf before departing Makkah?
optionsEn: She must pay a camel
Yes, she must do Tawaf during menstruation
Yes, she must wait two weeks in Makkah
No; the Prophet ﷺ explicitly exempted menstruating women from Tawaf al-Wada'
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that people were ordered to make their last covenant at the House, except that the Prophet ﷺ granted a clear concession (rukhshah) to menstruating women.

questionEn: Why did Safiyyah bint Huyayy (RA) weep or worry during the Farewell Hajj, and how did the Prophet's ﷺ response clarify menstruation rulings?
optionsEn: When Safiyyah (RA) began menstruating after Tawaf al-Ifadah, the Prophet ﷺ asked 'Is she going to delay us?' On learning she had already done Tawaf al-Ifadah, he ﷺ said 'Then let her depart'—showing Farewell Tawaf is waived for menstruating women
He canceled her pilgrimage
He ordered her to stay in Makkah for a month
He told her to repeat Sa'i ten times
explanationEn: This Hadith proves both that a woman cannot depart before her obligatory Tawaf (if not done) and that Tawaf al-Wada' is completely waived once menstruation occurs afterward.

questionEn: What is the etiquette when walking out of Al-Masjid al-Haram after completing Umrah or Farewell Tawaf?
optionsEn: Clap hands at the exit gate
Take a handful of marble pebbles as a souvenir
Walk backward all the way down the street staring at the Kaaba
Walk forward normally with the left foot first reciting the mosque-exit dua ('Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik'), NOT walking backward facing the Kaaba
explanationEn: Walking backward out of the Haram is a cultural innovation without basis in the Sunnah and causes tripping injuries; exiting forward peacefully with dua in the heart is the Prophetic way.

questionEn: When Quraysh rebuilt the Kaaba before Prophethood and disputed which clan would lift Al-Hajar al-Aswad into place, how did young Muhammad ﷺ resolve the crisis?
optionsEn: He drew arrows to pick one warrior
He chose Banu Hashim alone to carry it
He told them to leave the stone on the ground for ten years
He placed the Black Stone on a cloak, had leaders of every tribe hold an edge to lift it together, and then placed it into the corner with his own blessed hands
explanationEn: This famous incident at age 35 prevented bloodshed among Quraysh clans and showcased the future Prophet's ﷺ unmatched wisdom, trustworthiness (al-Amin), and care for the Sacred House.

questionEn: Why did Quraysh leave the semi-circular area of Hijr Ismail outside the roofed cube when rebuilding the Kaaba?
optionsEn: They resolved to build the Kaaba solely from pure, lawful (halal) wealth and ran short of lawful funds to cover the full Abrahamic foundation
They forgot the original dimensions
A flood washed away the stones overnight
They wanted a courtyard for horses
explanationEn: Even pre-Islamic Quraysh refused to mix usury or ill-gotten money into Allah's House; lacking enough halal funds, they shortened the northern side and marked the remainder with a low curved wall (Hijr Ismail).

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ refrain from demolishing the Kaaba and rebuilding it over Hijr Ismail with two ground-level doors?
optionsEn: Out of wisdom and mercy toward the newly Muslim Quraysh, fearing their hearts might feel alienated by altering the House so soon after the Conquest
Because Hijr Ismail was outside the Haram
Because Quraysh forbade him
Because he lacked builders in Makkah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Aisha (RA): 'Were it not that your people are newly out of disbelief, I would have demolished the Kaaba, built it on the foundations of Ibrahim, and made two ground doors for entry and exit.'

questionEn: Who temporarily rebuilt the Kaaba upon the original Abrahamic foundations including Hijr Ismail based on Aisha's (RA) narration before al-Hajjaj later restored Quraysh's structure?
optionsEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)
Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (RA)
Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA)
explanationEn: Hearing the Prophet's ﷺ wish from his aunt Aisha (RA), Ibn al-Zubayr (RA) restored the Kaaba over Hijr Ismail with two doors; after his martyrdom, al-Hajjaj returned it to Quraysh's dimensions, and later Abbasid caliphs left it so it would not become a plaything of rulers.

questionEn: Why is the single door of the Kaaba elevated above ground level rather than flush with the Mataf floor?
optionsEn: To match Roman palaces
To keep Zamzam floods out permanently
Because iron hinges were too long
Quraysh elevated the door so they could control who entered—whereas the Prophet ﷺ noted Ibrahim's (AS) House originally had two ground-level doors for entry and exit
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) asked why the door was raised; the Prophet ﷺ explained Quraysh raised it to admit whom they wished and bar whom they wished.

questionEn: Which direction does the main facade containing the Door of the Kaaba face?
optionsEn: Northeast (roughly toward Maqam Ibrahim and Zamzam)
Due West toward the Red Sea
Due South toward Yemen
Due North toward Syria
explanationEn: The northeastern wall houses the Door of the Kaaba, the Black Stone on its eastern/southeastern corner, and al-Multazam right between them.
reference: Geography of the Kaaba; Akhbar Makkah

questionEn: What are the names of the four corners of the Kaaba in counter-clockwise Tawaf order starting from the Black Stone?
optionsEn: Al-Hajar al-Aswad (Eastern), Al-Rukn al-Iraqi (Northern), Al-Rukn al-Shami (Western), and Al-Rukn al-Yamani (Southern)
Makki, Madani, Misri, and Yemeni
Safa, Marwah, Mina, and Arafah
Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, and Tabuk
explanationEn: Walking counter-clockwise around the Kaaba passes the Black Stone corner, then the Iraqi corner (toward Iraq), then around Hijr Ismail past the Shami corner (toward Sham/Levant), then the Yemeni corner (toward Yemen), and back to the Black Stone.

questionEn: In what Hijri year did Umrat al-Hudaybiyyah—the Prophet's ﷺ first post-Hijrah Umrah expedition—take place?
optionsEn: 2 AH (Ramadan)
6 AH (Dhul-Qa'dah)
4 AH (Shawwal)
9 AH (Muharram)
explanationEn: In Dhul-Qa'dah 6 AH, the Prophet ﷺ set out with around 1,400–1,500 unarmed Companions wearing Ihram and driving sacrificial camels for Umrah, only to be halted at al-Hudaybiyyah.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ bring sacrificial camels (Hady) along on the Hudaybiyyah Umrah journey even though Hady is usually associated with Hajj?
optionsEn: To sell them in Jeddah markets
Because Hady is obligatory for every ordinary Umrah
Because Muslims could not find sheep in Madinah
To demonstrate unmistakably to Quraysh and Arab tribes that he came strictly in peace for worship (Umrah), not for war, and to offer sacrifice upon arriving
explanationEn: Garlanding camels (taqlid) and marking them (ish'ar) was a universally recognized Arabian sign of peaceful pilgrimage; though Hady is optional (not obligatory) for regular standalone Umrah, it served both worship and clear peaceful intent.

questionEn: Even though the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were blocked at al-Hudaybiyyah before reaching the Kaaba, why do scholars still count Hudaybiyyah among his four Umrahs?
optionsEn: Because he entered full Ihram for Umrah at Dhul-Hulayfah and received Allah's reward for sincere intent and obedience through Ihsar, though its physical completion occurred the next year in Umrat al-Qada'
Because Hudaybiyyah lies inside the Mataf
Because he prayed toward Jerusalem instead
Because he secretly performed Tawaf at night
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas and Anas (RA) listed four Umrahs because he assumed Ihram four times for Umrah; Ibn al-Qayyim and al-Nawawi explain Hudaybiyyah was counted due to his Ihram and reward despite obstruction.

questionEn: What solemn pledge did the Companions give the Prophet ﷺ beneath a tree at al-Hudaybiyyah when rumors spread that Uthman ibn Affan (RA) had been killed?
optionsEn: The First Pledge of Aqabah
Bay'at al-Ridwan (the Pledge of Allah's Good Pleasure), pledging steadfastness and not to flee
The Treaty of Medina
The Pact of al-Fudul
explanationEn: Allah praised those believers in Surah Al-Fath (48:18): 'Certainly Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree' and sent tranquility down upon them.

questionEn: During the Hudaybiyyah treaty negotiations, what did Quraysh envoy Suhayl ibn Amr object to in the opening wording, prompting the Prophet's ﷺ remarkable forbearance?
optionsEn: He objected to writing 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim' and 'Muhammad, Messenger of Allah', asking instead for 'Bismika Allahumma' and 'Muhammad ibn Abdullah'—which the Prophet ﷺ gently accepted for peace
He refused to sign unless Makkah was burned
He insisted on writing the treaty in Greek
He objected to mentioning the Kaaba
explanationEn: By showing extraordinary patience and vision during those Umrah negotiations, the Prophet ﷺ secured a ten-year truce that opened Arabia to Islam peacefully.

questionEn: Which Muslim poet walked ahead of the Prophet ﷺ reciting stirring poetry upon entering Makkah for Umrat al-Qada' (7 AH)?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA)
Labid ibn Rabi'ah
Imru' al-Qays
Abu Sufyan ibn Harb
explanationEn: When Umar (RA) moved to hush Ibn Rawahah (RA) inside the Haram, the Prophet ﷺ told Umar: 'Leave him, O Umar! For his words are sharper against them than arrows.'

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers did the Prophet ﷺ marry during or upon concluding Umrat al-Qada' (7 AH) in Sarif (outside Makkah)?
optionsEn: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA)
Maymunah bint al-Harith (RA)
Hafsah bint Umar (RA)
Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA)
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ married Maymunah (RA) in 7 AH (while reports differ slightly on whether the contract occurred before or after exiting Ihram at Sarif—with Abu Rafi' and Maymunah herself confirming he was halal/out of Ihram, harmonizing with Uthman's Hadith barring marriage in Ihram).

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ leave Makkah promptly after three days during Umrat al-Qada' even when he requested to host his wedding feast there?
optionsEn: Because food ran out in Makkah
To honor the exact three-day limit stipulated in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah without breaking his word
Because an earthquake struck Mount Safa
Because Madinah was under attack
explanationEn: When Quraysh insisted on the three-day treaty deadline, the Prophet ﷺ immediately complied and moved out to Sarif, exemplifying Muslim fidelity to covenants.

questionEn: Where was al-Ji'ranah located, from which the Prophet ﷺ entered Ihram for his third Umrah in 8 AH?
optionsEn: On the Red Sea coast near Jeddah
On the summit of Mount Arafah
Inside the northern gate of Madinah
A watering valley outside the northeastern Haram limits between Makkah and Ta'if
explanationEn: Al-Ji'ranah lies roughly 24 km northeast of Masjid al-Haram outside the Haram boundary; today Masjid al-Ji'ranah marks that historic place of Ihram.

questionEn: At what time of day did the Prophet ﷺ depart al-Ji'ranah to perform his third Umrah, and why?
optionsEn: At high noon with trumpets
At night, entering Makkah calmly, performing Tawaf and Sa'i, and returning to his camp in al-Ji'ranah before morning so he remained like one who spent the night there
During a solar eclipse
Only on Friday afternoon
explanationEn: Narrations in Abu Dawud and Ahmad mention he entered Ihram from al-Ji'ranah by night, completed his Umrah peacefully, and returned before dawn—showing Umrah at night is authentic Sunnah.

questionEn: Which of the Prophet's ﷺ four Umrahs was performed alongside Hajj as Hajj al-Qiran?
optionsEn: His fourth Umrah during the Farewell Pilgrimage (10 AH)
Umrat al-Ji'ranah (8 AH)
Umrat al-Qada' (7 AH)
Umrat al-Hudaybiyyah (6 AH)
explanationEn: In 10 AH, the Prophet ﷺ combined Hajj and Umrah in Qiran (entering Ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah saying 'Labbayk Allahumma 'Umratan fi Hajjah'), completing both under one continuous Ihram.

questionEn: Who originally rediscovered and excavated the buried Well of Zamzam centuries after Jurhum had concealed it, shortly before the Prophet's ﷺ birth?
optionsEn: Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, the grandfather of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
Abu Talib
Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib
Waraqah ibn Nawfal
explanationEn: Guided in repeated dreams, Abd al-Muttalib dug between the two idols Isaf and Na'ilah and restored Zamzam water to serve pilgrims (al-Siqayah), a noble office later entrusted to al-Abbas (RA).

questionEn: Which Companion's family was confirmed by the Prophet ﷺ to continue serving pilgrims with Zamzam water (Siqayah) at the Conquest of Makkah?
optionsEn: Abu Lahab's sons
Umayyah ibn Khalaf
Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA), the Prophet's ﷺ uncle
Suhayl ibn Amr
explanationEn: On the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ abolished all pre-Islamic claims except the custodianship of the Kaaba (Sidanah, to Banu Shaybah) and supplying Zamzam water (Siqayah, to al-Abbas RA).

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ drank Zamzam water from the leather bucket drawn by al-Abbas's (RA) sons during the Farewell Pilgrimage, what beautiful humility did he show?
optionsEn: He told them: 'Were it not that people would overwhelm you (turning Siqayah into a rushed rite), I would pull the water rope up with you myself,' and drank standing up
He demanded a golden cup
He ordered the well sealed
He forbade anyone else from drinking Zamzam
explanationEn: This touching narration in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim shows both the Prophet's ﷺ eagerness to serve pilgrims and his constant foresight to prevent crowding and hardship for future generations.

questionEn: What happened to the idols around the Kaaba when the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah in 8 AH?
optionsEn: He moved them to Madinah
He pointed at the 360 idols around the Kaaba with his staff reciting Qur'an 17:81 ('Truth has come and falsehood has vanished') and they collapsed onto their faces
He ignored them during Tawaf
He kept three small idols inside Hijr Ismail
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ struck/pointed at the idols reciting 'Ja'al-haqqu wa zahaqal-batil', purifying the Kaaba forever for pure worship of Allah alone.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in his Conquest of Makkah address regarding the timeless sanctity of Makkah?
optionsEn: 'Only residents of Madinah must honor Makkah'
'Makkah is sacred only during Dhul-Hijjah'
'Allah made Makkah sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth; it is sacred by Allah's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection'
'Makkah became sacred only after 8 AH'
explanationEn: This foundational declaration in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim establishes Makkah's perpetual inviolability since Creation—not even one hour of combat was ever permitted except a brief exception on Conquest morning.

questionEn: Who was the first person to drape a full cloth covering (Kiswah) over the Kaaba according to early historical accounts referenced by scholars?
optionsEn: Abraha of Abyssinia
Heraclius of Byzantium
Pharaoh of Egypt
Tubba' (As'ad al-Himyari), king of Yemen, before Islam, followed by Quraysh and then the Prophet ﷺ and Caliphs in Islam
explanationEn: Classical historians such as al-Azraqi and Ibn Hisham report Tubba' clothed the Kaaba, later maintained by Quraysh and honored in Islam by the Prophet ﷺ and Umar (RA).
reference: Akhbar Makkah by al-Azraqi; Sahih al-Bukhari 1592

questionEn: What is the meaning of 'Al-Haram' vs 'Al-Masjid al-Haram'?
optionsEn: Both terms mean only the two-meter space around Zamzam
Al-Haram refers to Jeddah
Al-Masjid al-Haram includes Madinah and Ta'if
Al-Masjid al-Haram is the Grand Mosque housing the Kaaba, whereas Al-Haram is the entire sacred territory surrounding Makkah marked by boundary pillars (from Tan'im to Arafat border)
explanationEn: Understanding this distinction clarifies why cutting native plants or hunting is barred throughout the entire Haram territory, while Wudu/mosque etiquette applies specifically inside Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: Approximately how far is Masjid al-Tan'im (Masjid Aisha) from the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Directly adjacent to Mount Marwah
About 7–8 kilometers northwest, just outside the Sacred Haram boundary
About 450 kilometers away near Madinah
About 90 kilometers east near Ta'if
explanationEn: Al-Tan'im is the closest border point of al-Hil outside Makkah's Haram limits, making it the primary site for Makkah residents (or Aisha RA historically) to enter Ihram for Umrah.

questionEn: What is the historical significance of 'Al-Bayt al-Atiq' (the Ancient House), a Qur'anic title for the Kaaba mentioned in Surah Al-Hajj (22:29)?
optionsEn: It refers to a palace in Syria
Scholars explain it means the oldest house of worship built on earth for mankind (Surah 3:96) and the House Allah freed/protected from tyrants
It means a house abandoned forever
It means a house built after the Hijrah
explanationEn: Abu Dharr (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ which mosque was built first on earth; he ﷺ answered 'Al-Masjid al-Haram' (followed 40 years later by Al-Masjid al-Aqsa).

questionEn: According to Abu Dharr's (RA) Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, how many years separated the founding of Al-Masjid al-Haram and Al-Masjid al-Aqsa?
optionsEn: Forty years
One thousand years
Four hundred years
Five years
explanationEn: This authentic narration affirms the ancient roots of Al-Masjid al-Haram as humanity's earliest appointed sanctuary of monotheistic worship.

questionEn: Which two tribes settled in the Makkah valley shortly after Zamzam appeared, enabling Isma'il (AS) to grow up among them and marry from them?
optionsEn: Tribe of Ghassan
Tribe of Quraysh initially
Tribe of Thamud
Tribe of Jurhum (from Yemen)
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari 3364 recounts how a passing Jurhum caravan saw birds circling above the valley, discovered Hajar and Isma'il (AS) beside Zamzam, and settled there with Hajar's permission.

questionEn: What did Hajar (AS) say to the Jurhum travelers when they asked to settle near the spring of Zamzam?
optionsEn: 'Yes, you may settle here, but you have no ownership rights over the water'
'You may own the well permanently'
'No, leave the valley immediately'
'Give me half your camels first'
explanationEn: Hajar (AS) welcomed righteous neighbors so Isma'il (AS) would not grow up lonely, while wisely safeguarding the stewardship of Zamzam.

questionEn: What is 'Bab al-Salam' (Gate of Peace) historically famous for in Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: It leads exclusively to Mina
Its proximity to the ancient Bab Bani Shaybah entrance on the eastern/northeastern side near Safa, traditionally used by arriving pilgrims entering toward the Black Stone
It is the entrance to Madinah's market
It is a gate inside Jeddah airport
explanationEn: While pilgrims today may enter through any open gate directed by Haram attendants, Bab al-Salam remains a cherished historic landmark beside the Mas'a.

questionEn: What was 'Bab al-Umrah' in the historical western wing of Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: A gate at Qarn al-Manazil
The entrance to Cave Hira
One of the historic gates of Al-Masjid al-Haram facing the western/Tan'im road approach traditionally used by Umrah pilgrims entering from al-Tan'im
A gate inside Masjid Quba
explanationEn: Bab al-Umrah served for centuries as a prominent western entry gate for pilgrims arriving via the al-Tan'im road.

questionEn: What happened to the original placement of Maqam Ibrahim during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)?
optionsEn: He buried it underground permanently
Umar (RA) threw it into the sea
He placed it inside Mount Marwah

Originally touching the Kaaba wall in early times (or moved back slightly), Umar (RA) placed it back to its current position away from the wall so Tawaf walkers and those praying two rak'ahs would not obstruct one another
explanationEn: Ibn Hajar notes in Fath al-Bari that during the Prophet's ﷺ time or flood events it shifted, and Umar (RA) wisely fixed it further back from the Kaaba wall to preserve clear Mataf flow—a layout preserved ever since.

questionEn: In which Sahih collection is the long, detailed Hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) describing the Prophet's ﷺ complete pilgrimage sequence recorded?
optionsEn: Shama'il al-Tirmidhi only
Sahih Muslim (Hadith 1218)
Muwatta Imam Malik only
Al-Adab al-Mufrad only
explanationEn: Jabir's (RA) detailed narration in Sahih Muslim 1218 is considered the primary step-by-step eyewitness reference for Tawaf, Maqam Ibrahim, Zamzam, and Sa'i between Safa and Marwah.

questionEn: Which Sahabi preserved detailed reports of the Prophet's ﷺ Umrahs and stood on Safa explaining 'Wattakhidhu min maqami Ibrahima musalla'?
optionsEn: Abu Lahab
Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA)
Musaylamah
Umayyah ibn Khalaf
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) was one of the foremost narrators of the Prophet's ﷺ pilgrimage rituals, teaching later generations like Imam al-Baqir every detail of Tawaf and Sa'i.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Umrah on behalf of someone who passed away WITHOUT ever having performed their own obligatory Umrah (or Hajj) despite having left behind wealth?
optionsEn: Scholars holding Umrah/Hajj obligatory rule that an executor should arrange Badal pilgrimage from the deceased's estate (before inheritance distribution) just as a debt to Allah
The estate must be donated to non-relatives first
Only neighbors may pay for it after 20 years
Debts to Allah are ignored completely
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told the woman whose mother died without fulfilling her vow/pilgrimage: 'A debt to Allah has even more right to be fulfilled.'

questionEn: Can a woman perform Badal Umrah on behalf of a deceased man (such as her father), or a man perform Badal Umrah on behalf of a deceased woman (such as his mother)?
optionsEn: Only spouses may represent each other
Only brothers may represent brothers
No, men may only represent men and women only represent women
Yes; cross-gender proxy pilgrimage is completely valid by consensus—proven by the Khath'amiyyah woman asking about performing pilgrimage for her elderly father and the Prophet ﷺ permitting it
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1513, a woman asked about performing pilgrimage for her aged father and the Prophet ﷺ approved it, establishing that gender need not match between proxy and beneficiary.

questionEn: Is it permissible for someone to charge an exorbitant commercial profit to perform Badal Umrah on someone else's behalf, or what is the right intention?
optionsEn: Covering legitimate travel expenses and modest compensation is allowed by many scholars, while doing it sincerely out of devotion and love for Allah (not treating worship merely as a commercial trade) is strongly emphasized
Doing ten Badal Umrahs in one day using one Tawaf is valid
Proxies do not need to enter Ihram at Miqat
Selling Badal Umrah like auction tickets for profit is praised
explanationEn: Jurists warn against exploiting Badal Umrah as a profit-making business or delegating to untrustworthy persons; selecting a pious, knowledgeable Muslim who sincerely prays for the deceased is best.

questionEn: If a person intentionally wears stitched clothing, perfume, or clips nails while in Ihram WITHOUT a valid excuse, what must they do?
optionsEn: Skip Sa'i
Stop the violation immediately, repent sincerely to Allah, and offer Fidyah al-Adha (fast 3 days, feed 6 poor people, or sacrifice a sheep)
Continue breaking Ihram rules until Jeddah
Cancel their Umrah and leave Makkah
explanationEn: Deliberate violation without excuse carries sin requiring Tawbah plus Fidyah al-Adha (choice of fasting 3 days, feeding 6 needy, or slaughtering a sheep).

questionEn: What is the penalty (Jaza' al-Sayd) prescribed in Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:95) if a pilgrim in Ihram intentionally kills a wild land game animal?
optionsEn: Praying two rak'ahs behind Safa
Offering an equivalent domestic livestock animal (mithl) judged by two upright persons, OR feeding the poor with its food equivalent, OR fasting equivalent days
Shaving half the head
Jumping over Zamzam
explanationEn: Qur'an 5:95 details three proportional remedies—an equivalent livestock sacrifice brought to the Kaaba, feeding the needy an equivalent value, or fasting one day per mudd of food.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim in Ihram kills a pigeon inside the Haram of Makkah?
optionsEn: Prohibited both because of Ihram and the Haram's sanctuary; classical Companions such as Umar and Uthman (RA) judged the penalty for a Haram pigeon to be one sheep
Requires only washing hands
Permitted for children
Permitted if the pigeon landed near the hotel
explanationEn: Haram pigeons are protected wildlife inside the Sacred Sanctuary; Umar, Uthman, and Ibn Abbas (RA) ruled that killing one deliberately incurs a sheep sacrifice for the poor of the Haram.

questionEn: In comparative fiqh, how does the Hanafi school view performing Umrah Tawaf with minor impurity (no Wudu) compared to the Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanbali schools?
optionsEn: Hanafis treat Wudu as Wajib for Tawaf (so Tawaf without Wudu counts legally but requires a Dam/sheep unless repeated with Wudu), whereas the majority treat Wudu as a condition without which Tawaf itself is invalid
Shafi'is require Ghusl before every single circuit
Hanafis say Tawaf needs no Wudu and no Dam
All four schools hold Wudu is banned in Tawaf
explanationEn: Knowing this scholarly distinction helps pilgrims always keep Wudu carefully for Tawaf—satisfying every school without question or penalty.

questionEn: What is the Hanafi ruling if someone performs Tawaf while in a state of major ritual impurity (Janabah or menstruation), versus the majority view?
optionsEn: It converts Umrah into Hajj
It is encouraged in all schools
The majority rule such a Tawaf invalid (must be repeated after Ghusl), while Hanafis hold it severely sinful and requiring a Badana (camel/cow) unless repeated in purity
It requires only one date in charity
explanationEn: Both camps strongly forbid entering the mosque or performing Tawaf in major impurity/menstruation, underscoring why a menstruating woman waits until Ghusl before entering for Tawaf.

questionEn: If a woman's return flight is imminent and she is still menstruating without any possibility of delaying her flight or returning later to Makkah, what exceptional ruling did Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim discuss?
optionsEn: She must stay unmarried in Jeddah airport forever
She may skip Tawaf altogether and still finish Umrah
She must perform Tawaf in Madinah instead

In extreme unavoidable necessity (darurah) where waiting or returning is genuinely impossible, Ibn Taymiyyah permitted her to wash, bind securely with sanitary pads, perform Tawaf and Sa'i (per Hanafi validity + lifting Dam under extreme necessity) rather than remaining indefinitely in Ihram—while stressing every effort must first be made to wait or delay travel
explanationEn: First priority is ALWAYS waiting until pure (or using doctor-approved delay pills beforehand or rescheduling travel); only in true, inescapable departure emergency do modern scholars cite Ibn Taymiyyah's necessity concession (for Hajj Tawaf al-Ifadah especially, and discussed by contemporary fatwa bodies for trapped Umrah travelers).
reference: Majmu' Fatawa Ibn Taymiyyah; I'lam al-Muwaqqi'in; Fatawa Contemporary Councils

questionEn: What happens if a woman experiences non-menstrual spotting or chronic irregular bleeding (Istihadah) during Umrah?
optionsEn: She must skip Sa'i
She must wait forty days before Tawaf
She cannot enter Ihram
Istihadah does NOT bar her from Tawaf or prayer; she washes cleanly, uses fresh sanitary protection, makes fresh Wudu for each prayer/Tawaf, and performs Umrah normally
explanationEn: Unlike menstruation (hayd) or postpartum bleeding (nifas), istihadah allows all acts of worship—prayer, Tawaf, and Sa'i—with fresh Wudu and proper protection.

questionEn: If a woman in Ihram finishes Tawaf and then her period begins right before or during Sa'i, how should she proceed?
optionsEn: She must repeat Tawaf after menstruation
