She continues and completes Sa'i between Safa and Marwah normally (since Wudu/purity from hayd is NOT a condition for Sa'i, and the Mas'a is not treated identically to the Kaaba Mataf by most jurists), then trims her hair at Marwah/hotel to exit Ihram
She cannot trim her hair until next month
She must wait in Makkah until pure before Sa'i
explanationEn: Since she already completed the only purity-conditioned rite (Tawaf) before menstruation began, she finishes Sa'i and Taqsir normally and completes a completely valid Umrah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1650; Fatawa Ibn Baz; Al-Mughni

questionEn: What is the minimum amount of hair a man must trim in Taqsir according to each of the classical Sunni schools?
optionsEn: Trimming is invalid for men; only razors count
All four schools require shaving eyebrows
All schools require trimming only one single hair

Hanbalis and Malikis require trimming evenly from the entire head; Hanafis require at least a quarter of the head by a fingertip's length; Shafi'is allow at least three hairs (though all agree trimming the entire head evenly is best and safest)
explanationEn: Trimming evenly across the whole head with clippers or scissors satisfies every school unanimously and honors the Qur'anic wording 'muhalliqina ru'usakum wa muqassirin' (48:27).

questionEn: Can a pilgrim perform Tawaf on behalf of a healthy friend who is too tired to walk down from their Makkah hotel?
optionsEn: Only brothers can do someone else's Tawaf
Yes, for 50 Riyals
No; Umrah Tawaf and Sa'i must be performed personally by the pilgrim (on foot or in a wheelchair/cart)—nobody can delegate their own Tawaf while alive in Makkah
Yes, friends can swap Tawaf shifts
explanationEn: Each pilgrim in Umrah must personally perform their own Tawaf and Sa'i; if unable to walk, they use a wheelchair/electric cart so they still complete the circuit in person.

questionEn: If an elderly pilgrim on a wheelchair becomes sleepy and dozes off briefly while being pushed during Tawaf or Sa'i, is their circuit valid?
optionsEn: Wheelchair users never need Wudu for Tawaf
They must repeat Umrah from home
Sleeping for one second permanently voids Islam
Light drowsiness where Wudu is not broken does not break Tawaf or Sa'i; if deep sleep breaks Wudu during Tawaf, they refresh Wudu cleanly and finish the remaining circuits
explanationEn: Keeping the pilgrim awake in dhikr and supplication preserves both Wudu and spiritual engagement during wheelchair-assisted Tawaf.

questionEn: How should a deaf or blind pilgrim navigate Tawaf and Sa'i in Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: They must pay a double fee
Deaf pilgrims cannot enter Ihram
With a trusted companion or Haram guide assisting direction and lap counts, using tactile guidance or Braille/audio dua resources, enjoying equal full reward
Blind pilgrims are barred from Umrah
explanationEn: Historically, blind Companions such as Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA) and Ibn Abbas (RA) in later life attended the mosques and pilgrimage; physical impairment never diminishes spiritual reward.

questionEn: What should a diabetic pilgrim keep on hand during Tawaf and Sa'i while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Walk barefoot on burning outdoor plazas
Stop taking insulin until Halq
A small pouch with glucose tablets/dates, water, medical ID bracelet, prescribed insulin/glucometer, and comfortable sandals to protect feet from blisters
Avoid drinking water even if dizzy
explanationEn: Preserving life and health (hifz al-nafs) is an overarching objective of Shari'ah; carrying fast sugar, staying hydrated, and protecting neuropathic feet with clean approved sandals or padded medical slippers (if medically necessary) prevents serious injury.

questionEn: If a diabetic male pilgrim has severe foot ulcers requiring soft closed diabetic shoes even during Ihram, what is the ruling?
optionsEn: He must fly home immediately
He cannot perform Umrah ever

He may wear the prescribed medical footwear out of necessity; if it covers the ankles/upper foot fully like normal shoes without cutting, scholars advise offering Fidyah al-Adha (fast 3 days, feed 6 poor, or 1 sheep)—and there is zero sin
He must walk barefoot on open wounds
explanationEn: Necessity permits medical footwear while protecting health; offering Fidyah al-Adha satisfies the clothing rule cleanly without any guilt.

questionEn: Is a pilgrim on kidney dialysis, oxygen concentrator, or wearing a colostomy/urine bag permitted to perform Umrah?
optionsEn: No, medical bags make Tawaf impossible
They must skip Wudu completely

Yes; people with continuous medical conditions (like permanent urinary incontinence or stoma bags) follow the 'Ma'dhur' ruling: clean the bag/area, wrap securely, make fresh Wudu at the time of Tawaf/Salah, and worship peacefully
They must wait until cured even if lifelong
explanationEn: Just as the Prophet ﷺ guided women with continuous bleeding (istihadah), a pilgrim with a chronic leakage condition (salas al-bawl / stoma) secures the pouch cleanly, makes fresh Wudu when starting prayer/Tawaf, and ignores minor involuntary drops during the rite.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim loses consciousness or requires emergency hospitalization after entering Ihram before finishing Tawaf?
optionsEn: Doctors must shave them before surgery and they owe ten camels
Their Ihram disappears automatically after 2 hours

If they made Ishtirat at Miqat, they exit Ihram without penalty if unable to continue; otherwise, if they recover soon in Makkah they simply complete Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq once stable—or if permanently blocked (Ihsar), exit via Hady + Halq
Hospitalization automatically completes Tawaf
explanationEn: Ihram remains active until completed or properly exited via Ihsar/Ishtirat; treating the medical emergency always takes first priority.

questionEn: Why does Islamic etiquette discourage pushing to take selfies right in front of the Kaaba or live-streaming one's Tawaf?
optionsEn: Recording video invalidates Halq
It risks falling into Riya' (ostentation), breaks personal humility and concentration, violates others' privacy, and stalls foot traffic in the Mataf
Cameras destroy the marble
Photos break Wudu
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ feared hidden ostentation (al-shirk al-asghar) for his Ummah; keeping the phone tucked away in the Mataf protects sincerity and the sanctity of the moment.

questionEn: How should a pilgrim handle mobile phones inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Switch the phone to silent mode so ringtones and music never disturb worshippers in prayer or Tawaf
Take long loud business phone calls during Tawaf
Play loud ringtones during Fajr prayer
Leave alarms blasting beside sleeping pilgrims
explanationEn: Respecting the tranquility of Allah's House means silencing ringtones and reserving phone calls for outside the prayer and Mataf areas.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when he heard companions raising their voices loudly in supplication during a journey, and how does this apply to Umrah?
optionsEn: 'Never make dua on journeys'
'Shout as loudly as possible inside mosques'
'Only elders may speak above a whisper'
'Be gentle on yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent—you are calling upon the All-Hearing, Near One'
explanationEn: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) narrated this gentle reminder, encouraging calm, heartfelt, un-boisterous supplications during Tawaf and Sa'i (while raising the voice slightly in Talbiyah outdoors/on travel per its specific Sunnah).

questionEn: Is it permissible for men and women to perform Tawaf and Sa'i in the same spacious Mataf and Mas'a halls?
optionsEn: Women are barred from entering Al-Masjid al-Haram
Women may only perform Tawaf once every ten years

Yes; throughout Prophetic history men and women have performed Tawaf and Sa'i in the Sacred Mosque, while observing utmost modesty, lowering the gaze, and avoiding needless physical crowding against the opposite gender
Men and women perform Umrah in different cities
explanationEn: Umm Salamah (RA) performed Tawaf behind the people by the Prophet's ﷺ instruction (Bukhari 1619); maintaining outer-ring space and modesty honors both worship and chastity.

questionEn: What advice did Aisha (RA) give to a woman who boasted of having touched the Black Stone directly despite heavy male crowds?
optionsEn: Aisha (RA) praised crowding around men
Aisha (RA) said touching it is obligatory for women
Aisha (RA) disapproved of women pushing into dense men's crowds around the Black Stone, advising her to perform Tawaf peacefully from the outer space and point from afar
Aisha (RA) told her to push harder next time
explanationEn: Reported in Musnad al-Shafi'i and classical manuals, Aisha (RA) emphasized preserving female dignity and modesty by staying in wider lanes rather than squeezing into tight male crowds at the Stone.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ instruct Umm Salamah (RA) when she felt unwell during Hajj Tawaf?
optionsEn: 'Crawl through the inner ring'
'Wait in Madinah'
'Perform Tawaf behind the people while riding'—demonstrating both care for her health and maintaining modest distance from dense crowds
'Skip Tawaf completely'
explanationEn: Riding behind the main crowd allowed Umm Salamah (RA) to complete her 7 circuits comfortably while the Prophet ﷺ prayed beside the House.

questionEn: What common misconception exists about 'Masjid al-Haram' prayer lines when Salah begins—specifically, can women pray inside men's rows right beside the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Women cannot pray inside Al-Masjid al-Haram at all
No; the Haram organizes dedicated women's prayer sections and clear walkways—honoring orderly separation during congregational Salah preserves valid row etiquette and prevents confusion
Men must stand behind women
Everyone must stand mixed in the exact same spot
explanationEn: Following Haram stewards' guidance to designated women's/family prayer areas ensures comfortable, valid, and distraction-free Salah for everyone.

questionEn: What is the correct etiquette if you see an elderly pilgrim drop their cane, sandal, or water bottle during Tawaf or Sa'i?
optionsEn: Quickly and safely pick it up and hand it to them with a smile—helping a fellow guest of Allah in the Sanctuary is deeply rewarded
Step over them and ignore it
Kick it out of the lane
Tell them speaking during Tawaf is forbidden
explanationEn: Remember the Prophet's ﷺ words: 'Allah is in the aid of His servant so long as the servant is in the aid of his brother' (Muslim 2699).

questionEn: Why is it important NOT to perform 'Tawaf' around graves, shrines, or anything other than the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Only circling trees is allowed
Circling Maqam Ibrahim seven times is also required
Because graves are too small
Tawaf is an exclusive act of worship commanded solely around Allah's Sacred House (the Kaaba); circling graves or monuments is strictly forbidden in Islam
explanationEn: Circumambulation as a rite of devotion belongs exclusively to the Kaaba ('wal-yattawwafu bil-baytil-'atiq', 22:29); never circle Maqam Ibrahim, Green Dome, or any tomb.
reference: Surah Al-Hajj 22:29; Majmu' Fatawa Ibn Taymiyyah

questionEn: What superstition do some uninformed visitors mistakenly practice at Safa, Marwah, or Kaaba pillars, which scholars urge pilgrims to avoid?
optionsEn: Tying threads/cloths for wishes, rubbing walls or brass railings for barakah, or throwing coins into wells/corridors
Raising hands in dua at Safa facing the Kaaba
Saying 'Allahu Akbar' at the Black Stone
Drinking Zamzam while making dua
explanationEn: Seeking blessings only through Prophetic Sunnah (pure dua, dhikr, Tawaf, Sa'i, Zamzam) keeps worship free of superstition and innovation.

questionEn: If a pilgrim forgets how many laps of Sa'i they have completed—uncertain between 5 and 6—what should they do?
optionsEn: Ask a cleaner to guess
Build on certainty (5 laps) and complete laps 6 and 7 so they finish firmly at Mount Marwah
Restart all 7 laps from the beginning
Build on 6 laps and end early at Safa
explanationEn: Just like in Tawaf and Salah, certainty governs: note also that ending at Safa immediately reveals an even lap count (2, 4, 6), whereas ending at Marwah corresponds to odd laps (1, 3, 5, 7)!

questionEn: Look at the geometry of Sa'i: if you think you finished Lap 7, yet you find yourself standing at Mount Safa, what do you know immediately?
optionsEn: You finished Lap 7 correctly
You actually finished an EVEN number of laps (6 or 8), because Lap 7 MUST end at Mount Marwah!
You must shave at Safa
Safa and Marwah switched places
explanationEn: This handy self-check saves countless pilgrims: starting at Safa means laps 1, 3, 5, and 7 always arrive at Marwah; arriving at Safa is always an even lap (2, 4, or 6).

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if they realize they only walked 6 laps of Sa'i and stopped at Safa before trimming their hair?
optionsEn: Repeat Tawaf first
Repeat all 7 laps from scratch
Simply walk the 7th lap from Safa to Marwah right away, and then perform Halq or Taqsir
Pay a Dam
explanationEn: Because they have not exited Ihram yet (and even if they had trimmed early by mistake), completing the missing 7th lap from Safa to Marwah fulfills Sa'i cleanly.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim mistakenly stopped Sa'i after 6 laps, went to the barber and shaved their head, and ONLY THEN realized lap 7 was missing?
optionsEn: They must do 7 more Tawafs
Their Umrah can never be fixed

Walk the missing 7th lap from Safa to Marwah immediately (and pass the razor over the head/trim again if any hair remains, with no sin for genuine mistake; scholars differ on whether a minor fidyah applies for early shaving out of ignorance, with strong scholarly views excusing genuine ignorance/forgetfulness)
They must wait until next Ramadan
explanationEn: Scholars note that Sa'i must be completed to all 7 laps for Umrah to finish validly; completing the 7th lap promptly restores the pillar cleanly.

questionEn: Why is it helpful to use simple mental anchors (or a quiet finger count) during Tawaf and Sa'i rather than relying on distracting electronic apps with loud beeps?
optionsEn: Digital apps invalidate Tawaf
Counting quietly on fingers or beads/simple silent counter keeps your heart anchored in humble dua without breaking khushu' or disturbing neighbors
Smartphones explode near the Kaaba
Finger counting is forbidden in Hanbali fiqh
explanationEn: While a silent ring counter or simple finger count is permissible, keeping focus on Allah rather than staring at screens elevates the spiritual depth of Tawaf.

questionEn: Does touching the 'black line' or green line on the floor in the Mataf pause your Tawaf or require bowing?
optionsEn: You must kiss the marble floor
You must stop and prostrate on the floor line

No; it is merely a visual alignment guide for the Black Stone corner (modern marble no longer even has a black painted stripe, using wall/pillar green lights instead)—you simply raise your right hand toward the Black Stone, say 'Allahu Akbar', and keep walking smoothly
You must jump over the line
explanationEn: Standing still in the moving stream of pilgrims causes pile-ups; aligning with the green light marker, saluting briefly while moving (or pausing a fraction of a second safely), and continuing smoothly keeps everyone safe.

questionEn: Why did the Masjid al-Haram authorities replace the old brown/black floor stripe with green alignment lights on the upper wall/pillars?
optionsEn: Because the paint wore off
To mark where Zamzam pipes run
To indicate the end of Sa'i
Because pilgrims mistakenly stopped abruptly or bowed on the floor stripe, creating dangerous bottlenecks during Tawaf
explanationEn: Green lights above eye level allow effortless visual alignment with the Black Stone corner without causing people to look down or stop mid-lane.

questionEn: What is the virtue of performing Umrah with family members—such as parents, spouse, or children?
optionsEn: Spouses are forbidden from making dua together
Children lose their parents' reward
Families must walk in silence without speaking to one another
Strengthening family bonds in obedience to Allah, earning immense reward for serving elderly parents (birr), and planting lifelong love for the Sacred House in children's hearts
explanationEn: Caring patiently for parents or teaching children the rites around the Kaaba turns an Umrah journey into enduring sadaqah jariyah and family mercy.

questionEn: If a pilgrim speaks briefly during Tawaf to check on an elderly mother, ask a companion which lap they are on, or give Salam, does it invalidate Tawaf?
optionsEn: No; brief, necessary, or wholesome speech is completely permissible in Tawaf (as the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah has permitted speech in it—so whoever speaks should speak only good')
Yes, speaking one word voids Tawaf completely
One must restart from Lap 1
Only speaking Arabic is allowed
explanationEn: Unlike Salah where speech breaks prayer, helpful or kind speech during Tawaf is lawful, while idle chatter, gossip, or arguing should always be avoided.

questionEn: If someone greets you with 'As-salamu alaykum' while you are praying the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim, how should you respond?
optionsEn: Say 'Wa alaykumus-salam' aloud in the middle of Al-Fatihah
Stop praying and shake hands immediately
Do NOT speak words during Salah; either wait until after Salam to reply verbally or wave/nod a subtle hand gesture if right beside you, keeping your prayer valid
Walk away from Maqam Ibrahim
explanationEn: During Salah itself (unlike Tawaf), intentional speech invalidates prayer; the Prophet ﷺ occasionally returned Salam with a gentle hand sign while praying.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if someone walks directly in front of them while they are praying the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: Strike the passerby with a sandal

Try to pray behind a pillar, bag, or person (as a Sutrah) away from heavy walking lanes—and note that many scholars cite authentic reports showing Al-Masjid al-Haram's crowded nature makes passing unavoidable (and per Ibn Abbas/Aisha reports, avoid creating fights over walkways)
Restart Umrah from Miqat
Shout angrily during Surah Al-Fatihah
explanationEn: Praying in designated prayer sections (well back from moving Mataf circulation) prevents passersby altogether, while gentle restraint avoids disputes in the Sacred Mosque.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing 'Umrah' during the white nights (13th–15th) or Mondays/Thursdays versus any other ordinary day?
optionsEn: Umrah is valid only on the 14th of every month
All days of the year carry valid Umrah reward (with Ramadan specifically highlighted by authentic Hadith); fasting optional Mondays/Thursdays or Ayyam al-Bid is separate from Umrah itself
Umrah is forbidden on Tuesdays
Only Ramadan Umrah is valid
explanationEn: Outside the Hajj-day scholarly restriction (9–13 Dhul-Hijjah), any day or night of the week is equally valid for Umrah.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is fasting a voluntary fast (e.g., Monday/Thursday or six days of Shawwal) when arriving in Makkah in intense heat for Umrah, what is wiser?
optionsEn: One must never drink Zamzam on Mondays
Fainting from dehydration is mandatory
Breaking a voluntary fast cancels Umrah
Since voluntary fasting may be broken for ease or travel/vitality, drinking Zamzam and staying hydrated to perform Tawaf and Sa'i with full energy and presence of heart is permitted and often wiser
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told travelers who fasted in exhausting heat that breaking the fast to stay strong was better ('Those who broke their fast took all the reward today' in service/strength); one can fast another day calmly.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about those who fasted vs those who broke their fast during a grueling journey when the non-fasters pitched tents and watered mounts?
optionsEn: 'Never help fellow travelers'
'Today, those who broke their fast have taken the reward' (Dhahabal-muftiruna bil-ajr)—honoring practical strength and service to fellow travelers
'Watering mounts breaks Ihram'
'Those who fainted are always forbidden from Umrah'
explanationEn: Narrated by Anas (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, this beautiful Hadith teaches balance between voluntary fasting and serving/sustaining strength during demanding travel.

questionEn: How does performing Umrah impact a believer's prayer life and spiritual habits after returning home?
optionsEn: It removes the obligation of Fajr prayer at home
It allows neglecting family duties for a year
An accepted Umrah inspires greater attachment to the five daily prayers, sincere repentance, humility, and charity long after leaving Makkah
It means one never needs to repent again
explanationEn: Early scholars taught that the clearest sign of an accepted pilgrimage is returning better in worship and character than before departing.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a male pilgrim experiences a wet dream (nocturnal emission / ihtilam) while sleeping in Ihram?
optionsEn: He must wait seven days before Tawaf
His Ihram and Umrah remain completely valid with zero penalty; he simply performs Ghusl cleanly (using unscented water) before performing Tawaf or Salah
He must return to the Miqat and restart Niyyah
His Umrah is permanently invalidated and he owes a camel
explanationEn: Involuntary nocturnal emission during sleep incurs neither sin nor fidyah, and does not break Ihram; the pilgrim simply takes a purifying Ghusl (without perfume) before entering prayer or Tawaf.

questionEn: Is eating or drinking naturally aromatic foods—such as mint tea, cardamom coffee, apples, or citrus fruits—permissible while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Only plain bread and water are permitted
Cardamom coffee requires a Dam
Yes, consuming food and beverages with natural aroma is completely permissible; only applying perfume (tib) and deliberately smelling pure saffron/musk oils as fragrance is avoided
No, coffee and fruit are forbidden in Ihram
explanationEn: Natural foods and spices used in meals or drinks (unless pure raw saffron/perfume added as cosmetic fragrance) are lawful nutrition, not wearing perfume.

questionEn: What if a hotel bedsheet or towel smells strongly of floral fabric softener or perfume while a pilgrim is in Ihram?
optionsEn: Fast three days for walking past a hotel laundry
Avoid sleeping directly on strongly perfumed linens (use your own unscented travel sheet or request unfragranced linens) so perfume does not transfer onto your body or Ihram wraps
Sleep standing up outside
Burn the bedsheets immediately
explanationEn: Preventing direct transfer of heavy fragrance onto skin or Ihram cloth keeps one safely away from Ihram violations without undue hardship.

questionEn: May a pilgrim in Ihram carry sealed bottles of attar/perfume inside their luggage as gifts for family back home?
optionsEn: No, even looking at a perfume shop breaks Ihram
Only after returning to Jeddah
Carrying sealed bottles in luggage requires a sheep sacrifice
Yes; possessing or transporting sealed perfume bottles in a bag without applying them to one's body or Ihram clothes is completely permissible
explanationEn: The prohibition is on wearing or applying fragrance—not owning or packing sealed bottles safely inside luggage.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim in Ihram passes by a perfume shop in Makkah and unintentionally smells the fragrance wafting in the air?
optionsEn: Holding your breath for 200 meters is mandatory
Passing a perfume shop cancels Tawaf
One must wash their clothes three times immediately
Inhaling ambient scent unintentionally while walking past incurs no sin and no penalty; only deliberately applying perfume or lingering intentionally to inhale concentrated perfume oil is avoided
explanationEn: Unavoidable ambient scents in public walkways carry zero penalty in Islamic law.

questionEn: Is applying pure unscented olive oil, coconut oil, or plain Vaseline (petroleum jelly) to chapped lips or chafed skin permissible in Ihram?
optionsEn: No, skin moisturizers of any kind are banned
Only allowed on the palms
Yes, plain unscented petroleum jelly, olive oil, or medical ointment to relieve dryness or skin chafing is completely permissible
Petroleum jelly requires feeding six poor persons
explanationEn: Unscented moisturizers and anti-chafing balms protect pilgrims from painful thigh chafing during Sa'i and dry lips without violating the perfume prohibition.
reference: Fatawa Ibn Uthaymin; Medical Umrah Care

questionEn: If a pilgrim in Ihram accidentally steps on or kills a louse or biting mosquito/flea on their body, what is the ruling?
optionsEn: Killing biting mosquitoes, fleas, or harmful pests incurs nothing; even regarding body lice, classical narrations from Ibn Abbas (RA) mention giving a small handful of food (or nothing for involuntary swatting of mosquitoes)
One must stay in Ihram for another year
Swatting a mosquito requires sacrificing a camel
It invalidates Umrah completely
explanationEn: Mosquitoes, flies, and biting insects are harmful pests (similar to the permitted harmful creatures), not hunted land game.

questionEn: What is the ruling on pronouncing divorce (Talaq) or taking a wife back (Raj'ah) during revocable divorce while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Divorce turns into a camel sacrifice
Both Nikah and Raj'ah are identical
Valid; the prohibition in Ihram applies specifically to initiating a new marriage contract (Nikah) or proposal, not revoking a divorce or legal marital separation
Spouses lose legal marriage status in Ihram
explanationEn: Uthman's (RA) Hadith specifically bars Nikah and Khitbah (marriage and proposal); jurists distinguish taking back a revocably divorced wife (raj'ah) as continuing an existing bond.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim in Ihram donate blood in an urgent medical emergency or receive a blood transfusion?
optionsEn: Yes; saving life or undergoing necessary medical bleeding/cupping is permissible in Ihram, as the Prophet ﷺ himself underwent Hijamah (cupping) while in Ihram
No, any blood drop breaks Ihram
Only after Halq
Blood transfusions require restarting from Miqat
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ was cupped while in Ihram; drawing blood for testing, donation, or medical necessity does not violate Ihram (so long as hair is not needlessly shaved unless medically necessary with fidyah).

questionEn: If a pilgrim breaks a tooth or needs emergency dental extraction while in Ihram, is that permissible?
optionsEn: Dental care requires sacrificing a sheep
Yes, dental treatment or removing a painful broken tooth is completely permissible without any penalty
They must wait until returning to their home country
No, teeth count as nails
explanationEn: Ihram prohibits cutting hair and nails—not necessary dental or surgical care to relieve pain or protect health.

questionEn: If a pilgrim has a layover at Jeddah Airport for 3 hours flying onward to Riyadh (NOT intending Umrah or Makkah on that trip), must they enter Ihram?
optionsEn: Only men must wear Ihram on layovers
No; crossing Miqat toward Jeddah is NOT bound by Ihram unless the traveler actually intends to perform Hajj or Umrah
Yes, every Muslim flying over Saudi Arabia must wear Ihram
Yes, airport transit passengers must do Tawaf
explanationEn: As established by the Prophet's ﷺ Hadith ('for whoever passes them intending Hajj or Umrah') and his own entry into Makkah at the Conquest without Ihram, non-pilgrimage travel needs no Ihram.

questionEn: What if a Muslim lives and works in Jeddah for a week on business WITHOUT initially intending Umrah, and then after finishing work decides to go to Makkah for Umrah?
optionsEn: Because they formed the Umrah intention while inside Jeddah (which is inside the outer Miqat boundary in al-Hil), they enter Ihram directly in Jeddah before traveling to Makkah
They must fly out of Saudi Arabia and fly back in
They must pay a Dam
They must travel to Dhul-Hulayfah first
explanationEn: Once someone is lawfully settled/visiting inside the Miqat line without prior Umrah intent, their starting point ('min haythu ansha'a') is where they form the intention (Jeddah).

questionEn: Conversely, what if a Muslim travels from overseas TO Jeddah intending to visit a relative for two days AND THEN go to Makkah for Umrah from the very start of the trip?
optionsEn: They can always delay Ihram until leaving their relative's house in Jeddah
They skip Ihram altogether

Since they already intended Umrah when setting out from abroad, they must enter Ihram at the outer Miqat before landing in Jeddah (or return to an outer Miqat if they delayed)—they should NOT pass the Miqat without Ihram planning to start from Jeddah
They can start from Masjid Aisha instead
explanationEn: The decisive factor is whether Umrah was intended when crossing the outer Miqat; an intending pilgrim does not bypass the Miqat un-muhrim.

questionEn: If a resident of Riyadh (Najd) drives to Ta'if for vacation intending to stay two days and ALSO intending Umrah afterward, where should they enter Ihram?
optionsEn: At Jeddah port

Since they pass Qarn al-Manazil (or Wadi Muharram between Ta'if and Makkah), residents/travelers entering Ta'if before passing Wadi Muharram/Qarn al-Manazil enter Ihram at Qarn al-Manazil / Wadi Muharram before descending toward Makkah
At Dhul-Hulayfah
Inside Al-Masjid al-Haram
explanationEn: Note that Ta'if lies just outside Qarn al-Manazil/Wadi Muharram; crossing Wadi Muharram (al-Hada) or Qarn al-Manazil (al-Sayl al-Kabir) on the descent to Makkah places them right at the Miqat.

questionEn: If a pilgrim commits TWO separate violations of the SAME type in Ihram before offering Fidyah—for example, putting on perfume twice or wearing a shirt twice—how many Fidyahs are owed according to major scholars?
optionsEn: Zero expiation even if deliberate

One Fidyah suffices for repeated acts of the same category before expiation (just as one Fidyah covers repeating the same prohibition), unless different categories (like wearing a shirt AND shaving hair) were violated, or hunting game where each animal has its own penalty
One hundred fasts
Ten camels per minute
explanationEn: Classical jurists (Hanbali/Shafi'i/Hanafi details) distinguish: different categories of mahzurat before expiation or hunting separate animals each trigger their own penalty, whereas repeating the same minor type (like perfume/clothing) prior to offering fidyah merges into one fidyah in major opinions.

questionEn: When a sacrificial animal (sheep/goat) is slaughtered as a Dam or Fidyah in Makkah due to an Umrah violation, may the pilgrim eat from that penalty meat?
optionsEn: Yes, the pilgrim must eat the entire sheep alone
Only the head is given away
The meat must be thrown into the Red Sea
No; meat from a Dam/Fidyah of atonement or omitted Wajib must be distributed entirely to the poor of the Haram—unlike voluntary Hady or Tamattu'/Qiran Hady from which the pilgrim may eat
explanationEn: Jurists strictly distinguish celebratory/ritual Hady of Tamattu'/Qiran (where eating is Sunnah per Qur'an 22:28) from penalty Dam/Fidyah (which belongs exclusively to the needy of Makkah).

questionEn: Where must a penalty Dam (such as for bypassing the Miqat without Ihram) be slaughtered and distributed?
optionsEn: Within the Haram boundaries of Makkah, with its meat distributed to the poor of the Haram (through trusted official channels like Adahi or verified charities)
In the pilgrim's home country after returning
Anywhere outside Arabia
In Jeddah airport
explanationEn: Penalty sacrifices (Dima' al-Jubran) are tied to the Sacred Precinct of Makkah so the poor residing around Allah's House benefit directly.

questionEn: If a pilgrim owes a Dam (for bypassing the Miqat or omitting a Wajib) and genuinely cannot afford the price of a sheep in Makkah, what substitute applies?
optionsEn: They must walk back to their homeland

By scholarly analogy to Hajj Tamattu' (Qur'an 2:196), one fasts 10 days—three days during the pilgrimage/stay and seven upon returning home (note: for Fidyah al-Adha like clothing/hair/perfume, the choice is already 3 fasts, feeding 6 poor, or 1 sheep)
Their Umrah is permanently canceled
They must borrow at high interest
explanationEn: Understanding the distinction between Fidyah al-Adha (which already gives the easy 3-day fast / 6-poor option) and Dam al-Wajib (where inability transfers to 10 days fasting per major jurists) prevents unnecessary anxiety.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performs Tawaf while carrying a child whose diaper is clean, versus carrying a child whose diaper contains impurity?
optionsEn: Only mothers may carry infants in Tawaf
Children can never be carried in Tawaf

If the diaper holds Najis impurity, majority scholars forbid carrying the child during Tawaf or Salah (just as the Prophet ﷺ held Umamah RA only when pure); ensure the child has a fresh, clean diaper right before Tawaf
Diapers do not matter even if soaked with impurity
explanationEn: Checking and changing the baby into a fresh clean diaper immediately before Tawaf ensures both comfort and ritual purity while following the Prophetic example of carrying Umamah bint Abi al-'As (RA) in Salah.

questionEn: If a male pilgrim in Ihram needs to carry his toddler on his shoulders during Tawaf, does the child sitting on his shoulders violate the prohibition on 'covering the head'?
optionsEn: No; carrying a child or a bag briefly on the shoulders/head is not wearing a tailored head-covering like a cap or turban (though resting the child on the shoulders/arms avoids touching the crown of the head directly anyway)
Only fathers may carry girls
Yes, carrying a child on shoulders requires a camel sacrifice
Children must walk alone in dense crowds
explanationEn: Supporting a child safely on one's shoulders or chest in a baby carrier keeps them safe in crowds without violating Ihram.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim use a structured baby carrier (front/back sling) over their Ihram wraps to carry an infant safely during Tawaf and Sa'i?
optionsEn: No, baby carriers count as stitched shirts
Only woven reed baskets are allowed
Yes, using a baby carrier over the Ihram wraps is completely permissible and much safer than holding a wriggling toddler by one hand in dense crowds
Baby carriers are allowed only in Sa'i
explanationEn: A baby carrier is equipment to hold the child—not a garment worn by the pilgrim—just like a backpack or belt.

questionEn: What should you do if an older child gets lost in the Mataf or Mas'a during Umrah?
optionsEn: Leave children without any ID info
Shout across the entire Mataf without checking lost-child desks
Abandon your child and go home

Attach an ID wristband with parent's phone number and hotel name beforehand, designate a clear meeting point (like a numbered gate or Zamzam cooler pillar), and immediately alert Haram security officers who assist lost children
explanationEn: Preparation—wristbands, clear landmarks, and calm coordination with Haram security—protects children and keeps parents calm.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is praying the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim and notices their Izar slipping slightly, how should they adjust it?
optionsEn: Ask a passerby to tie it during prostration
Stop praying and run out of the mosque
Leave the Awrah uncovered until finishing Salah
Adjust it promptly with minimal calm hand movement so the Awrah stays covered without unnecessary excessive motion
explanationEn: Covering the Awrah is a condition of Salah; small purposeful adjustments to keep oneself covered are required and do not invalidate prayer.

questionEn: What is the minimum Awrah that a man must keep covered in Ihram during both Tawaf and Salah?
optionsEn: Only from mid-thigh to ankle
Only the upper chest
Men have no Awrah in Ihram
From the navel to the knees at minimum—and during Salah (including the 2 rak'ahs after Tawaf), at least one/both shoulders must also be covered with the Rida'
explanationEn: Keeping the Izar securely wrapped well above the waist/navel and reaching below the knees/mid-calf ensures Awrah stays covered even while briskly walking or sitting in Tashahhud.

questionEn: What happens if a male pilgrim performs the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim while forgetting to pull his Rida' back over his bare right shoulder (still in Idtiba')?
optionsEn: His entire Umrah is void
He must repeat Tawaf seven times
He owes a camel sacrifice

Because his left shoulder is still covered, his prayer remains valid according to the majority (Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanafi, and Hanbali views noting the Hadith 'let none pray in a single garment with nothing over his shoulders'—covering one shoulder fulfills the minimum while covering both is better and avoids Makruh)
explanationEn: While covering both shoulders before standing for Salah is the clear Sunnah to avoid any Makruh state, a forgotten uncovered right shoulder when the left shoulder is draped does not nullify the prayer.

questionEn: If a pregnant woman performing Umrah experiences severe fatigue or Braxton-Hicks contractions during Tawaf or Sa'i, what should she do?
optionsEn: Force herself to walk without stopping even if fainting
Sit immediately to rest, hydrate, or switch to a wheelchair/electric cart—saving her strength and protecting her unborn baby is Islamically prioritized
Skip Sa'i completely
Go home without finishing Umrah
explanationEn: Using a wheelchair or motorized cart on upper levels protects mother and child while fulfilling every pillar of Umrah validly.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim hire a wheelchair pusher who guarantees 'finishing Tawaf and Sa'i in 15 minutes' by weaving aggressively through crowds?
optionsEn: No; ask the pusher to move steadily, courteously, and safely on the dedicated wheelchair lanes without bumping others—and verify all 7 full circuits and 7 Sa'i laps are genuinely completed
Wheelchair users only need 5 laps
Yes, pushers know shortcuts through Hijr Ismail
Yes, speed is more important than counting laps
explanationEn: Pilgrims using pushed wheelchairs should personally count their own 7 circuits of Tawaf and 7 laps of Sa'i and remind pushers to stay gentle and avoid cutting corners.

questionEn: Are the official electric mobility scooters/carts provided on the upper floors of Al-Masjid al-Haram valid for Tawaf and Sa'i?
optionsEn: No, motorized wheels invalidate worship
Electric carts may only be used in Sa'i, never Tawaf
Only manual pushchairs are valid
Yes, riding an electric cart for Tawaf and Sa'i is completely valid (especially for the elderly, sick, or weak, and permitted generally when crowded/needed)
explanationEn: Just as riding a camel was valid for the Prophet ﷺ and Umm Salamah (RA), modern mobility carts on designated tracks are fully valid.

questionEn: If an elderly man riding a wheelchair during Umrah Tawaf asks whether he needs to do Raml, what is the answer?
optionsEn: He owes a fidyah
No; Raml is Sunnah only for able-bodied men walking on foot in the lower open laps without crowding—wheelchair riders are completely excused and walk/roll at normal pace
He must get out and run lap 1
Yes, the pusher must sprint all 7 laps
explanationEn: Raml applies only when physically able and uncrowded; pushing a wheelchair calmly honors everyone's safety.

questionEn: Is it permissible for a male pilgrim to use a wheelchair in Tawaf or Sa'i ONLY if he is paralyzed, or also if he has arthritis, heart disease, severe blister pain, or exhaustion?
optionsEn: Only complete paralysis allows a wheelchair
Heart patients must still walk on foot
Any genuine physical weakness, joint pain, heart condition, or severe exhaustion justifies using a wheelchair or electric cart in Tawaf and Sa'i without penalty
Using a wheelchair for knee pain requires a Dam
explanationEn: Islam removes hardship ('He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty', 22:78); painful knees, shortness of breath, or frailty are completely valid reasons for assisted mobility.

questionEn: What if a healthy young adult uses an electric cart solely out of laziness without any physical need?
optionsEn: While their Tawaf/Sa'i still counts according to most jurists (especially for Sa'i/riding precedents), scholars strongly advise able-bodied youth to walk on foot to follow the Sunnah and leave carts for the needy and elderly
They must pay ten sheep
Walking on foot is forbidden for youth
Their Umrah is null and void
explanationEn: Walking when able honors the Prophetic norm and preserves carts for frail elders and sick pilgrims.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is on the ground floor Mataf and realizes the crowd around the Kaaba has become dangerously tight, what should they do?
optionsEn: Climb onto someone's shoulders
Gradually drift outward toward the wider, calmer outer circles of the Mataf (or move up to the first/second floor ring) where breathing room and safety are far better
Stop walking and sit down in the moving stream
Push aggressively inward toward the Kaaba wall
explanationEn: All rings of the Mataf—whether close to the Kaaba or near the outer arches—count equally for Tawaf, and safety always takes precedence over proximity.

questionEn: Does circling closer to the Kaaba wall give a 'more valid' Tawaf than circling in the outer courtyard or upper floor?
optionsEn: Upper floors only count in Ramadan
Yes, only the innermost 3 meters count
Outer rings require 14 circuits
No; every ring inside Al-Masjid al-Haram is equally valid—and circling further out where you have space for humble dua and Khushu' without being shoved is often spiritually superior
explanationEn: Proximity without focus or while harming others diminishes spiritual presence; calm outer rings allow serene devotion and proper Sunnah pace.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if a security guard gently directs foot traffic away from a congested zone near the Black Stone or Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: Shove the guard while shouting Takbir
Leave Makkah in anger
Argue and force past the barrier
Comply politely and promptly—obeying orderly crowd safety instructions protects lives and prevents stampedes
explanationEn: Obedience to lawful safety organization in the Haram fulfills Qur'an 4:59 and reflects the gentle prophetic character of a guest of Allah.

questionEn: What is the ruling if someone takes a small stone, piece of marble, or sand from the Sacred Haram home as a keepsake?
optionsEn: Collecting Haram rocks is Sunnah

Scholars discourage and forbid removing stones or earth from the Haram territory (even more so mosque property), advising pilgrims to leave everything in the Sanctuary intact and bring home Zamzam water and pious habits instead
Everyone must carry a pebble from Safa
Taking sand doubles the reward of Umrah
explanationEn: Reports from Ibn Abbas and classical scholars (like Imam Ahmad) disapproved taking stones or soil out of Makkah's Haram, respecting the sanctity of the Sacred Land.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim wipe or clean the Kaaba floor or pick up stray tissues inside Al-Masjid al-Haram if they see litter?
optionsEn: Only paid staff may pick up trash
Picking up litter invalidates Wudu
Yes; removing litter from a mosque—especially Allah's Sacred House—is an honorable act of humility and service (like the woman who cleaned the Prophet's ﷺ mosque whom he ﷺ honored)
No, touching stray paper breaks Ihram
explanationEn: Remember the Prophet ﷺ inquired about the woman who cleaned his mosque and prayed over her grave—keeping Allah's House spotless is deeply beloved.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing 'Umrah' during an eclipse prayer (Salat al-Kusuf) or Eid prayer inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Umrah is canceled if an eclipse occurs
Eid prayer replaces Tawaf
Wait briefly to join the congregational prayer (Eid or Eclipse prayer) with the Imam, then resume Tawaf or Sa'i cleanly right afterward
Keep walking through prayer rows during Eid prayer
explanationEn: Whenever an organized congregational prayer stands inside Al-Masjid al-Haram, joining the rows and pausing Tawaf/Sa'i smoothly maintains mosque unity and order.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in the middle of Sa'i between Safa and Marwah when the Adhan and Iqamah for Dhuhr are called, what should they do?
optionsEn: Keep walking past praying rows during Dhuhr

Pause at their current spot (remembering which lap and direction they were walking), join the Dhuhr prayer in congregation right there inside the Mas'a or hall, and continue walking that exact lap after Salah
Discard all previous Sa'i laps and restart from Safa
Skip Dhuhr prayer until after Halq
explanationEn: Just like Tawaf, pausing Sa'i for Fard Salah and resuming from the very point of pause is completely valid and avoids walking past people standing in prayer.

questionEn: If you forget your lap count in Tawaf and have a trusted companion walking right beside you who counted attentively, may you rely on their count?
optionsEn: No, speaking to a companion voids Tawaf
Yes; if you trust their attentive count and feel reassured, you may accept it—and if genuine uncertainty still persists between two numbers, build on the lower certain count
Only an Imam's count counts
You must always ignore companions and add 3 extra laps
explanationEn: Confirming the lap count calmly with your spouse or travel partner walking alongside you is practical and permitted.

questionEn: Is it permissible for a group leader to carry a small umbrella or simple colored flag/hat? Wait—for MEN in Ihram, can a male group guide wear a bright hat to stay visible?
optionsEn: No! A male in Ihram may NOT wear a hat or cap; instead, he can hold a small raised sign, scarf tied on a bag, or colored umbrella above his head without touching/covering his head
Yes, yellow caps are allowed in Ihram
Yes, group leaders are exempt from head-covering rules
Guides must wear helmets
explanationEn: Every male muhrim—guide or pilgrim—must keep his head uncovered; holding a small raised umbrella or tying a colored ribbon to a backpack keeps groups together lawfully.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Umrah Tawaf while wearing a smartwatch or fitness band?
optionsEn: Only digital watches without straps are allowed
Prohibited because metal watches are tailored garments
Completely permissible (as long as it does not emit loud alarms/ringtones or distract from sincere worship during Tawaf)
Smartwatches invalidate Wudu
explanationEn: Watches are permitted in Ihram; keeping notifications silenced ensures focus on Allah rather than step counts or messages.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim wipe over regular non-leather cotton socks during Wudu before Tawaf?
optionsEn: Wiping over bare ankles without socks is valid

First, men in Ihram do not wear regular socks; second, even for women in Ihram or non-muhrim voluntary Tawaf, scholars differ on wiping over thin cotton socks (Hanbalis/some scholars allow thick non-transparent socks satisfying conditions, whereas Hanafi/Maliki/Shafi'i majority require thicker khuffs or washing bare feet unless thick/leather-soled)—washing bare feet in Wudu is universally valid and avoids doubt!
Men in Ihram must wear wool socks
Wudu requires no water inside Makkah
explanationEn: Because washing feet directly in Wudu is undisputed across all schools and easy in Haram ablution halls, washing feet cleanly prevents any dispute.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in a hotel in Makkah and performs Tayammum (dry ablution) ONLY because they dislike walking to the bathroom, is their Tawaf valid?
optionsEn: Yes, Tayammum is always equal to Wudu even next to water taps
No; Tayammum is valid only when water is genuinely absent or using water would cause actual medical harm—not out of mere laziness
Tawaf requires neither Wudu nor Tayammum
Tayammum is forbidden even for sick patients
explanationEn: Qur'an 5:6 limits Tayammum to illness, travel without water, or inability to use water safely; when clean water is readily available, performing Wudu properly is required.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is hospitalized in Makkah with severe burns or a medical condition forbidding water contact, how do they achieve purity for Tawaf/Salah?
optionsEn: They perform Tayammum with clean earth/dust (or hospital staff assist them), which completely fulfills ritual purity in illness
They must pour perfume instead of water
They cannot pray at all until healed
They must skip Salah for weeks
explanationEn: Allah's mercy provides Tayammum whenever water cannot be safely used due to illness or wounds.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing 'Umrah' for a living person who is financially poor (lacking money) yet physically healthy and strong?
optionsEn: Poor people must walk across oceans

Not valid as Badal Umrah; poverty is NOT physical incapacity—someone physically healthy who lacks money simply has no obligation to perform Umrah until Allah grants them means (though someone may gift them travel money so they go in person!)
A rich friend should do Badal Umrah on behalf of a healthy poor neighbor
Healthy people can outsource their Umrah for convenience
explanationEn: Gifting a poor, healthy Muslim a plane ticket to go perform Umrah themselves is tremendous charity, whereas Badal proxy applies only to the deceased or permanently physically unable.

questionEn: If a rich child sponsors their healthy elderly parents to travel for Umrah, does that relieve the parents' obligation or give immense reward?
optionsEn: Parents must refuse all gifts from children
Only strangers may pay for tickets
Sponsoring parents invalidates one's own Umrah
It enables the parents to perform Umrah themselves while the child earns extraordinary reward for filial righteousness (birr) and facilitating worship
explanationEn: Funding and accompanying parents on Umrah is among the noblest forms of kindness to parents and 'cooperating in righteousness and piety' (5:2).

questionEn: When a pilgrim completes Umrah and wishes to perform another Umrah while staying in Makkah for 10 days, how must they enter Ihram for the second Umrah?
optionsEn: Put on Ihram inside their Makkah hotel lobby
Repeat Sa'i without Tawaf

Step outside the Sacred Haram boundaries into al-Hil (such as Masjid al-Tan'im / Masjid Aisha or al-Ji'ranah), enter Ihram there, and then return for Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir—remembering many scholars advise prioritizing abundant voluntary Tawaf over daily repeated Umrahs
Skip Ihram for the second Umrah
explanationEn: If one chooses to perform an additional Umrah on behalf of a deceased relative or oneself, leaving the Haram to al-Hil (e.g., Tan'im) is necessary; meanwhile, Imam Malik, Ibn Taymiyyah, and many early scholars noted the Salaf preferred multiplying voluntary Tawafs over frequent short-interval Umrahs.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1785; Majmu' Fatawa Ibn Taymiyyah

questionEn: Why did Imam Ahmad, Ibn Taymiyyah, and other classical scholars recommend focusing on voluntary Tawaf rather than performing multiple Umrahs in rapid succession on every day of a short stay?
optionsEn: Because extra Umrahs are sinful in all schools
Because Masjid Aisha is closed in Ramadan

Because neither the Prophet ﷺ nor his Companions exited Makkah repeatedly to al-Tan'im for multiple Umrahs in one trip, and multiplying Tawaf around the Kaaba directly follows the Sunnah of residents/visitors
Because only one Tawaf per lifetime is allowed
explanationEn: Understanding both sides—that extra Umrahs from Tan'im are permitted by many jurists (e.g., for deceased parents) while voluntary Tawaf is the clear Prophetic norm—helps pilgrims make wise, non-judgmental choices.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performs Umrah during a short 3-day trip and also wants to visit historic Islamic sites in Makkah (like Jabal al-Noor / Cave Hira or Jabal Thawr), are those visits part of the Umrah rituals?
optionsEn: No; historical sites like Cave Hira and Cave Thawr are educational/reflective places to learn Seerah from afar—climbing them is NOT a rite of Umrah and carries no special ritual prayer
Without climbing Jabal Thawr, Umrah is invalid
Pilgrims must shave their heads inside Cave Hira
Yes, climbing Cave Hira is the 8th lap of Sa'i
explanationEn: Distinguishing obligatory/Sunnah Umrah rites (Ihram, Tawaf, Sa'i, Halq/Taqsir) from optional historical reflection prevents innovations and unnecessary dangerous climbs in intense heat.

questionEn: Is touching, praying toward, or writing names on rocks at Jabal al-Noor (Cave Hira) or Mount Arafah a Sunnah of Umrah?
optionsEn: Every pilgrim must bring a rock from Arafah
No; writing wishes on rocks, tying cloths, or seeking special blessings from mountain stones has no basis in the Sunnah and should be avoided
Praying toward Cave Hira replaces Qiblah
Yes, writing one's name on Jabal al-Noor guarantees acceptance
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ never climbed Cave Hira after Hijrah even when entering Makkah at Conquest or Farewell Hajj; pure Tawhid keeps devotion directed to Allah alone.

questionEn: What is the relationship between Qiblah direction when praying inside Al-Masjid al-Haram and the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Worshippers inside Al-Masjid al-Haram arrange themselves in concentric circles facing directly toward the physical Kaaba itself ('Ayn al-Ka'bah)
Everyone faces due North regardless of where they stand
Everyone faces Safa instead of the Kaaba
Only one wall of the Kaaba is a valid Qiblah
explanationEn: All four sides of the Kaaba are Qiblah; concentric circular rows inside Al-Masjid al-Haram symbolize the unity of the global Ummah revolving around one spiritual center.

questionEn: When you stand on Mount Safa or Mount Marwah during Sa'i and raise your hands to make dua, which direction do you face?
optionsEn: Face the floor continuously
Face due East away from the Kaaba
Face toward the Kaaba (even though a wall or colonnade stands in between on modern floors, face its known direction)
Spin slowly in circles
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ climbed Safa until he saw the House and faced it while proclaiming Takbir, Tahlil, and dua.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim raise their hands while making dua on Safa and Marwah (as in general dua), versus during Tawaf itself?
optionsEn: Raising both hands in dua while standing still on Safa and Marwah is explicit Sunnah (Muslim 1218), whereas during Tawaf walking one only raises the right hand briefly when saluting the Black Stone without walking with both hands raised continuously
Raise both hands overhead throughout all 7 laps of Tawaf
Point both feet toward the Kaaba
Never raise hands on Safa or Marwah
explanationEn: During Tawaf, one walks calmly with hands relaxed (raising only the right hand toward the Black Stone at the start of each lap); at Safa and Marwah, standing and raising both palms in earnest dua follows Jabir's (RA) report.

questionEn: What is the authentic wording of the dhikr the Prophet ﷺ recited three times on Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: 'SubhanAllah' 33 times only

'Allahu Akbar (3x), La ilaha illAllahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir; la ilaha illAllahu wahdah, anjaza wa'dah, wa nasara 'abdah, wa hazamal-ahzaba wahdah'
'Astaghfirullah' 100 times without facing Qiblah
Surah Al-Baqarah from beginning to end
explanationEn: He ﷺ said this declaration of Tawhid and victory, then made personal dua at length, repeated the dhikr a second time, made dua again, and repeated the dhikr a third time before descending toward Marwah.

questionEn: What historical victory is recalled by the phrase 'He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone' in the Safa-Marwah dhikr?
optionsEn: The building of Jeddah port
Allah's fulfillment of His promise at the Conquest of Makkah and the Battle of the Trench (al-Ahzab), reminding pilgrims that all triumph comes from Allah alone
A flood in Yemen
A pre-Islamic trade treaty
explanationEn: Reciting this on Safa—right where the Prophet ﷺ once stood calling Quraysh to Islam in early Makkah—connects the believer to Allah's faithfulness across history.

questionEn: Do you make the triple dhikr and dua again at the end of the 7th lap on Marwah, or after each turn 1–6?
optionsEn: It is forbidden to make dua on Marwah at all
One must repeat it 10 times on Marwah only
One must sit on Marwah for 2 hours

It is clearly Sunnah on Safa and Marwah at turns 1 through 6 (between laps); at the end of lap 7 on Marwah, some scholars say you may conclude with brief gratitude/dua while others note the Prophet's ﷺ Sa'i ended upon reaching Marwah
explanationEn: Every pause at Safa (start + turns 2, 4, 6) and Marwah (turns 1, 3, 5) is a golden opportunity for prolonged, heartfelt personal supplication.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim jog or run between the green lights during Sa'i if doing so would bump into elderly pilgrims, strollers, or wheelchairs?
optionsEn: Women must sprint faster than men
No; jogging between the green lights is a Sunnah for men ONLY when space permits safely—never sprint recklessly into crowds or risk injuring anyone
Everyone must jump over wheelchairs
Yes, sprinting fast is obligatory even if knocking people down
explanationEn: Safety and gentleness in the House of Allah always outrank an optional Sunnah pace; brisk walking/light jogging only in clear lanes preserves peace.

questionEn: If a male pilgrim forgets to jog between the green lights on lap 1 or lap 2 of Sa'i, does he owe any penalty or need to repeat those laps?
optionsEn: He owes a sheep
No penalty and no repetition; jogging between the green lights is a Sunnah, not a pillar or Wajib
He must repeat Tawaf
Yes, he must restart Sa'i from Safa
explanationEn: Walking calmly across the entire Mas'a still yields a 100% valid Sa'i.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is pushing an elderly parent in a wheelchair during Sa'i, should they run fast between the green lights?
optionsEn: Exit the Mas'a
Maintain a controlled, safe brisk pace only if the wheelchair lane is wide open and comfortable for the elder; never jolt or endanger the passenger
Push at top running speed through pedestrians
Leave the wheelchair behind to run alone
explanationEn: Dedicated wheelchair lanes in the Mas'a allow smooth, dignified rolling at a safe, steady speed.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performs Tawaf in the morning, rests at the hotel for a few hours due to heat/illness, and then returns to Masjid al-Haram in the evening to perform Sa'i?
optionsEn: Completely valid; while doing Sa'i soon after Tawaf is best and Sunnah, resting for a few hours (remaining in Ihram prohibitions throughout!) does not invalidate Sa'i
Invalid—Tawaf must be repeated
They may wear regular clothes during the hotel break
Sa'i becomes double (14 laps)
explanationEn: Crucially, the pilgrim must remember they are STILL in full Ihram during that hotel rest until Sa'i and Halq/Taqsir are completed!

questionEn: Can a pilgrim stay in Makkah for several days in a state of Ihram without finishing Sa'i just to enjoy extra days?
optionsEn: Delaying Sa'i without genuine need (like sudden illness or fatigue) is contrary to the Sunnah of completing Umrah promptly and unnecessarily prolongs the risk of Ihram violations
One can take off Ihram clothes during the delay
Ihram expires automatically after 24 hours
Yes, staying in Ihram for three weeks before Sa'i is Sunnah
explanationEn: Completing Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir promptly upon arrival protects the pilgrim from accidental violations and brings peaceful completion.

questionEn: What is 'Ihram al-Tamattu'' compared to 'Umrah al-Mufradah' if someone intends Hajj later in the year?
optionsEn: Every Umrah performed in any month automatically forces Hajj

If someone performs Umrah in Ramadan and returns home (or leaves Makkah) before Hajj, that is Umrah al-Mufradah; if they perform Umrah during Shawwal/Dhul-Qa'dah/early Dhul-Hijjah and remain in Makkah to do Hajj that same season, it becomes Hajj al-Tamattu'
Ramadan Umrah requires offering a Hajj Hady
They are completely unrelated concepts
explanationEn: Timing in Ashhur al-Hajj plus staying for Hajj in the same season defines Tamattu' (Qur'an 2:196).

questionEn: If a resident of Madinah visits Makkah for Umrah in Shawwal and then returns home to Madinah (NOT staying in Makkah for Hajj), do they owe a Tamattu' Hady?
optionsEn: No; because they returned home to Madinah after Umrah without combining it into Hajj in Makkah (and even if returning for Hajj later from home, majority scholars note returning home breaks the Tamattu' link except in specific details)
Yes, they must fast 10 days
Yes, every Shawwal Umrah owes a camel
Umrah in Shawwal is forbidden
explanationEn: Tamattu' Hady applies to one who enjoys Umrah in the Hajj months and proceeds onto Hajj in that same journey/season without returning to their distant homeland.

questionEn: What if a resident of Makkah itself performs Umrah (from Tan'im) during Shawwal and also Hajj that year—do Makkah residents owe a Tamattu' Hady?
optionsEn: Yes, Makkah residents owe two sheep
No; Surah Al-Baqarah 2:196 explicitly exempts those whose families are present at Al-Masjid al-Haram (residents of Makkah/Haram) from the Tamattu' Hady
Makkah residents cannot perform Hajj
They must travel to Jeddah to slaughter
explanationEn: Allah says: 'That is for he whose family is not in the area of Al-Masjid al-Haram' (2:196), showing divine ease and clarity.

questionEn: Why is shaving or trimming hair (Halq/Taqsir) in Umrah an act of worship rather than mere grooming?
optionsEn: It symbolizes total submission and humility before Allah, marking the solemn exit from the sacred state of Ihram just as Salam marks the end of Salah
Because hair becomes impure in Makkah
Because barbers near Marwah require customers
To cool down in summer heat only
explanationEn: Just as Takbir opens prayer and Salam closes it, Niyyah/Talbiyah opens Umrah and Halq/Taqsir closes it in humble obedience to Allah's command.

questionEn: What is the 'Qaza'' hairstyle warned against by the Prophet ﷺ, which men should avoid even when trimming hair after Umrah?
optionsEn: Trimming all hair evenly with clippers
Shaving the entire head cleanly
Leaving the head uncovered
Shaving part of the head bald while leaving other tufts/patches long—instead, either shave the whole head evenly (Halq) or trim all over evenly (Taqsir)
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ saw a boy with part of his head shaved and part left and forbade Qaza', saying: 'Shave all of it or leave all of it' (and in Umrah Taqsir, trim evenly all over).

questionEn: Can a pilgrim cut their own hair (using clean scissors or electric clippers) in their hotel room after Sa'i rather than going to a barber shop?
optionsEn: Cutting one's own hair invalidates Sa'i
No, only licensed Makkah barbers make Taqsir valid
Electric clippers are forbidden in Islam
Yes; performing Taqsir or Halq oneself (or having a spouse/friend assist) in private at the hotel is completely valid so long as hair is trimmed evenly across the whole head
explanationEn: Using clean personal clippers or scissors (especially for women trimming modestly in private, or men doing Taqsir cleanly) is convenient, hygienic, and 100% valid.

questionEn: Does Halq or Taqsir at the end of Umrah have to be performed inside the Haram boundaries of Makkah, or is it valid if someone performs it outside (e.g., if forgotten until leaving)?
optionsEn: Must be done only at Mina
Cannot be done at a hotel
Must be done inside the Black Stone corner

Doing Halq or Taqsir in Makkah (outside Marwah or at your hotel) is the standard Sunnah, though if someone forgot until leaving Makkah/Haram, performing it wherever they remember still completes Umrah validly
explanationEn: Unlike sacrificial slaughter tied to the Haram, hair-cutting may be completed anywhere if inadvertently delayed past departure—though doing it promptly in Makkah before changing clothes is proper.

questionEn: Wait: what if a pilgrim chooses to shave/trim right in the hotel instead of a street shop outside Marwah—must they stay in Ihram on the walk from Marwah to the hotel?
optionsEn: They may spray cologne in the hotel elevator first
Yes! On the walk back from Mount Marwah to the hotel, they are still fully in Ihram (avoiding perfume, head-cover, etc.) until they actually finish cutting their hair in the room
They must walk backward to the hotel
No, Ihram expires once you step onto the street
explanationEn: Keeping this simple reminder in mind prevents using scented hotel soap or putting on a cap before actually finishing Taqsir/Halq.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Makkah and notices a stray cut hair from Taqsir on the street or floor, do they have to bury all shaved hair inside the Haram?
optionsEn: Hair must be burned
Disposing of cut hair cleanly and respectfully in trash bins (or burying if outdoors naturally) is tidy and good; there is no obligation to transport hair home or bury it inside the mosque
Pilgrims must bury hair under Maqam Ibrahim
Leaving shaved hair in bins invalidates Umrah
explanationEn: Keeping the Sacred City clean by placing trimmed hair neatly into bins honors hygiene and public cleanliness.

questionEn: After exiting Ihram via Halq or Taqsir, which previously restricted things become completely lawful again?
optionsEn: Everything that was prohibited solely due to Ihram: regular stitched clothes, head coverings, perfume, cutting nails, and lawful marital intimacy
Only drinking Zamzam
Skipping daily prayers
Hunting wild animals inside Makkah's Haram (note: Haram hunting & native plants remain forbidden for everyone inside Makkah!)
explanationEn: Notice the sharp distinction: Ihram restrictions lift completely at Tahallul, whereas Haram Sanctuary laws (not hunting Haram birds/game or uprooting native Haram plants) bind everyone inside Makkah at all times!

questionEn: Why must pilgrims remember that Haram sanctity rules (like not pulling native plants or harming pigeons) still apply even AFTER shaving their head and wearing normal clothes?
optionsEn: Because normal clothes do not work in Makkah
Because Ihram lasts until returning to one's home airport
Because pigeons belong to Jeddah
Because those rules belong to the Sacred Territory of Makkah (al-Haram) itself, applying to both muhrims and non-muhrims alike
explanationEn: Distinguishing Ihram rules from Haram rules protects visitors from harming Makkah's protected sanctuary environment after Tahallul.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing 'Umrah' during an illness that prevents fasting or standing, such as severe knee arthritis?
optionsEn: Arthritis patients must crawl
Completely valid and deeply rewarded; one prays seated, uses a wheelchair/cart for Tawaf and Sa'i, and fulfills every rite within ability
Invalid unless standing upright for all 7 laps
They must wait until completely cured
explanationEn: Allah never burdens any soul beyond its capability (2:286); seated Salah and wheelchair Tawaf/Sa'i fulfill every pillar cleanly.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in severe pain and must take oral painkillers (like paracetamol/ibuprofen) while in Ihram, is that permissible?
optionsEn: Yes, taking oral medication, inhalers, or eye/ear drops for health is completely permissible in Ihram
Painkillers require a Dam
Only herbal tea is allowed
No, medicine breaks Ihram
explanationEn: Preserving health and treating pain with lawful medication has zero conflict with Ihram.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim wearing a medical nicotine patch or unscented adhesive pain-relief patch wear it while in Ihram?
optionsEn: No, any adhesive tape counts as stitched clothing
Patches invalidate Wudu
Only allowed on the left leg
Yes, unscented medical patches and bandages are permissible in Ihram
explanationEn: Unscented medical bandages and patches are permitted necessities (while making sure any waterproof patch does not cover a required Wudu limb unnecessarily unless genuinely needed as a medical dressing/jabirah over a wound).

questionEn: What is the 'Jabirah' rule if a pilgrim has a bandaged wound or cast on their forearm or foot when making Wudu for Tawaf?
optionsEn: Skip Wudu completely
Tear off surgical stitches to wash the wound directly
Cancel Tawaf until the cast comes off six weeks later
Wash the uncovered healthy skin around it and wipe lightly with wet hands over the medical bandage/cast itself without removing it or harming the wound
explanationEn: Islamic jurisprudence grants effortless relief via wiping over medical dressings (mas-h 'alal-jabirah) so injured believers can purify and perform Tawaf comfortably.

questionEn: If a pilgrim wears eyeglasses with a cloth cord around the back of the neck to prevent dropping them in crowds, does that violate Ihram?
optionsEn: Neck lanyards invalidate Tawaf
Yes, neck cords count as shirts
No; an eyeglass cord or lanyard holding an ID badge/Nusuk permit around the neck is completely permissible
Only metal chains are allowed
explanationEn: Practical accessories like lanyards, ID badges, waist pouches, and eyeglass straps are not tailored garments.

questionEn: Why is it recommended for pilgrims—especially elders—to wear a sturdy neck pouch or inner security belt for passport/hotel key/cash during Umrah?
optionsEn: Because carrying cash is forbidden without a pouch
Because pouches are a pillar of Tawaf
Because crowded zones can cause items in loose pockets to fall out or be targeted by pickpockets; securing essentials peacefully prevents distress
Because hotel keys must touch the Kaaba
explanationEn: Taking practical precautions ('Tie your camel, then trust in Allah') safeguards valuables so one's heart stays tranquil during worship.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ mean by 'Tie your camel first, then put your trust in Allah (Tawakkul)' when applied to an Umrah journey?
optionsEn: Walk without looking where you step
Travel without visas or water
Combine sincere reliance upon Allah with smart practical steps: learning rulings, staying hydrated, securing documents, wearing comfortable sandals, and pacing oneself
Skip medical prescriptions
explanationEn: True Tawakkul marries deep spiritual dependence on Allah with responsible preparation and care.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim loses their Ihram Rida' (upper wrap) or Izar gets torn badly during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Immediately wrap spare cloth or ask a companion/security for an extra sheet so Awrah remains strictly covered—if Awrah becomes exposed briefly by accident, cover it at once and continue (repeating only if a substantial portion of a lap was walked uncovered deliberately)
Continue walking naked around the Kaaba
Put on a stitched shirt without exiting Ihram
Leave Makkah permanently
explanationEn: Securing the Izar well with a belt prevents tearing/slipping; if an accident occurs, prioritizing instant modesty preserves dignity and validity.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim wear an Ihram sheet that has small brand logos or faint woven stripes, or must it be 100% plain?
optionsEn: Any small weave invalidates Umrah
Only silk sheets are valid
Designer logos are mandatory
Plain white cotton is best and most modest, though a small manufacturer tag or subtle woven border does not invalidate Ihram
explanationEn: Simplicity without ostentatious display reflects Ihram's spirit, while minor fabric weaves or tags carry no legal harm.

questionEn: Why should men avoid silk Ihram garments?
optionsEn: Silk is allowed only during Sa'i
Silk is forbidden for women too
Pure natural silk (harir) is always forbidden for Muslim men to wear—both in and outside Ihram
Silk melts in Makkah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade pure silk and gold for men of his Ummah (Bukhari 5837); soft breathable cotton terry or woven cotton is both lawful and ideal.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Umrah Tawaf in the heat while holding a small handheld battery fan or misting bottle of plain water?
optionsEn: Cooling oneself is forbidden during Umrah
Completely permissible (as long as the mist is pure unscented water and does not splash others uncomfortably)
Plain water mist breaks Wudu
Battery fans violate Ihram
explanationEn: Cooling oneself safely with plain water prevents heat exhaustion without infringing any Ihram rule.

questionEn: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to swim or immerse in a pool/tub to cool off?
optionsEn: Water above the ankles is banned in Ihram
Immersing in water washes away Niyyah
Bathing or immersing gently in plain unscented water to cool off or clean up is permissible (just avoid chlorine/scented additives if scented, avoid rubbing hair vigorously, and cover Awrah properly)
Only Zamzam water may touch skin
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) and Umar (RA) entered water/baths while in Ihram; ordinary bathing never breaks Ihram.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Hajj, Bab Ightisal al-Muhrim)

questionEn: If a pilgrim is unsure whether they already exited Ihram because they forgot whether they trimmed their hair, what should they do?
optionsEn: Repeat Tawaf seven times
Return to Jeddah
Assume they are free immediately
Treat themselves as still in Ihram until they actually perform Taqsir/Halq cleanly, since certainty of entering Ihram is only lifted by certainty of completing Halq/Taqsir
explanationEn: By the maxim 'Certainty is not removed by doubt' (al-yaqin la yazulu bish-shakk), one remains bound by Ihram until sure Halq/Taqsir occurred.

questionEn: What Prophetic travel supplication is Sunnah to recite upon sitting in your vehicle or boarding an airplane to depart for Umrah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Takathur seven times
'Allahu Akbar (3x), Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila rabbina lamunqalibun...'
'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim' three times
'Bismillah' before sleeping only
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated this complete travel dua in Sahih Muslim (1342), glorifying Allah for subjugating transport and asking for righteousness, piety, and safe return to family and property.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verses form the core of the Prophetic travel supplication recited at the start of an Umrah flight or bus journey?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Zukhruf 43:13–14 ('Glory be to Him who subjected this to us, and we could never have controlled it, and indeed to our Lord we will return')
Surah Al-Masad 111:1–2
Surah Al-Humazah 104:1–2
Surah Al-Qari'ah 101:1–3
explanationEn: Surah Al-Zukhruf (43:13–14) teaches travelers gratitude to Allah who enables safe travel across land, sea, and sky while remembering our ultimate return to Him.

questionEn: In the Prophetic travel dua (Sahih Muslim 1342), what three things does a traveler ask Allah to grant upon the journey?
optionsEn: Righteousness (al-Birr), piety (al-Taqwa), and deeds that please Him ('wa minal-'amali ma tarda'), plus ease and closeness of distance
Fame among neighbors
Luxury hotels, fast flights, and fine souvenirs
Exemption from daily prayers
explanationEn: Before even stepping onto the plane, the Prophetic travel dua focuses the Umrah traveler's heart on Birr, Taqwa, and deeds pleasing to Allah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah to protect his family and home from when reciting the travel dua before setting out?
optionsEn: Seeking refuge from seeing friends ever again
'O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Guardian (Khalifah) over the family'—and seeking refuge from travel hardship, gloomy return, and evil sight regarding wealth and family
Asking for rain every hour
Asking to forget all relatives
explanationEn: Entrusting one's household to Allah ('al-Khalifatu fil-ahl') brings immense peace of mind while away performing Umrah.

questionEn: What dhikr did the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions recite when ascending high terrain (such as climbing hills toward Makkah) and when descending into valleys?
optionsEn: 'Allahu Akbar' (Takbir) when ascending and 'SubhanAllah' (Tasbih) when descending
Remaining silent on every hill
Reciting Surah Al-Fil uphill only
Clapping hands uphill and whistling downhill
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (2993) that whenever they ascended they pronounced Takbir and whenever they descended they pronounced Tasbih—reminding pilgrims that Allah is Greater than every peak and exalted above every low.

questionEn: Which short Prophetic dua is recommended whenever stopping or lodging at a hotel, airport, or rest station along the Umrah route?
optionsEn: Lighting incense in every room
Knocking on doors seven times
'A'udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq' (I seek refuge in Allah's perfect words from the evil of what He created)
Reciting Surah Al-Naba' backward
explanationEn: Khawlah bint Hakim (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ promised that whoever stops at a lodging and says this dua will not be harmed by anything until departing from it.

questionEn: Why does Surah Al-Baqarah (2:197) emphasize 'And whatever good you do—Allah knows it' right in the middle of the pilgrimage verses?
optionsEn: To encourage hidden acts of kindness—helping elders, sharing water, patience in lines—even when nobody else sees or applauds them
To discourage smiling at strangers
To forbid good deeds outside Makkah
To require announcing every charity on microphones
explanationEn: In crowded sanctuaries, quiet unheralded kindness to fellow guests of Allah is noticed and treasured by the All-Knowing Lord.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:200–202), what contrast does Allah draw between two kinds of people making dua during pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Those who ask ONLY for worldly things ('Our Lord, give us in this world') having no share in the Hereafter, versus believers who ask for goodness in BOTH this world and the Hereafter and protection from the Fire
Those who walk fast versus those who ride camels
Those who speak Arabic versus those who speak other tongues
Those who stay in hotels versus tents
explanationEn: That is why 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar' (2:201) became the most frequent dua of the Prophet ﷺ during Tawaf and life!

questionEn: According to Anas ibn Malik (RA), which comprehensive dua was the one the Prophet ﷺ recited MOST frequently in general, and specifically between Rukn al-Yamani and the Black Stone?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab'
'Subhanaka Allahumma' alone
'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar'
Only a prayer for worldly wealth
explanationEn: Anas (RA) confirmed this short Qur'anic prayer encompasses every wholesome blessing of both worlds and eternal safety.

questionEn: What did Ibrahim (AS) ask Allah in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:126) for the city of Makkah?
optionsEn: 'Fill this valley with gold mines only'
'Make this city a fortress closed to believers'
'Keep travelers out of this valley'
'My Lord, make this a secure city (Baladan Amina) and provide its people with fruits—whoever of them believes in Allah and the Last Day'
explanationEn: Allah granted Ibrahim's (AS) prayer—and even extended earthly sustenance to all inhabitants while reminding believers of gratitude and accountability.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas (28:57) and Surah Al-Ankabut (29:67), what blessing unique to Makkah does Allah remind its people and visitors to appreciate?
optionsEn: That Makkah never needs worship
That Makkah receives snow every month
That Allah established Makkah as a 'Haram Amina' (secure sanctuary) where fruits and provisions from every region are brought in abundance while turmoil raged around them
That Makkah has the tallest rivers in Asia
explanationEn: Every Umrah pilgrim witnesses this living miracle of Ibrahim's (AS) prayer—fresh fruits, security, and people gathering peacefully from every corner of the globe.
