questionEn: Which short Makkah surah reminds Quraysh and believers to worship the Lord of the Kaaba ('Rabb hadhal-Bayt') in gratitude for food against hunger and security against fear?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Ma'un (Chapter 107)
Surah Quraysh (Chapter 106)
Surah Al-Kafirun (Chapter 109)
Surah Al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112)
explanationEn: Surah Quraysh links trade security and abundant nourishment in Makkah directly to worshipping 'the Lord of this House' (the Kaaba).

questionEn: In Surah Al-Tin (95:3), by which city does Allah swear alongside the fig, the olive, and Mount Sinai?
optionsEn: Cairo
'Wa hadhal-baladil-amin' — 'And by this City of Security (Makkah)'
Baghdad
Damascus
explanationEn: Commentators agree 'this City of Security' refers to Makkah, linking the sanctuaries of revelation from Sinai and Jerusalem to the final revelation in Makkah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Balad (90:1–2), Allah swears by 'this city' (Makkah) and specifically mentions the Prophet ﷺ being lawful/resident in it—what does that affirm?
optionsEn: That Surah Al-Balad speaks about Ta'if
That no believer may live in Makkah
That Makkah is an ordinary town
Makkah's supreme honor as the birthplace of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and seat of the Sacred House
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas and classical exegetes note the immense honor bestowed upon Makkah through both the Kaaba and the Prophet's ﷺ presence there.

questionEn: Which verse in Surah Al-Imran (3:96) declares the Kaaba in Bakkah as the very first House appointed for all humanity?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Imran 3:14
'Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah—blessed and a guidance for the worlds'
Surah Al-Imran 3:185
Surah Al-Imran 3:190
explanationEn: 'Bakkah' is an ancient Qur'anic name for Makkah (or specifically the Mataf/Kaaba area where crowds gather), highlighting its universal welcome for all peoples.

questionEn: Why do scholars explain Makkah is also called 'Bakkah' in Surah Al-Imran (3:96)?
optionsEn: From 'tabakka' (crowding/thronging together in humility) or breaking the arrogance of tyrants who seek to harm it
Because it was built in a single week
Because only camels could enter
Because it was named after a Roman river
explanationEn: Classical lexicons and Tafsir works cite both meanings—people thronging shoulder-to-shoulder around the Kaaba in Tawaf and the humbling of arrogant oppressors.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Imran (3:97), what three 'clear signs' (Ayatun Bayyinat) are specifically noted at the Sacred House?
optionsEn: Snowfall on Safa
Clear signs, foremost among them Maqam Ibrahim, and whoever enters it is safe—alongside the duty of pilgrimage for whoever can find a way
Three gold gates only
A palace on Mount Thawr
explanationEn: Surah Al-Imran 3:97 highlights Maqam Ibrahim, the Sanctuary's aura of safety, and humanity's duty to make pilgrimage to Allah's House when able.

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:35), what did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) pray immediately after asking Allah to make Makkah secure?
optionsEn: 'Give my sons absolute kingship over Persia'
'Exempt my family from prayer'
'Build tall towers around Safa'
'And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols' (wa jnubni wa baniyya an na'budal-asnam)
explanationEn: Even the Father of Prophets feared falling into shirk and begged Allah for steadfast monotheism—teaching every Umrah pilgrim humility and constant vigilance over their Tawhid.

questionEn: What did Ibrahim (AS) pray in Surah Ibrahim (14:40–41) while standing in the Makkah sanctuary—a dua every Umrah pilgrim can echo in Tawaf?
optionsEn: 'My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication. Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established'
'My Lord, make my descendants skip Fajr'
'Forgive only me and nobody else'
'Grant wealth without worship'
explanationEn: Ibrahim's (AS) moving prayer weaves together devotion in Salah, pious offspring, forgiveness for parents, and mercy for the entire community of believers.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj (22:25), how seriously does Allah warn against committing oppression or profaning sanctity ('Ilhad') inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Wrongdoing in Makkah carries half the sin of elsewhere
Whoever intends therein deviation or wrongdoing unjustly, Allah causes him to taste a painful punishment
Minor wrongdoing in Makkah is ignored
Only outward actions count, never intentions
explanationEn: Scholars warn that just as good deeds are multiplied in Makkah, intending evil, fraud, arrogance, or harm inside the Sacred Sanctuary is unusually grave—calling pilgrims to extreme conscientiousness.

questionEn: How should a pilgrim regard commercial honesty (e.g., among merchants or customers in Makkah markets) in light of Surah Al-Hajj (22:25)?
optionsEn: Charging triple prices to foreigners is fine in Makkah
Lying in trade is overlooked during Ramadan
Be strictly honest, fair, gentle, and never cheat, shortchange, or exploit fellow pilgrims in the Sacred Land
Pilgrims should bargain harshly with insults
explanationEn: Honoring Makkah's sanctity includes pure truthfulness in transactions, gentleness in negotiation, and never taking unfair advantage of visitors.

questionEn: Why did Allah remind pilgrims in Surah Al-Hajj (22:30) that honoring Allah's sacred ordinances ('Hurumatillah') is better for them with their Lord?
optionsEn: Because outward dress matters more than hearts
Because pilgrims should avoid visiting family
Because only kings can enter the Kaaba
Because revering the boundaries of Ihram, the Haram, and its rituals elevates spiritual rank and sincerity
explanationEn: Honoring Hurumatillah means loving what Allah made sacred and staying conscientiously clear of what He prohibited during pilgrimage.

questionEn: When making dua during Tawaf or at Safa/Marwah, is it permissible to supplicate in one's native language (e.g., English, Urdu, Malay, Turkish, French) if one does not know extensive Arabic duas?
optionsEn: Yes! Allah understands every language and hears the whispers of every heart; praying earnestly in your mother tongue during Tawaf, Sa'i, and after Salah is completely permissible and deeply encouraged (while keeping formal Salah recitation itself in Arabic)
Only Arabic speakers may raise hands at Safa
One must remain silent unless fluent in classical Arabic
No, duas in English are rejected by Allah
explanationEn: Sincerity and heartfelt understanding matter immensely in dua; mixing memorized Prophetic Arabic duas with heartfelt prayers in your own tongue brings deep humility.

questionEn: What is the best posture of the heart when reciting the dua 'Allahumma inna nas'aluka ridaka wal-jannah, wa na'udhu bika min sakhatika wan-nar' during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Expecting automatic immunity from future sin
Shouting to impress nearby tour groups
Reciting mechanically while texting on a phone
Humble hope and awe—begging Allah for His pleasure and Paradise and protection from His displeasure and Hellfire
explanationEn: Pairing sincere awe (khawf) with deep hope (raja') makes every circuit around the Kaaba alive with devotion.

questionEn: Which Prophetic dua for forgiveness did the Prophet ﷺ teach Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) that is wonderful to recite in the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim (before Salam) and during Tawaf?
optionsEn: 'Subhana man la yashghaluhu sam'un' ten times
'Astaghfirullah' once without reflection
'Allahumma ahlikil-kuffar' only
'Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathiran wa la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa ant, faghfir li maghfiratan min 'indika warhamni, innaka antal-Ghafurur-Rahim'
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (834), this deeply humble confession of need and plea for Allah's mercy captures the essence of standing before the Sacred House.

questionEn: Which supplication did the Prophet ﷺ teach Aisha (RA) for Laylat al-Qadr—also deeply beloved to recite during Ramadan Umrah Tawafs?
optionsEn: 'La ilaha illa Anta Subhanaka' only
'Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana' only
'Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru...' only
'Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbul-'afwa fa'fu 'anni' (O Allah, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me)
explanationEn: Asking Allah for complete pardon ('afw—erasing sin without trace) in the last ten nights of Ramadan inside Al-Masjid al-Haram is among the sweetest spiritual moments of Ramadan Umrah.

questionEn: Is sending Salawat (blessings) upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ during Tawaf and Sa'i encouraged?
optionsEn: Salawat may only be said on Mondays
No, Salawat is permitted only in Madinah
Yes; sending Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ is among the finest acts of dhikr and keys to having one's supplications answered
Salawat breaks Wudu during Tawaf
explanationEn: Scholars encourage praising Allah, sending Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ, and then making personal dua—reflecting the etiquette of accepted supplication (Tirmidhi 3477).

questionEn: Why is it praiseworthy to begin and end personal duas at Safa, Marwah, and after Zamzam with praise of Allah and Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ taught a companion who prayed without praising Allah or sending Salawat to begin with glorifying Allah, then send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and then ask whatever he wished
Because otherwise the Mataf doors close
Because it replaces Surah Al-Fatihah
Because it reduces the number of Sa'i laps
explanationEn: Fudalah ibn Ubayd (RA) narrated this golden etiquette of dua in Sunan Abi Dawud and Jami' al-Tirmidhi.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about making dua for an absent Muslim brother or sister—a beautiful practice to carry into your Tawaf and Sa'i list?
optionsEn: Only dua for oneself is answered in Makkah
Whenever a Muslim supplicates for an absent brother/sister, an appointed angel says: 'Amin, and for you the same!'
Mentioning friends' names during Tawaf is forbidden
Duas for others reduce one's own blessings
explanationEn: Bringing a thoughtful list of family, sick loved ones, teachers, and the struggling Ummah to pray for during Tawaf and Sa'i invites angelic 'Amin' upon your own life too.

questionEn: What is the virtue of making abundant Istighfar (seeking Allah's forgiveness) during Tawaf around the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Istighfar softens the heart, opens doors of mercy, and aligns with the purpose of Umrah as spiritual purification and expiation
Istighfar replaces Wudu
Istighfar is reserved only for Friday evening
Saying 'Astaghfirullah' during Raml is forbidden
explanationEn: Combining Sayyid al-Istighfar and heartfelt repentance while walking around Allah's House embodies the humble servant returning to their Lord.

questionEn: How does Sayyid al-Istighfar ('Allahumma Anta Rabbi la ilaha illa Anta...') connect deeply with the spirit of Umrah?
optionsEn: It is recited only by children
It affirms Allah's Lordship, admits our servant covenant ('wa ana 'ala 'ahdika wa wa'dika mastata't'), thanks Him for His blessings, and confesses sins seeking sole forgiveness from Him
It lists tribal ancestors
It requests worldly business discounts
explanationEn: Reciting Sayyid al-Istighfar with conviction morning and evening during one's stay in Makkah deepens gratitude and spiritual renewal.

questionEn: What is the meaning of 'Al-Tawaf bil-Qalb' (Tawaf of the heart) emphasized by spiritual scholars like Ibn al-Qayyim and al-Ghazali?
optionsEn: Ignoring Wudu if your heart feels good
Ensuring that while the body circles the stone Kaaba, the heart revolves in awe, love, and obedience around the Lord of the Kaaba
Skipping physical Tawaf altogether and imagining it at home
Counting laps only in your sleep
explanationEn: Physical Tawaf without presence of heart misses its soul, while combining valid outward Sunnah with inner reverence turns every step into worship.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:125), what did Allah covenant with Ibrahim and Isma'il (AS) regarding purifying the Sacred House?
optionsEn: 'Allow only travelers from Iraq'
'Keep the House closed except once a decade'
'Purify only the outer plaza'
'Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf, those who stay [there for worship / I'tikaf], and those who bow and prostrate'
explanationEn: Every Umrah pilgrim performing Tawaf, sitting in reflection/I'tikaf, and bowing in Salah behind Maqam Ibrahim directly fulfills the purpose mentioned in 2:125.

questionEn: What does 'I'tikaf' inside Al-Masjid al-Haram mean for an Umrah visitor who already finished their Umrah?
optionsEn: Selling goods near the mosque gates
Leaving Makkah immediately
Sleeping across prayer rows blocking others
Making intention to remain in the mosque devoted to Salah, Qur'an recitation, and dhikr—even for an hour or day between prayers (as well as full 10-day Ramadan I'tikaf)
explanationEn: Sitting peacefully between Fajr and Sunrise (Ishraq) or Maghrib and Isha in Al-Masjid al-Haram with I'tikaf intention multiplies spiritual benefit.

questionEn: What reward did the Prophet ﷺ mention for praying Fajr in congregation, sitting remembering Allah until sunrise, and then praying two rak'ahs (Salat al-Ishraq)?
optionsEn: Reward equal to a complete Hajj and Umrah—'complete, complete, complete' (not replacing the obligation, yet huge in spiritual reward)
Exemption from Friday prayer
Reward equal to one voluntary fast
Exemption from Zakah
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated this encouraging Hadith in Jami' al-Tirmidhi (586)—making sunrise dhikr in Al-Masjid al-Haram after Umrah extra precious.

questionEn: When sitting inside Al-Masjid al-Haram to read Qur'an after completing Umrah, what etiquette should be observed toward fellow pilgrims?
optionsEn: Keep voice soft so you do not drown out neighbors praying or reading, return Mushafs neatly to shelves, and leave open space for newcomers
Stack five bags across empty prayer spots for friends arriving two hours later
Rest shoes on Qur'an stands
Read loudly into a portable speaker
explanationEn: Remember the Prophet ﷺ gently corrected companions raising their voices in Qur'an inside the mosque so they would not confuse one another's recitation.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim reserve spots in Al-Masjid al-Haram using prayer rugs, bags, or water bottles hours before prayer while leaving to shop or sleep?
optionsEn: Yes, laying 10 empty rugs for an entire tour group is Sunnah
Only VIP guests may sit in front rows
Yes, bags may hold spots all week
No; scholars disapprove saving empty space with rugs/items while absent—instead, whoever arrives early and sits there personally has first right to that spot
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that mosques belong equally to all worshippers who arrive early; blocking space while absent deprives arriving elders and worshippers of shade and rows.

questionEn: What is the etiquette of walking through seated rows inside Al-Masjid al-Haram if you arrive slightly late for Jama'ah?
optionsEn: Fill open gaps peacefully without stepping over people's necks/shoulders or pushing through seated worshippers
Step directly over seated elderly men's shoulders to reach row 1
Force seated worshippers to stand up and move for you
Walk across prayer rugs wearing muddy outdoor shoes
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ rebuked a man stepping over necks on Jumu'ah, saying: 'Sit down, for you have harmed [others]!'

questionEn: How should outdoor shoes be handled when entering Al-Masjid al-Haram for Umrah?
optionsEn: Place them neatly inside a personal cloth/drawstring shoe bag carried with you (or in designated shoe racks)—never drop them loosely in walkways or carry them soles-out touching other pilgrims' white Ihram clothes
Walk on the prayer carpets wearing street sandals
Throw sandals onto the Kaaba steps
Leave sandals scattered across the Mataf entrance stairs
explanationEn: Using a simple shoe pouch keeps sandals from getting lost, keeps paths clear, and avoids staining anyone's clean white Ihram.

questionEn: What does seeing Muslims of every skin color, language, and nation walking shoulder-to-shoulder in identical white Ihram sheets symbolize?
optionsEn: That cultural languages must be erased
Universal brotherhood and equality in Islam—fulfilling the Farewell Sermon message that no Arab is superior to a non-Arab except through Taqwa
That nationality determines reward
That wealthy pilgrims stand in separate rings
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13) and the Prophet's ﷺ Farewell Sermon come vividly alive during Umrah Tawaf, dissolving pride of race, wealth, or class.

questionEn: How should an Umrah pilgrim interact with Haram janitors, water-dispensers, and wheelchair attendants?
optionsEn: Leave trash on the floor expecting them to clean it up immediately
Refuse to say Salam to workers
Ignore them or bark impatient orders
With genuine warmth, gratitude, patience, polite smiles, and respect—never looking down on service workers who keep Allah's House clean
explanationEn: Good character (husn al-khuluq) toward humble workers in Makkah and Madinah reflects true reverence for the Prophet's ﷺ example.
reference: Sahih Muslim 45 (on removing arrogance); Riyad al-Salihin

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if someone accidentally steps on their heel or bumps them hard during a crowded Tawaf or Sa'i?
optionsEn: Forgive graciously, smile, say 'May Allah forgive us both' or 'No problem', and guard your tongue from anger or sharp retorts
Shove them back harder
Follow them outside to argue
Curse them loudly in the Mataf
explanationEn: Remember Qur'an 2:197 ('no disputing during pilgrimage') and 41:34 ('repel evil with that which is better'); swallowing anger in Makkah safeguards your reward.

questionEn: Why do scholars advise keeping conversation during meals and hotel breaks in Makkah centered on gratitude, Seerah stories, and reflection rather than gossip or political arguments?
optionsEn: Because talking at hotel tables breaks Ihram
Because hotels forbid talking
Because sharing food is forbidden in Makkah
To protect the purity of the heart and avoid wasting sacred Makkah hours in backbiting (ghibah) or idle quarrels (jidal)
explanationEn: Time spent in Makkah is precious; guarding the tongue from ghibah and idle debate preserves the spiritual glow of Umrah.

questionEn: What is the virtue of giving quiet charity (Sadaqah) to genuine needy laborers or feeding fellow pilgrims during an Umrah trip?
optionsEn: Giving charity cancels Tawaf
Charity in the Sacred City of Makkah carries multiplied reward and expresses gratitude to Allah for inviting you to His House
Charity is forbidden during Umrah
Only gold coins count as charity in Makkah
explanationEn: Feeding others (it'am al-ta'am) and spreading peace were among the earliest acts of righteousness taught by the Prophet ﷺ; offering bottled water, dates, or meals quietly in Makkah is deeply blessed (while avoiding supporting organized street begging gangs inside prayer rows).

questionEn: Why should pilgrims avoid making a public show of how many Umrahs they have completed ('This is my 12th Umrah!')?
optionsEn: Because talking about past trips breaks Wudu
Because counting trips invalidates the 12th one
Because boasting about numbers risks Riya' (showing off) and 'Ujub (self-conceit), which can burn away spiritual reward
Because performing more than 3 Umrahs is illegal
explanationEn: Keeping worship humble between oneself and Allah protects sincerity from ego.

questionEn: When returning home after Umrah, why should a pilgrim avoid demanding to be called by special honorific titles or expecting praise from neighbors?
optionsEn: Honorific titles are obligatory in Islam
Neighbors must bow to returning pilgrims
Sincerity seeks Allah's acceptance alone—not human applause or status—and true gratitude shows in improved character and quiet worship at home
Otherwise Umrah must be repeated
explanationEn: Umar (RA) and the pious predecessors wept out of awe wondering whether Allah accepted their deeds rather than boasting over titles.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the sign of Allah's forgiveness and acceptance when a servant strives in worship—what should the returning pilgrim strive to maintain?
optionsEn: Sleeping all day for forty days
Never speaking to neighbors again
Steadfastness (Istiqamah) in daily prayers, honesty, kindness to family, and staying away from past sins
Abandoning work completely
explanationEn: Ibn Rajab and classical scholars note that 'the reward of a good deed is another good deed after it'; continuing in obedience after returning from Makkah is the brightest sign of an accepted Umrah.

questionEn: Is there any truth to the cultural myth that after performing Umrah, a pilgrim must never listen to ordinary permissible news, must stay indoors 40 days, or cannot touch non-pilgrims?
optionsEn: Yes, staying indoors for 40 days is an Umrah pillar
No; that is an unfounded cultural superstition—upon returning home, a Muslim resumes normal lawful family, community, and work life with renewed spiritual mindfulness
Returning pilgrims may not shake hands for a week
Working within 30 days cancels Umrah
explanationEn: Islam celebrates active, ethical engagement in family and society right after returning from Makkah.

questionEn: When welcoming guests back home with small gifts like Zamzam water and Madinah Ajwa dates, what intention makes that Sunnah doubly blessed?
optionsEn: Refusing to share Zamzam with non-relatives
Sharing Allah's blessing generously out of love and hospitality—not showing off—and asking loved ones to make dua for acceptance and future invitation to the Haramayn
Bragging about hotel prices
Charging guests for each cup of Zamzam
explanationEn: Gifting Zamzam and dates spreads joy and kindles longing in others' hearts to visit the House of Allah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ promise regarding Ajwa dates of Madinah (often brought back alongside Zamzam on Umrah-Madinah trips)?
optionsEn: 'Ajwa dates must be eaten only during Tawaf'
'Only kings may eat Ajwa dates'
'Ajwa dates replace Wudu'
'Whoever eats seven Ajwa dates in the morning will not be harmed by poison or magic that day'
explanationEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) narrated this authentic blessing in Sahih al-Bukhari (5445) and Sahih Muslim (2047).

questionEn: If an Umrah traveler visits Madinah before Makkah (entering from Madinah airport first), what etiquette honors Masjid al-Nabawi before setting off for Umrah?
optionsEn: Entering Ihram inside Masjid al-Nabawi three days early
Walking around the Green Dome seven times like Tawaf

Praying calmly in Masjid al-Nabawi, sending peaceful salutations at the Prophet's ﷺ grave and those of Abu Bakr and Umar (RA), visiting Quba on Saturday if possible, and then entering Ihram cleanly at Dhul-Hulayfah on departure to Makkah
Skipping Masjid al-Nabawi altogether if traveling via Madinah
explanationEn: Remember never to circle the Sacred Chamber—salute respectfully facing the grave (or Qiblah for personal dua), then travel to Dhul-Hulayfah to begin Umrah Ihram.

questionEn: If an Umrah traveler visits Makkah FIRST and Madinah AFTER completing Umrah, do they wear Ihram when traveling to Madinah?
optionsEn: Madinah has its own mandatory Ihram sheets
No! Ihram ends completely upon Halq/Taqsir in Makkah; the journey onward to Madinah is made in normal clean modest clothing
Yes, pilgrims must wear Ihram inside Madinah too
Yes, they must shave again at Masjid Quba
explanationEn: Madinah has no Ihram ritual; Ihram belongs exclusively to Umrah and Hajj in Makkah.

questionEn: Why is visiting Masjid Quba on a Saturday (or any day) during the Madinah leg of an Umrah trip so beloved?
optionsEn: Because praying there cancels Fard Hajj
Because Masjid Quba is a Miqat for Yemen
The Prophet ﷺ used to go to Masjid Quba every Saturday walking or riding, and taught that making Wudu at home and praying two rak'ahs in Masjid Quba carries the reward of an Umrah!
Because Masjid Quba replaces Tawaf around the Kaaba
explanationEn: Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) narrated this magnificent virtue (Bukhari 1193; Ibn Majah 1412)—though in spiritual reward only, not replacing actual Umrah in Makkah.

questionEn: Does praying two rak'ahs in Masjid Quba replace the actual obligation of traveling to Makkah for Umrah?
optionsEn: Only during Dhul-Hijjah
Yes, after praying at Quba seven times
No; just like Umrah in Ramadan equaling Hajj in reward, Masjid Quba grants an Umrah-equivalent spiritual reward without replacing the actual physical rite of Umrah at the Kaaba
Yes, residents of Madinah never need to visit Makkah
explanationEn: Equivalence in reward (ajr) encourages devotion without ever abolishing the physical acts commanded by Allah in Makkah.

questionEn: What is the virtue of praying inside Masjid al-Nabawi during an Umrah-and-Ziyarah itinerary?
optionsEn: Equal to 10 prayers
Equal to 100,000 prayers
A single prayer in Masjid al-Nabawi is better than 1,000 prayers in any other mosque except Al-Masjid al-Haram
Only Friday prayers are multiplied
explanationEn: Combined with 100,000x in Makkah, visiting both Sanctuaries on an Umrah journey offers unmatched opportunities for devotion.

questionEn: What spiritual attitude should fill a believer's heart during the final moments before leaving Makkah after Umrah?
optionsEn: Relief that worship is finally over
Complaining loudly about hotel logistics
Gratitude to Allah for facilitating the visit, humble pleading for acceptance ('Rabbana taqabbal minna'), and sincere longing to return again
Pride that one is superior to non-travelers
explanationEn: Just as Ibrahim and Isma'il (AS) begged 'Rabbana taqabbal minna innaka Antas-Sami'ul-'Alim' (2:127) while building the House, pilgrims depart begging Allah for acceptance.

questionEn: Why did Ibrahim and Isma'il (AS) pray 'Our Lord, accept from us' (Rabbana taqabbal minna) even while raising the very walls of the Kaaba by direct divine command?
optionsEn: Because they expected immediate worldly payment
Because they were unsure which city they were in
To model supreme humility—never taking acceptance for granted, knowing only Allah accepts sincere deeds from the God-conscious (5:27)
Because they forgot how to pray
explanationEn: Echoing 'Rabbana taqabbal minna' after Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq keeps arrogance away and anchors the soul in humble hope.

questionEn: What does 'Rabbana wa-j'alna muslimayni laka wa min dhurriyyatina ummatan muslimatan lak' (2:128) inspire Umrah pilgrims to pray for?
optionsEn: Steadfast submission for oneself AND righteous Muslim generations among one's children and grandchildren
Long vacations in Europe
Exemption from prayer for grandchildren
Worldly palaces for children only
explanationEn: Standing near Maqam Ibrahim praying this exact Abrahamic dua for your family and future generations carries timeless spiritual power.

questionEn: What is the meaning of Allah's description of the Kaaba in Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:97) as 'Qiyaman lin-nas' (a means of standing/support for mankind)?
optionsEn: The Kaaba anchors humanity's spiritual, moral, and communal order—uniting believers in worship, safety, and mercy
People must stand upright 24 hours without sleeping
It refers to a bridge across the Red Sea
Only merchants benefit from Makkah
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) and exegetes explain the Sacred House and Sacred Months uphold both religious devotion and worldly stability for humanity.

questionEn: Which two emotions should balance a pilgrim's heart while standing before the Kaaba for the first time?
optionsEn: Boredom
Anger at crowds
Deep reverence/awe of Allah's majesty and overflowing love/hope in Allah's boundless mercy
Fear without hope, or carelessness without awe
explanationEn: Scholars liken worship to a bird flying with two wings: love/hope in Allah's mercy and awe/fear of His majesty.

questionEn: How can a Muslim who cannot physically or financially travel for Umrah right now still earn Umrah-like rewards while preparing sincerely?
optionsEn: Perform Tawaf around a picture of the Kaaba at home (strictly invalid!)
Pretend on social media to be in Makkah
Skip saving and take high-interest loans

Make sincere intention and save halal means patiently, pray Fajr in congregation and sit until Ishraq (Tirmidhi 586), and visit Masjid Quba when in Madinah—for Allah rewards sincere longing and intention
explanationEn: Never create innovations like circling photos or objects at home; instead combine sincere dua for invitation to Makkah with authentic Prophetic daily deeds carrying Umrah-like reward.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say upon returning from Tabuk regarding companions left behind in Madinah due to valid excuse—how does this console Muslims unable to travel for Umrah due to illness or caring for frail parents?
optionsEn: 'Indeed in Madinah there are people who, whenever you traveled a distance or crossed a valley, were with you [in reward], held back only by valid excuse'
'Only travelers receive any reward ever'
'Ill people lose all past deeds'
'Caregivers are sinful for staying home'
explanationEn: Anyone prevented by genuine poverty, chronic illness, or caring for dependent parents shares in the reward through sincere longing and intention.

questionEn: Why is it important not to delay performing obligatory Umrah/Hajj for decades once one IS healthy and financially able?
optionsEn: Because health, wealth, and life are unpredictable—the Prophet ﷺ urged hastening to pilgrimage before illness, poverty, or unforeseen obstacles intervene
Because Miqats close after age 50
Because airlines ban older passengers over 35
Because Umrah is invalid for seniors
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ advised: 'Hasten to Hajj (and likewise obligatory Umrah), for none of you knows what obstacle may befall him.'

questionEn: What does the phrase 'Labbaika la sharika laka labbayk' affirm against subtle modern forms of shirk or superstition?
optionsEn: That pilgrims may wear protective talismans
That stars decide Umrah acceptance
That only stones bring good fortune
That no saint, amulet, lucky charm, astrology, or human partner shares in Allah's power to grant wishes, heal, or forgive—all worship and hope belong strictly to Allah
explanationEn: Entering Makkah chanting 'La sharika lak' cleanses the heart from superstition and centers trust solely in Allah.

questionEn: When praying inside Al-Masjid al-Haram after Umrah, why should men and women dress cleanly and modestly (even outside Ihram)?
optionsEn: Because only white clothes are valid outside Ihram
To honor Qur'an 7:31 ('Take your adornment at every mosque') with clean, dignified, non-distracting attire worthy of Allah's Sacred House
Because shoes must be worn on prayer rugs
Because colorful dresses void Salah
explanationEn: Cleanliness, fresh breath (avoiding raw garlic/onion before congregation per Muslim 564), and modest dignified dress honor both the Sanctuary and fellow worshippers.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid eating raw garlic or onions right before entering a mosque congregation—and why does this etiquette especially matter in dense Haram rows?
optionsEn: Because onions invalidate Wudu
Because strong unpleasant odors distress both fellow worshippers and the angels attending prayers
Because cooked onions are also forbidden
Because garlic is haram in all meals
explanationEn: Keeping breath fresh with Miswak or brushing before entering packed Mataf and prayer rows shows deep courtesy to neighbors.

questionEn: If a pilgrim wears medical compression stockings on a long flight to Jeddah to prevent deep vein thrombosis (DVT), when should a male pilgrim remove them?
optionsEn: Remove them before making the Niyyah of Ihram at the Miqat—unless a physician deems keeping them on medically essential throughout landing, in which case he wears them out of necessity and offers Fidyah al-Adha
Never wear compression stockings on flights
Cut off the toes only and keep ankles covered
Keep them on throughout Umrah without consulting anyone
explanationEn: Changing into Ihram and removing socks just before the Miqat announcement preserves normal Ihram compliance, while true medical necessity is accommodated via Fidyah al-Adha without sin.

questionEn: Are unscented alcohol-based hand sanitizers permissible for pilgrims in Ihram inside airports and Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: No, rubbing sanitizer breaks Wudu and Ihram
Sanitizers require sacrificing a sheep
Only rosewater is allowed for cleaning hands
Yes; pure medical/unscented hand sanitizer used for hygiene is not a cosmetic perfume (tib) and is permissible, while scented sanitizers loaded with cologne fragrance should be avoided
explanationEn: Jurists distinguish antiseptic alcohol used for medical sanitization from perfume (tib); choosing fragrance-free sanitizers and wipes avoids all doubt.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim in Ihram use plain unscented wet wipes to freshen up during long bus rides from Madinah to Makkah?
optionsEn: Only allowed after Sa'i
No, wet wipes invalidate Ihram
Wet wipes require repeating Niyyah
Yes, plain unscented baby wipes or water-only wipes are completely permissible; avoid perfumed wipes
explanationEn: Staying clean and refreshed with fragrance-free wipes is lawful and considerate toward fellow bus passengers.

questionEn: What is the ruling on using unscented lip balm (such as plain beeswax or petroleum jelly) in Makkah's dry desert air while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Permissible when completely unscented; avoid flavored or perfumed lip glosses/cosmetics
Allowed only at night
Requires fasting three days
Strictly forbidden even if lips crack and bleed
explanationEn: Unscented lip balm protects cracked lips as skin care rather than perfume or adornment.

questionEn: If a pilgrim flies via a connecting hub like Riyadh or Dammam BEFORE taking a domestic flight to Jeddah for Umrah, when do they cross the Miqat?
optionsEn: They enter Ihram at Riyadh baggage claim
They never cross a Miqat on domestic flights
The domestic flight from Riyadh or Dammam to Jeddah crosses Qarn al-Manazil (or its alignment), so they prepare Ihram before boarding the domestic leg and make Niyyah when crossing that Miqat
They must enter Ihram in London before flying to Riyadh even if staying in Riyadh two days
explanationEn: For an immediate transit connection straight through Riyadh/Dammam onward to Jeddah for Umrah, entering Ihram on the domestic leg right before Qarn al-Manazil is clean and accurate (and if staying days in Riyadh first, definitely enter before the Riyadh-Jeddah flight crosses Qarn al-Manazil).

questionEn: What if a pilgrim arrives at Jeddah port by sea (cruise ship or ferry across the Red Sea) intending Umrah?
optionsEn: They enter Ihram onboard when the ship aligns parallel to their nearest Miqat (such as Yalamlam from the south or al-Juhfah/Rabigh from the north/west) before reaching Jeddah
Sea travelers have no Miqat obligation
They must swim ashore first
They wait until stepping onto the Jeddah dock
explanationEn: Just like air routes, sea routes follow the Muhadhat principle—assuming Ihram onboard when parallel to the Miqat line before entering Jeddah.

questionEn: Can a male pilgrim tie the waist of his Izar in a knot instead of using a belt?
optionsEn: Men must knot both the Izar and Rida' around the neck

Folding and tucking the Izar securely with a sturdy belt is safest and most modest; tying the fabric itself into a knot (without tearing or exposing Awrah) is permissible in necessity, though many jurists prefer folding/belting cleanly rather than knotting the Rida' around the neck
Belts are forbidden for men
Using a knot invalidates Umrah
explanationEn: Scholars note that knotting the upper Rida' around the neck/chest to resemble a stitched collar is avoided, whereas tucking the lower Izar firmly and securing it with an Ihram belt keeps it neat and secure.

questionEn: Are women in Ihram permitted to wear simple hair clips, elastic bands, or pins to keep their hijab securely in place during crowds?
optionsEn: No, hijab pins count as tailored garments
Only wooden hairpins are allowed
Women must let their headscarves blow loose
Yes; elastic hair ties, undercaps, and hijab pins are completely permissible for women in Ihram
explanationEn: Securing the hijab cleanly prevents hair from becoming uncovered in crowds or wind during Tawaf and Sa'i.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim suffers a sudden minor nosebleed during Tawaf around the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Skip the rest of Tawaf
Abandon Umrah completely

Step out immediately to avoid dripping blood on the Haram floor, wash cleanly, pinch/pack the nose until bleeding stops, refresh Wudu if required by their school (Hanafis hold flowing blood breaks Wudu; Shafi'is/Hanbalis hold minor nosebleed does not break Wudu unless heavy/impure concern—yet refreshing Wudu is quick and cautious), and resume
Keep bleeding onto the Kaaba floor
explanationEn: Protecting the Sacred Mosque from blood contamination comes first; stopping the bleeding cleanly and renewing Wudu if needed allows calm continuation.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim unexpectedly vomits during Tawaf due to motion sickness or heat?
optionsEn: Continue walking inside the Mataf while vomiting
Cancel Umrah permanently

Step aside promptly into a restroom/bin area, clean mouth and clothes cleanly from any impurity, refresh Wudu (mandatory in Hanafi/Hanbali mouthful-vomit views and cautious across all schools), rest briefly, and resume or restart Tawaf
Skip Sa'i afterward
explanationEn: Stepping out quickly preserves mosque cleanliness, and washing up with fresh Wudu restores complete calm and purity.

questionEn: If a pilgrim mistakenly walks 8 circuits of Tawaf instead of 7 because they forgot they already finished lap 7, does the 8th lap ruin Tawaf?
optionsEn: Yes, 8 laps completely voids Umrah
They must complete 14 laps now
They owe a camel sacrifice

If they realize mid-8th lap that they already completed 7 with certainty, they simply stop right away, cover the right shoulder, and pray the 2 rak'ahs—if they completed an extra lap unintentionally, their 7-circuit Tawaf remains completely valid
explanationEn: Unintentionally adding an extra step or circuit does not invalidate the completed seven circuits (though one must NEVER intentionally make Tawaf 8 laps).

questionEn: What if a pilgrim intentionally decides to perform 8 circuits in one Umrah Tawaf 'just to be extra generous'?
optionsEn: Encouraged—10 circuits in one Tawaf is even better
Each person may pick any odd number from 3 to 11
Adding 1 lap saves doing Sa'i

Not permissible; Tawaf is fixed by the Shari'ah at seven circuits—if someone wants more reward after finishing the 7-circuit Umrah Tawaf and its 2 rak'ahs, they should perform a separate voluntary 7-circuit Tawaf later
explanationEn: Worship follows Prophetic measure ('Take your rituals from me'): 7 circuits per Tawaf, just as Maghrib has 3 rak'ahs and Fajr has 2.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performs Tawaf on the open-air roof of Al-Masjid al-Haram during sunny midday, may they carry a handheld umbrella while walking?
optionsEn: Yes; carrying a handheld umbrella over your head (without touching/wrapping the head in cloth) is permissible in Ihram during both Tawaf and Sa'i, taking care not to poke nearby walkers
No, umbrellas are forbidden inside the Haram
Only women may carry umbrellas
Umbrellas invalidate Tawaf
explanationEn: Sun protection with a compact umbrella prevents heatstroke on the upper open roof while staying careful not to bump anyone's face in dense lines.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim wear clean indoor mosque shoes/slippers during Sa'i between Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: Yes; wearing clean sandals or clean light indoor slippers during Sa'i (and walking on the tiled Mas'a floor) is completely permissible and protects feet over the ~3 km walk
Shoes must be removed at the green lights
No, Sa'i must always be done completely barefoot
Only wooden shoes are permitted in Sa'i
explanationEn: Clean sandals (for men, leaving ankles/upper foot open; for women, comfortable modest shoes) prevent heel pain and blisters during the 7 laps of Sa'i.

questionEn: What if a pilgrim accidentally misses walking up to the marble base of Safa or Marwah by stopping 15 meters short before turning back?
optionsEn: Stopping 50 meters early still counts
Turning near the green lights suffices

Because they did not cover the full span between Safa and Marwah, that shortened lap is incomplete according to jurists; ensure you reach all the way to the marked ascending base/slope of Safa and Marwah on every single turn
Only laps 1 and 7 need to reach the hills
explanationEn: Walking right up to the visible rocky base/raised ramp of both Safa and Marwah guarantees every lap covers the entire prescribed distance.

questionEn: How do the electric golf-style carts on the Mas'a track work for pilgrims needing mobility assistance during Sa'i?
optionsEn: They skip Mount Marwah entirely
They only drive halfway between the hills
They follow the dedicated oval vehicle lane between Safa and Marwah, covering the full 7 laps up to both hill stations so riders can pause and make dua comfortably
They require riders to jump off while moving
explanationEn: Official Haram electric carts traverse the entire Safa–Marwah span along dedicated tracks, allowing elderly or unwell pilgrims to perform Sa'i peacefully.

questionEn: What if a woman has very short hair (above the ears) when performing Taqsir after Sa'i?
optionsEn: She must shave completely bald
She trims her eyelashes instead
She skips Taqsir altogether
She trims a tiny bit (~1–2 cm, or as much as a fingertip/reasonable tip) evenly from the ends of her hair—and never shaves her head
explanationEn: Even short hair is trimmed slightly from the ends evenly across the head (never shaving, and never cutting eyebrows/eyelashes).

questionEn: What if a male pilgrim shaved his head completely bald ONE DAY BEFORE departing for Umrah, so by the time he finishes Sa'i his scalp has only tiny 1 mm stubble?
optionsEn: He must shave his beard instead
He cannot perform Umrah for six months
Pass the clean razor over his scalp (removing the tiny stubble cleanly), which fulfills Halq properly
He must glue hair back onto his scalp
explanationEn: Passing a fresh razor over short stubble removes whatever grew and fulfills the Sunnah of Halq cleanly; next time, leaving hair untrimmed a couple weeks before Umrah makes Halq/Taqsir even clearer.

questionEn: Is trimming the mustache at the end of Umrah sufficient instead of shaving or trimming head hair?
optionsEn: No! Halq and Taqsir apply specifically to the hair of the HEAD ('muhalliqina ru'usakum wa muqassirin', 48:27)—trimming only the mustache or beard does NOT complete Umrah
Yes, trimming the mustache replaces head hair
Yes, trimming armpit hair suffices
Yes, clipping fingernails completes Umrah
explanationEn: Qur'an 48:27 explicitly specifies shaving or trimming 'your heads'; cutting facial hair or nails never fulfills the rite of Tahallul.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim cut their fingernails right after finishing Halq or Taqsir?
optionsEn: One must wait until arriving home before trimming nails
Yes; once Halq or Taqsir is completed, Tahallul takes effect immediately and cutting nails, showering with scented soap, wearing stitched clothes, and using perfume all become lawful
No, nails remain forbidden for 30 days after Umrah
Only toenails remain forbidden
explanationEn: Umrah has only one complete Tahallul (unlike Hajj's two stages), so every Ihram restriction ends right upon Halq or Taqsir.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in a hurry to catch a flight from Jeddah and trims only two strands of hair instead of trimming evenly over the head, what should they be advised?
optionsEn: Take one extra minute to trim evenly across the entire head (or shave) so their Taqsir is unquestionably valid across all schools of fiqh
Trimming one strand with teeth is enough
Two strands is the preferred Sunnah
Skip trimming altogether if in a hurry
explanationEn: Because trimming only two or three hairs violates the ruling of the Maliki, Hanbali, and Hanafi schools, taking sixty seconds to trim evenly across the whole scalp protects one's Umrah completely.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim brings a small pair of pocket scissors in their travel bag (checked luggage, per airport security rules) for personal Taqsir at the hotel?
optionsEn: Owning scissors during Umrah is haram
Scissors may only be bought in Madinah
Completely permissible and very convenient (remembering airport security bars blades/scissors from cabin carry-on bags, so pack scissors inside checked baggage or buy clean scissors in Makkah)
Women must never touch scissors
explanationEn: Packing small scissors in checked luggage—or purchasing clean ones at a Makkah pharmacy—avoids airport confiscation while facilitating private Taqsir for women and families.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performing Umrah on behalf of a deceased relative (Badal Umrah) is in Makkah, whose hair is shaved/trimmed at the end?
optionsEn: Only the barber trims his own hair
A family member back home shaves instead
The proxy pilgrim (who actually entered Ihram and performed Tawaf and Sa'i) shaves or trims their own hair to exit Ihram
Nobody's hair is trimmed
explanationEn: The person wearing Ihram completes all physical rites—Ihram, Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir—while dedicating the reward/fulfillment on behalf of the named beneficiary.

questionEn: When performing Badal Umrah for a deceased parent, should the proxy ask Allah to reward/forgive that parent throughout Tawaf, Sa'i, and Zamzam?
optionsEn: One may only make dua for oneself
One must read the parent's will during Tawaf
No, mentioning the parent in dua is forbidden
Yes! Alongside fulfilling the ritual with Niyyah at the Miqat on their behalf, making heartfelt dua for their forgiveness, light in the grave, and high Paradise is wonderful
explanationEn: Combining Badal Umrah with abundant filial supplication honors the Hadith that a righteous child's dua benefits deceased parents continuously.

questionEn: If a Muslim wants to perform Umrah on behalf of a living elderly mother who has severe dementia (lost memory/capacity permanently), is that valid?
optionsEn: Yes; permanent loss of physical/mental capacity to travel (such as advanced dementia or incurable paralysis) makes Badal Umrah on her behalf permissible according to major scholars
Only deceased people qualify
Only fathers qualify, never mothers
No, dementia patients must travel alone
explanationEn: Classical jurists apply the ruling of permanent incapacity ('ajiz) to chronic severe frailty or irreversible medical disability where recovery is not expected.

questionEn: If someone is performing Umrah in Ramadan and finds that intense heat + daytime fasting makes them dangerously dizzy during Tawaf, what does Islam teach?
optionsEn: Either perform Umrah calmly at night after Iftar (when it is cooler and you are hydrated), OR use the traveler's legal concession to break the fast safely and make up that day after Ramadan
Stop performing Tawaf forever
Ramadan Umrah is valid only between noon and 3 PM
Fainting on the floor without water is required
explanationEn: Performing Ramadan Umrah during cooler night hours after Taraweeh or Suhoor lets you preserve both your fast and safe hydration—and if traveling, the Qur'anic travel concession remains open.

questionEn: During Ramadan, what happens inside Al-Masjid al-Haram right before Maghrib Adhan as pilgrims sit waiting to break their fast?
optionsEn: Eating dates in the Haram is forbidden
Zamzam taps are shut off during Ramadan
Long rows of hospitality cloths with dates, Zamzam water, and yogurt are shared freely among strangers in extraordinary warmth and brotherhood—and one should keep carpets spotless afterward
Pilgrims argue over seating
explanationEn: Remember the Prophet's ﷺ promise: 'Whoever provides iftar for a fasting person receives a reward like theirs without diminishing the fasting person's reward' (Tirmidhi 807), while packing up wrappers neatly keeps the mosque pristine.

questionEn: Can you combine performing Umrah on Laylat al-Qadr night with praying Qiyam al-Layl (Tahajjud) in Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: One cannot pray Witr after Umrah
Tahajjud is canceled if you did Umrah
Umrah is invalid in the last ten nights
Yes; finishing Umrah smoothly earlier in the evening or after Qiyam allows devoting the peak prayer hours of the blessed night to focused standing, Qur'an, and dua
explanationEn: Planning Umrah timing wisely outside the immediate congestion of Taraweeh/Tahajjud prayer rows helps maximize tranquil Qiyam al-Layl.

questionEn: When leaving Makkah for the airport on the final day after an Umrah trip, what is the best timing for Farewell Tawaf (if performed)?
optionsEn: Perform it before your first Umrah
Perform it three days before leaving while continuing to shop
Perform it in Jeddah airport
Perform it as your very last act in Makkah after packing bags and checking out of the hotel, just before boarding the bus/car toward Jeddah or Madinah
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated: 'The people were commanded that their last covenant (time) be at the House'—doing Tawaf right before departing leaves the Kaaba as one's final memory.

questionEn: After completing Farewell Tawaf and praying its two rak'ahs, may a departing pilgrim buy quick takeaway food/water for the road or pause briefly to gather family/luggage at the hotel door?
optionsEn: No, buying a bottle of water forces repeating Farewell Tawaf
Waiting five minutes for a taxi voids Umrah
They must run non-stop to Jeddah without luggage
Yes; brief practical departure necessities like buying road food/water, collecting parked bags, or waiting for the airport transfer do NOT require repeating Farewell Tawaf
explanationEn: Scholars clarify that ordinary travel readiness and picking up bags/water on the way out are completely compatible with Tawaf al-Wada'.

questionEn: Why is it forbidden in Islam to perform a 'Tawaf' or 'Sa'i' via proxy livestream while sitting at home in another country?
optionsEn: Only audio calls count, not video
Because internet signals weaken near Zamzam

Because ritual worship in Makkah requires the pilgrim's actual bodily presence (or qualified live human Badal in Makkah for the deceased/incapacitated)—remote 'virtual Umrah' has zero validity in Islamic law
Virtual Umrah counts during winter only
explanationEn: While watching live broadcasts of Al-Masjid al-Haram inspires love and longing, actual Umrah requires physical arrival at Miqat and the Sacred Mosque.

questionEn: If a pilgrim in Ihram wears a belt whose buckle contains a tiny metal spring or clasp, does that invalidate Ihram?
optionsEn: Only wooden buttons are allowed
No; belts with buckles, snaps, or zippered pockets to secure money and phone are completely permissible for men in Ihram
Yes, metal buckles are forbidden
Zippers require a sheep penalty
explanationEn: An Ihram waist belt is an accessory worn over the Izar, not a body-fitted garment.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Bab al-Hizyam); Fatawa Ibn Baz

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim accidentally steps on a stray drop of water on the Haram marble and wonders if it might be impure?
optionsEn: One must wash their entire body seven times after touching any puddle
Any wet spot on marble automatically breaks Wudu
Marble floors are always impure

In Islamic jurisprudence, the default assumption for water and surfaces in a clean mosque is purity (taharah) unless clear color, odor, or certainty proves impurity—do not fall into obsessive doubts (waswas)
explanationEn: Rejecting unfounded doubts (waswas) about clean Zamzam/cleaning water on spotless Haram marble protects peace of mind during worship.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if they suffer from severe obsessive doubts (Waswas) about whether their Wudu broke or whether they missed a step in Tawaf?
optionsEn: Restart Tawaf twenty times every day
Stop drinking water permanently
Ignore mere whispers unless accompanied by unmistakable certainty (sound/smell for Wudu, or clear certainty for lap count), seek refuge in Allah, and move forward confidently
Never perform Umrah again
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed not to leave prayer unless one hears a sound or detects an odor (Bukhari 137), liberating believers from paralyzing doubt.

questionEn: Is it permissible to drink cold bottled water or eat light dates/snacks inside the Mas'a corridor if feeling faint?
optionsEn: Yes; hydrating with water or eating a quick date to maintain blood sugar when needed (keeping everything spotless without dropping crumbs or spills) is permissible and wise
Eating dates anywhere in Makkah breaks Umrah
Drinking water inside the Mas'a voids Sa'i
Only Zamzam water may be consumed in Makkah
explanationEn: Maintaining energy and blood sugar prevents fainting, while disposing of pits and wrappers neatly honors the Mosque's cleanliness.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim keep in mind regarding air-conditioned blasts inside Al-Masjid al-Haram and the Mas'a?
optionsEn: Air conditioning breaks Ihram
Going straight from hot outdoor sun/sweating into chilled indoor halls can cause chills—carrying an extra unscented shawl or warm Rida' (and keeping hydrated) helps prevent illness
Men may wear winter coats over shirts in Ihram
Women must remove hijabs indoors
explanationEn: Using a second clean unstitched white shawl/towel over the shoulders protects against cold drafts inside the Haram.

questionEn: If a pilgrim catches a seasonal cough or flu during Umrah, what courteous precautions should they take inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Refuse to wear a mask even when coughing heavily
Cough directly into crowded rows
Wear a clean unscented mask, use tissues cleanly when coughing/sneezing, wash hands often, and pray slightly apart in less crowded edges so infection is not spread to elderly pilgrims
Leave used tissues on prayer mats
explanationEn: Protecting vulnerable elders from respiratory illness embodies the Prophetic rule 'La darar wa la dirar' (cause neither harm nor reciprocal harm).

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim has an artificial pacemaker, metal knee replacement, or dental crown while entering Ihram and circling the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Metal implants must be declared at Miqat with a Dam
Dental crowns invalidate Wudu
Completely permissible with zero restriction; medical implants never affect Ihram or worship
Pacemakers forbid Raml and Sa'i
explanationEn: Internal medical devices and dental restorations have no bearing on Ihram or ritual purity.

questionEn: Can a woman perform Tawaf if she has nail polish on her fingernails from home?
optionsEn: Waterproof nail polish allows Wudu water to pass through
Women do not need Wudu for Salah or Tawaf
Waterproof nail polish forms a barrier preventing Wudu water from reaching the nails—so removing waterproof polish BEFORE making Wudu for Tawaf/Salah is necessary for valid Wudu!
Nail polish may be kept on during Wudu without concern
explanationEn: Removing impermeable nail polish prior to Wudu ensures water reaches the entire nail surface, keeping both Salah and Tawaf completely valid (while natural henna stains without a coating layer do not block water).

questionEn: What about hair extensions or wigs during Umrah—are they permissible?
optionsEn: Hair extensions are Sunnah in Umrah
Trimming a wig counts as Taqsir
Wigs are required at Safa
Attaching artificial or human hair extensions/wigs (wasl al-sha'r) is prohibited in Islam generally, and during Wudu/Ghusl/Taqsir wigs can also interfere with proper washing and trimming natural hair
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade hair-joining/wigs (Bukhari 5933); moreover, Taqsir must trim the woman's own real hair, not synthetic extensions.

questionEn: What if a convert Muslim has non-Muslim parents back home who are worried or curious about their Umrah trip?
optionsEn: Reassure them warmly, keep them updated on safe travel, share kindness and gifts upon return, and make sincere dua for their guidance—honoring Qur'an 31:15 to accompany parents gracefully in this world
Cut off all communication with non-Muslim parents
Hide the trip completely and never speak to them again
Invite them inside Al-Masjid al-Haram (note: Makkah Haram entry is exclusively for Muslims)
explanationEn: Islam commands deep kindness and respectful companionship toward even non-Muslim parents (31:15), making good conduct after Umrah a living reflection of Islam's beauty.

questionEn: Why is entry into the Sacred Precinct of Makkah restricted exclusively to Muslims?
optionsEn: Only during winter months
Based on the Qur'anic decree in Surah Al-Tawbah (9:28) and the Prophetic directive preserving the pure monotheistic sanctuary dedicated solely to Allah's worship
Only residents of Arabia may enter
Because Makkah lacks hotels
explanationEn: Surah Al-Tawbah (9:28) established after the Conquest that polytheists should not approach Al-Masjid al-Haram, safeguarding the Sacred House as a sanctuary of pure Tawhid.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is teaching their young child (say age 8) how to perform Umrah for the first time, what gentle approach works best?
optionsEn: Force them to sprint 7 laps in midday heat without water
Leave them behind at the hotel alone
Explain the stories of Ibrahim, Hajar, and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warmly beforehand, keep them hydrated and rested, carry or wheel them if tired, and praise their effort lovingly
Scold them harshly if they miscount a lap
explanationEn: Connecting rituals to vivid stories of Hajar (AS) and Prophet Ibrahim (AS) turns Umrah into an unforgettable spiritual memory for children.
reference: Riyad al-Salihin; Prophetic Gentleness with Children

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do when his little grandchildren al-Hasan and al-Husayn (RA) climbed on his back while he was praying?
optionsEn: He prolonged his prostration gently until the child climbed down on his own, modeling unmatched patience toward children inside the mosque
He shouted at them mid-prayer
He forbade children from ever entering mosques
He pushed them out of the mosque
explanationEn: Sunan al-Nasa'i (1141) records this tender Prophetic example—reminding parents and congregants in Makkah to treat children inside Al-Masjid al-Haram with gentle guidance and warmth.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing 'Tawaf' while holding a small bottle of water or pocket dua book?
optionsEn: Water bottles require an extra lap
Completely permissible—carrying light items like a small dua booklet, prayer beads/ring counter, or water bottle in one's hand/pouch does not affect Tawaf
Holding any object invalidates Tawaf
Only red dua books are allowed
explanationEn: Just keep items light and unobtrusive so you do not bump others or drop anything in walking lanes.

questionEn: Are Tasbih beads (Subhah) or digital finger clickers permitted for counting laps or dhikr during Tawaf and Sa'i?
optionsEn: No, counting laps is forbidden
Only digital clickers count; fingers are banned
Yes, silent finger clickers or counting on one's fingers (the Sunnah way!) are completely permissible for keeping track of 7 laps or dhikr
Tasbih beads invalidate Ihram
explanationEn: Counting on one's fingers follows the Prophet's ﷺ own practice (Abi Dawud 1501), and a simple silent counter also helps elders never lose track of lap 7.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1501; Fatawa Ibn Baz

questionEn: What if a pilgrim loses one of their sandals outside Al-Masjid al-Haram after finishing Umrah?
optionsEn: Take the nearest stranger's nice sandals instead
Repeat Tawaf barefoot
Walk angrily cursing inside the mosque
Do not take someone else's sandals without permission; wear disposable socks/hotel slippers or ask attendants/companions to help pick up a new pair from nearby shops calmly
explanationEn: Remember never to violate another Muslim's property; carrying your own sandals inside a small drawstring shoe bag prevents losing them altogether!

questionEn: Why do experienced Umrah guides advise arriving inside Al-Masjid al-Haram well before Fard Adhan times if you plan to start Tawaf?
optionsEn: Because gates lock for 6 hours after every prayer
Because walkways close or slow as Jama'ah rows form around the Mataf ~20–30 minutes before Adhan; arriving outside immediate prayer rush lets you finish Tawaf smoothly without cramped bottlenecks
Because Wudu rooms open only once daily
Because Tawaf is banned during daylight
explanationEn: Timing Tawaf smoothly between prayer windows (e.g., an hour after Fajr, late morning, or late night after Isha) makes the experience deeply serene.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performs Umrah late at night (say 1:00 AM), when do they pray Fajr?
optionsEn: Umrah exempts one from Fajr that day
At the normal Fajr time of Makkah (~4–5 AM depending on season), after finishing Umrah or resting briefly
Skip Fajr because they prayed at 1 AM
Pray Fajr right after Sa'i regardless of clock time
explanationEn: Each of the five daily prayers remains strictly tied to its appointed astronomical time (Qur'an 4:103), even on Umrah night.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Umrah Tawaf during the Friday Khutbah (sermon) while the Imam is speaking?
optionsEn: Keeping walking in Tawaf during the Friday Khutbah is encouraged
Talking loudly during Khutbah is allowed in Makkah
Jumu'ah prayer is optional in Makkah

Once the Friday Imam ascends the pulpit and begins the Khutbah, listening attentively in silence is obligatory for everyone attending Jumu'ah—do NOT walk around chatting or performing Tawaf during the Khutbah; sit, listen, pray Jumu'ah, and do Tawaf before or after
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded total attentive silence during the Friday Khutbah (Bukhari 934); therefore arrive early before the Khutbah or start Umrah after Jumu'ah ends.

questionEn: When praying Jumu'ah or any Fard prayer inside Al-Masjid al-Haram, why must worshippers make sure they stand BEHIND the Imam's line (toward the outer rings relative to the Kaaba rather than closer to the Kaaba than the Imam if the Imam stands at a set ring)?
optionsEn: Everyone must stand in a straight line facing Madinah

Actually, in Al-Masjid al-Haram, the Imam prays near the Kaaba (often by Maqam Ibrahim/Kaaba edge), so all circular rows radiate outward around the Kaaba—just ensure you follow the row organization directed by Haram staff and never stand closer to the Kaaba than the Imam's front row on his direction!
Pilgrims stand on the roof with backs to the Qiblah
Congregational rows face away from the Kaaba
explanationEn: In the concentric circle around the Kaaba, everyone's Qiblah is the Kaaba center; standing behind the Imam's front ring on every side keeps every row validly aligned behind the Imam.

questionEn: How does a pilgrim know when a funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) is about to be prayed right after an obligatory prayer in Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: The Mu'adhdhin announces 'As-salatu 'alal-mayyit...' (for man/woman/child); staying for those few minutes of four Takbirs earns a 'Qirat' of reward equal to Mount Uhud!
One must leave the mosque before Janazah
Janazah prayer is never prayed in Makkah
A siren sounds inside the Kaaba
explanationEn: Remembering the Prophet's ﷺ promise of a mountain-sized Qirat of reward for praying Janazah (Bukhari 1325) makes staying an extra two minutes after Fard prayer in Makkah a priceless habit!

questionEn: Does Salat al-Janazah have any bowing (Ruku') or prostration (Sujud)?
optionsEn: Performed sitting on the ground
Only one Takbir
Yes, two Ruku' and four Sujud
No; Salat al-Janazah is prayed standing with four Takbirs, reciting Al-Fatihah, Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ, sincere dua for the deceased, and Salam
explanationEn: Many first-time Umrah visitors are surprised when Janazah is called after Fard Salah—knowing its simple 4-Takbir standing format lets them participate smoothly.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if the Imam in Al-Masjid al-Haram recites a verse of Sajdah (Prostration of Recitation) during prayer?
optionsEn: Follow the Imam seamlessly—prostrate when he says 'Allahu Akbar' into Sajdat al-Tilawah and rise back up with his Takbir (never drop out of sync or stay standing alone)
Sit down for five minutes
Run out of the row immediately
Prostrate twice instead of once
explanationEn: Following the Imam attentively ('Innama ju'ilal-imamu li-yu'tamma bih') ensures smooth unity across thousands of worshippers.

questionEn: If a pilgrim visits Makkah during the cooler winter months (December–February), what practical tips enhance Umrah comfort?
optionsEn: Men may wear wool sweaters over their Rida' in Ihram
Perform only 5 circuits in winter
Pack an extra warm unstitched white blanket/shawl for breezy nights at the Mataf/open roof, moisturize skin with unscented balm, and still drink plenty of Zamzam despite cooler weather
Skip Wudu because water is cool
explanationEn: Staying warm with an extra unstitched shawl (without wearing tailored sweaters or caps in Ihram) keeps winter Umrah cozy and valid.

questionEn: What is the ruling on using a warm unscented sleeping bag or flat wool blanket while resting overnight in a chilly room in Ihram?
optionsEn: Sleeping bags covering the head are encouraged
Blankets are prohibited in winter
One must sleep outdoors without blankets
Using a flat blanket up to the neck (leaving the head uncovered) is completely permissible; avoid zip-up mummy sleeping bags that enclose the body like a tailored garment or cover the head
explanationEn: A simple open flat blanket avoids mimicking form-fitting tailored garments and leaves the head uncovered.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim performing Umrah take prescription medications that happen to have a faint natural herbal smell (like menthol throat lozenges or eucalyptus chest rub for severe congestion)?
optionsEn: If taken strictly for genuine medical relief (throat lozenges swallowed for cough, or medical necessity), oral medicines are permissible; avoid rubbing strongly scented aromatic balms onto skin unless truly medically necessary (with fidyah only if deliberately used as fragrance without excuse)
All cough drops invalidate Umrah
Sick pilgrims must never treat congestion
Throat lozenges require sacrificing a camel
explanationEn: Oral cough drops used to soothe a sore throat are medicine/food, not cosmetic perfume, so there is no harm in taking them.

questionEn: If an elderly pilgrim experiences involuntary urine leakage or weak bladder control during Tawaf, how should they manage purity?
optionsEn: They must stop and remake Wudu every 20 seconds

Follow the Ma'dhur (chronic condition) ruling: wear a clean absorbent pad, clean up and make fresh Wudu right before starting Tawaf (or each prayer time), and complete all 7 circuits without stopping for minor involuntary drops
They may skip Tawaf
They are barred from Tawaf permanently
explanationEn: Allah's mercy frees elders with chronic incontinence from impossible hardship—one fresh Wudu at the start lets them complete their Tawaf in full peace.

questionEn: What is the best way for a group of elderly and younger family members to stay together during Tawaf without losing one another?
optionsEn: Run ahead leaving elderly parents behind alone
Form a 10-person wide linked arm chain blocking the Mataf

Walk at the pace of the slowest/eldest member, keep everyone on the outer/upper calmer ring if needed, hold the elder's arm gently, and agree on a clear landmark meeting spot (e.g., near Gate X or Safa base) in case separated
Split into opposite directions around the Kaaba
explanationEn: Honoring elders by matching their gentle pace and choosing calmer outer circles reflects Prophetic mercy ('He who does not show mercy to our young and respect our elders is not of us').

questionEn: What should you do if you accidentally lose your group or spouse right in the middle of Tawaf?
optionsEn: Panic and run backward against Tawaf flow searching for them
Stop Tawaf immediately and go back to the hotel
Climb onto Maqam Ibrahim to shout their name

Stay calm, continue and complete your own remaining Tawaf circuits (counting carefully), pray the two rak'ahs, and then meet at your pre-arranged landmark (or call/message once safely aside out of walking lanes)
explanationEn: Never turn around and walk backward against the counter-clockwise current of Tawaf; finishing calmly and meeting at the agreed gate keeps everyone safe.

questionEn: Why is it dangerous to bend down abruptly in the dense inner Mataf to tie a bag or pick up a dropped phone?
optionsEn: Pilgrims walking behind cannot see someone crouching suddenly and can trip over them, risking a pile-up; step smoothly toward a calmer outer gap or wait for a clear space before bending
Phones vanish if dropped
Bending down cancels 3 laps
Bending down breaks Wudu
explanationEn: Maintaining spatial awareness protects both yourself and elderly walkers right behind you.

questionEn: If you wish to make extra dua in front of the Kaaba AFTER completing Umrah, where is the best place to stand?
optionsEn: Step out of the active moving Mataf lanes into a stationary prayer/courtyard area facing the Kaaba so you can weep and supplicate calmly for as long as you wish without obstructing Tawaf
Stand directly in front of the Kaaba door stairs blocking traffic
Stand frozen right next to the Black Stone blocking everyone
Lie down horizontally inside Lap 1 lane
explanationEn: Moving back behind the active Mataf flow gives you uninterrupted serenity for deep personal munajat (intimate conversation with Allah).

questionEn: What should a pilgrim know about kissing the Kaaba's door or climbing onto its threshold?
optionsEn: Hanging onto the golden doorknob completes Umrah
Everyone must sit on the Kaaba threshold
Climbing the Kaaba door stairs is obligatory
Do NOT climb onto the Kaaba threshold/Shadhrawan or block the doorway; only the Black Stone (when truly clear without crowding) and Rukn al-Yamani (touching) are part of Tawaf Sunnah
explanationEn: Honoring the Sacred House means following the Prophet's ﷺ measured Sunnah rather than risky physical climbing.

questionEn: In Islamic pilgrimage terminology, what does the word 'Muhrim' specifically refer to?
optionsEn: Any pilgrim—male or female—who has entered the sacred state of Ihram by Niyyah for Umrah or Hajj
Only a barber working near Marwah
Only a blood relative prohibited from marriage (note: that is 'Mahram'!)
Only the Imam of Masjid al-Haram
explanationEn: Learners often confuse 'Muhrim' (a person in the sacred state of Ihram) with 'Mahram' (an unmarriageable close male relative/guardian).

questionEn: Who is a 'Mahram' for a Muslim woman traveling on Umrah?
optionsEn: Any friendly tour guide from her neighborhood
Her male cousin or brother-in-law
Her husband or any male permanently prohibited from marrying her due to blood, breastfeeding, or marriage ties (such as father, son, brother, uncle, nephew, father-in-law)
A family friend of her father
explanationEn: Knowing the exact definition prevents confusion: cousins and brothers-in-law are non-mahrams, whereas fathers, brothers, sons, uncles, and husbands are mahrams.

questionEn: What does the term 'Muhill' (or 'Halal') mean in contrast to 'Muhrim' in Hadith literature on Umrah?
optionsEn: Someone living in Madinah
A pilgrim walking during Raml
A person who is NOT in the state of Ihram (having either not entered Ihram yet or already exited via Halq/Taqsir)
A person who entered Ihram twice
explanationEn: In Hadith such as Abu Qatadah's hunting narration ('nahnu muhrimun wa huwa muhill'), 'muhill' denotes someone outside the state of Ihram.

questionEn: What is 'Miqat Zamani' in contrast to 'Miqat Makani'?
optionsEn: The designated TIME period valid for a ritual—for Hajj it is Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and early Dhul-Hijjah, whereas for Umrah the entire year is valid
The distance measured in meters inside the Mataf
The weight of a sacrificial sheep
The height of Mount Safa
explanationEn: Miqat Makani denotes spatial boundaries around Makkah, while Miqat Zamani denotes valid times: Umrah's temporal window spans year-round (outside active Hajj days per scholarly nuance).

questionEn: What does 'Ashhur al-Hajj' refer to, and why does it matter for someone planning Umrah in Shawwal or Dhul-Qa'dah?
optionsEn: The months of Muharram and Safar
Months when Tawaf is suspended
Months when Sa'i has 3 laps
The months of Hajj (Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah)—performing Umrah then AND remaining for Hajj makes one a Mutamatti', whereas returning home without Hajj keeps it a standalone Umrah
explanationEn: Many Muslims perform Umrah right after Ramadan in Shawwal and return home; that is a completely normal standalone Umrah with no Hajj Hady owed.

questionEn: In Umrah terminology, what does 'Tawaf al-Tatawwu'' mean?
optionsEn: Running between Safa and Marwah
Circling Maqam Ibrahim
Voluntary circumambulation of the Kaaba performed outside an obligatory rite, in ordinary clean clothes without Ihram
Mandatory Umrah Tawaf
explanationEn: Pilgrims staying multiple days in Makkah after completing Umrah can offer abundant Tawaf al-Tatawwu' (with 7 laps + 2 rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim) whenever they enter Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: Can you perform a voluntary 'Sa'i al-Tatawwu'' (voluntary 7 laps between Safa and Marwah) by itself without an accompanying Umrah or Hajj?
optionsEn: Yes, Sa'i replaces Fajr prayer
No; jurists agree Sa'i is ONLY performed as part of Umrah or Hajj after a ritual Tawaf—there is no standalone voluntary Sa'i in Islam (unlike voluntary Tawaf, which IS recommended on its own)
Voluntary Sa'i is done only on Tuesdays
Yes, pilgrims should do 50 voluntary Sa'is per day
explanationEn: Classical scholars note that voluntary worship around the House is Tawaf and Salah, whereas Sa'i between Safa and Marwah is strictly legislated within Umrah and Hajj.

questionEn: What is 'Badanah' in pilgrimage penalty rulings, and when does it apply vs an ordinary sheep (Shah)?
optionsEn: A full camel or cow (seven shares)—required specifically for major violations like sexual intercourse before Tahallul (or Hanafi penalty for Tawaf in major Janabah), whereas standard Dam/Fidyah requires one sheep/goat
A pair of cotton sandals
A small bird
A cup of Zamzam
explanationEn: Knowing that standard Dam/Fidyah is a sheep/goat (or one-seventh of a camel/cow) while Badanah applies only to the gravest violations prevents exaggerated confusion.

questionEn: What does 'Mudd' vs 'Sa'' refer to when measuring food distributed for Fidyah al-Adha?
optionsEn: Hours of daylight

Traditional Prophetic volume measures: 1 Mudd equals roughly two cupped adult hands (~600–750 grams of grain/rice), and 1 Sa' equals 4 Mudds (~2.5–3 kg), so half a Sa' per poor person is 2 Mudds (~1.5 kg)
Lengths of fabric in yards
Gold coins from Syria
explanationEn: Understanding these traditional measures clarifies how easy it is to feed six needy persons half a Sa' (~1.5 kg of rice/dates/wheat each) when Fidyah al-Adha applies.

questionEn: In Qur'an 2:196, what are the exact words naming the three options of Fidyah al-Adha?
optionsEn: 'Praying two nights at Mina'
'Walking to Madinah'
'Building a bridge in Jeddah'
'Fa-fidyatun min siyam-in aw sadaqatin aw nusuk' (a ransom of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explained to Ka'b ibn Ujrah (RA) that 'sadaqah' means feeding 6 poor people, 'siyam' means 3 days fasting, and 'nusuk' means sacrificing a sheep.

questionEn: Which two animals qualify as 'Shah' (ordinary sacrificial sheep/goat) for Hady or Dam in Makkah?
optionsEn: A wild mountain gazelle
Any young chick or rabbit

A healthy sheep (jadha'ah, at least 6 months old per Hanbali/Hanafi, or 1 year per Shafi'i/Maliki) or goat (at least 1 year old) free of disqualifying defects (one-eyed, visibly sick, severely lame, emaciated)
A sick, blind lamb
explanationEn: Sacrificial animals offered to Allah must meet age and health standards taught by the Prophet ﷺ in Sunan al-Nasa'i and Abu Dawud.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say 'Al-Hajju Arafah' (Hajj is Arafah)—what equivalent central pillar defines Umrah?
optionsEn: Tawaf around the Kaaba (paired with Ihram and Sa'i), since Umrah is centered directly upon visiting and circling the Sacred House
Staying three nights at Mina
Climbing Mount Uhud
Visiting Ta'if gardens
explanationEn: Just as missing Arafah misses Hajj, missing Tawaf means Umrah has not been performed—while combining Ihram, Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir completes it cleanly.

questionEn: According to Imam Malik and Imam Abu Hanifah, what is the status of 'Tawaf' vs 'Sa'i' in Umrah?
optionsEn: Malikis omit Sa'i completely
Hanafis omit Tawaf completely
Both schools ban Umrah in Dhul-Qa'dah

Both schools hold Tawaf is an indispensable Pillar (Rukn), while Malikis count Sa'i a Pillar too and Hanafis classify Sa'i and Halq/Taqsir as Wajib (still mandatory to perform, incurring Dam if omitted)
explanationEn: In practice across all four schools, every pilgrim performs Ihram, 7 circuits of Tawaf, 7 laps of Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir—no school ever skips Sa'i.

questionEn: What is the position of the Shafi'i school on Halq/Taqsir in Umrah compared to the Hanafi and Hanbali schools?
optionsEn: Shafi'is count Halq/Taqsir among the Pillars (Arkan) of Umrah (so one does not exit Ihram without it), whereas Hanafis and Hanbalis classify it as Wajib (though Hanbalis still hold Ihram's remaining prohibitions—especially intimacy—wait for Tahallul/Halq too!)
Hanafis allow men to shave before Tawaf
Hanbalis require shaving twice
Shafi'is forbid cutting hair after Umrah
explanationEn: Across every madhhab, completing Halq or Taqsir at the end of Sa'i is essential to complete Umrah properly and exit Ihram cleanly.

questionEn: What did Ibn Abbas (RA) narrate about whether the Prophet ﷺ ever prayed inside the Kaaba during his Umrahs or Conquest?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ banned anyone from ever praying inside
Entering the Kaaba is required for every Umrah pilgrim
The Kaaba has no interior floor

Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) and Bilal (RA) confirmed the Prophet ﷺ entered the Kaaba on the Conquest of Makkah and prayed two rak'ahs inside between the pillars (whereas Ibn Abbas RA heard he made dua in its corners during Hajj without praying inside)
explanationEn: Bilal's (RA) eyewitness testimony in Sahih al-Bukhari (397) affirms praying inside the Kaaba is valid—and praying inside Hijr Ismail offers the same spiritual blessing easily without needing access through the Kaaba door.

questionEn: Which Sahabi entered the Kaaba with the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Conquest and later pointed out the exact spot where the Prophet ﷺ stood and prayed?
optionsEn: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb
Khalid ibn Sa'id
Amr ibn al-As
Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) (alongside Usamah ibn Zayd and Uthman ibn Talhah RA)
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) hastened to ask Bilal (RA) immediately when the Kaaba door opened, learning the Prophet ﷺ stood with one pillar to his left, two to his right, and three behind him, facing the western wall.

questionEn: What is the meaning of 'Al-Rawdah' vs 'Al-Mataf'—which one is in Makkah and which one is in Madinah?
optionsEn: Al-Mataf is inside Mount Uhud
Al-Rawdah is behind Maqam Ibrahim
Al-Mataf is the Tawaf plaza around the Kaaba in Makkah, whereas Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah is the blessed area between the Prophet's ﷺ house/chamber and his Minbar in Masjid al-Nabawi, Madinah
Both are inside Masjid Quba
explanationEn: Pilgrims visiting both holy cities cherish praying calmly inside Al-Mataf in Makkah and seeking a slot in Al-Rawdah ('a garden from the gardens of Paradise') in Madinah.
