questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when someone enters Ihram and intends to visit both Makkah (for Umrah) and Madinah—does visiting Madinah require a separate Miqat?
optionsEn: Yes, travelers must shave their heads upon leaving Madinah
Madinah has five separate Miqats
Yes, every visitor to Madinah must wear two white sheets
No; Madinah has no Miqat for entering Madinah—Miqats exist ONLY for entering Makkah in Ihram for Umrah or Hajj
explanationEn: Miqats ring Makkah specifically; Dhul-Hulayfah (outside Madinah) is the Miqat for pilgrims LEAVING Madinah toward Makkah.

questionEn: Why did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) encourage pilgrims leaving Makkah after Hajj or Umrah not to linger lazily with empty idle gatherings, or wait too long before returning home after rites?
optionsEn: Because fasting was banned in Makkah
Classical narrations record Umar (RA) reminding visitors to fulfill their rites with devotion, return responsibly to their families and duties, and keep the Sacred City reverent and uncluttered
Because Umar (RA) banned visiting Makkah twice
Because hotels did not exist
explanationEn: Umar (RA) balanced deep veneration for the Sanctuary with responsible stewardship of crowds and family duties back home.
reference: Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah; Akhbar Makkah

questionEn: What did Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) explain about why the Prophet ﷺ performed Raml ONLY from the Black Stone to Rukn al-Yamani (or the first 3 circuits) in Umrat al-Qada'?
optionsEn: Because Quraysh sat watching from the hills north/west toward Qu'ayqi'an; the Prophet ﷺ walked normally behind the Kaaba where hidden (between Rukn al-Yamani and Black Stone per early report) and later established Raml across all 3 full circuits
Because stones cut their sandals
Because they were carrying heavy bags
Because Raml was forbidden on the western side
explanationEn: Sahih Muslim (1266) records Ibn Abbas (RA) explaining this origin in 7 AH, while Jabir (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) in 10 AH preserved the final established Sunnah of Raml throughout the entire first 3 circuits.

questionEn: Why does the Sunnah of Raml and Idtiba' continue today even though Quraysh are no longer watching as enemies?
optionsEn: Because angels count running speed

Out of loving obedience to the Prophet ﷺ (Ittiba' al-Sunnah), as Umar (RA) affirmed: why do Raml now that Allah strengthened Islam? Yet we will not abandon a practice we saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do!
Because Makkah is still controlled by Quraysh polytheists
Because otherwise Tawaf is invalid
explanationEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) famously asked himself why Raml continued after Islam prevailed, and answered: 'It was something the Prophet ﷺ did, and we do not like to leave it' (Bukhari 1605)—preserving living historical memory!

questionEn: What does 'Tawakkul' look like in the story of Hajar (AS) running between Safa and Marwah seven times?
optionsEn: She walked away from her infant permanently
She combined complete certainty in Allah ('Then He will not abandon us!') with active tireless physical effort (climbing Safa and Marwah searching for help/water) until Allah sent relief
She doubted Allah's command
She sat still waiting without looking around
explanationEn: Sa'i immortalizes balanced Islamic reliance: trusting Allah completely with your heart while taking every lawful practical effort with your feet.

questionEn: When Hajar (AS) ran seven times between Safa and Marwah, why did she hasten specifically through the lowest middle valley?
optionsEn: Because when she descended into the low valley floor (Batn al-Mas'a), she lost sight of baby Isma'il (AS), so she hurried anxiously across the dip until climbing back into view!
Because she was racing travelers
Because wild lions chased her
Because the marble was hot
explanationEn: Scholars and historians note a mother's tender love: whenever the dip hid infant Isma'il from her sight, Hajar (AS) jogged swiftly until she could see him again—eternally honored by the Green Lights today!

questionEn: What did Hajar (AS) do when she saw water gushing from Zamzam, and what did the Prophet ﷺ say about her action?
optionsEn: She built a small earthen basin around it saying 'Zam! Zam!' to contain it; the Prophet ﷺ said: 'May Allah have mercy on the mother of Isma'il—had she left Zamzam alone without scooping/damming it, it would have been a flowing river!'
She sold cups to travelers
She washed her clothes inside the spring
She covered it with rocks so no one could drink
explanationEn: Narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari 3364, this vivid detail shows how a mother's instinct to preserve water for her thirsty infant turned Zamzam into a blessed eternal well.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:199), Allah commands pilgrims: 'Then depart from the place from where [all] the people depart and ask forgiveness of Allah.' How does that spirit of Istighfar carry into Umrah?
optionsEn: Istighfar is said only after sleeping
Pilgrims never seek forgiveness during Umrah
Even at the peak of sacred worship, believers never feel smug—they conclude rites seeking Allah's forgiveness and mercy
Only Quraysh stay apart from other tribes
explanationEn: Both Qur'an 2:199 and Prophetic practice (saying 'Astaghfirullah' three times right after every Salah) teach ending worship in humility and repentance.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about someone who performs Umrah and returns without arguing or committing sin vs one who returns to old sins immediately?
optionsEn: Once you do Umrah, all future sins are automatically permitted
Sins after Umrah do not count
Guarding one's tongue and conduct during and after Umrah preserves the expiation of sins, whereas returning deliberately to sin forfeits spiritual growth (requiring renewed repentance)
Only words spoken in Arabic count as sins
explanationEn: Umrah is a fresh clean slate—not a license to sin; guarding righteousness afterward keeps its light alive.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim enters Ihram at Miqat while intending Umrah, and BEFORE reaching Makkah realizes they forgot to bring enough money or hotel booking—can they exit Ihram just because plans feel inconvenient?
optionsEn: Dropping Ihram at Jeddah airport is penalty-free
Yes, anyone can quit Ihram whenever tired

No! Once entered, Ihram cannot be casually dropped for minor inconvenience; one must complete Umrah (unless genuinely blocked by true insurmountable obstruction/Ihsar, or unless Ishtirat was explicitly made for that obstacle)
Just take off the white towels and go sightseeing
explanationEn: Qur'an 2:196 commands: 'Complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah'—entering Ihram is a solemn commitment before Allah that binds the pilgrim until Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir (or valid Ihsar).

questionEn: Why is it important NOT to say 'Labbayk Allahumma bi-'Umrah' carelessly as a joke or rehearsal before you actually intend to enter Ihram?
optionsEn: Because combining heart intent or uttering the initiation carelessly can cause confusion; rehearse the Talbiyah wording beforehand purely as study if learning, and declare Niyyah sincerely only at the Miqat
Because saying it twice breaks Ihram
Because rehearsal is forbidden in Islam
Because Talbiyah has 100 verses
explanationEn: Learning and practicing pronunciation before travel is great—just distinguish practicing pronunciation from forming the actual Niyyah at Miqat.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is unsure about Arabic pronunciation of the Talbiyah or duas, should they worry that mispronouncing a vowel invalidates their Umrah?
optionsEn: One must pass an Arabic grammar exam at Jeddah
No! Allah rewards sincere effort—learn the simple Talbiyah clearly as best you can (listening to audio beforehand helps), and minor accent differences never invalidate your Umrah
Yes, any accent invalidates Ihram
Only native Makkah residents have valid Talbiyah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ reassured believers that one who struggles through reciting while striving sincerely earns double reward.

questionEn: What is the meaning of 'Al-Izar' and 'Al-Rida'' historically in Arabian dress?
optionsEn: Leather boots and gloves
The two basic unsewn wraps worn across Arabia—Izar wrapped around the waist/lower body and Rida' draped over the shoulders/upper torso
Silk robes with gold buttons
Heavy metal armor
explanationEn: Men in Ihram wear these humble simple wraps mirroring timeless modesty and equality—the very same cloths in which a pilgrim in Ihram would even be shrouded if passing away.

questionEn: How should a male pilgrim wrap his Izar cleanly so it never blows open in wind or slips down during Raml?
optionsEn: Wrap it loosely once with no overlap and no belt
Wrap it only down to mid-thigh
Wear it above the shoulders
Overlap the edges broadly around the waist (so neither thigh nor knee shows when striding briskly), fold the top waistband down securely twice, and tighten an Ihram belt over the folded waist
explanationEn: A generous overlap plus double-roll waist tuck and secure belt keeps the Izar completely steady through brisk Raml and sitting in Salah.

questionEn: How do men wrap the Rida' during ordinary moments vs during Umrah Tawaf (Idtiba')?
optionsEn: Never wear the Rida' during Sa'i

Normally (on flight, bus, and during all prayers), drape the Rida' comfortably over BOTH shoulders covering chest and back; ONLY for the 7 circuits of Umrah Tawaf, slip it under the right armpit onto the left shoulder (Idtiba'), then restore both shoulders before praying behind Maqam Ibrahim
Throw the Rida' over the head
Keep Idtiba' from Miqat until shaving
explanationEn: Practicing wrapping both normal Rida' and Idtiba' once at home before travel eliminates any awkward fumbling at the airport or Mataf.

questionEn: If a pilgrim brings a small safety pin or plastic clip for the Rida', where should they avoid pinning it so it doesn't mimic a tailored shirt?
optionsEn: Sewing sleeves onto the Rida' is Sunnah

Minor scholars caution against pinning/sewing the Rida' tightly into closed sleeves, though pinning two edges loosely at the front/shoulder just to keep it from blowing off in wind is permitted by many contemporary jurists—better yet, learning a clean tucked drape needs no pins at all!
Pins must pierce the skin
Clips are forbidden even on waist belts
explanationEn: A simple shoulder tuck holds the Rida' securely without turning it into a fitted garment.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Umrah Tawaf while holding an infant in one's arms if the parent wants to keep both hands ready for safety?
optionsEn: Only fathers may hold infants during Tawaf
Infants must walk alone from age 1
Completely permissible (provided the child is dressed cleanly and diaper is free of impurity); you can carry the child safely in your arms or baby carrier
Holding an infant breaks Tawaf
explanationEn: Using a front carrier or holding a clean baby securely keeps both hands balanced and follows the Prophet's ﷺ gentleness carrying Umamah (RA) in Salah.

questionEn: Does a child who performs Umrah in infancy get spiritual reward, and do their parents also get rewarded?
optionsEn: Neither parent nor child gets any reward
The child gets sin for crying
Only the father gets reward
Yes! The Prophet ﷺ told a mother who lifted her baby: 'Yes, [pilgrimage counts for him], and for you is a reward'
explanationEn: Sahih Muslim (1336) promises full reward to both the child and the caring parent/guardian who guides them through the rites.

questionEn: When a boy or girl who performed Umrah as a child later reaches puberty (Baligh), must they perform their obligatory lifetime Hajj/Umrah again once financially/physically able?
optionsEn: Yes; Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ taught that any child who performs pilgrimage before puberty must perform their obligatory pilgrimage again after reaching maturity (once able)
Only girls must repeat it
Only if they forgot the trip
No, childhood Umrah forever discharges adult obligation
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) preserved this explicit Prophetic ruling (al-Nasa'i / al-Hakim / Ibn Abi Shaybah): childhood pilgrimage brings full voluntary reward while adult obligation begins after puberty.

questionEn: What is the ruling on an elderly parent who is physically able to ride in a plane and wheelchair, versus one who is medically forbidden by doctors from traveling altogether?
optionsEn: If safe to travel with wheelchair support, performing Umrah in person brings tremendous joy and reward; if physicians certify travel poses serious danger/incapacity, Badal Umrah on their behalf is permissible
Wheelchair users are banned from airplanes
Doctors' medical advice must be ignored
Badal Umrah is mandatory even for healthy 50-year-olds
explanationEn: Consulting both a trusted physician and family care ensures elders worship safely—either personally via wheelchair or via Badal when truly unable.

questionEn: What is the virtue of serving an elderly parent during Umrah—pushing their wheelchair through Tawaf and Sa'i, fetching Zamzam, and helping them rest?
optionsEn: Children should hire strangers rather than serve parents themselves when able
It is among the highest acts of Birr al-Walidayn (filial righteousness), earning reward for your own Umrah plus immense reward for serving your parents
Pushing a wheelchair prevents you from counting your own laps
Helpers lose half their Tawaf reward
explanationEn: When Ibn Umar (RA) saw a Yemeni man carrying his elderly mother on his back during Tawaf, the man asked if he had repaid her; Ibn Umar (RA) replied: 'Not even a single labor pain!'—showing how priceless serving parents at the Kaaba is.

questionEn: In al-Adab al-Mufrad, what touching question did the man carrying his mother on his back during Tawaf ask Abdullah ibn Umar (RA)?
optionsEn: 'Does carrying her count as 14 laps?'
'Must I run Raml with her?'
'Do you think I have repaid her?'—to which Ibn Umar (RA) replied: 'No, not even for a single contraction/sigh of childbirth!'
'Can I leave her at Safa?'
explanationEn: This unforgettable authentic scene from al-Bukhari's al-Adab al-Mufrad reminds every pilgrim to serve their parents at the Kaaba with bottomless love and humility.

questionEn: What is the Islamic ruling if a woman's husband passes away and she is observing her waiting period ('Iddah of widowhood, 4 months and 10 days)—should she travel for a voluntary Umrah during 'Iddah?
optionsEn: Majority jurists (all four Sunni schools) rule she remains in her marital home during 'Iddah and delays travel for Hajj or Umrah until her waiting period finishes (unless she was already mid-journey past Miqat/far from home, where scholars provide tailored guidance)
She may go only to Jeddah
She must depart for Umrah immediately on the day of burial
Widows have no 'Iddah in Islam
explanationEn: Observing 'Iddah at home obeys Qur'an 2:234 and Prophetic guidance to Furay'ah bint Malik (RA), after which she may travel freely for Umrah.
reference: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:234; Sunan Abi Dawud 2300; Al-Mughni

questionEn: What if a woman already entered Ihram and was well on her way to Makkah when news reached her of her husband's passing—how do scholars guide her?
optionsEn: She must abandon Ihram permanently
If she has already entered Ihram and cannot easily return (or has arrived near Makkah), scholars allow her to complete her Umrah she already bound herself to, then return home to finish her 'Iddah
Her Umrah is invalid
She must stay in Makkah for 5 years
explanationEn: Because entering Ihram makes completing the Umrah obligatory (2:196), finishing the started rite responsibly before observing the rest of 'Iddah at home resolves both duties cleanly.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing 'Tawaf' around the Kaaba while wearing a backpack containing a small Qur'an or spare prayer mat?
optionsEn: Bags must be left unlocked at the door
Carrying a Qur'an inside the Mataf is prohibited
Permissible, though keeping backpacks compact so they don't bump pilgrims behind you—or using a light drawstring/crossbody bag—is much more considerate in tight crowds
Only leather bags are valid
explanationEn: Bulky hiking backpacks whack neighboring pilgrims' faces and shoulders; a slim crossbody pouch keeps essentials secure without obstructing anyone.

questionEn: Why is it helpful to memorize or write down the hotel address/name in Arabic (and save a phone photo of the hotel card) before stepping out for Umrah?
optionsEn: Because you must read the hotel address during Tawaf
Because phones stop working near Safa
Because Al-Masjid al-Haram has dozens of similar-looking exits and streets; having the exact Arabic hotel card helps security or taxi drivers guide you back effortlessly if disoriented
Because hotels forbid non-Arabic speakers
explanationEn: Especially for elderly parents who might step out through a different gate (e.g., King Fahd vs King Abdulaziz vs Marwah exit), a lanyard card with the hotel's Arabic name and family phone number is invaluable.

questionEn: What happens if you accidentally walk out of the Mas'a on the WRONG exit door after finishing Lap 7 at Marwah?
optionsEn: No problem at all for your Umrah validity—simply orient yourself using Haram gate numbers, head to any clean barber shop (or back to your hotel) for Halq/Taqsir, and remember which gate faces your hotel
Exiting the wrong door invalidates Sa'i
You must repeat Ihram at Miqat
You must walk 7 more laps
explanationEn: Gate numbers and courtyard landmarks help you orient smoothly; all exits around Marwah lead cleanly out toward barber areas and plazas.

questionEn: Why are barber shops clustered right outside the Marwah exit plaza?
optionsEn: Because shaving must occur within 10 meters of Marwah
Because barbers are forbidden near hotels
Because Mount Safa is outside Makkah
Because Lap 7 of Sa'i always finishes at Mount Marwah, allowing male pilgrims to step right outside for Halq or Taqsir immediately upon concluding Sa'i
explanationEn: Stepping out from Marwah straight toward authorized clean barber shops (or walking calmly back to your hotel room to trim/shave) completes Umrah seamlessly.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim wear their Izar and Rida' cleanly inside hotel dining halls before finishing Umrah, or change clothes before finishing Sa'i?
optionsEn: Keep wearing the Izar and Rida' cleanly throughout all breaks until Halq or Taqsir is completed—never change into regular trousers or shirts before shaving/trimming!
Change into regular jeans right after Tawaf while resting
Take off the Rida' at restaurants
Wear regular clothes during Sa'i
explanationEn: Remember: Ihram remains active through Tawaf, Maqam Ibrahim prayer, Sa'i, and up until Halq/Taqsir—only after cutting hair do you put regular garments back on.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is extremely exhausted after Sa'i and puts on a stitched shirt in their hotel room BEFORE trimming their hair out of pure forgetfulness, what should they do upon realizing five minutes later?
optionsEn: They must sacrifice a camel
Their entire Umrah must be redone from Jeddah
They must fast 60 days
Remove the stitched shirt immediately, perform Halq or Taqsir right away, and then put regular clothes back on—no sin and no penalty for genuine forgetfulness according to major scholars
explanationEn: Promptly removing the garment, performing Halq/Taqsir, and seeking ease under Qur'an 2:286 ('Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget') resolves the mistake cleanly.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim deliberately removes their Ihram wraps and wears normal clothes before Halq/Taqsir simply because they felt warm?
optionsEn: Nothing—warm weather cancels Halq
They must pay nothing
They must repent, immediately restore Ihram until performing Halq/Taqsir, and offer Fidyah al-Adha (fast 3 days, feed 6 poor, or sacrifice a sheep) for deliberately wearing tailored clothing in Ihram
They must do 21 laps of Tawaf
explanationEn: Deliberate violation without valid necessity triggers both repentance and Fidyah al-Adha.

questionEn: How does the spiritual beauty of Umrah remind believers of the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah)?
optionsEn: By ignoring fellow believers
Millions standing stripped of worldly badges in white shroud-like wraps, leaving homeland and wealth behind to gather before Allah in humility and hope of mercy
By comparing hotel star ratings
By rushing to buy luxury souvenirs
explanationEn: Al-Ghazali and classical scholars beautifully draw parallels between leaving home for Makkah, wearing the two white shroud-like sheets, and standing humble before the Lord of the Worlds.

questionEn: What does 'Labbaika Allahumma labbayk' awaken in the believer regarding responding to Allah's commands AFTER Umrah ends?
optionsEn: Just as you answered Allah's call to Makkah saying 'Here I am!', you continue answering His call to Fajr prayer, honesty, charity, and kindness every day back home
It releases you from praying five times a day
It means only pilgrimage matters in Islam
It applies only inside Jeddah airport
explanationEn: Living 'Labbayk' every morning when the Fajr Adhan sounds back home keeps the transformation of Umrah alive all year round.

questionEn: When a traveler arrives in Makkah for Umrah and prays behind the resident Imam of Al-Masjid al-Haram, should they pray two shortened rak'ahs (Qasr) or complete all four rak'ahs of Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha?
optionsEn: Skip congregational prayers while in Makkah
Leave the congregation early after two rak'ahs
Complete all four rak'ahs following the resident Imam, as established in Sunnah ('When you pray behind a resident Imam, pray four')
Stand silently during the last two rak'ahs
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) taught that a traveler praying behind a resident Imam must complete all four rak'ahs—only when praying alone or with fellow travelers does Qasr apply.

questionEn: While traveling on the bus or train between Madinah and Makkah for Umrah, how should a pilgrim perform Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha?
optionsEn: Delay all prayers until arriving at the hotel next morning
Skip Salah on travel days
Shorten 4-rak'ah prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, Isha) to 2 rak'ahs (Qasr), and combine Dhuhr+Asr or Maghrib+Isha (Jam') when genuinely on the road
Pray without facing Qiblah even when stopped at a rest station
explanationEn: Traveling between Madinah (~450 km) and Makkah exceeds travel distance, granting the Prophetic concessions of Qasr and Jam' at rest stops cleanly.

questionEn: If you are praying an obligatory Salah on an airplane en route to Jeddah before crossing the Miqat, what is the proper way to pray?
optionsEn: Skip Salah completely on flights

Make Wudu (or Tayammum if water is unavailable), face the Qiblah direction as closely as possible in a designated prayer area standing up if able (or seated if turbulence/no space prevents standing), and never miss the prayer's time window
Only pray when landing
Wait until arriving in Makkah two days later
explanationEn: Preserving every obligatory Salah within its time—standing and facing Qiblah as best possible—keeps the Umrah journey grounded in obedience from the sky down to the Haram.

questionEn: When praying Witr inside Al-Masjid al-Haram during Ramadan (or voluntary night prayers), how does an Umrah visitor earn the reward of praying the entire night?
optionsEn: Pray faster than the Imam
Leave halfway through Taraweeh
Skip Witr completely
Stay with the Imam until he finishes all prayers including Witr ('Whoever stands with the Imam until he finishes, it is recorded for him as praying the whole night')
explanationEn: Narrated by Abu Dharr (RA) in Jami' al-Tirmidhi (806) and Abu Dawud (1375), praying Taraweeh and Witr with the Imam in Al-Masjid al-Haram brings the reward of Qiyam for the entire night.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performs Witr with the Imam in Al-Masjid al-Haram and later wakes up for Tahajjud before Fajr, should they pray a second Witr?
optionsEn: No; pray two-by-two voluntary rak'ahs before Fajr without repeating Witr, because the Prophet ﷺ said: 'There are not two Witrs in one night'
Never wake up for Tahajjud after praying Witr
Repeat Isha prayer
Yes, pray Witr three times every night
explanationEn: Talq ibn Ali (RA) narrated: 'There are not two Witrs in one night' (Abi Dawud 1439); praying extra pairs of Tahajjud before Fajr without another Witr is completely Sunnah.

questionEn: Why is the silver frame encasing Al-Hajar al-Aswad present around the Black Stone?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ carved a silver ring around it
To reflect sunlight toward Safa
To mark the entrance to Zamzam
To hold together and protect the smaller fragments of the Black Stone (which suffered historical damage centuries ago) safely inside the corner
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) originally encased the Black Stone in silver after fires/sieges cracked it, and subsequent Muslim rulers maintained the protective silver bezel—notice one touches/kisses the stone inside, not merely the silver frame.
reference: Akhbar Makkah; History of the Kaaba

questionEn: How many small fragments of the original Black Stone remain visible inside the dark oval silver bezel at the southeastern corner of the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Seven to eight small dark stones embedded together in wax/resin inside the silver setting
One giant boulder three meters tall
Twelve gold blocks
Forty white pebbles
explanationEn: Visitors who get an uncrowded glimpse see these small dark stones set inside the recessed silver frame—making clear why pushing violently in crowds to reach them is unsafe and unnecessary when pointing from afar is authentic Sunnah.

questionEn: Which historical event damaged the Black Stone and led to its later restoration in the 4th Islamic century (10th century CE)?
optionsEn: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
The Conquest of Makkah
The Qarmatian raid on Makkah in 317 AH (930 CE), after which the stone was recovered and returned to the Kaaba ~22 years later
The Battle of Badr
explanationEn: Even during the 22 years when the Qarmatians removed the stone, Muslims still aligned their Tawaf at the Black Stone corner, proving worship is directed to Allah and His Sanctuary—never mere stone worship.

questionEn: Where is the ancient Well of Zamzam situated relative to the Kaaba today?
optionsEn: On top of Mount Marwah
Five kilometers outside Makkah

Approximately 20–21 meters east/southeast of the Kaaba (near the Black Stone / Maqam Ibrahim side, now covered beneath the marble Mataf plaza with chilled fountains serving pilgrims around the mosque)
Inside the northern wall of Hijr Ismail
explanationEn: The subterranean Zamzam shaft beneath the eastern Mataf was covered cleanly to widen Tawaf space while pumping pure chilled and ambient Zamzam water to thousands of dispensers throughout Makkah and Madinah.

questionEn: Why is Zamzam water never chemically altered with perfumes or artificial flavors at Haram dispensers, though chilled or unchilled containers are provided?
optionsEn: To preserve its pure natural mineral composition cleanly—and note unchilled ('non-cold') Zamzam containers are clearly labeled for elderly pilgrims or those with sensitive throats
Because warm Zamzam is banned
Because cooling Zamzam is forbidden
Because adding ice breaks Wudu
explanationEn: Reading the dispenser labels ('Cold' vs 'Not Cold / Ambient') helps elders or anyone with a sore throat choose comfortable ambient Zamzam easily.

questionEn: When a pilgrim says 'Bismillah' and pours a little Zamzam water over their head or face after drinking, does that follow a Companion or Prophetic precedent?
optionsEn: Yes; Jabir (RA) and other reports mention the Prophet ﷺ drank Zamzam and poured/sprinkled water upon his head, and scholars approve seeking blessing via washing/drinking Zamzam cleanly (outside prayer carpets)
Only children may wash their face with Zamzam
Pouring Zamzam on the face breaks Ihram
No, Zamzam may never touch skin
explanationEn: Just avoid spilling puddles onto carpeted prayer rows or slippery marble lanes where walkers could slip.

questionEn: Which corner of the Kaaba faces roughly south toward Yemen, and why is it named Al-Rukn al-Yamani?
optionsEn: The corner inside Hijr Ismail
The corner containing the Kaaba door
The corner facing Syria
The southwestern/southern corner facing the direction of Yemen, hence called the Yemeni Corner
explanationEn: Touching Al-Rukn al-Yamani gently with the right hand (without kissing it or crowding) on the way toward the Black Stone is an authentic Sunnah.

questionEn: When touching Al-Rukn al-Yamani in Tawaf, what do some pilgrims mistakenly do that has NO basis in the Sunnah?
optionsEn: Touching it gently with the right hand if uncrowded
Keeping the Kaaba on their left
Raising their hand to point at Al-Rukn al-Yamani from afar or shouting 'Allahu Akbar' at it when unable to reach it—pointing and Takbir belong specifically to Al-Hajar al-Aswad!
Passing by smoothly while reciting 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah...'
explanationEn: Scholars consistently clarify: touch Rukn al-Yamani only if right next to it without crowding; if distant, simply pass by reciting 'Rabbana atina...' without pointing or Takbir.

questionEn: What common mistake happens when pilgrims try to touch the Black Stone with their LEFT hand?
optionsEn: Walking counter-clockwise puts the Kaaba on your LEFT, so touching/pointing should still use the RIGHT hand (the Sunnah hand for noble acts), turning the face/chest briefly toward the stone without blocking traffic
Using the right hand is forbidden
One must touch it with both elbows
One must jump up and clap
explanationEn: Because the right hand is honored for greeting and noble acts, one extends or raises the right hand toward Al-Hajar al-Aswad.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 168 (Sunnah of right hand); Al-Sharh al-Mumti'

questionEn: What is the approximate perimeter of one circuit around the Kaaba near the center vs on the outer courtyard ring?
optionsEn: Upper floors require 14 laps because they are wider
Outer rings count for two laps each

Close to the Kaaba (~150–200 meters per lap, taking ~15–25 minutes total for 7 laps), whereas outer courtyard/upper rings are wider (~400–600+ meters per lap, taking ~45–75 minutes)—both count identically!
Every ring is exactly 10 meters
explanationEn: Understanding time differences helps families plan hydration, rest, and prayer schedules cleanly whether walking near the Kaaba or on calmer upper tiers.

questionEn: Why does Al-Masjid al-Haram restrict the ground-floor inner Mataf strictly to pilgrims wearing Ihram during peak Umrah seasons like Ramadan?
optionsEn: Because the ground floor closes permanently
Because non-muhrims are banned from Makkah in Ramadan

As a crowd-safety measure so Ihram-wearing Umrah pilgrims can complete their obligatory Umrah Tawaf smoothly without excessive gridlock, while voluntary Tawafs in regular clothes use the upper rings peacefully
Because regular clothes invalidate voluntary Tawaf
explanationEn: Respecting this seasonal arrangement helps newly arrived tired pilgrims finish their mandatory Umrah Tawaf safely while voluntary Tawaf remains open upstairs.

questionEn: If a pilgrim arrives at a Miqat mosque (like Abyar Ali or Qarn al-Manazil) and forgets to enter Ihram BEFORE leaving the mosque, then remembers 5 km down the highway toward Makkah, what should they do?
optionsEn: Stop immediately or turn back to the Miqat station (only a few minutes away) to make Niyyah properly, or make Niyyah right away if still parallel/not past—turning back a few kilometers eliminates any Dam worry completely
Enter Ihram at the Makkah hotel
Skip Umrah altogether
Keep driving all the way to Makkah ignoring it
explanationEn: Turning back those few kilometers right away before entering Makkah resolves the oversight cleanly with zero penalty.

questionEn: If someone enters Ihram at Miqat for Umrah al-Tamattu' in Dhul-Qa'dah and THEN changes their mind inside Makkah deciding NOT to stay for Hajj (returning home after Umrah), do they owe a Hady?
optionsEn: Their Umrah becomes void
No! Because they did not actually combine Hajj with that Umrah—their Umrah stands complete as a valid independent Umrah with zero Hajj Hady due
Yes, they still owe a camel
Yes, they are barred from leaving Makkah
explanationEn: Tamattu' Hady becomes obligatory only upon actually entering Hajj after that Umrah in the same season.

questionEn: What is the key difference in Talbiyah stopping time between Umrah and Hajj?
optionsEn: In both, Talbiyah stops at Jeddah airport
In Umrah, Talbiyah continues for a full month afterward
In Hajj, Talbiyah stops before Arafah
In Umrah, Talbiyah stops upon beginning Tawaf at the Black Stone; in Hajj, Talbiyah continues until throwing the first pebble at Jamrat al-Aqabah on 10 Dhul-Hijjah
explanationEn: Al-Fadl ibn Abbas (RA) narrated the Hajj timing (Bukhari 1544), while Ibn Abbas/Tirmidhi 919 preserved the Umrah timing—a classic distinction every pilgrim should know.

questionEn: What is the difference between 'Tawaf al-Qudum' (Arrival Tawaf) and 'Tawaf al-Umrah'?
optionsEn: Tawaf al-Qudum is the greeting Tawaf performed by a Mufrid (Hajj-only) or Qarin pilgrim upon arriving in Makkah, whereas Tawaf al-Umrah is the obligatory pillar Tawaf of Umrah (which itself counts as arrival greeting for the Umrah/Tamattu' pilgrim)
They are two completely identical names for Sa'i
Umrah pilgrims must perform Tawaf al-Qudum AND Tawaf al-Umrah separately (14 laps)
Tawaf al-Qudum has 3 laps only
explanationEn: An Umrah pilgrim does NOT perform an extra arrival Tawaf before Umrah Tawaf—their single 7-circuit Tawaf al-Umrah fulfills both!

questionEn: When a pilgrim performs Hajj al-Qiran (combining Umrah and Hajj in one Ihram), do they shave their head after completing their arrival Tawaf and Sa'i?
optionsEn: Qarin pilgrims never shave at all
No! A Qarin remains in Ihram until 10 Dhul-Hijjah after stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah and sacrificing Hady—only a Tamattu' or standalone Umrah pilgrim exits Ihram with Halq/Taqsir after Umrah Sa'i
Yes, Qarin pilgrims exit Ihram twice
Qarin pilgrims skip Tawaf
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ remained in Ihram as a Qarin during the Farewell Pilgrimage because he had brought Hady, telling companions without Hady to exit after Umrah (Tamattu').

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:196), what is the exact ruling on 'Tamattu'' if a pilgrim cannot afford a sacrificial Hady animal?
optionsEn: Fast three days during the Hajj days and seven days when returning home—ten complete days in total
Skip Hajj permanently
Feed one neighbor
Perform three extra Umrahs instead
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:196) explicitly lays out this merciful three-plus-seven fasting alternative for Mutamatti' pilgrims lacking Hady means.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ explain about the 'Days of Mina' (Days of Tashriq: 11, 12, 13 Dhul-Hijjah) regarding fasting vs eating?
optionsEn: Water is forbidden in Mina
'The days of Tashriq are days of eating, drinking, and remembrance of Allah'—except fasting the 3-day Tamattu' substitute when one could not afford Hady and did not fast before Arafah
Umrah is required on 11 Dhul-Hijjah
Everyone must fast all three days of Tashriq
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih Muslim (1141) and Sahih al-Bukhari (1997, Aisha & Ibn Umar's exception for Tamattu' fasters lacking Hady).

questionEn: Why does the Qur'an pair 'al-Hajj' and 'al-Umrah' together in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:196?
optionsEn: Because Hajj has no Arafah
Because Umrah is only allowed during Hajj days
Because both share the core sacred principles—entering Ihram purely for Allah, honoring the Sacred House, completing rites faithfully, and observing Fidyah/Ihsar safeguards
Because both require 14 laps of Tawaf
explanationEn: Qur'an 2:196 anchors the entire legal framework of both Major and Minor Pilgrimage.

questionEn: If a pilgrim enters Ihram intending ONLY Hajj (Ifrad) during Hajj season, can they switch their intention to Umrah (Tamattu') upon arriving in Makkah if they didn't bring Hady?
optionsEn: Converting invalidates both Hajj and Umrah

Yes! The Prophet ﷺ explicitly commanded his Companions at Makkah who had entered for Ifrad without Hady to convert it into Umrah (Faskh al-Hajj ila al-'Umrah), perform Tawaf, Sa'i, and Taqsir, and later enter Ihram for Hajj on 8 Dhul-Hijjah
Only residents of Yemen can convert
No, intention can never change upward or downward
explanationEn: Many scholars (especially Hanbalis and Ibn Abbas/Ibn al-Qayyim) highlight this authentic Prophetic concession as valid and rewarding when lacking Hady.

questionEn: On the other hand, what if a pilgrim enters Ihram for Umrah in Dhul-Hijjah and suddenly faces an urgent reason (like a woman whose menstruation started before Tawaf near 8 Dhul-Hijjah) preventing finishing Umrah before Arafah?
optionsEn: She can never perform Hajj
She must leave Saudi Arabia immediately
She must perform Tawaf while menstruating

Just as the Prophet ﷺ instructed Aisha (RA), she merges Hajj into her Umrah (converting to Qiran: 'Labbayk bi-Hajj wa Umrah'), performs all Hajj rites at Arafah/Muzdalifah/Mina, and completes one Tawaf and Sa'i after purifying
explanationEn: This is the exact compassionate solution the Prophet ﷺ gave Aisha (RA) at Sarif when her cycle began just before Hajj.

questionEn: What is the minimum distance from Makkah of the closest Miqat (Qarn al-Manazil / al-Sayl al-Kabir) versus the farthest Miqat (Dhul-Hulayfah / Abyar Ali)?
optionsEn: Dhul-Hulayfah is 10 km away and Qarn al-Manazil is 800 km away
Both are 5 km from the Kaaba
All five Miqats are inside Jeddah
Qarn al-Manazil is roughly 75–90 km east of Makkah, whereas Dhul-Hulayfah is roughly 420–450 km north near Madinah
explanationEn: Seeing this geographic layout explains why Madinah travelers travel several hours in Ihram while Ta'if/Riyadh road travelers enter Ihram closer to Makkah.

questionEn: Which Miqat is located nearest to the Red Sea coast north-northwest of Makkah?
optionsEn: Yalamlam
Qarn al-Manazil
Al-Juhfah (near Rabigh)
Dhat Irq
explanationEn: Al-Juhfah sits near Rabigh along the coastal corridor between Madinah/Egypt/Sham and Makkah.

questionEn: Which two Miqats serve travelers arriving from the south and east respectively?
optionsEn: Al-Tan'im serves India
Al-Juhfah serves Iraq
Dhul-Hulayfah serves Yemen and Yalamlam serves Madinah
Yalamlam serves the south (Yemen and southern maritime/air routes), while Qarn al-Manazil (east/Najd) and Dhat Irq (northeast/Iraq) serve eastern routes
explanationEn: Knowing the five directional stations clarifies why airlines announce specific Miqat names depending on flight path.

questionEn: What is 'Masjid al-Bay'ah' near Mina, and is visiting it part of Umrah rituals?
optionsEn: Sa'i ends at Masjid al-Bay'ah
The historic mosque marking the site of the Pledges of Aqabah between the Prophet ﷺ and the Ansar; it is an inspiring Seerah landmark, NOT part of Umrah rituals
It is a Miqat station for Umrah
Pilgrims must pray two rak'ahs there after Tawaf
explanationEn: Umrah takes place inside Makkah/Al-Masjid al-Haram (and Miqat entry); Mina, Muzdalifah, and Arafah belong to Hajj and historical reflection.
reference: Sirah Ibn Hisham; Fiqh of Umrah

questionEn: What is 'Masjid al-Jinn' in Makkah historically associated with, and is it part of Umrah?
optionsEn: Tawaf starts at Masjid al-Jinn
It is one of the five Miqats
Historically associated with the site where a group of Jinn listened to the Prophet ﷺ reciting the Qur'an and believed (Surah al-Jinn); it is a local Makkah mosque, NOT an Umrah ritual
Pilgrims must stop there before Sa'i
explanationEn: Keeping clear boundaries between Prophetic Umrah rituals and local historic mosques prevents superstitious tour itineraries.

questionEn: What is 'Al-Ma'la' (Jannat al-Mu'alla) cemetery in Makkah, and who prominent is buried there?
optionsEn: Makkah's historic cemetery north of Al-Masjid al-Haram, where Umm al-Mu'minin Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA) and early Muslims rest; visiting to pray for the dead reminds one of the Hereafter (though NOT an Umrah pillar)
The cemetery where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is buried (note: he ﷺ is buried in Madinah)
The fifth Miqat station
A shopping bazaar near Safa
explanationEn: If visiting Jannat al-Mu'alla (men per Sunnah cemetery etiquette), remember to greet the deceased and make dua facing Qiblah—never seeking favors from graves or wiping walls.
reference: Sahih Muslim 974 (cemetery greeting); History of Makkah

questionEn: Can women visit cemeteries like Jannat al-Mu'alla or Jannat al-Baqi during an Umrah trip?
optionsEn: Women must climb onto graves during Umrah
Cemeteries are open only to children

Scholars differ: many prohibit frequent/customary cemetery visits for women based on 'Allah cursed female visitors of graves' (while Hanafis and others allow occasional visits without wailing, citing Aisha RA's visit and the Prophet's ﷺ cemetery dua)—yet practically in Makkah/Madinah women normally offer Salam from outside the gates or follow their trusted scholar's guidance without crowding
Visiting cemeteries is a pillar of Umrah
explanationEn: In Saudi Arabia, cemetery enclosures are organized accordingly—and remembering that visiting cemeteries is never part of Umrah or Madinah Ziyarah conditions keeps everything serene.
reference: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 1056; Sahih Muslim 974; Fatawa Ibn Baz

questionEn: Why is it important for Umrah pilgrims not to buy 'special blessed prayer rugs' or 'blessed rings' sold on streets claiming magical Umrah powers?
optionsEn: Because rings break Tawaf
Because street vendors only sell gold
Because prayer rugs are banned in hotels
Because attributing supernatural barakah or luck to commercial trinkets has no basis in Islam and borders on superstition; true blessing lies in sincere faith, Qur'an, Sunnah, and Zamzam
explanationEn: Guided awareness protects pilgrims from commercial scams while anchoring faith purely in Allah.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim check before donating money to unauthorized street solicitors around Makkah or Madinah hotels?
optionsEn: Scold every poor person harshly
Give all travel funds to strangers at hotel doors
Refuse to help anyone ever
Channel substantial charity through official licensed charitable foundations (or directly buy food/water for genuinely needy workers) rather than fueling organized street begging networks
explanationEn: Surah Al-Duha (93:10) teaches never repelling a beggar harshly ('Wa ammas-sa'ila fa-la tanhar'), while wise giving ensures charity truly reaches those in real need.

questionEn: What is the etiquette when someone asks you to pass a bottle of Zamzam water or share space on your prayer mat inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Pull your mat away angrily
Pretend not to see them
Tell them to buy their own mat
Welcome them warmly, shift slightly to make room ('tafassahu fil-majalis', 58:11), and serve them joyfully—hospitality inside Allah's House is noble
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mujadilah (58:11) explicitly rewards believers who make room for others in assemblies: 'When you are told, Make space in assemblies, then make space; Allah will make space for you.'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ praise making space for a fellow believer in the mosque row?
optionsEn: Empty gaps attract blessings
Allah fills the gaps of mercy for those who connect rows and welcomes gentle accommodation for fellow worshippers
Sharing space shortens Salah
Only front-row worshippers enter Paradise
explanationEn: Gentle warmth when squeezing one more elder onto a shaded courtyard spot creates brotherhood across languages and borders.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if they see someone performing an obvious error in Umrah (such as walking clockwise around the Kaaba or starting Sa'i at Marwah)?
optionsEn: Laugh loudly and record them for social media
Yell at them in anger
Advise them gently, privately, and with warm wisdom ('Ud'u ila sabili rabbika bil-hikmati wal-maw'izatil-hasanah', 16:125)—never humiliate or scold anyone publicly
Push them physically out of the Mataf
explanationEn: Remember how the Prophet ﷺ gently taught the Bedouin who urinated in the mosque and the man who prayed hastily—kindness opens hearts to truth.

questionEn: If you do not speak the same language as a pilgrim next to you who seems confused about where Safa or the Black Stone green light is, how can you help?
optionsEn: Point in the wrong direction as a joke
Ignore them because you don't share a language
Smile kindly and point clearly toward the Black Stone alignment light or Safa archway (or walk a few steps guiding them gently)
Tell them to ask later
explanationEn: A warm smile and a clear helpful gesture transcend every language barrier in the Sacred Sanctuary.

questionEn: What is the virtue of smiling cheerfully at your Muslim brother or sister while in Makkah and Madinah?
optionsEn: Only frowning shows piety
Smiling breaks Ihram
Smiling is forbidden during Tawaf
The Prophet ﷺ taught: 'Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity (Sadaqah)'—so cheerful courtesy in crowded hallways is constant effortless charity!
explanationEn: True reverence (khushu') lives peacefully alongside gentle warmth and kindness toward Allah's guests.

questionEn: Why is it recommended to learn basic Arabic phrases like 'JazakAllahu khayran', 'Afwan', 'Tafaddal', and 'Min fadlik' before traveling for Umrah?
optionsEn: To express gratitude, polite excuses, and warmth to fellow pilgrims and Sanctuary staff smoothly
Because Arabic phrases replace Talbiyah
Because hotel doors only open to Arabic words
Because speaking English in Makkah is illegal
explanationEn: Simple courteous phrases build instant rapport and ease daily communication in Makkah and Madinah.

questionEn: If a pilgrim misses a flight or faces hours of airport immigration delay while already wearing Ihram, how should they respond spiritually?
optionsEn: Take off Ihram in frustration and curse
Refuse to drink water
Treat the delay as a test of Sabr (patience) and opportunity for extra Talbiyah, Qur'an, and Istighfar rather than losing temper at airline staff
Abandon Umrah in the terminal
explanationEn: Tests of patience often arrive before stepping onto the Mataf; responding with composure and dhikr earns immense hidden reward.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim is delayed at Jeddah immigration for 8 hours while in Ihram—does any time limit make Ihram 'expire'?
optionsEn: Ihram expires automatically after 4 hours
No! Ihram has no expiration clock—whether it takes 2 hours or 2 days to reach Makkah, you simply stay calmly in Ihram prohibitions until completing Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir
You must repeat Niyyah every hour
Delays over 6 hours cancel Umrah
explanationEn: Knowing Ihram never expires removes panic during travel or traffic delays on the Jeddah–Makkah highway.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim stop at a hotel in Makkah to drop off luggage, use the restroom, shower gently (unscented), or take a quick nap BEFORE heading to Al-Masjid al-Haram for Umrah?
optionsEn: No, one must go straight from the bus into Tawaf carrying heavy suitcases
Napping before Tawaf breaks Ihram
Yes, completely permissible and often very wise after an overnight flight—stay strictly within all Ihram rules while resting and freshening up, then head to the Haram refreshed and focused!
Showering before Tawaf is forbidden
explanationEn: Taking 45 minutes to check in, leave heavy bags safely, refresh Wudu, and eat a light bite makes Tawaf and Sa'i focused and joyful rather than dizzy.

questionEn: If a pilgrim rests at the hotel first before going to Al-Masjid al-Haram, may they use the hotel's fragrant shampoo or scented body wash?
optionsEn: No! Remember you are already in full Ihram—pack your own unscented soap/shampoo from home and avoid complimentary scented hotel toiletries until AFTER Halq/Taqsir!
Yes, only perfume sprays are forbidden
Soap is forbidden altogether even if unscented
Yes, hotel soap doesn't count
explanationEn: This is one of the easiest slips to avoid by bringing a small fragrance-free soap bar/wash in your carry-on bag.

questionEn: What is the ruling on applying unscented petroleum jelly between the thighs before starting the ~3 km Sa'i walk to prevent painful skin chafing?
optionsEn: Completely permissible (provided it is 100% fragrance-free) and highly recommended for walking comfort in warm weather
Prohibited in Ihram
Invalidates Sa'i
Counts as wearing tailored trousers
explanationEn: Preventing painful chafing helps pilgrims complete all 7 laps of Sa'i comfortably without distraction.

questionEn: What is the ruling on taking oral motion-sickness medication before riding buses from Madinah to Makkah in Ihram?
optionsEn: Requires a Dam
Breaks Wudu
Completely permissible; oral tablets do not conflict with Ihram in any way
Prohibited until Halq
explanationEn: Taking non-drowsy or prescribed motion-sickness tablets ensures a peaceful ~5-hour ride from Dhul-Hulayfah to Makkah.

questionEn: What is the approximate travel distance between Madinah (Dhul-Hulayfah) and Makkah by highway today?
optionsEn: Roughly 440–450 kilometers (around 4.5–6 hours by bus/car, or ~2–2.5 hours via the Haramain High-Speed Train)
About 2,000 kilometers
About 5 kilometers
About 30 kilometers
explanationEn: Appreciating this distance—once crossed on camelback by the Prophet ﷺ over ~8–10 days!—inspires deep gratitude for modern transport and patience during a short bus or train ride.

questionEn: How long did it take the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions to travel the ~450 km from Madinah to Makkah on camelback during Umrah and the Farewell Pilgrimage?
optionsEn: One afternoon
Roughly 8 to 10 days across rugged desert valleys and mountain passes
Six months
Two hours
explanationEn: Reflecting on the sacrifice and endurance of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions deepens humility when traveling in air-conditioned buses and trains today.

questionEn: During Umrah Tawaf, why should a pilgrim avoid leaning their arm or hand OVER the curved wall of Hijr Ismail while walking past it?
optionsEn: Because touching marble invalidates Wudu
Because the wall is electrified
Because part of their arm or torso would pass inside the interior space of the Kaaba foundations; keep your entire body cleanly outside the outer face of Hijr Ismail's wall
Because Hijr Ismail is outside Makkah
explanationEn: Jurists point out that circling around the Kaaba requires one's whole body to remain outside the House—including Hijr Ismail's wall and Shadhrawan.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim climb or walk along the top rim of the curved wall of Hijr Ismail during Tawaf?
optionsEn: No; walking atop Hijr Ismail's wall places one inside the boundary of the Kaaba foundations and voids that circuit, besides being unsafe
Only children should walk atop the wall
It is required on lap 7
Yes, walking atop the wall counts as two laps
explanationEn: Always walk along the Mataf floor safely outside Hijr Ismail's wall.

questionEn: If a pilgrim wants to perform TWO separate voluntary Tawafs after finishing Umrah, should they walk 14 continuous circuits first and then pray 4 rak'ahs afterward, or pray 2 rak'ahs after each 7-circuit Tawaf?
optionsEn: Skip the 2 rak'ahs on voluntary Tawafs
Pray 1 rak'ah after every single lap
Walk 21 laps before praying once
Complete one 7-circuit Tawaf, pray its 2 Sunnah rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim, and ONLY THEN start the next 7-circuit Tawaf (never combine 14 laps before praying)
explanationEn: Just as Ibn Umar (RA) practiced ('Every seven circuits has two rak'ahs'), separating each Tawaf cleanly with its two rak'ahs follows the Prophetic unit of worship.

questionEn: If an elderly pilgrim feels faint or falls down in the middle of the Mataf while you are doing Tawaf, what should you do?
optionsEn: Ignore them because you are in Ihram
Keep walking past them so you don't interrupt your lap
Restart Umrah from home if you stop to help
Pause your Tawaf immediately to help lift them safely aside, give water, or alert Haram paramedics—saving or aiding a distressed believer takes priority, and you simply resume your lap afterward!
explanationEn: Rescuing or assisting a fallen person is an urgent moral obligation that never invalidates your Tawaf; step back into your circuit calmly once they are safe.

questionEn: Is there any Sunnah in Umrah requiring adults to weigh their shaved hair and give its weight in silver as charity (Sadaqah)?
optionsEn: No; weighing shaved hair in silver is Sunnah ONLY for a newborn baby's Aqiqah on the 7th day after birth (al-Tirmidhi 1519)—NOT for adults after Halq in Umrah or Hajj
Without weighing hair, Tahallul fails
Yes, every adult Umrah pilgrim must weigh shaved hair in gold
Yes, barbers weigh hair before issuing Umrah certificates
explanationEn: Confusing newborn Aqiqah sunnahs with adult Umrah Halq is a common mix-up; adults simply shave or trim cleanly and give general Sadaqah joyfully as they wish.

questionEn: Can a pre-pubescent minor (even a bright 11-year-old) be appointed to perform Badal Umrah on behalf of a deceased grandparent?
optionsEn: No; jurists require a Badal proxy to be a legally accountable adult (Baligh, sane) who has already performed their own Umrah first
Any 5-year-old suffices
Only children under 10 qualify
Yes, infants can perform Badal Umrah
explanationEn: Because a minor is not yet legally accountable (mukallaf) and their own Umrah counts as voluntary, proxy Umrah must be carried out by an adult Muslim who completed their own Umrah.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in the middle of Tawaf and becomes severely parched in summer heat, may they step briefly to a Zamzam dispenser at the Mataf edge to sip water and resume?
optionsEn: Yes; taking a brief sip of water when genuinely thirsty and returning immediately to the exact spot does not break Tawaf continuity
No, drinking water mid-Tawaf voids all circuits
One must restart from lap 1
Water may only be drunk during lap 7
explanationEn: Staying hydrated prevents heat exhaustion; quick hydration is excused, while sitting down for a formal long Zamzam dua session is best after the 2 rak'ahs.

questionEn: How do the mountain passes 'Kada'' (upper Makkah) and 'Kuda'' (lower Makkah) relate to the Prophet's ﷺ entrance and exit in Umrah and Hajj?
optionsEn: They are names for Safa and Marwah
Ibn Umar (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah from the upper pass (Kada' near al-Mu'alla) and exited from the lower pass (Kuda' near al-Shubaykah)
They are islands in the Red Sea
They are two gates inside Masjid Quba
explanationEn: Mentioned in Sahih al-Bukhari (1576) and Sahih Muslim (1257), entering from one direction and departing another was the Prophet's ﷺ gentle habit, though any modern road is completely valid today.

questionEn: Who wrote down the actual text of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah during the Prophet's ﷺ 6 AH Umrah expedition?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)
Abu Hurayrah (RA)
Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
explanationEn: When Ali (RA) hesitated out of reverence to erase 'Messenger of Allah' at Suhayl ibn Amr's demand, the Prophet ﷺ asked Ali to point to the words and erased it with his own blessed hand.

questionEn: During the Hudaybiyyah Umrah (6 AH), what miraculous provision of water occurred for the 1,400+ Companions when their camp ran dry?
optionsEn: They drank seawater from Jeddah
They marched straight to Ta'if for snow
They had zero water until returning to Madinah
Water sprang abundantly from between the Prophet's ﷺ fingers placed in a vessel/well (or an arrow placed in the shallow well at Hudaybiyyah), quenching all 1,400–1,500 men and their animals
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) and al-Bara' ibn Azib (RA) preserved this famous miracle in Sahih al-Bukhari (3576, 4152) during the Hudaybiyyah Umrah expedition.

questionEn: From which elevated hillside overlooking Al-Masjid al-Haram did the chiefs of Quraysh watch the Muslims perform Umrat al-Qada' (7 AH)?
optionsEn: Mount Qu'ayqi'an (northwest of the Kaaba)
Jabal al-Rahmah at Arafah
Mount Sinai
Mount Uhud
explanationEn: Quraysh gathered on Qu'ayqi'an saying the fever of Yathrib had weakened the Muslims—prompting the Prophet's ﷺ order to perform brisk Raml to display strength and vitality.

questionEn: When Quraysh chiefs watched the Muslims performing Raml during Umrat al-Qada', what did they say to one another in astonishment?
optionsEn: 'They forgot how to walk'
'They are leaving Makkah right now'
'Are these the people you claimed were weakened by fever? They leap faster than gazelles!'
'They brought zero companions'
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated this exact reaction in Sahih Muslim (1266), illustrating the immediate dignity and morale boost of Raml.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ NOT stay in Makkah permanently after Umrat al-Qada' (7 AH), nor even after the Conquest of Makkah (8 AH)?
optionsEn: Because Quraysh banned him in 9 AH
Out of deep loyalty to the Ansar of Madinah—remembering his pledge to live and pass away among them ('Life is with you and death is with you') after Allah gave him Makkah
Because he disliked the Kaaba
Because Makkah had no drinking water
explanationEn: Even after conquering Makkah and performing Umrat al-Ji'ranah, the Prophet ﷺ honored his covenant with the Ansar and returned to Madinah (Sahih Muslim 1780).

questionEn: Does performing Umrah during Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, or Sha'ban carry full validity just like Dhul-Qa'dah?
optionsEn: Only odd-numbered months are valid
Only Dhul-Qa'dah and Ramadan are valid
Yes! All Islamic months outside active Hajj days (9–13 Dhul-Hijjah) are completely valid for Umrah—with Ramadan specifically singled out for Hajj-equivalent reward
No, Safar Umrah is forbidden
explanationEn: Correcting pre-Islamic superstitions around 'unlucky months' like Safar, Islam affirms every day and month created by Allah is blessed for worship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5757 (no bad omen in Safar); Fiqh al-Sunnah

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Umrah in Sha'ban right before Ramadan begins?
optionsEn: Completely valid and rewarding—while if someone specifically times entering Ramadan in Makkah, performing Umrah inside Ramadan itself earns the special Hadith equivalence to Hajj
Umrah in Sha'ban is prohibited
One must wait until Eid al-Fitr
Sha'ban Umrah counts as Hajj
explanationEn: Every Umrah carries expiation of minor sins between consecutive Umrahs (Bukhari 1773), and timing one inside Ramadan adds that special virtue.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim know if they arrive in Makkah on the last day of Sha'ban, enter Ihram and do Tawaf/Sa'i before Maghrib, and Ramadan's crescent is sighted at Maghrib?
optionsEn: They must repeat Sha'ban's Umrah
Sha'ban Umrah automatically converts backward
Their Umrah completed cleanly in Sha'ban; to earn the Ramadan-specific Umrah reward, one performs Umrah AFTER Ramadan has actually begun (post-Maghrib sighting)
Ramadan begins only at Fajr
explanationEn: Islamic months begin at Maghrib sunset upon crescent confirmation; starting Umrah after the first Maghrib of Ramadan places the full Umrah inside Ramadan.

questionEn: If a pilgrim begins Tawaf at 11:50 PM on the 29th/30th night of Ramadan and finishes Sa'i and Taqsir BEFORE Fajr on Eid al-Fitr morning (after Maghrib of Shawwal already began!), is that Ramadan Umrah or Shawwal Umrah?
optionsEn: Umrah on Eid night is invalid
Ramadan lasts until noon on Eid day
Once Maghrib sets on the night before Eid al-Fitr (Laylat al-Ja'izah), Ramadan has ended and Shawwal has begun—so their Umrah is a valid Shawwal Umrah!
Shawwal starts only after Eid prayer
explanationEn: Remembering the Islamic day runs Maghrib-to-Maghrib prevents mistaking Eid night (1st night of Shawwal) for Ramadan.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Umrah on Eid al-Fitr day itself (1st of Shawwal)?
optionsEn: Completely valid! Unlike Eid al-Adha (10 Dhul-Hijjah, which falls within Hajj days), Eid al-Fitr is the first day of Shawwal and Umrah is fully permissible
Prohibited for seven days after Ramadan
Only valid for children on Eid al-Fitr
Requires sacrificing a sheep
explanationEn: Many pilgrims pray Eid al-Fitr prayer in Al-Masjid al-Haram and then travel to/from Makkah performing Umrah peacefully on Eid or early Shawwal.

questionEn: Why do Hanafi scholars view performing standalone Umrah on the 9th through 13th of Dhul-Hijjah (Day of Arafah and Eid/Tashriq days) as prohibited/makruh tahriman?
optionsEn: Because the Kaaba is closed on those days
Because Safa and Marwah are flooded
Because Zamzam stops flowing
Because those five days are specifically dedicated exclusively to Hajj rites (Arafah, Muzdalifah, Mina, Jamarat), as narrated from Aisha and Ibn Abbas (RA) regarding those days
explanationEn: Knowing this classical Hanafi position (and practical Saudi Hajj-season permit restrictions keeping Makkah focused on Hajj pilgrims during Dhul-Hijjah) explains why Umrah trips pause during core Hajj days.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is in Makkah and feels sick during Tawaf, what distinguishes a minor dizziness from true 'Ihsar' (obstruction)?
optionsEn: Waiting 20 minutes at the gate counts as Ihsar

Minor dizziness or temporary fever simply warrants resting at the hotel for a day or using a wheelchair, whereas true Ihsar means being genuinely unable to complete the rites at all (e.g., severe hospitalization, border blockade, deportation)
Missing one meal counts as Ihsar
Any sneeze counts as Ihsar
explanationEn: As long as you remain in Makkah and can recover or use a wheelchair to finish Tawaf and Sa'i safely, you simply rest and complete your Umrah without resorting to Ihsar.

questionEn: Can an Umrah pilgrim enter Ihram from a Miqat if they are unsure whether their hotel in Makkah is ready—can you enter Ihram before checking into a hotel?
optionsEn: No, hotel keys must be picked up before Miqat
Hotel receptionists assign your Miqat
Waiting at a hotel lobby before Tawaf voids Niyyah
Yes! Entering Ihram at the Miqat depends strictly on crossing the Miqat boundary intending Umrah—hotel check-in timing has zero effect on Ihram validity
explanationEn: Pilgrims routinely cross the Miqat first, arrive in Makkah, drop bags at their hotel, refresh Wudu, and walk into Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: If a woman wears a dark abaya and headscarf over ordinary light cotton clothes in Ihram, does she have to wear white?
optionsEn: Yes, women must wear white towels like men
Dark abayas invalidate Ihram
Only green hijabs are valid
No! Wearing modest black, navy, grey, beige, or any clean non-ostentatious color is completely valid for women in Ihram (just no niqab, no gloves, and no perfume)
explanationEn: Comfort, breathability, opacity, and full modesty are what matter for women's attire—white is never obligatory for women.

questionEn: What should a woman check about her headscarf/khimar before starting Umrah if she plans to drape it loosely (Sadl) over her face near crowds?
optionsEn: Use a thick opaque mask tied tightly behind her ears
Pin a stitched veil across her nose
Walk with eyes completely closed
Choose a lightweight, breathable, non-transparent fabric that lets her see her footing clearly on stairs and curbs without tripping, and never uses tailored niqab elastic/eye-slits
explanationEn: Safety while walking stairs and crowded plazas paired with effortless modesty makes a breathable draped khimar ideal.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1833; Practical Women's Umrah Guide

questionEn: Is a woman allowed to wear a broad-brimmed sun visor or cap attached to her headscarf if outdoors in Makkah heat while in Ihram?
optionsEn: Sun hats are mandatory for men and women
Visors must be stitched onto the face
Umbrellas are banned for women
Scholars advise avoiding rigid visor hats mimicking a cap/niqab if unnecessary, while shading with a handheld umbrella is unanimously permissible, safe, and keeps face/head unencumbered
explanationEn: A compact UV umbrella provides far better full-body shade without touching the face or head.

questionEn: What is the ruling on women wearing comfortable athletic walking sneakers (with socks) during the ~3 km walk of Sa'i?
optionsEn: Strictly forbidden—women must wear open flip-flops
Footwear must be removed at Safa
Sneakers are allowed only for men
Completely permissible and highly recommended for women in Ihram to prevent foot fatigue, blisters, and heel strain
explanationEn: Because closed shoes and socks are forbidden only for men in Ihram, women can wear supportive clean socks and walking shoes comfortably (keeping outdoor street shoes clean or switching to dedicated indoor walking shoes inside the Mas'a!).

questionEn: Why is carrying a pair of clean dedicated indoor socks/slippers (never worn outdoors on street asphalt) helpful for women inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Because indoor socks replace Wudu
It keeps the Haram marble and carpets completely clean from street dust while cushioning heels during long Tawaf and Sa'i walks
Because bare feet are forbidden indoors
Because outdoor shoes are confiscated permanently
explanationEn: Dedicated soft-soled mosque slippers or clean non-slip socks protect both knee joints on hard marble and the pristine cleanliness of the Sanctuary.

questionEn: What is the ruling on men wearing soft barefoot-style 'house socks' ONLY after exiting Ihram (during voluntary Tawafs later in the week) vs while IN Ihram?
optionsEn: Men must wear wool socks inside Ihram
Socks break Wudu after Halq
While IN Ihram, men avoid socks covering the ankles/feet (wearing open sandals exposing ankles); AFTER Halq/Taqsir (when out of Ihram), men may wear clean socks freely during voluntary Tawafs
Men can never wear socks inside Makkah ever
explanationEn: Remembering what belongs specifically to Ihram vs post-Tahallul makes multi-day Makkah stays effortless.

questionEn: If a pilgrim performs Umrah and forgets to say 'Bismillah, Allahu Akbar' when pointing at the Black Stone during lap 3 and lap 4, is their Tawaf still valid?
optionsEn: Yes, completely valid; saying Takbir and pointing at the Black Stone are Sunnah acts whose accidental omission never invalidates Tawaf
They owe a sheep
No, laps 3 and 4 must be repeated
They must restart from Miqat
explanationEn: Only the essential pillars/conditions (7 complete counter-clockwise circuits outside Hijr Ismail with Wudu and Awrah covered) determine Tawaf validity; missing a Sunnah dhikr never invalidates it.

questionEn: If you miss raising your right hand toward the Black Stone on lap 5 because you were gently supporting an elderly parent with both hands, is your lap valid?
optionsEn: Lap 5 does not count
No, both hands must be free at every corner
100% valid! Supporting your parent safely takes precedence, and saying 'Allahu Akbar' softly in your heart/tongue suffices without even needing to raise a hand
You must drop the elder's hand immediately
explanationEn: Prioritizing an elderly parent's stability over an optional hand gesture reflects deep fiqh wisdom and kindness.

questionEn: What does 'Istilam' literally mean in Arabic, and why is it used for greeting the Black Stone?
optionsEn: Derived from 'silm' or 'salam' (greeting/touching smoothly in peace), meaning greeting the Stone by kissing, touching, or saluting it from afar
Climbing onto a stone
Throwing pebbles
Washing with soap
explanationEn: Classical lexicons explain Istilam as greeting the Stone peacefully as an act of submission to Allah's Sunnah.

questionEn: Did the Prophet ﷺ ever push or wrestle through crowds to kiss the Black Stone when the area was packed?
optionsEn: He skipped Tawaf when crowded
Yes, he ordered guards to push crowds aside every lap
He stopped Tawaf until everyone left
Never! When riding his camel or amidst crowds during the Farewell Pilgrimage, he ﷺ simply pointed toward the Black Stone from afar with his curved staff and said 'Allahu Akbar'
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ own gentle example—pointing calmly from a distance whenever crowded—keeps the Mataf peaceful and safe.

questionEn: If a pilgrim is lucky enough to find the Black Stone area completely uncrowded and kisses it gently, what should they NEVER do afterward?
optionsEn: Smile gratefully
Keep walking smoothly into the next lap
Never linger there blocking others behind, never shout/boast, and never assume kissing the Stone replaces any obligation or wipes out major sins without repentance
Say 'Allahu Akbar'
explanationEn: A brief respectful touch/kiss (taking care not to smear lipstick/perfume—wait: in Ihram, perfume is already absent!) followed by moving smoothly keeps traffic safe.

questionEn: Why do Haram attendants politely remind pilgrims NOT to apply perfume near the Black Stone even AFTER finishing Umrah?
optionsEn: Because men cannot use perfume ever
Because perfume dissolves marble
Because Black Stone smells naturally like roses

Because scenting the Black Stone transfers fragrance onto Ihram-wearing pilgrims who touch or kiss it, risking unintended Ihram perfume contact for them (and kissing/touching the Kaaba walls/Black Stone is guarded gently for everyone's safety)
explanationEn: Wait—even when the Kaaba/Black Stone IS occasionally perfumed by official custodians outside peak hours, if a pilgrim in Ihram touches it and smells heavy fragrance transferring onto their hands/face, they simply wipe/wash it off cleanly with no sin!

questionEn: What if a male pilgrim in Ihram kisses the Black Stone and notices wet fragrance transferred from the Kaaba's perfumed corner onto his forehead or lips?
optionsEn: He must shave immediately before finishing Tawaf
He must restart Umrah from Jeddah

He should immediately wipe/wash the fragrance off with plain water so it does not linger—since he did not intend to apply perfume, there is no sin and no penalty (and scholars advise muhrims simply to point from afar if they see wet scent on the Stone)
He owes a camel sacrifice
explanationEn: Pointing calmly from afar avoids both crowd crush and accidental perfume transfer cleanly!
reference: Fatawa Ibn Baz; Fatawa Ibn Uthaymin

questionEn: What is 'Al-Hajar al-Isma'il' vs 'Hijr Ismail'—which spelling/meaning is correct?
optionsEn: 'Hajar Ismail' means the Black Stone
It refers to a cave in Madinah
'Hijr Ismail' (with 'H-i-j-r', meaning enclosed/protected space or lap/courtyard) is the curved stone enclosure beside the Kaaba, NOT 'Hajar' (stone)
Both mean Mount Safa
explanationEn: Distinguishing 'Hijr' (enclosure/chamber) from 'Hajar' (stone, as in al-Hajar al-Aswad) avoids a common pronunciation mix-up.

questionEn: Is Prophet Isma'il (AS) or Hajar (AS) actually buried inside Hijr Ismail, or is it simply named for their legacy?
optionsEn: Prophetic/authentic consensus emphasizes it is part of the Kaaba's foundation (not a shrine for grave-worship), and historical narrations about burials there are weak/unconfirmed—nor would burying graves inside a mosque/Kaaba be venerated
One must kiss the floor of Hijr Ismail
It is a graveyard closed to prayer
Pilgrims must pray toward Hijr Ismail instead of the Kaaba
explanationEn: When you enter Hijr Ismail (outside Tawaf!), you pray facing the Kaaba wall—because you are literally praying inside the original Abrahamic perimeter of Allah's Sacred House!
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 2028; Majmu' Fatawa Ibn Taymiyyah

questionEn: If you want to pray two voluntary rak'ahs inside Hijr Ismail AFTER finishing your Umrah, which direction should you face?
optionsEn: Face upward only
Face toward Mount Safa
Face toward Madinah with your back to the Kaaba
Face directly toward the northern wall of the Kaaba (never facing outward toward the crowd with your back to the Kaaba!)
explanationEn: Facing the stone wall of the Kaaba ensures your Qiblah aligns accurately—and avoid lingering long inside Hijr Ismail during crowds so hundreds waiting in line also get a turn.

questionEn: What is the 'Shami' (Levantine) corner of the Kaaba, and does a pilgrim kiss or point at it during Tawaf?
optionsEn: The northwestern corner adjacent to Hijr Ismail facing Sham/Syria; you neither touch, kiss, nor point at it during Tawaf—simply walk calmly past it in dhikr and dua
One must pray two rak'ahs beside it mid-Tawaf
One must kiss it on lap 1
One must point at it saying 'Allahu Akbar'
explanationEn: Remember Ibn Abbas's (RA) report: only the Black Stone and Rukn al-Yamani are touched—never the Iraqi or Shami corners.

questionEn: When a pilgrim completes Sa'i at Mount Marwah and looks back toward the Kaaba, what feeling often fills the heart?
optionsEn: Relief that no more prayer is needed
Deep gratitude to Allah for carrying them safely from Miqat through Tawaf and Sa'i, coupled with sincere dua for acceptance and transformation
Anger at walking 3 km
Pride over being faster than everyone else
explanationEn: Closing Sa'i with heartfelt thankfulness and humility before Halq/Taqsir seals the spiritual beauty of Umrah.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing 'Tawaf' around the Kaaba while wearing prescription hearing aids or cochlear implants?
optionsEn: Must be removed at Miqat
Prohibited inside Masjid al-Haram
Requires a Dam
Completely permissible without any effect on Ihram, Wudu, or Tawaf
explanationEn: Assistive medical devices allow hearing-impaired believers to hear the Adhan, Imam's Qur'an recitation, and companions clearly.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim with asthma or seasonal allergies carry inside their Umrah waist pouch?
optionsEn: Using an inhaler requires repeating Tawaf
Inhalers are forbidden in Ihram
Asthma patients must avoid Makkah

Their prescribed rescue inhaler and unscented tissues—using an inhaler in Ihram is completely permissible (and even during daytime fasting, many scholars note rescue inhalers do not break the fast as vapor/medicine enters lungs, though keeping water/inhaler ready protects life)
explanationEn: Keeping life-saving inhalers accessible ensures immediate relief in dusty wind or dense crowds.

questionEn: If a pilgrim needs to take emergency diabetes medication with a sip of water during a daytime Ramadan Umrah because of severe hypoglycemia (dangerously low blood sugar), what must they do?
optionsEn: Refuse sugar and pass out in the Mataf
Sacrifice a camel
Never take medicine during Umrah
Break the fast immediately to treat the hypoglycemia and save their health/life, and simply make up that single fast day later after Ramadan without guilt
explanationEn: Preserving human life is mandatory in Islam (2:195, 4:29); treating hypoglycemia promptly and making up the missed fast later is both obligatory and merciful.

questionEn: What is the difference between 'Hajj Mabrur' / 'Umrah Mabrurah' and an Umrah performed merely for tourism or social prestige?
optionsEn: Accepted Umrah requires a five-star suite overlooking the Kaaba
Social media followers decide acceptance
An accepted Umrah is funded from halal earnings, anchored in sincerity (ikhlas), aligned with the Sunnah, free from sin/quarreling, and bears fruit in gentler, more God-conscious character afterward
Tourism Umrah takes 14 laps
explanationEn: Checking one's intention repeatedly—'O Allah, I ask You for sincerity and acceptance'—guards the journey from becoming mere sightseeing.

questionEn: What does the Prophet's ﷺ saying 'Allah does not look at your appearances or your wealth, rather He looks at your hearts and your deeds' teach an Umrah pilgrim?
optionsEn: That outer cleanliness does not matter
That poor pilgrims should not travel
That wealthy pilgrims have higher status in Salah
That whether one stays in a modest distant guesthouse or a clock-tower hotel, walks barefoot or rides a wheelchair, sincerity of heart and righteous action determine rank with Allah
explanationEn: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (RA) in Sahih Muslim (2564), this principle brings immense comfort to modest-income pilgrims standing beside anyone in Makkah.

questionEn: Why should pilgrims avoid feeling envious of VIPs, private hotel views, or front-row access during Umrah?
optionsEn: Because upper balconies receive zero reward
Because hotels are forbidden to view the Kaaba
Because envy doubles Tawaf speed
Because Allah accepts hearts wherever they stand in Al-Masjid al-Haram—and contentment (qana'ah) preserves spiritual peace and purity of heart
explanationEn: Every prayer anywhere inside Al-Masjid al-Haram carries the same 100,000-fold promise, and the Kaaba welcomes every sincere heart equally.

questionEn: What is the virtue of making dua for one's spouse, children, teachers, and friends who asked you to pray for them at the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Only family names are allowed in Makkah
One must charge a fee for remembering friends
Praying for friends reduces your own reward
Fulfilling promises of brotherhood ('Make dua for us at the House of Allah!'), which softens hearts and draws angelic 'Amin, and for you the same!'
explanationEn: Jotting a short note of people's dua requests before departing lets you honor every promise peacefully while resting or walking between Safa and Marwah.

questionEn: Remembering Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) when he visited Makkah—what did the Prophet ﷺ say to Umar when Umar asked permission to perform Umrah?
optionsEn: 'Skip Safa and Marwah'
'Never come back to Madinah'
'Pray only for yourself'
'O my brother, do not forget us in your righteous supplications!' (La tansana ya ukhayya min du'a'ik)
explanationEn: Though the chain in Abu Dawud/Tirmidhi has scholarly discussion, scholars fondly cite its beautiful spirit of asking departing Umrah travelers to remember loved ones in dua.

questionEn: What is the ruling on writing personal prayer lists on a small piece of paper or phone note to read quietly at Safa, Marwah, and after Zamzam?
optionsEn: Prohibited—duas must only be improvised
Reading from paper voids Sa'i
Completely permissible and very practical so you don't forget anyone's name or important dua amidst the awe of seeing the Kaaba
Only bound leather books are valid
explanationEn: Keeping a concise, heartfelt dua list helps keep your mind calm and present rather than scrambling to remember requests.

questionEn: Should a pilgrim place written paper wish-notes or photos inside the cracks of the Kaaba walls, Maqam Ibrahim, or Rawdah grilles?
optionsEn: No! Slipping paper notes, photos, locks, or coins into sanctuary walls is an unfounded superstition—speak directly to Allah, the All-Hearing who knows every secret of your heart without paper!
Yes, written slips guarantee instant answers
Coins thrown at Maqam Ibrahim fulfill Umrah
Photos must be taped onto Safa
explanationEn: Allah is closer to us than our jugular vein (50:16) and needs no slips of paper tucked into stone crevices; pure heartfelt dua is the Prophetic way.

questionEn: Why is it important to keep emergency contact info and blood-type/allergy details on a small card inside your Ihram belt?
optionsEn: Because blood type changes after Tawaf
Because cards replace Talbiyah
So if sudden heat exhaustion or fainting happens in a crowd, Haram medical responders can contact your companion/group and treat you safely without delay
Because security requires medical cards for Taqsir
explanationEn: Thoughtful medical preparedness protects lives—especially for elders or people with heart conditions, asthma, or severe allergies.

questionEn: If an international pilgrim lands in Jeddah intending Umrah, mistakenly forgets to enter Ihram before the plane crosses the Miqat, drives into Makkah, and THEN goes to Masjid Aisha (al-Tan'im) to enter Ihram—does going to al-Tan'im lift the Miqat violation Dam?
optionsEn: Yes, al-Tan'im replaces all five Miqats
Jeddah airport counts as al-Tan'im
Yes, if they pray four rak'ahs at al-Tan'im
